Endoscopic necrosectomy of infected pancreatic Walled-Off Necrosis using two types of Lumen-Apposing Metal Stents
articles.abstract: Background Lumen-apposing metal stent (LAMS) placement enables transmural drainage of walled-off necrosis (WON) with secure anchoring and provides endoscopic access for subsequent necrosectomy. This study compared the efficacy and safety of two commercially available LAMS designs (Hot-Axios vs. Micro-Tech) in patients with infected WON. Methods We retrospectively reviewed patients with infected WON who underwent endoscopic ultrasound (EUS)-guided LAMS placement followed by endoscopic debridement at our center between August 2020 and June 2025. Results Thirty-one patients were included (Hot-Axios, n = 21; Micro-Tech, n = 10). The overall necrosectomy success rate was 80.65% (25/31). Necrosectomy success was numerically higher with Hot-Axios than with Micro-Tech (85.71% vs. 70.00%), but the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.358). There was a statistically significant difference in the incidence of complications between the two groups (P = 0.007); bleeding occurred more frequently in the Hot-Axios group (33.33% vs. 0%), whereas stent migration was more common in the Micro-Tech group (0% vs. 20.00%). Conclusions In conclusion, endoscopic necrosectomy for infected WON using LAMS is feasible and effective. Hot-Axios may provide more secure fixation and better resistance to migration; however, it may carry a higher risk of bleeding.

articles.title: Equivalent linearization modeling and experimental validation of natural frequency and vibration isolation performance in metal braided hoses
articles.abstract: Metal braided hoses are widely used in the petroleum industry, marine engineering, aerospace, and other fields for their excellent displacement compensation and vibration damping. Stiffness properties have attracted most of the research so far, while the dynamic behavior of the hose remains comparatively understudied. This paper therefore establishes single-degree-of-freedom axial and bending dynamic models based on the Bouc-Wen hysteresis model and linearizes the nonlinear equations through energy-equivalent linearization, using the energy dissipated by the hysteresis loop. The linearized equations are solved analytically and validated against frequency sweep tests. The model predicts axial natural frequencies of 11.91 Hz and 19.60 Hz for the first two modes and 13.2 Hz for the first bending mode, all close to the measured values, so the equivalent linearized model can be considered reliable for engineering calculation in the low-frequency range. Experiments on hoses with different diameters, lengths, and braiding-layer numbers further show that the bellows size mainly determines the hose stiffness: larger bellows are stiffer but damp less, and adding braiding layers improves damping only until the accompanying increase in stiffness weakens isolation. In the measurements, the two-layer DN25 hose reached the highest axial vibration level difference of 12.83 dB, the longer DN25 hose reached 25.46 dB in bending, and the stiffer DN50 hose isolated much less, at 7.27 dB axially. These quantitative results provide concrete guidance for the design and application of metal braided hoses.

Knowledge, attitudes, and organ donor registration among medical and health sciences students: A cross-sectional study in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE
articles.abstract: Background Healthcare students serve as frontline ambassadors in promoting public awareness and shaping attitudes toward organ donation. This study assessed knowledge, attitudes, and organ donor registration among university students in Ras Al Khaimah, UAE, and identified factors associated with organ donor registration. Methods A cross-sectional study was conducted among undergraduate health sciences students using a structured self-administered questionnaire to collect data on sociodemographic characteristics, knowledge of organ donation and transplantation, attitudes, and donor registration status. Results The study included 428 students. The mean knowledge score was 7.77 ± 2.85 out of 19, indicating gaps in understanding of the definition of brain death, donor eligibility, and legal requirements. The mean attitude score was 41.58 ± 6.61 out of 65, suggesting generally positive attitudes towards organ donation, although concerns regarding organ misuse, body disfigurement, lack of trust, and fear of reduced quality of medical care were reported. Only 28.0% of participants were registered as organ donors, with a lack of awareness (39.0%) being the most frequently reported barrier among non-registered students. In multivariable logistic regression analysis, non-Arab students had lower adjusted odds of registration than Arab students, including Emiratis (aOR = 0.149, 95% CI: 0.072–0.310, p < 0.001). Compared with medical students, pharmacy (aOR = 0.050), dentistry (aOR = 0.032), and nursing students (aOR = 0.024) had significantly lower adjusted odds of registration (all p < 0.001). Students with a medical parental educational background also had lower adjusted odds of registration than those with a non-medical parental background (aOR = 0.129, 95% CI: 0.063–0.264, p < 0.001). Knowledge and attitude scores were not significantly associated with registration. Conclusion Despite generally positive reported attitudes toward organ donation, self-reported donor registration remained low, highlighting a discrepancy between stated willingness and registration behavior. Educational and awareness initiatives should address knowledge gaps, misconceptions, trust-related concerns, and perceived barriers to registration.

articles.title: Light meal consumption among university students in China: A multi-regional cross-sectional study of behavioral patterns, influencing factors, and service optimization strategies under supply-side heterogeneity
articles.abstract: This study surveyed 270 college students from seven major geographic regions of China and, using multiple ordinal logistic regression, structural equation modeling (SEM), importance–performance analysis (IPA), and K-means clustering, examined their light meal consumption behavior, its determinants, and service optimization pathways. Results show that light meal consumption is characterized by diversified demands, regular-meal-oriented timing, rigid price sensitivity, and functionalized categories; specific dietary needs are the core driver of consumption frequency (B = −1.985, p < 0.001), whereas grade, gender, monthly living expenses, and campus supply conditions are not significant. In universities without a light meal supply, consumption intention follows an “attitude–norm/control–intention” multiple mediation pathway, with subjective norm showing the strongest direct effect (β = 0.392). In universities with a light meal supply, supply–demand gaps across all six service dimensions are highly significant (p < 0.001), with taste and variety falling into the IPA improvement quadrant as core shortcomings. K-means clustering identifies three student groups in supplied universities (high-satisfaction loyal, differentiated rational, and low-satisfaction wait-and-see) and two in non-supplied universities (high-demand expectant and low-demand wait-and-see). The findings confirm that intrinsic health demands, rather than external supply conditions, are the core driver; peer effects are a key lever; taste and variety are the primary bottlenecks to repeat purchases; and student heterogeneity necessitates stratified strategies.

articles.title: Pain, sensory acceptability, and treatment compliance following cryotherapy and topical anesthetics in children: A randomized clinical trial
articles.abstract: This randomized clinical trial aimed to compare the effects of cryotherapy, anesthetic spray, and gel on pain, anxiety, physiological responses, taste acceptability, and treatment compliance in children aged 7–10 years undergoing their first dental treatment. 100 healthy children were randomly allocated into four groups: 10% lidocaine spray, 20% benzocaine gel, cryotherapy with distilled water cooled to +4 °C, and lidocaine spray cooled to +4 °C. Following topical application, buccal infiltration anesthesia was administered. Anxiety, pain, and physiological responses were assessed using the Modified Dental Anxiety Scale and Facial Image Scale, Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, and pulse-oximeter. Taste acceptability and treatment compliance were evaluated using a three-point Hedonic Scale and the FRANKL Scale. Repeated Measures ANOVA, Mann-Whitney U, and Kruskal-Wallis tests were applied. No significant differences were observed among the groups in anxiety, pain, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, or taste acceptability (p > 0.05). Pulse rate increased from the pre-operative to the post-operative period in all groups (p = 0.006), with no significant group × time interaction. FRANKL scores were significantly higher in the cryotherapy-distilled water group compared with the gel and cooled-spray groups (p = 0.001), a finding considered exploratory. Pain and anxiety outcomes following cryotherapy did not differ significantly from those of the topical anesthetic agents, while treatment compliance was higher, suggesting that cryotherapy may be a promising non-pharmacological option, pending confirmation in non-inferiority trials. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov NCT07198022

articles.title: Rigorous nested cross-validation and external generalization-gap analysis of a machine-learning classifier for U-251 glioblastoma cytotoxicity
articles.abstract: Glioblastoma remains difficult to treat, and drug-repositioning strategies require efficient methods to evaluate chemical libraries. Here, we developed a machine-learning binary classifier for compound activity against U-251 glioblastoma cells using a corrected single-center dataset of 236 compounds evaluated under a standardized cell-viability assay. Compounds were labeled as active or inactive using a predefined viability criterion (<50% vs. ≥ 50%) within a single-point screening framework using 10 µM as the upper screening concentration. To reduce optimistic bias and information leakage, we used repeated nested cross-validation in which preprocessing, feature selection, and hyperparameter optimization were performed within the training folds. ExtraTrees was selected based on Matthews correlation coefficient, showing moderate internal performance (ROC-AUC, 0.76; balanced accuracy, 0.66; MCC, 0.36). Structural analyses using nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity and Bemis–Murcko scaffolds indicated that the training set was scaffold-diverse with limited series bias. However, when the locked model was applied to an independent external set of 53 compounds, all compounds were classified as inactive, resulting in zero sensitivity, balanced accuracy of 0.5, and MCC of 0. The external ROC-AUC based on continuous prediction scores was 0.37, indicating poor threshold-independent ranking performance. Nearest-neighbor Tanimoto similarity did not explain prediction correctness or rescue active-compound recovery. Y-randomization supported the presence of a non-random internal signal, whereas scaffold-grouped cross-validation suggested that internal ROC-AUC was not solely driven by scaffold leakage. Overall, this study provides a reusable dataset and reproducible workflow, and highlights a substantial generalization gap between internal validation and external prediction in small chemical machine-learning datasets.

articles.title: Secondary school students’ perspectives on their school food environments and their proposed solutions for improvement: Case study in Northern Benin
articles.abstract: Background The food environment within and around schools plays a critical role in shaping secondary school students’ current and future eating behavior, food choices, and perceptions of healthy diets. However, little is known about how secondary school students in low-income settings perceive these environments and how such perceptions may influence their food practices. Methods A qualitative study was conducted in the municipalities of Natitingou (urban) and Boukombe (rural), Northern Benin, to explore secondary school students’ perceptions of their school food environments. In each municipality, two focus group discussions were held: one with lower-secondary students (11–15 years), and one with upper-secondary students (14–19 years), ensuring equal gender representation. Discussions addressed the types of foods available within and around schools, students’ food preferences and perceptions, and suggestions for improving their food environments. Data were analyzed thematically. Results Students reported access to a wide variety of foods within and near their schools, particularly in urban settings. However, most of these foods were energy-dense and high in sugar, while fruit and vegetables were rarely available. Participants perceived their school food environments as largely unhealthy, citing inadequate food hygiene practices and poor vendor sanitation as major concerns. Conclusion Findings highlight the need to integrate secondary school students’ perspectives into efforts to improve school food environments in Benin. Policies promoting the availability of nutritious foods and strengthening hygiene standards in and around schools could support healthier dietary behaviors among students. Future research should examine how these environments and perceptions influence secondary school students’ long-term nutrition and health outcomes.

articles.title: Sex and educational inequalities across functional ability trajectories in Chile: A sequence analysis of a 17-year national panel
articles.abstract: Context Research on disability and functional ability has increasingly moved from cross-sectional descriptions toward longitudinal analyses of intra-individual change. This shift has shown that functional ability follows heterogeneous pathways, encompassing stability, progressive deterioration, fluctuating limitations, partial recovery, and death. However, evidence remains concentrated in high-income countries, and fewer studies have examined long-term functional ability trajectories in Latin American contexts marked by rapid population aging and high socioeconomic inequality. In addition, comparisons across sex and educational groups require trajectory typologies that are constructed in a way that makes group comparisons methodologically comparable. Methods We used six observation points from the Chilean Social Protection Survey, a nationally representative longitudinal survey, covering the period 2004–2020. The analytic sample included 2,681 individuals aged 46–65 at baseline, contributing 16,086 person-wave observations. Functional ability was measured through self-reported limitations in activities of daily living and classified into five states: no limitation, low limitation, middle limitation, high limitation, and deceased. We reconstructed individual functional ability sequences over 17 years and applied optimal matching followed by hierarchical clustering. To ensure comparability across sex and educational groups, trajectory typologies were estimated within each baseline age group using the full age-group-specific sample. We then examined how membership in these pooled trajectory types varied by sex and educational attainment, referencing the composition of each trajectory type to the overall composition of its baseline age group. Findings Across the four baseline age groups, detailed trajectories were grouped into three broader types: mostly non-declining, progressive-declining, and equivocal-declining. Mostly non-declining trajectories were prevalent in all age groups, although their internal composition changed with baseline age, moving from stable good functional ability in younger age groups toward preserved functional ability before death in older age groups. Progressive-declining trajectories were especially visible among respondents aged 56–60 at baseline and remained substantial among those aged 61–65. Equivocal-declining trajectories were more frequently composed of women, most markedly among respondents aged 61–65 at baseline, and of respondents with primary education or less in the three younger age groups. Sex differences in trajectory membership were statistically significant in all age groups, while educational differences were statistically significant in the first three age groups. Conclusions Long-term functional ability trajectories in Chile are heterogeneous and socially patterned. By deriving pooled trajectory typologies within each baseline age group before comparing sex and educational groups, and by referencing group composition to the marginal composition of each age group, this study provides comparable evidence on how functional aging unfolds across socially stratified groups in an understudied Latin American context.

articles.title: Sex difference in survival benefits of immune checkpoint inhibitors in advanced non-small cell lung cancer: A meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background Whether sex influences the survival benefit of immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) in advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains uncertain. Methods We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Scopus up to April 1, 2026, for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing ICIs with chemotherapy and reporting overall survival (OS) or progression-free survival (PFS) stratified by sex. A random-effects model was used for meta-analysis. Results Sixty-three publications (reporting 42 phase 3 RCTs) involving 25,827 patients (18,772 male; 7,055 female) were included. Compared with chemotherapy, ICIs significantly improved both OS and PFS in males (OS: HR 0.74 [95% CI 0.71–0.78]; PFS: HR 0.59 [95% CI 0.54–0.64]) and females (OS: HR 0.83 [95% CI 0.77–0.90]; PFS: HR 0.76 [95% CI 0.66–0.86]). Pooled treatment-by-sex interaction analyses demonstrated significantly greater OS (interaction HR = 0.90 [95% CI 0.84–0.97]; P = 0.01) and PFS (interaction HR = 0.82 [95% CI 0.73–0.92]; P = 0.0006) benefits in males than in females. In subgroup analyses, sex‑based differences in OS reached statistical significance in patients receiving ICI monotherapy (P = 0.02), including those treated with anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (P = 0.04) and those with PD‑L1 expression ≥50% (P = 0.02). However, these differences did not persist after the False Discovery Rate (FDR) correction (adjusted P = 0.07, 0.10, and 0.07, respectively). In contrast, sex‑based differences in PFS remained statistically significant after FDR correction in the ICI monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), anti‑PD‑1 monotherapy (adjusted P = 0.001), and PD‑L1 ≥ 50% (adjusted P = 0.004) subgroups. No significant sex‑based differences in either OS or PFS were observed among patients treated with ICI plus chemotherapy. Conclusions Although ICIs are superior to chemotherapy in both sexes, the PFS benefit of ICI monotherapy appears to be attenuated in females relative to males. Given the imbalances in baseline confounders coupled with the underrepresentation of females in the included trials, these findings should be interpreted with caution and warrant confirmation in future RCTs designed specifically to investigate sex‑based differences.

articles.title: Short-video content perceptions, intention, and self-reported behavior in special forces-style tourism: Evidence from Chinese generation Z university students
articles.abstract: Special Forces-style tourism is an emerging high-intensity, low-cost travel phenomenon among young people in China. Drawing on a modified Theory of Planned Behavior, this study analyzes survey data from 526 Chinese Generation Z university students using PLS-SEM and fsQCA. Perceived content appeal, perceived content trustworthiness, attitude, and perceived behavioral control are positively associated with intention, which is positively associated with self-reported behavior; short-video platform usage intensity strengthens this association. fsQCA identifies two configurations for high and eight for low self-reported behavior. Intention, perceived content trustworthiness, perceived behavioral control, and platform usage intensity form the common core of both high-outcome configurations, while low perceived content trustworthiness appears in six low-outcome configurations. No single condition is necessary, and the results indicate configurational asymmetry.

articles.title: Spreading depolarization drives distant connectivity changes in the focally injured cortex
articles.abstract: by Daria A. Lachinova, Maria P. Smirnova, Ilya V. Sysoev, Lyudmila V. Vinogradova Cortical spreading depolarization (SD), a slow-propagating wave of transient cellular depolarization, reliably occurs after acute brain injury but usually remains undetected. Focal brain injury is known to produce a network-level dysfunction that changes the strength and direction of connectivity far beyond lesion site (connectional diaschisis) that can underlie post-injury neurological dysfunction. We suggested that injury-induced SD could contribute to connectional diaschisis and studied the effects of SD on functional and effective connectivity in neural networks supporting cognitive and sensory functions. Electrographic recordings of cortical activity were obtained in freely behaving rats immediately after focal micro-injury of the frontal cortex. The injury-induced SD propagated over the cortex of the ipsilesional hemisphere but never invaded the contralesional cortex. Strength and direction of connectivity were estimated using non-directional (mutual information function) and directional (transfer entropy) measures calculated for recordings from the retrosplenial (a key hub of the default-mode network) and somatosensory cortex. Mutual information analysis showed initial hypercoupling within the injured hemisphere (during SD) followed by longer interhemispheric decoupling (after SD termination). During post-SD hypoconnectivity, influence of the uninjured cortex on the injured one increased in both cortical regions. The retrosplenial cortex, component of the default-mode network, showed strong interhemispheric coupling during the baseline period and complex changes in connectivity after SD. Therefore, SD arising in the injured cortex disturbs long-range connectivity in distant cortical regions and causes widespread network alterations involving the default-mode network. Given the key role of the network in cognition, connectivity changes produced by injury-induced SD could contribute to the mechanisms of cognitive deficit after brain injury.

articles.title: Spreading the Joy of Literacy: A community-based survey of parents by parents
articles.abstract: Background Literacy is an important social determinant of health. Failure to develop emergent literacy skills before kindergarten is a risk factor for academic failure, poverty, incarceration, and early death. Reading comprehension depends on both language comprehension and alphabetic decoding skills. The Home Literacy Environment literature tends to focus on reading aloud to develop oral language but less is known about letter-themed tools. Design Our hypothesis was that letter-themed toys and books would be acceptable to all families but that lower socio-economic status (SES) households would be less likely to have them. Using methods of Community Based Participatory Research, 3 caregivers with young children living in the City of Rochester, NY, completed IRB training and provided cultural context for decisions throughout this study. We surveyed a convenience sample of 156 caregivers at 10 community events. We showed a poster with pictures of alphabet-themed toys and asked caregivers to count how many they had in the home. ZIP code was used as a proxy for SES. Results We surveyed 156 caregivers, excluding 13 responses because of missing information. Of the 143 remaining, 139 (97.2%) thought it was important that a child know most of the alphabet letters before kindergarten. 1 in 4 of our respondents didn’t have a single literacy toy in their home and an additional 1 in 6 had only one. We calculated a p value of 0.0004 for the hypothesis that there is a difference by SES in the number of these items in the home. Conclusions Our results are consistent with the hypothesis that joyful letter-themed tools are acceptable to parents in general but that low-SES households are less likely to have them. Closing the gap in early alphabet exposure could contribute to reducing inequities in school success and lifelong health.

articles.title: State-aware adaptive multimodal fusion for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting using sky cloud images
articles.abstract: As renewable energy penetration continues to increase, accurate ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting is essential for improving energy utilization and supporting power system operation. However, irradiance variations are jointly influenced by historical trends and rapid cloud changes, making traditional single-modal methods insufficient for capturing complex dynamics under varying weather conditions. This paper proposes a multimodal solar irradiance forecasting framework based on the collaborative representation of sky cloud images and numerical sequences. The framework introduces a heterogeneous modal state encoding mechanism and a state-aware adaptive selective attention fusion mechanism to enhance interactions between visual weather information and historical physical patterns. Specifically, the numerical modality captures irradiance trends and temporal correlations through dependency modeling, while the image modality extracts cloud structures and evolution features through spatiotemporal representation. The proposed fusion mechanism dynamically adjusts modality contributions according to forecasting conditions, enabling effective integration of complementary information. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed framework outperforms benchmark models in forecasting accuracy and robustness, validating the effectiveness of combining visual cloud information with numerical evolution patterns for ultra-short-term solar irradiance forecasting.

articles.title: Strengthening continuity of care for multiple long-term conditions in India through integrated referral and follow-up systems (SYNC-RF): A mixed-methods study protocol
articles.abstract: Introduction Multiple long-term conditions (MLTC) or multimorbidity are becoming increasingly common in low- and middle-income countries, such as India, placing demands on constrained primary healthcare systems that are still predominantly organised around acute care and single-condition management. Weak referral, counter-referral, and follow-up processes contribute to fragmented care and poor continuity for people living with MLTC. This programme of work aims to develop an integrated referral and follow-up model for people with MLTC who seek care in the primary healthcare system in India. Methods This sequential, multistage mixed-methods research programme will be conducted in three interlinked phases. First, a systematic review of global literature will be conducted, which will synthesise evidence on referral and follow-up models or systems for providing MLTC care. Second, a convergent mixed-methods assessment will be undertaken in Jodhpur district, Rajasthan, including facility assessments of Primary Health Centres and linked referral facilities, a cross-sectional survey of adults with MLTC, and in-depth interviews with patients, caregivers, healthcare providers, and policymakers. Quantitative data will be analysed using descriptive and inferential statistics, while qualitative data will be analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Third, an integrated referral and follow-up model, SYNC-RF (SYstem for Navigation, Coordination, Referral, and Follow-up), will be developed based on the triangulated evidence and refined through expert consultation to ensure feasibility and contextual relevance. Conclusion The study will generate context-specific evidence on gaps, barriers, and enabling factors affecting referral and follow-up for MLTC care. The integrated model developed through this research is expected to strengthen continuity of care, improve coordination across various levels of the health system, and improve health outcomes for those living with MLTC.

articles.title: Variation in recommendations for management of pediatric fever and neutropenia across databases and languages: A systematic review of clinical practice guidelines
articles.abstract: Background Fever with neutropenia (FN) is a common complication of cancer therapy associated with significant morbidity, mortality, and resource use. Clinicians currently may access multiple Clinical Practice Guidelines (CPG) for FN in children to guide decision-making, however variation in content could impact care globally. We performed a systematic review and content analysis of CPG to assess the impact of databases searched and publication language on the quantity, quality, and content of recommendations identified for pediatric FN. Methods We conducted a systematic search of PubMed, Embase, and Web of Science databases to identify evidence-based CPG published in the last 10 years addressing FN in children. We categorized CPG by language, extracted recommendations, characterized recommendation type (diagnostic, prognostic, or treatment), direction, and agreement with a recently developed international guideline. Methodological quality was assessed using the AGREE-II instrument and comparison between English and non-English CPG was performed using the Mann-Whitney U test. Comparisons of recommendation type (treatment, prognosis, diagnosis) and agreement with a reference guideline were assessed using the Chi-square test. Results Fourteen CPG met inclusion criteria. Ten were published in English and four in non-English languages. There was no significant difference in methodological quality between language categories across AGREE-II domains except for scope and purpose (95.2% versus 90.5%; p = 0.036). Each database contained one unique guideline and only 36% (5/14) of the CPG were indexed in three databases. Percentage agreement between recommendations covered by 14 CPG and the reference CPG ranged between 33% and 100%. Conclusions Using pediatric FN as an index topic, we found that language or database restrictions limit the quantity and content of recommendations. Since CPG have variable methodological quality regardless of source, clinicians should design appropriate search strategies based on context. We recommend a broad search strategy when healthcare context or disease prevalence differs across settings.

articles.title: Yield determinants in rice under organic and conventional production systems: Implications for selection strategies
articles.abstract: The persistent yield gap remains a major challenge in organic agriculture despite its increasing importance for sustainable food production. The present study compared the performance of 80 diverse rice genotypes (62 landraces and 18 modern varieties) under two contrasting production systems (organic and conventional). The experiment was conducted during the Kharif seasons of 2023 and 2024 using an alpha lattice design (8 × 10) with three replications. Agro-morphological and yield-related traits were analysed through pooled mixed-model analysis of variance (ANOVA), genetic variability parameters, correlation and path coefficient analyses, as well as principal component analysis (PCA). The results revealed significant genotypic variation and differential trait expression between the two production systems, with the relative contribution of agro-morphological traits to grain yield varying between production systems. Integrated analysis of genetic variability, correlation, path coefficient analysis, and principal component analysis identified production system-specific trait combinations associated with grain yield. Under the conventional production system, flag leaf breadth (FLB), number of productive tillers per plant (NPTP), hundred seed weight (HSW), and flag leaf length (FLL) were prominent traits, with strong positive direct effects in path analysis, whereas leaf area (LA), NPTP, HSW, plant height (PH), and days to 50% flowering (DFF) were prominent under the organic production system, also showing positive direct effects in path analysis. Genotypic best linear unbiased prediction (BLUP) estimates identified Ponmani samba (G40), Varakkal (G60), and Sengalapattu sirumani (G49) with the highest yield BLUP estimates under the organic production system, whereas Mani samba (G29), TKM1 (G80), and Bavani (G6) showed the highest yield BLUP estimates under the conventional production system. Milagu samba (G31), Polinel (G39), and Ponmani samba (G40) consistently ranked among the top-performing genotypes based on yield BLUP estimates across both production systems, indicating their potential as breeding materials for further evaluation.

articles.title: Bundibugyo Ebola outbreak: DRC cases climb to more than 10 000
articles.abstract: bmj;395/nov03_13/e101314/F1F1f1Xinhua/AlamyThe graves of people who have died from Ebola virus disease continue to spread around the outskirts of Bunia, the capital of the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s Ituri province. The outbreak has now claimed almost 5000 lives, and the number of confirmed cases has surpassed 10 000, the country’s health ministry announced on 30 October.This outbreak is driven by the rare Bundibugyo virus. There is currently no approved vaccine for the strain, but a phase 2/3 clinical trial is under way.1Among the recent fatalities is a doctor, Marie-France Shogogo, who was working in northeastern DRC, reported the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention.

articles.title: COP31: The Belem action plans are an opportunity to align climate, gender, and health
articles.abstract: The Belém Gender Action Plan on gender equity in climate governance and the Belém Health Action Plan on climate resilient health systems were adopted at COP30 in 2025. 12 Taken together, they explicitly state that climate related risks for health systems, healthcare staff, and patients are shaped by structural gender inequalities and that effective climate adaptation will require direct action to tackle inequalities. With COP31 quickly approaching, there is an important window to ensure health and gender responsive approaches move beyond commitments and are implemented to strengthen climate resilience and accelerate just transition.The adoption of the frameworks represents an important shift. Climate and health policy has often approached vulnerability primarily through geography or exposure to climate related threats. The Belém frameworks broaden this understanding by focusing on the social conditions that determine who is most affected by climate related health harm, who can access care, and whose needs remain invisible...

articles.title: Doctors struck off in Italy during covid pandemic could regain registration under new bill
articles.abstract: Doctors struck off Italy’s medical register during the covid-19 pandemic because of their antivaccine views could soon be allowed to apply for reinstatement.1On 27 October, one of the country’s political bodies, the Italian Chamber of Deputies, approved the move, arguing that as the evidence on covid-19 vaccines was still emerging during the pandemic, this uncertainty may have led some doctors to speak out against vaccination.The legislation could allow around 200 doctors to apply to a national commission to be reinstated on the medical register, according to Italian news outlet Il Post, although representatives of the medical profession say that the actual number of doctors concerned is much lower.Expert panels would still have to assess whether the doctors meet the relevant professional and ethical criteria.2The bill is now with the Italian Senate for debate but is expected to pass by the end of the year.However, the legislature has sparked an outcry...

articles.title: Early warning system for deteriorating children to expand to emergency departments across England
articles.abstract: An early warning system to spot deteriorating children will be rolled out across England’s emergency departments this winter.Called the Paediatric Early Warning System (PEWS), this requires staff to measure, record, and assess children’s vital signs, before assigning them a score. A higher score will result in the child receiving more urgent attention.Even if their clinical score is low, a child’s care can be escalated if medical staff, parents, or the patient themselves raise concerns, according to the plans announced by NHS England (NHSE).The PEWS system is already in use across 90 paediatric inpatient wards. Data show that these trusts have consistently lower rates of cardiac arrests among patients, NHSE said.1A similar system is also in use for adults across NHS hospitals. However, the children’s system includes age appropriate charts reflecting the different clinical needs of babies, children, and teens.While standardised scoring systems have been used in Denmark and across some...

articles.title: PFAS: UK population exposure to be examined in new study
articles.abstract: A new study to examine levels of so called “forever chemicals” in the UK population and their potential effects on human health will be launched by health officials.The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) will look at blood and urine samples to examine population level exposure to perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) and other chemicals such as lead and arsenic, with initial findings expected in 2027.The agency said there was limited existing evidence for effects of PFAS on health, but the strongest data currently available indicated possible links to raised cholesterol concentrations and lower birth weight.PFAS are a large group of more than 10 000 human-made chemicals that have been used in a wide range of industrial processes and consumer products since the 1950s. These range from everyday items such as food packaging, non-stick frying pans, clothing, and cosmetics to firefighting foams, waterproofing, and medicines.They are sometimes called “forever chemicals” because...

articles.title: We are failing to acknowledge or respond proportionately to the potential dangers of AI agents
articles.abstract: The BMJ covered the OpenAI hack of an Australian government health website1 and its potential implications.2 But the scale and severity of the implications do not seem to be fully appreciated. This event presents some simple truths, but it’s unclear if we can bring ourselves to acknowledge them or respond proportionately.Frontier AI models are, and will remain, far more advanced than most governmental cybersecurity systems. This hack is an “important prompt” for action, but “retrofitting our current cybersecurity with the ability to repel agentic AI attacks”1 is clearly insufficient. AI agents can, and likely will, access healthcare systems and their supporting infrastructure (energy, transport, water, and so on). Optimising cybersecurity is important, but we must prepare for fundamental healthcare technology to become unreliable, untrustworthy, or even to start actively harming patients.OpenAI took three months to disclose this event, yet AI “progress” is beyond fast. What else has happened since? We...

articles.title: [Articles] Long-term outcomes after percutaneous coronary intervention with drug-eluting stents versus coronary artery bypass grafting for left main coronary artery disease: a prospective analysis of the multicentre IRIS-MAIN registry
articles.abstract: In this non-randomised registry analysis of patients with left main coronary artery disease, there was no statistically detectable difference in all-cause mortality between PCI and CABG. For patients considered suitable for either strategy, multidisciplinary Heart Team discussion might help patients and clinicians weigh potential trade-offs in the choice between PCI and CABG. These findings are observational and cannot establish causal treatment effects or equivalence in survival.

articles.title: [Comment] Foodborne disease outbreaks in the USA and the need for prevention
articles.abstract: In 2026, the USA has grappled with large foodborne disease outbreaks, the most notable due to Cyclospora cayetanensis linked to iceberg lettuce. This outbreak, affecting thousands, has made international news and drawn criticism of the USA's reduced national capacity to conduct surveillance for foodborne diseases.1 Although foodborne diseases are more frequent in countries with inadequate sewerage and water and food safety infrastructure, they occur everywhere. It is a mistake to think that they are rare events in high-income countries.

articles.title: Estimated global treatment costs for 31 cancer types by stage, year, and follow-up period: a systematic review and modelling study
articles.abstract: Cancer is a growing health and economic burden worldwide, yet comprehensive global estimates of cancer treatment costs are sparse. Such data are crucial for economic evaluations to inform policy making and practice to improve cancer control and outcomes. We aimed to synthesise available estimates of direct cancer treatment costs by stage, year, and follow-up period and predict global cancer treatment costs. In this systematic review and modelling study, we extracted estimates of cancer treatment costs (ie, direct treatment costs only) from the medical literature, screening 25 896 studies, of which 196 were included in our final dataset, covering 31 cancer types across 44 countries. Costs were standardised as a ratio of country GDP per capita and adjusted for follow-up period. We used a Bayesian hierarchical model to synthesise the estimates as a function of GDP per capita, accounting for cancer type, stage (I-IV), year of diagnosis, and follow-up period. We then estimated global and regional treatment costs (overall and by cancer type) in US$ 2022 based on the latest available incidence data from GLOBOCAN. This study is registered on PROSPERO (#CRD420251138446). Globally, total 10-year treatment costs for newly diagnosed cancers in 2022 were estimated to be $771·48 billion (95% UI 719·99-823·81), with breast cancer being the largest driver of costs ($96·07 billion [80·78-109·43]), followed by leukaemia ($86·11 billion [80·36-94·87]) and lung cancer ($84·36 billion [73·18-95·28]). North America and Europe accounted for 64% of total costs, but only 36% of diagnosed cancer cases. Mean costs per diagnosed patient were $38 650 (95% UI 36 070-41 280) globally, ranging from $3380 (95% UI 2960-3820) in eastern Africa to $93 600 (95% UI 87 170-100 150) in North America. As a ratio of GDP per capita, treatment costs declined with increasing GDP per capita (from 3·16 [95% UI 2·61-3·81] at $500 GDP per capita to 1·36 [1·07-1·70] at $100 000 GDP per capita), especially for stage IV cancers, which declined from 8·06 (6·57-9·61) at $500 GDP per capita to 4·53 (3·48-5·83) at $100 000 GDP per capita. Cancer types with the highest mean cost ratios were bone cancer (6·27 [95% UI 2·45-11·73]), leukaemia (6·16 [5·59-7·01]), and multiple myeloma (5·74 [3·78-6·74]). Treatment costs remained stable over time by year of diagnosis for stage I-II cancers, but steadily increased for stage III cancers, and rose substantially for stage IV cancers. These cost estimates provide new important data for economic evaluations, which can support expenditure planning, priority setting, and policy making to help guide strategic investment and resource allocations to improve cancer care and outcomes across different settings. Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health.

articles.title: Trends at 50: a mission that matters
articles.abstract: What makes a great review article in your field? As more research is published every day, it has become increasingly difficult to keep up with the latest developments and to ensure that you are hearing from the leading scientists driving these innovations and advances. How do you know what is new and what is valuable?

articles.title: Acral melanoma: a unique subtype requiring unique solutions
articles.abstract: Acral melanoma (AM) is a ‘rare-by-rare’ melanoma subtype arising on the volar skin of the palms, soles, or nail apparatus. Unlike sun-exposed cutaneous melanoma (CM), AM has a low mutational burden but extensive structural genomic alterations, including clustered copy number events (‘hailstorms’/tyfonas) that contain amplification of oncogenes such as CCND1 and TERT. Mechanical stress and distinct clonal evolution, with late, often subclonal, MAPK mutations, may mediate AM development and progression. Nevertheless, AM management is largely extrapolated from CM. Benefits of immunotherapy and targeted therapies remain unclear due to limited trial enrollment and under-representation of diverse patient populations. In this review, we integrate current knowledge with critical challenges in AM research and outline priorities to accelerate AM-specific discoveries and treatments, close critical knowledge gaps, and improve patient outcomes through global collaboration.

articles.title: Decoding the functional specificity of E2F3 isoforms
articles.abstract: E2F3 is a central regulator of cell cycle progression, development, differentiation, and oncogenesis. Alternative promoter usage generates two major homologous isoforms, E2F3A and E2F3B, differing only at their N-termini. Although E2F3A is traditionally considered an activator and E2F3B a repressor of transcription, studies suggest that both isoforms have overlapping and isoform-specific functions, shaped by differences in temporal expression, protein stability, and target gene specificity. In this review, we examine how E2F3A and E2F3B contribute to proliferation, differentiation, and cancer. We also discuss contradictions and limitations in experimental approaches that have complicated the interpretation of these functions. Finally, we explore how clarifying these roles could help resolve long-standing questions in cell cycle regulation, differentiation, and cancer, where E2F3 plays a major role.

articles.title: Trends at 50: a mission that matters
articles.abstract: What makes a great review article in your field? As more research is published every day, it has become increasingly difficult to keep up with the latest developments and to ensure that you are hearing from the leading scientists driving these innovations and advances. How do you know what is new and what is valuable?

articles.title: What can behavior tell us about neural dynamics?
articles.abstract: For decades, systems neuroscience treated behavior as an endpoint: a simplified output, such as a button press, lick, or saccade, used to isolate neural computations. Richer behavioral measurements have expanded this view by revealing neural dynamics hidden by simple outputs. Yet behavior is not a direct readout of brain activity, because similar behavioral outputs can arise from different neural mechanisms. Interpreting neural dynamics is therefore an inverse problem with no straightforward solution. Behavior can constrain this problem by exposing sensorimotor loops, narrowing plausible explanations for population activity, and formalizing neural–behavioral relationships in joint models. Together, these approaches position behavior as a principled constraint on interpreting neural dynamics and latent cognitive, affective, and computational states.

articles.title: A Preventive Effect of Exercise in a Mouse Model of Essential Tremor
articles.abstract: The effects of exercise have not been widely studied for potential benefits in essential tremor (ET), while this has been growing for other neurodegenerative disorders. This study examines the effects of two types of exercise [high-intensity interval training (HIIT) and resistance training (RT)] on mice that were subjected to harmaline injections to trigger tremor. We employed a repeated-measures design with three groups: a HIIT group, a RT group, and a sedentary (SED) control group. Each group received an injection before and after the intervention. Tremor kinetics (power within the 8-14 and 14-29 Hz bands) were assessed using accelerometry. Tremor kinematics were also assessed using high-speed video analysis, for validation. As potential signalling molecules from exercise, we also tested for blood lactate and BDNF in each group. Compared to pre-intervention measurements, we found a significant decrease in power within the 8-14 Hz band combined with an increase in the 14-29 Hz band, for the HIIT group, but not in the RT or SED groups. We also found a change in BDNF concentration for the HIIT group. These results suggest that the HIIT protocol may have helped the animal to shift tremor frequency to higher bands, thereby offering functional resistance to harmaline-induced tremor. This study supports high intensity aerobic physical exercise as a potential therapeutic/preventive intervention for ET, with translational implications for human studies.

articles.title: A baseline for aquatic parasite diversity in West African mangroves: host-parasite records, DNA barcodes, and an experimental design for future use
articles.abstract: Macroparasites represent a major fraction of biodiversity and biomass in marine ecosystems, yet remain substantially underrepresented in ecological surveys and food-web models, particularly in the Global South. This study addresses this geographic bias by providing the first comprehensive ecological survey of macroparasite communities of fishes in a West African Marine Protected Area (MPA) and adjacent Open-Access Area (OAA) characterised by mangrove forests. We collected 5,020 parasite specimens from 10 fish and one crab species in the Saloum Delta, Senegal, identifying 27 parasite species across all major taxa. Our findings include 15 new records for Senegal of which 11 are also new for West Africa. Additionally, 64% of host-parasite combinations constitute new host records. We provide 208 DNA barcodes, offering the first molecular data for 31% of these species globally and establishing a reference library for future DNA metabarcoding efforts in the region. Using sample size-corrected biodiversity indices and mixed-model analyses, we detected significant variations in parasite infracommunities and component communities between the MPA and OAA, demonstrating the feasibility of using comparative study designs to monitor fisheries impacts on parasite diversity in the Saloum Delta. Furthermore, the identification of trophically transmitted parasites provided evidence of unstudied food-web connections, e.g. predator-prey linkages between fishes and higher-trophic-level definitive hosts including birds and elasmobranchs. By integrating morphological identification, molecular data, and archiving of voucher specimens into publicly accessible, curated collections, this study establishes a new baseline for marine parasite biodiversity in West Africa and provides a methodological blueprint for surveying understudied regions.

articles.title: A cotranslational role for selenocysteine in productive protein folding
articles.abstract: Selenocysteine (Sec) is generally regarded as the catalytic determinant that distinguishes selenoproteins from their cysteine (Cys)-containing counterparts. Consequently, the biological significance of Sec has largely been attributed to its unique chemical properties within mature proteins. Here, we uncover an unexpected role for Sec in protein biogenesis. Using the endoplasmic reticulum selenoprotein SELENOM as a model, we show that replacement of Sec with Cys redirects the protein into an alternative assembly pathway, resulting in formation of a stable domain-swapped homodimer. Biochemical and structural analyses demonstrate that this phenotype cannot be explained solely by altered active-site chemistry, as dimerisation persists following extensive active-site mutagenesis. Remarkably, reintroduction of Sec at alternative positions suppresses dimer formation, including when Sec is placed within a cleaved signal peptide and is absent from the mature protein. Thus, identical protein sequences can adopt distinct folding outcomes depending on whether Sec incorporation occurred during biosynthesis. These findings reveal a previously unrecognised role for Sec in productive protein folding and raise the possibility that evolutionary retention of the Sec incorporation pathway reflects advantages not only in catalysis but also in protein folding.

articles.title: A mouse model of metastasis-induced breast cancer cachexia with non-cachectic controls bearing isogenic primary tumors
articles.abstract: Background Patients with advanced cancer frequently develop cachexia, an involuntary weight-loss condition that correlates strongly with metastatic burden. Despite this clinical association, metastasis is rarely considered in preclinical research of cancer cachexia, which is in part due to the lack of rigorously established animal models to investigate metastasis-associated cancer cachexia. Methods To establish an animal model of metastasis-associated cancer cachexia, here we focused on syngeneic mouse models of breast cancer. Using the metastatic 4T1 murine breast cancer cell line and its isogenic non-metastatic 67NR cell line, we generated primary tumors via orthotopic injection into the mammary fat pad and surgically resected the primary tumor to allow sufficient time for spontaneous metastatic outgrowth, or generated experimental lung metastases by direct intravenous injection into the tail vein. Across these tumor-bearing groups, we systematically characterized the metastatic burden and cachectic phenotypes of the mice, including body weight, food intake, body composition, muscle mass, grip strength, locomotor activity, energy expenditure, and respiratory exchange ratio. To isolate the contribution of reduced food intake to the cachectic phenotypes, we pair-fed orthotopic 4T1 tumor-bearing mice (which were non-cachectic) to mice with 4T1 lung metastases (which were cachectic). We further measured muscle atrophy gene expression and profiled circulating cytokines and metabolic hormones for the mouse groups. Results Body weight loss occurred exclusively in mice bearing lung metastases from 4T1 tumors, with no weight loss observed in mice bearing either primary 4T1 tumors or 67NR lung tumors, thus presenting a model of cancer cachexia that is driven by 4T1 lung metastasis. Comprehensive cachexia characterization demonstrated that the 4T1 metastasis model recapitulates all key features of cachexia, manifesting as reduced food intake (or anorexia), depletion of adipose tissues, loss of lean mass including muscle mass loss, and reduced grip strength. Pair-feeding non-cachectic primary 4T1 tumor-bearing mice to 4T1 metastatic mice led to the same losses in body weight, fat, and lean mass as in cachectic mice, but no change in grip strength, indicating that anorexia is the primary driver of tissue wasting whereas muscle weakness arises through a food intake-independent mechanism. Moreover, we identified distinct circulating cytokines and metabolic hormones associated with the metastasis-driven cachexia. Conclusions Our results establish a metastasis-induced breast cancer cachexia model with a tightly matched control group, providing a platform for the field to identify metastasis-derived cachectic mediators and pathways.

articles.title: A phase decoder for reconstructing missing muscle activity
articles.abstract: Upper-limb assistive devices are commonly controlled with electromyographic (EMG) signals, but nerve injury, muscle loss, or practical limits on electrode placement can leave only a few usable signals, which constrains the decoding of intended movements. Here, we introduce a decoder that reconstructs missing muscle activations from sparse EMGs using a two-stage real-time approach: (1) estimating ongoing movement phase from available signals, and (2) retrieving corresponding muscle activations from a library of pre-recorded muscle activity templates. In proof-of-concept tests, neurologically intact participants (N=4) performed object-transfer tasks under simulated denervation conditions. The decoder accurately estimated movement phase (median root-mean-square error [RMSE] <0.17 of movement duration) and reconstructed missing muscle activations (RMSE 0.08-0.34; correlation up to 0.97) within ~2 ms, in a previously unseen participant. The results indicate that template based reconstruction could leverage sparse EMG for low latency control of assistive technology. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. This work was supported by the Office of the Assistant Secretary of Defense for Health Affairs through the Restoring Warfighters with Neuromusculoskeletal Injuries Research Program (RESTORE) under Award No. W81XWH-21-1-0138 (SY). articles.title: AI-based structural modelling and pathogenic variant mapping across the human protein interactome
articles.abstract: Spanning the complex landscape of the human proteome, physical interactions between proteins coordinate cellular organization, signaling, regulation, and homeostasis. Yet the three-dimensional structures of most of these interactions remain unresolved. Here, we performed AI-based modelling of 109,282 human protein interaction structures, generating a structural resource for large-scale analysis. The predicted structures were systematically characterized through analysis of interface residue involvement, buried surface area, intermolecular bonding, and energetic properties. Additionally, we mapped pathogenic variant data onto the predicted structures, identifying interface-localized mutations for over 4,000 annotated disease categories. Acute myeloid leukemia, Alzheimer's disease, and cardiomyopathy were examined as representative disease contexts for exploring the distribution of interface mutations within disease-associated protein interaction networks. Strengths and limitations of predictive capabilities were also assessed, including through experimental structure comparisons. Collectively, this structural resource and accompanying analyses offer a basis for developing novel hypotheses and informing experimental studies involving human protein interactions in physiological and disease contexts.

articles.title: APP functions at the endomembrane system
articles.abstract: INTRODUCTION: APP is a type I transmembrane protein, and its intracellular domain (AICD) interacts with FE65, X11, and mDAB1, et al., through the YENPTY motif. Accordingly, it has been proposed that the functions of APP are similar to Notch, which regulates gene expression through releasing NICD after combining with its ligands. However, the detailed underlying mechanisms of how FE65 is regulated by APP, as well as their target genes, remain unknown. METHODS: We overexpressed APP695 in N2a cells, and deleted/mutated APP in H4 cells by CRISPR-Cas9, respectively. The impacts of APP overexpression and ablation were detected by proteome comparison and immunoblotting. Thereafter, the subcellular localizations of APP and its binding protein FE65 were examined by immunofluorescence. RESULTS: APP overexpression not only resulted in its retention in Golgi apparatus (GA) and Endoplasmic reticulum (ER), but also induced FE65 clustering. In addition, it significantly reduced the protein level of ATF4 in N2a cells. On the contrary, knockdown of FE65 restored the protein level of ATF4. More importantly, APP overexpression also impaired autophagy. In contrast, knockout of APP rescued LC3 conversion. Of note, the APP Swedish mutant did not impact ER stress or the autophagic flux. Nevertheless, it facilitated the cleavage of APP-CTFs by gamma-secretase. DISCUSSION: The evidence presented in the current study demonstrates that APP is involved in stabilizing the endomembrane system and the subcellular transport of FE65. More importantly, the role of APP in regulating autophagy indicated that full-length APP could be considered a therapeutic target for preventing the development of AD. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: ARCADE disentangles cell abundance from continuous transcriptional state in spatial transcriptomics
articles.abstract: Spatial transcriptomics is widely used to infer both cell-type abundance and within-type transcriptional variation, but these signals are difficult to separate in mixed spot-level measurements. Here, we present ARCADE, a computational framework that addresses two major sources of uncertainty in spatial analysis: unstable single-cell references and entanglement between abundance and cell state. ARCADE first builds a robust reference through hyperparameter optimization and consensus filtering, then performs spatial inference in two stages by estimating cell-type composition before modeling continuous intratype transcriptional programs around this compositional anchor. Across simulated and semi-synthetic benchmarks, ARCADE improves deconvolution accuracy and yields more stable state inference than existing approaches. In matched human dorsolateral prefrontal cortex datasets with spatial proteogenomic readouts, ARCADE distinguishes localized cell enrichment from astrocyte and microglial activation programs. These results show that decoupled modeling can improve the interpretability of spatial transcriptomic signals in complex tissues.

articles.title: Adipocyte Kindlin-2 Coordinates an E-cadherin/β-catenin/IGFBP2 Endocrine Axis to Regulate Skin Regeneration and Diabetic Wound Healing
articles.abstract: Skin wound healing is a complex, multicellular process essential for maintaining tissue integrity and homeostasis. Despite advances in biomaterial and cell-based therapies, the mechanisms by which adipose tissue regulates skin regeneration remain incompletely understood. Here, we identify adipocyte Kindlin-2 as a critical regulator of cutaneous wound repair. Adipocyte-specific deletion of Kindlin-2 markedly accelerates wound closure in mice by enhancing fibroblast proliferation, angiogenesis, and suppressing inflammation. Transplantation of visceral white adipose tissue (vWAT) from Kindlin-2-deficient mice similarly promotes wound healing, indicating an endocrine contribution of vWAT to skin regeneration. Mechanistically, loss of Kindlin-2 promotes E-cadherin proteolysis, resulting in increased release of a 33-kDa C-terminal fragment (CTF2) that activates {beta}-catenin signaling and induces transcriptional upregulation and secretion of insulin-like growth factor binding protein 2 (IGFBP2). Elevated circulating IGFBP2, in turn, stimulates integrin signaling in target cells to enhance wound repair. Pharmacological inhibition of {beta}-catenin signaling abrogated the healing advantage conferred by Kindlin-2 deficiency. Conversely, local delivery of IGFBP2 via lentiviral significantly accelerates wound closure in both wild-type C57BL/6 and diabetic ob/ob mice. Collectively, these findings uncover a previously unrecognized adipose-skin endocrine axis governed by Kindlin-2 and IGFBP2 that orchestrates tissue regeneration. Targeting this Kindlin-2/E-cadherin/{beta}-catenin/IGFBP2 pathway offers a promising therapeutic strategy for enhancing wound healing, particularly in chronic and diabetic wounds.

articles.title: Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics reveals selective organization of α-synuclein inclusions
articles.abstract: -Synuclein inclusions, the lesions typical of Parkinson's disease, have been interpreted as protective deposits, toxic species or failed degradation products, each predicting a different composition and correlating that enrichment with neuron dysfunction and eventual degeneration. Distinguishing them requires measuring what an inclusion concentrates relative to the cell that built it. Here we developed Aggregate Deep Visual Proteomics, which uses ultrasensitive mass spectrometry to profile laser-microdissected inclusions against the remainder of the same cell or a matched host. In HEK293 cells, iPSC-derived dopaminergic neurons and post-mortem patient brain, each inclusion concentrated a selective subset of its cell's proteome, independent of abundance and dominated by membrane, in neurons largely presynaptic. Inclusions took up whole assemblies, with subunits moving together in 421 of 438 complexes, and the V-ATPase alone was enriched in all three systems. Degradation cargo stayed with the receptors that route it, consistent with sequestration and failed degradation acting together. Neuritic and somatic inclusions differed, the former rich in UBQLN2 and the latter in intermediate filaments. In the cell line, phosphorylated -synuclein was tenfold higher in the inclusion than in the rest of the cell, with about one third of the rise already present before an inclusion was visible. Measured against its host, the composition of an inclusion becomes a readout of how it formed and a source of candidate markers and therapeutic targets.

articles.title: Allocating resources across time in a cumulative allocation game
articles.abstract: We investigate an alternative to decision under risk where players begin with an endowment of wealth, and their goal is to increase this wealth as rapidly as possible by repeatedly investing part of it. In such a Cumulative Allocation Game (CAG), expected wealth can grow exponentially but - if wealth ever goes to zero - the game is over and the participant wins nothing (ruin). CAGs can be used to model a wide range of biological and economic activity from casino gambling to animal foraging to stock market investment (Kelly Criterion). However, there is little previous research concerning human performance in CAGs and how it relates to human performance in similar decision-under-risk tasks. In two experiments we asked participants to complete four CAGs designed to allow us to test a series of hypotheses about human performance and compare it to normative play maximizing their log rate of growth. In the main experimental conditions, participants performance was initially close to normative but their proportion bet decreased by almost a factor of two over the course of the experiment. This reduction in proportion-bet decreased their expected rate of growth by roughly 25% - a substantial deviation from optimal. Why would participants systematically abandon a normative strategy? We conjecture that a possible reason is loss aversion, well documented in decision under risk. We conjecture that while loss aversion in decision under risk is sub-optimal, there is an intrinsic asymmetry between losses and gains in CAGs that could explain the loss aversion we observe. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Amyloid/RNA Condensates with Germ Granule Characteristics Are Present in Rat Epididymal Spermatozoa and Exhibit Prion-Like Propagation Activity
articles.abstract: Environmental exposures to the germline can alter its epigenome resulting in new traits being acquired by offspring. While the epigenetic carrier in mammalian spermatozoa remains unknown, studies in C.elegans show that amyloids and sperm-specific populations of germ granules, phase-separated biomolecular condensates enriched in RNA-binding proteins and small noncoding RNAs, transmit heritable epigenetic phenotypes to descendant cells. Here we discovered that rat epididymal spermatozoa contain germ granule-like condensates in the head perforatorium, a cytoplasmic derived structure that participates in early post-fertilization events. The perforatoria condensates contain evolutionarily conserved germ granule markers and small noncoding RNAs and are enriched in amyloid, including those of the clinically relevant amyloidogenic proteins androgen receptor (AR) and TDP43. Further, perforatoria extracts exhibit prion-like propagation behavior by functioning as molecular seeds to template amyloid assembly in recombinant AR and TDP43. We propose that nature has conserved sperm germ granule-like structures throughout evolution to allow an organism to respond and adapt to a changed environment by passing environmentally encoded information to the embryo via a non-Mendelian protein-based mechanism of inheritance. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. John Templeton Foundation, https://ror.org/035tnyy05, 62184

articles.title: An Efficient Microfluidic Platform for Organ-Specific CyclicMultiaxial Loading and Differentiation of Progenitor Cells
articles.abstract: Mechanical loading is a fundamental regulator of tissue development, maturation, and function, yet existing in vitro systems predominantly apply uniaxial load/strain to cell-laden hydrogels, limiting their ability to reproduce physiologically relevant multiaxial on-chip tissue mechanics. Here, we present an engineered system to apply controlled multiaxial mechanical loading to real scaffolds with undifferentiated cells. The system enables programmable cyclic stretching and relaxation at the cell scaffold level and is compatible with both cell-laden native scaffold and engineered soft tissues. We have quantified the strain field experienced by the tissue with distinct mechanical loading periods using computation simulations and validated these with systematic experiments, demonstrating reproducible and various organ-relevant multiaxial strain profiles. As proof of concept, we applied the approach to human cardiac tissues, where cyclic multiaxial mechanical loading of mononuclear cells laden native tissue scaffold promoted cardiac structural organization and supports the emergence of spontaneous contractile activity. This approach provides a generalizable method for reproducing physiologically relevant tissue mechanics in vitro and enables systematic investigation of mechano-regulation across a plethora of human tissues. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors declare no competing interests, either financial or non-financial. However, the microfluidic device described in this study is covered under Indian Patent No. 202541028777, which has not yet been commercialized. Indian Council of Medical Research, Government of India, IIRPIG-2023-0000716

articles.title: An Ovol1 Variant in Endothelial Cells Regulates Slug and is Essential for Pathological Angiogenesis
articles.abstract: During development, the blood vasculature expands by sprouting angiogenesis, but the programs that guide this process can become dysregulated in the pathological angiogenesis of neovascular diseases leading to excessive disorganized blood vessels. We previously reported that in endothelial cells, the pro-mesenchymal transcription factor Slug critically regulates angiogenesis through a partial and reversible endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition (pEndoMT); however, the upstream regulators that activate Slug and may contribute to pathological activation of the pEndoMT pathway in disease are still poorly understood. Here, we show that endothelial cells express an unusual low molecular weight variant of Ovol1 - a zinc-finger transcription factor that regulates mesenchymal transition in epithelial cells. Ovol1 and Slug are co-expressed in angiogenic endothelial cells, and using ChIP, we confirm direct Ovol1 binding to the endogenous Slug gene at a species-conserved binding motif. Whereas Ovol1 is typically a transcriptional repressor in epithelial cells, we find using a combination of silencing RNA and lentiviral overexpression constructs that the endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug, and is sufficient to drive pEndoMT marker expression and enhance endothelial cell migratory capacity. Silencing of Ovol1 abolished sprouting angiogenesis in a 3D in vitro sprouting angiogenesis assay, whereas constitutive overexpression of Ovol1 produced overaggressive and disorganized hypersprouting that depends upon Slug. We generated Ovol1 or Slug endothelial-specific knockout mice (Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO) and found that healthy developmental angiogenesis of the neonatal mouse retina proceeds relatively normally in knockout animals. By contrast, Ovol1 was reduced in established post-natal blood vessels but became strongly re-expressed in tumor endothelial cells, and we found that colorectal cancer syngraft growth was significantly reduced in both Ovol1ECKO and SlugECKO mice alongside a failure of tumor angiogenesis. Lastly, neovascularization in the oxygen-induced retinopathy (OIR) model was also reduced in SlugECKO mice. In conclusion, we report that an endothelial Ovol1 variant upregulates Slug and drives a mesenchymal-like state, and that this Ovol1-Slug pEndoMT signaling axis is essential for pathological angiogenesis in neovascular disease models. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Louisiana Cancer Research Center, CR1305A6 NIH Common Fund, P30GM145498, GM135000-02 National Science Foundation, 2543698 Louisiana Board of Regents, 091A-24 EENT Foundation of New Orleans, EE221102 United States Department of Defense, W81XWH2110108 Tulane University, https://ror.org/04vmvtb21

articles.title: Antibiotics drive immunometabolic rewiring of human immune responses
articles.abstract: Antibiotics are routinely evaluated for their antimicrobial activity, potential host toxicity, and disruption of the microbiome. Certain antibiotics can also impact cell-intrinsic host processes, including evolutionarily conserved processes in the mitochondria. These raise the possibility that antibiotics can directly impact host immunity, which relies on mitochondrial function for their immunometabolic activation. However, the immunological consequences of most antibiotics in current use have not been systematically examined. Here, we performed a comprehensive analysis of the effects of clinically used antibiotics on activation of primary human immune cells. We uncovered an underappreciated antibiotic-specific modulation of immune function in healthy individuals and infectious disease patients. Focusing on the immunomodulatory antibiotic ciprofloxacin, we found altered mitochondrial gene expression across multiple immune populations, driving distinct, lineage-specific responses and heightened sensitivity of T-cells. Ciprofloxacin impaired primary human T-cell expansion and activation and altered mitochondrial function and metabolism. We further demonstrated immunomodulatory effects of selected antibiotics in response to inactivated bacteria and during live viral infection. Finally, to test the implications of our findings in vivo, we showed that immune activation is altered shortly after a single dose of antibiotic administration in mice. This work established a widespread impact of antibiotics on immune-cell function, and identified mitochondrial perturbation as one underlying mechanism, with implications for host-pathogen interactions and antimicrobial therapy. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.
