articles.title: Brain mitovesicles undergo stage-specific remodelling during the progression of amyloid-β pathology
articles.abstract: Mitochondrial dysfunction is an early feature of Alzheimer's disease that shows nonlinear changes as the disease progresses. However, how these changes are reflected in the mitochondrial material released by brain cells remains poorly understood. Mitovesicles are a recently described extracellular vesicle subpopulation of mitochondrial origin that provide a unique insight into mitochondrial alterations in the brain and could potentially show how nonlinear changes evolve across disease stages of amyloid-beta pathology. Here, we isolated forebrain-derived small extracellular vesicles and mitovesicles from wild-type and Amyloid precursor protein (App) knock-in (AppKI) mice, carrying familial AD mutations and progressively accumulating amyloid-beta plaques, at presymptomatic (2-month) and symptomatic (12-month) stages using high-resolution density gradient fractionation. Vesicle identity and composition were assessed by morphological, biophysical and quantitative proteomic analyses, and mitovesicle respiratory function was measured by extracellular flux analysis. We show that mitovesicles carry a distinct, predominantly mitochondrial inner membrane proteome that is remodelled by age and disease in a stage-specific manner. Compared with small extracellular vesicles, mitovesicle proteomic profiles captured disease progression more clearly, with symptomatic AppKI mice forming the most molecularly distinct group. At the presymptomatic stage, AppKI mitovesicles showed reduced mitochondrial protein representation, most notably of fatty acid {beta}-oxidation and lipid-metabolism proteins associated with astroglial and vascular signatures, preceding any detectable respiratory impairment. At the symptomatic stage this reversed: AppKI mitovesicles were enriched for oxidative phosphorylation, mitochondrial membrane and transporter proteins, yet showed reduced Complex IV-linked respiration, revealing a dissociation between mitochondrial cargo abundance and respiratory function. Selected cargo changes were not mirrored in whole-brain tissue, indicating selective remodelling of mitovesicle content. Comparison with mitovesicles from post-mortem human Alzheimer's disease frontotemporal cortex and hippocampus identified a conserved 62-protein mitovesicle core, dominated by oxidative phosphorylation subunits and mitochondrial carriers. In addition, 25 of these proteins were enriched in mitovesicles derived from Alzheimer's and AppKI forebrains, defining a conserved mitovesicular disease signature. Together, these findings establish forebrain-derived mitovesicles as a dynamically remodelled vesicle population that reflects progressive mitochondrial dysfunction in the Alzheimer's disease brain and provides a cross-species resource for future biomarker and mechanistic studies.

articles.title: Brain-wide representations of olfactory behavior in C. elegans
articles.abstract: Olfactory navigation emerges from dynamic interactions between sensory input, brain activity state and the animal's own movements. In C. elegans, a compact nervous system enables brain-wide imaging in behaving animals exposed to controlled olfactory environments, with an undulatory locomotion that reduces navigation to transitions among forward runs, reversals, and turns. Here, we used tracking microscopy to record and compare brain-wide neural activity in crawling worms navigating spatial odor gradients or isotropic environments, and in immobilized worms responding to temporal odor pulses. Across conditions, we identified strongly correlated brain-wide activity patterns spanning olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor interneurons. Comparisons between navigation in odor gradients and exploration in isotropic environments revealed a compact functional circuit linking olfactory sensory neurons, interneurons, and premotor neurons. Comparisons between different odors distinguished sensory activity relationships associated with odor identity from a shared sensorimotor circuit for navigational movement. Comparisons between crawling and immobilized animals revealed profound differences in motor-state transitions and brain-wide correlation structure, further demonstrating the dependence of sensory representations and motor decision-making on behavioral context. Our findings reveal a functional organization linking olfactory sensory activity to navigational movement and show how this organization depends on behavioral state and environmental context. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. articles.title: CTLA-4 checkpoint signalling modulates germinal centre dynamics and antibody avidity during Borrelia burgdorferi infection in mice.
articles.abstract: Borrelia burgdorferi, the causative agent of Lyme borreliosis, persists in mammalian hosts despite robust activation of innate and adaptive immunity. A hallmark of murine infection is the production of low-avidity antibodies, yet the immunological mechanisms underlying this defective humoral response remain poorly understood. Here, we used single-cell RNA sequencing of draining lymph node cells from Borrelia-infected mice at days 7 and 14 post-infection, comparing transcriptional profiles with those from mice immunised with heat-killed Borrelia or with a potent germinal centre-inducing protein immunisation. Borrelia infection induced a rapid germinal centre response, however, light zone B cells displayed diminished expression of co-stimulatory and T-B cell interaction molecules while maintaining core germinal centre identity markers, suggesting impaired positive selection. T follicular helper cells upregulated multiple inhibitory checkpoint receptor genes, most prominently Ctla4, alongside an active germinal centre engagement programme. Foxp3? regulatory T cells upregulated genes associated with follicular-homing and suppressive function, including those implicated in CTLA-4-mediated trans-endocytosis. To test whether inhibitory signalling contributes to the impaired humoral response, infected mice were treated with anti-CTLA-4 blocking antibody. CTLA-4 blockade significantly increased plasma cell numbers and enhanced both the magnitude and avidity of Borrelia-specific IgG responses, including the induction of complement-fixing IgG2a. These findings reveal that CTLA-4-dependent inhibitory signalling contributes to defective antibody quality during Borrelia infection, identifying a mechanism by which dysregulated T cell responses may facilitate impaired humoral control of a persistent spirochaetal pathogen.

articles.title: CardioShift: Resolving cell-to-cell functional heterogeneity in hiPSC-derived cardiomyocytes from high-throughput single-cell imaging
articles.abstract: High-content screening of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) is widely used for disease modeling, yet standard pipelines rely on whole-well averages that obscure cell-to-cell heterogeneity. Moving from well-averages to single-cell analysis reveals hidden variations, but may introduce a pseudoreplication bias if cells are analysed as independent data points. We present CardioShift, an open-source bioimage informatics framework designed to map single-cell distributions by properly accounting for this nested variance structure. Applying this framework to 32,818 Ca2+ transients and 10,719 contractility-lipid profiles, we show that cell-to-cell variability represents the largest source of variance for most functional parameters, demonstrating how traditional well averages mask condition-dependent phenotypes. Furthermore, unsupervised clustering identifies condition-dependent shifts in functional subpopulations, including a distinct cellular state that accumulates lipids but maintains baseline contraction kinetics that was not detected using well- and single-cell averaging approaches. CardioShift provides a robust analytical approach to resolve hidden single-cell distributions. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. articles.title: Cell-lineage selection interacts with development and life history to shape the rates and identity of heritable mutations
articles.abstract: Mutation rates determine the supply of heritable variation and are central to evolutionary theory, yet they are usually treated as properties of molecular mutational processes. We hypothesised that mutation rates are also shaped by selection among cell lineages within organisms and that the strength of this process depends on developmental and life-history traits. To test the extent of this idea, we combined mathematical modelling with experiments in Drosophila melanogaster and treated mutation rates as emergent properties of interactions among molecular mutagenesis, development, life history, and cell-lineage selection. The model predicts that even modest effects of mutations on cellular fitness can substantially alter the probability that mutations are transmitted, and that these effects depend strongly on developmental architecture, germline dynamics, and time to reproduction. In Drosophila , we experimentally demonstrate biased transmission of a mutation affecting cellular proliferation and show that this bias changes over the reproductive lifespan of the individual. Extending the model genome-wide reveals that the cellular distribution of fitness effects and its interaction with developmental parameters influence both the estimated mutation rate and the composition of transmitted mutations, producing transmission biases that favour mutations with particular cellular fitness effects. These results suggest that developmental and life-history parameters determine how cellular fitness effects translate into transmission bias; therefore, estimates of heritable mutational input can vary from species to species even under constant molecular mutagenesis. By filtering mutations before they enter populations, developmental and life-history evolution can modify both the rate and the nature of heritable variation and thereby influence evolutionary trajectories.

articles.title: Chronic hypertension disrupts the blood-brain barrier in the ventral hippocampus in females but not males in a rat model of vascular cognitive impairment
articles.abstract: Background: Chronic hypertension is a leading cause of cerebrovascular disease, ischemic stroke, and cognitive impairment. In addition, anxiety and hypertension often co-exist, however, little is known about the relationship between the two. Understanding how chronic hypertension impacts limbic brain regions such as the ventral hippocampus may provide insight into how cerebrovascular contributes to altered emotional behavior. Methods: An open field task was used to quantify locomotion, exploratory behavior, thigmotaxis, rearing and risk assessment behaviors in adult (7-month-old) male and female normotensive Wistar rats and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR; n=8/group). Blood-brain barrier (BBB) permeability was assessed by measuring extravasation of sodium fluorescein, 3 kDa Texas red dextran and 10 kDa cascade blue into the ventral hippocampus. Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays were used to measure markers of vascular signaling, inflammation, and central nervous system-specific proteins indicative of neuroaxonal and glial injury in serum from separate groups of male and female SHR (n=6/group). Main effects and interactions between two independent variables (sex and hypertension) were determined using two-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) with Tukey's post-hoc tests. Circulating factors were compared using a Welch's t-test. Relationships between BBB permeability and anxiety-like behavior were determined using Pearson's correlations. Results: Chronic hypertension increased circulating inflammatory factors and BBB permeability in female but not male rats. BBB permeability did not differ by sex in male and female normotensive rats. There was an anxiolytic effect of chronic hypertension on exploratory-related anxiety-like behavior, including less thigmotaxis, lower latency to cross through the center of the arena, and increased unsupported rearing. Risk assessment behavior, quantified as stretch-attend posture, was increased in female SHR. BBB permeability in the ventral hippocampus was correlated with anxiety-like behavior in females, but not in males, suggesting sex-dependent mechanisms of hypertension-induced changes in emotional behavior. Conclusions: These findings implicate a role for chronic hypertension-induced BBB disruption in neuropsychiatric disorders in the female sex and advances our understanding of cerebrovascular vulnerability in deep limbic brain regions. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke, 1R01 NS127284

articles.title: Closed-loop acoustic stimulation promotes local slow oscillation train initiation and persistence in elderly adults
articles.abstract: Slow oscillations (SOs) during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep support memory consolidation and metabolic waste clearance. Aging is associated with reduced SO amplitude and density and disrupted temporal organization, characterized by more isolated events and shorter SO trains. We investigated whether closed-loop acoustic stimulation (CLAS) could enhance the initiation and persistence of rhythmic SO activity in elderly adults. Twenty-seven participants underwent a baseline night followed by an experimental night, during which online-detected SOs were either stimulated using CLAS (STIM; n = 16) or left unstimulated (SHAM; n = 11). We quantified the proportions of isolated and consecutive SOs, train-initiation probability, and SO train length. Analyses assessed local effects around online-detected SOs and global effects across NREM sleep using offline detection. Locally, CLAS reduced the proportion of isolated SOs and increased the proportion of consecutive SOs, train-initiation probability, and mean train length. Global overnight effects were weaker but directionally consistent, primarily reflecting a shift toward longer SO trains. These changes occurred without a significant between-group difference in the change in SO density, and local effects remained significant after adjustment for SO density. Thus, CLAS promoted sustained rhythmic activity beyond changes in SO occurrence. These findings suggest that CLAS can modify the temporal organization of SOs in elderly adults, supporting its potential to mitigate age-related disruptions in SO dynamics. Temporal organization measures may complement conventional amplitude and density measures when evaluating CLAS effects. Further studies should establish whether these changes translate into cognitive benefits or improvements in other aspects of brain health. ### Competing Interest Statement RR and CF are co-founders of NeuroAcoustics Inc., a startup developing technologies for the detection of sleep slow oscillations and their modulation through closed-loop acoustic stimulation. The research presented in this manuscript is directly related to the company's technological development activities. The remaining authors declare no competing interests. Data collection was funded by NeuroAcoustics Inc.

articles.title: Comparison of Hydroponic and Substrate-Based Methods for Screening Pea Genotypes for Resistance to Fusarium oxysporum.
articles.abstract: Pea (Pisum sativum L.) is one of the most economically and nutritionally important legumes due to its protein, vitamin, and mineral content. It also represents a source of income for producers. One of the major constraints on pea production is vascular wilt caused by the fungus Fusarium oxysporum. One strategy for disease management is the use of resistant varieties, which highlights the need for efficient methodologies to evaluate genotype responses to the pathogen. The objective of this study was to compare the efficiency of hydroponic and conventional substrate-based methods for evaluating the responses of pea genotypes to F. oxysporum under semi-controlled conditions. The hydroponic method used a modified Hoagland and Arnon nutrient solution with adjusted nutrient concentrations, whereas the conventional substrate-based method used plastic bags containing one kilogram of peat. The pathogen inoculum was obtained from pea plants affected by the disease in the municipality of Puerres, Nariño, Colombia (isolate FPUE02). In both methods, six pea genotypes and an uninoculated control were evaluated using a randomized complete block design with three replicates. Plant growth parameters, disease incidence, and disease severity were recorded. The hydroponic method showed greater sensitivity in discriminating among susceptible genotypes and facilitated the monitoring of disease progression in the roots. These results highlight the potential of the hydroponic method as a tool for the phytopathological evaluation of pea germplasm. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Development and cross-cohort evaluation of a multimodal deep-learning model for ER, PR and HER2 status classification in breast cancer
articles.abstract: Background. Estrogen receptor (ER), progesterone receptor (PR) and HER2 status guide systemic treatment in breast cancer. Multimodal models are rarely benchmarked against key biomarker molecular baselines or evaluated for cross-cohort calibration. We assessed incremental value, dependence on label-proximal HER2 transcripts, and transport of discrimination and calibration. Methods. A model combining whole-slide images, transcriptomes, age and stage was developed in TCGA-BRCA (1051 patients; ER/PR/HER2 analysis sets: 1001/998/1006) and evaluated in CPTAC-BRCA (120 patients; 118/113/95). CPTAC had been observed during earlier development and included 13 HER2-positive cases. Analyses included paired model comparisons, transcript removal, alternative loss functions and recalibration. Internal discrimination used pooled out-of-fold predictions; external discrimination used fold-mean estimates, with ensemble calibration reported separately. Internal calibration and macro-AUC uncertainty were interpreted as exploratory. Results. Internal AUCs were 0.943 for ER, 0.901 for PR, and 0.860 for HER2; external AUCs were 0.952, 0.937, and 0.918, respectively. External macro-AUC was 0.936 for the multimodal model and 0.957 for logistic regression using ESR1, PGR, and ERBB2 (difference -0.021). Removal of the extended 29-transcript 17q12-q21 region changed HER2 AUC by -0.035 \[-0.058 to -0.013\] (95% CI) internally and by -0.042 \[-0.089 to -0.007] externally relative to the baseline multimodal model. For external 15-model ensemble predictions, recalibrated HER2 expected calibration error (ECE) was 0.236, exceeding the ECE reference ceiling of 0.125, while calibration-in-the-large was -1.657 [-2.373 to -1.023\] (profile-likelihood 95% CI), indicating systematic overprediction. ER and PR also showed overprediction. In paired fold-mean comparisons, HER2 ECE and Brier score favoured the three-transcript model (ESR1, PGR, and ERBB2). Conclusions. A multimodal deep-learning model achieved high discrimination across cohorts but did not demonstrate clear incremental value over a parsimonious three-transcript baseline, while cross-cohort calibration remained a substantial challenge. These findings highlight the importance of evaluating incremental value, calibration, and clinical utility alongside discrimination when assessing AI-based prediction models for medical use. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Diagnose Harmonisation (DHARM): An open-source tool for the harmonisation and analysis of batch effects in MRI-derived measures.
articles.abstract: Technical differences between scanners, acquisition protocols, machine hardware and processing pipelines can introduce systematic variation into MRI-derived measures. Numerous harmonisation methods have been developed to reduce these effects. However, validation of these methods is often performed using different criteria depending on the method itself, the datasets used and the study design. Consequently, determining whether harmonisation is required, selecting an appropriate method and establishing whether or not technical variation has been sufficiently removed without compromising biological signal remain challenging. In this manuscript, we introduce Diagnose Harmonisation (DHARM), an open-source Python toolbox for diagnosing batch effects, applying harmonisation and evaluating harmonisation performance in cross-sectional and repeated-measures settings. DHARM is user-friendly, comes with GUI-based and command-line interfaces, and has graphical reporting. It provides standardised reporting workflows combining complementary measures of batch-associated differences in feature location, scale, empirical distributions, covariance and multivariate structure, together with measures assessing preservation of biological covariate effects and repeated-measures consistency. The framework includes several established harmonisation approaches, but its evaluation workflow is method-agnostic: users can also supply data harmonised using external or newly developed methods and benchmark their outputs using the same common set of diagnostics. We demonstrate DHARM using multisite cross-sectional MRI measures from UK Biobank, Cam-CAN and OxBAC as well as travelling-heads data from the ON-Harmony dataset. Across the cross-sectional datasets, harmonisation substantially reduced additive batch effects, while residual differences in variance and empirical distributions varied between methods. Multivariate diagnostics further demonstrated that reduction of batch-associated structure can coexist with preservation or increased detectability of biologically relevant variation. In the repeated-measures example, harmonisation reduced batch-associated and within-subject variability, while broadly preserving subject-level and biological relationships. DHARM provides a reproducible framework for diagnosing batch effects, applying different harmonisation methods and evaluating harmonisation as a multi-criteria problem rather than relying on a single measure of success. By jointly characterising technical variation and preservation of biologically meaningful information, DHARM can support dataset- and objective-specific selection, benchmarking and validation of harmonisation strategies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. articles.title: Differential effects of chronic hypertension and sex on vascular density along the septotemporal axis of the hippocampus in a rat model of VCID
articles.abstract: Background: Chronic hypertension is a major modifiable risk factor for vascular contributions to cognitive impairment and dementia (VCID), yet vascular changes that precede cognitive dysfunction remain poorly understood. This is particularly relevant for the hippocampus, a deep brain structure critical to memory function, which differs along its septotemporal axis functionally and in its susceptibility to hypoxic/ischemic injury. The impacts of hypertension and sex on hippocampal vascularization remains unclear and could contribute to the development/progression of VCID. Methods: In this study, adult male and female Wistar and spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR) were used at 5 months old, an age before memory impairments. Vascular density and morphometric parameters in dorsal and ventral hippocampus were quantified using high-resolution confocal microscopy and 3D vascular reconstruction. Results: In SHR, vascular density was increased in the dorsal hippocampus in males and across dorsal and ventral hippocampus in females compared to normotensive rats. Diameter and length of the microvasculature shifted to be smaller and longer during hypertension in males, but not females. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate chronic hypertension increases vascular density differentially by sex along the septotemporal axis of the hippocampus in mid adulthood that may increase vascular resistance and potentiate perfusion deficits or increase sites of blood-brain barrier disruption and contribute to VCID. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. articles.title: Distinct antischistosomal profiles of antimalarials and TRP agonists
articles.abstract: Schistosomiasis control relies on praziquantel mass drug administration, but reports of field treatment failure and laboratory-selected resistance highlight the need for alternatives. Praziquantel activates a schistosome transient receptor potential (TRP) channel, TRPMPZQ. Alternative leads or chemotherapies include meclonazepam, which activates a distinct schistosome TRP channel, and the antimalarials artemether and mefloquine, whose flatworm targets are unknown. To compare molecular responses and assess cross-resistance, we conducted comparative RNA-seq and efficacy studies in infected mice. We profiled adult Schistosoma mansoni recovered 48 hours after artemether or mefloquine treatment and compared responses with existing datasets for TRP agonists praziquantel and meclonazepam. Transcriptional profiles clustered by drug class but showed largely distinct changes, with only 33 upregulated and 63 downregulated transcripts shared across treatments. Plexin domain-containing genes were strongly induced by both TRP agonists and, to a lesser extent, by antimalarials. Artemether downregulated gene families expressed in intestinal cells (saposins, cathepsins, and Bax inhibitor-like proteins), consistent with potential heme-dependent activity in the schistosome gut. Genes involved in glutamine metabolism, iron homeostasis and responses to oxidative damage were upregulated across multiple treatments. We evaluated all four treatments in mice infected with praziquantel-susceptible or resistant parasites. Praziquantel (200 mg/kg) reduced resistant male worm burdens by only 39.3%, versus 99.0% in susceptible parasites. Meclonazepam (83.0% versus 91.6% in susceptible parasites), mefloquine (99.1% versus 98.8%), and artemether (98.2% versus 99.4%) retained activity. The distinct transcriptional responses and retained activity against praziquantel-resistant parasites support further investigation of these compound classes as praziquantel alternatives or potential combination partners. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institutes of Health, https://ror.org/01cwqze88, R21 AI153545

articles.title: Distinct processing of visual motion by transcriptomic cell types in the superior colliculus
articles.abstract: How the brain organizes visual processing across distinct neuron types is a fundamental yet unresolved question. Here we study how visual motion is processed by transcriptomically defined cell types in the superior colliculus (SC). We generated or identified transgenic mouse lines to target three transcriptomic types of neurons in the superficial SC, the Cbln4+, Vip+, and Grp+ neurons. We find that each of these cell types encodes distinct ranges of stimulus direction, speed, size, and spatial and temporal features. In response to ecologically relevant visual flows, the three cell types occupy partitional spaces in the encoding manifold. The three cell types also show unique morphology and connectivity, including their retinal and intracollicular input and projection patterns. Together, these results reveal a genetic logic for visual motion processing in the SC, where transcriptomic cell types are likely the basic computational units with their specific feature selectivity, morphology, and input-output connectivity. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. NIH, EY026286, EY020950

articles.title: DoAggregate: a pipeline for aggregation testing for rare-variant on a gene and pathway level
articles.abstract: Motivation Aggregation tests overcome the classical limitation of rare variant analysis in cohort study design. Choosing the right statistical test remains one of the biggest challenges. Existing tools fall short in offering a comprehensive solution that includes automatic data processing, testing across all genes, as well as exploration of broader genetic regions such as pathways and Gene Ontology (GO) terms. Most aggregation tests only report p-values and basic statistics, lacking in the presentation of cohort level statistics and comparison of results across whole genome or exome scales. Results We introduce DoAggregate, an innovative, scalable pipeline designed to address these challenges. DoAggregate enables users to perform aggregation tests across genes, pathways, and GO terms. It leverages Excalibur, an ensemble approach combining 36 distinct aggregation methods. The pipeline enhances data analysis by presenting over-representation analysis and aggregation results in detailed Excel sheets, complete with annotations and plots to facilitate nuanced interpretation and comparison. Applied to public exome data from the 1000 Genomes Project, DoAggregate tested 10,447 genes, 49 over-represented pathways and 36 over-represented GO terms in a single run, returning annotated, cohort-level results for each region. Availability and implementation DoAggregate source code, documentation and installation instructions as well as test data sets and results are freely available at https://github.com/boutrys/DoAggregate and released under the MIT license. The repository contains the serial implementation (R package), the parallel implementation for Slurm-based computer clusters and the web application. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. articles.title: Evolution Shapes Cortical Interneuron Migration
articles.abstract: The cerebral cortex comprises excitatory neurons and inhibitory interneurons originating from distinct forebrain regions. During migration, cortical interneurons (cINs) interact dynamically with neighbouring cells and their microenvironment, contributing to cortical architecture. However, how evolutionary changes in cIN migration shape species-specific cortical development remains unclear. Comparative analyses in mouse, ferret, and human models revealed a conserved migratory sequence but distinct behaviours: human cINs migrate slower, display increased leading-process branching, and exhibit more frequent homotypic repulsive interactions than their mouse and ferret counterparts. These features promote dispersed cortical invasion of cINs in humans and ferrets, contrasting with the stream-like migration observed in mice. Mechanistically, elevated expression of the cytosolic carboxypeptidase CCP1 in human cINs reduces microtubule glutamylation and doublecortin recruitment, thereby facilitating leading-process branching. These findings identify a CCP1-dependent mechanism regulating cIN dispersion and suggest that evolutionary changes in cIN migration contribute to divergent patterns of cortical morphogenesis across mammals. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: Fast rate coding in heterogeneous spiking networks
articles.abstract: A network of spiking neurons is said to operate in the rate coding regime if its dynamics can be accurately described by a continuous rate network. But how can discrete spike-based communication between neurons give rise to continuous rate-based dynamics? Computational studies showing that heterogeneous spiking networks can approximate the dynamics of recurrent neural networks (RNNs), a special case of rate network, assume that spikes are approximately Poisson or that network dynamics are slow. Here, we show that neither assumption is necessary: heterogeneous networks of non-Poisson neurons can produce fast rate-based dynamics. To demonstrate this, we show that signal transmission in feedforward networks of integrate-and-fire-type neurons can be described by a history-dependent rate network that is asymptotically exact as network size grows, even if heterogeneity persists, while linear-nonlinear rate networks fail. By providing a constructive model of fast rate coding in heterogeneous networks, this work lays the foundation for extending rate-based analyses of neural recordings beyond the assumption of slow dynamics or Poisson rate codes. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Swiss National Science Foundation, https://ror.org/00yjd3n13, 200020-207426, 200021-236436, 222150

articles.title: Functional Reconstitution of Human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 in Proteoliposomes: Effect of Bicarbonate Gradients and Substrate-specific Stimulation on Transport
articles.abstract: The hepatic organic anion transporting polypeptides OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 are critical for the clearance of widely prescribed drugs, hepatotoxins, and endogenous metabolites. However, the thermodynamic driving force governing their transport has remained a subject of debate due to the complexity of cellular models. Here, we report a defined, reconstituted proteoliposome system to study the transport kinetics of isolated human OATP1B1 and OATP1B3. Through direct functional assays, real-time counter-ion tracking, and a novel ABCG2-OATP1B1 functional co-reconstitution, we identify an outwardly directed bicarbonate gradient as a thermodynamic driving force for concentrative substrate uptake. In contrast we find no evidence for the proposed role of reduced glutathione efflux as a possible driving force. Targeted mutagenesis experiments revealed that the conserved TM3 residue His115 is needed to couple the bicarbonate gradient to concentrative substrate uptake, mechanistically linking substrate antiport to local pH-sensitive bicarbonate processing. We also investigated the substrate-specific stimulatory effect of the green tea catechin epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG) on OATP1B3 transport, confirming that this effect is intrinsic to OATP1B3, substrate specific, and does not need the involvement of other cellular proteins. Our findings define the energetic basis of OATP1B1 and OATP1B3 hepatic xenobiotic clearance.

articles.title: GNG2-MRAS interaction regulates SHOC2-dependent RAF activation and MAPK signaling
articles.abstract: Dysregulation of the mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) signaling pathway is a hallmark of many human cancers and RASopathies. The SHOC2-MRAS-PP1Cα; (SMP) holophosphatase complex is a crucial regulatory node of this pathway. It activates the MAPK pathway by dephosphorylating the inhibitory phosphoserine on RAF kinases and thereby relieving RAF autoinhibition. Although GNG2, the γ-subunit of heterotrimeric G proteins, has recently emerged as a negative modulator of MAPK signaling, its molecular mechanism of action remains incompletely understood. Here, we identify GNG2 and its truncated variants as inhibitors of SMP complex assembly by directly targeting MRAS. Using NanoBiT live-cell bioluminescence, co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP), biolayer interferometry (BLI), and molecular dynamics simulation studies, we demonstrate that full-length GNG2 (residues 1-71aa) and two helical fragments (Δ1, residues 1-29aa and Δ2, residues 30-71aa) bind MRAS, disrupt SMP complex formation, and therefore prevent RAF dephosphorylation. Expression of the truncated GNG2 variants significantly reduced phosphorylation of ERK in cells, consistent with inhibition of pathway activation. Furthermore, a short peptide synthesized from the GNG2 Δ2 sequence effectively disrupted SMP complex formation in both purified protein systems and live cells and potently attenuated MAPK signaling. Molecular dynamics simulation studies revealed that GNG2 variants engage with the Switch I/II regions of MRAS, sterically interfering with SHOC2-PP1Cα association. Together, these findings establish GNG2 as a direct regulator of SMP complex assembly and demonstrate that GNG2-derived peptides represent a promising strategy for disrupting SHOC2-MRAS interactions and suppressing MAPK signaling in RAS/RAF-driven pathologies. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. NIH Common Fund, https://ror.org/001d55x84, R15GM163260, R01GM138671 New Jersey Health Foundation, https://ror.org/040may582

articles.title: Genome-wide loss of chromatin accessibility coexists with selectively elevated RNA abundance in nutrient-starved U2OS cells
articles.abstract: Background Chromatin accessibility is widely used as a proxy for regulatory potential and is often interpreted together with RNA-seq to infer gene-regulatory responses. However, the quantitative relationship between chromatin accessibility and transcript abundance may become difficult to interpret, particularly under acute cellular stress. Metabolic challenges such as nutrient deprivation are known to induce extensive chromatin remodelling and transcriptional reprogramming, raising the question of whether changes in transcript abundance are directly governed by chromatin accessibility in these contexts. Clarifying this relationship is critical for interpreting epigenomic data under stress conditions, and requires careful distinction between Tn5 accessibility, relative steady-state RNA abundance and transcriptional output. Results We integrated ATAC-seq and RNA-seq analyses in human U2OS osteosarcoma cells following 18 h of severe nutrient deprivation. We found that starvation was associated with a genome-wide reduction in accessibility and almost all significantly altered accessible regions showed reduced signal relative to actively growing cells. This decrease affected promoter- and enhancer-associated regions alike, including housekeeping-gene promoters and CTCF-motif sites. In contrast, RNA-seq revealed a more selective change in relative steady-state RNA abundance: only a minority of expressed genes were differentially regulated, and approximately 64% of differentially expressed genes showed increased relative RNA abundance. Changes in accessibility and transcript abundance were modestly correlated at promoters (Pearson r = 0.25) and weakly at enhancers (r = 0.10), and together explained only ~6% of the variance in transcript abundance changes. The relationship was graded: genes with the smallest promoter losses were about four times as likely to show increased RNA abundance as genes with the largest losses, independently of baseline promoter accessibility. Within-condition analyses similarly showed only modest relationships between promoter accessibility and RNA abundance in both actively growing and starved cells. Pathway-level analysis of mRNA abundance revealed the expected repression of biosynthetic and growth-related programmes, including ribosome biogenesis, translation and cellular growth, together with a less anticipated relative activation of stress-adaptive programmes, including extracellular matrix organisation, lipid and cholesterol metabolism, small GTPase signalling and developmental processes. For genes within these activated programmes, increased steady-state mRNA abundance was observed despite reduced ATAC-seq accessibility at associated regulatory regions. Exon-intron analyses of RNA-seq data indicated that these changes predominantly reflect altered RNA production. Metabolic labelling of nascent RNA at selected loci confirmed increased transcription of genes involved in adaptive programmes despite reduced promoter and enhancer accessibility, alongside with reduced production of biosynthetic transcripts and rRNA. Conclusions These findings demonstrate that chromatin accessibility and steady-state RNA abundance are only modestly coupled during severe nutrient deprivation, against a baseline of similarly modest promoter accessibility-abundance coupling. This underscores the limited ability of ATAC-seq accessibility to predict transcript abundance under this stress condition and supports a model in which chromatin accessibility acts as a permissive rather than deterministic layer of gene regulation. The selective induction of adaptive programmes, confirmed here at the level of RNA production, shows that transcriptional activation can occur despite genome-wide loss of ATAC-seq accessibility.…

articles.title: Graph neural network approach for inferring neuronal connectivity
articles.abstract: Understanding the connectivity of neuronal networks is essential for understanding brain function. Current anatomical mapping techniques, such as serial section microscopy and viral tracing, are resource-intensive and cannot capture the efficacy of connectivity. A complementary approach is to infer effective connectivity from single-neuron-resolution population activity. We developed a graph neural network (GNN)-based tool, CircuitGNN, that accurately infers neural effective connectivity from population activity. CircuitGNN accurately inferred the connectivity of several small circuits and detected both the strengthening and weakening of connections, such as those that occur during learning. CircuitGNN outperformed other methods when applied to simulated population activity generated by an invertebrate central pattern-generating circuit and a cortical microcircuit. CircuitGNN was evaluated on networks of varying size, recording duration, and proportion of hidden neurons. Although performance improved with longer recordings, CircuitGNN achieved high precision with recordings as short as 4 min, scaled to large circuits of up to ~750 neurons, and remained robust when 20% or 40% of neurons were hidden. These results establish CircuitGNN as an accurate and robust technique for inferring neural connectivity from activity. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. National Institutes of Health, R01 NS101356

articles.title: GxE and changes to the genetic architecture of flowering time in an overwintering environment
articles.abstract: Characterizing how the expression of genetic variation changes across environments is essential for understanding evolution in complex environments, the evolution of phenotypic plasticity, and the genetic architecture of adaptation. We investigated how the phenotypic distribution, large-effect loci, and polygenetic architecture of flowering time in Arabidopsis thaliana changes when grown in an ecologically realistic environment compared to standard chamber conditions. We grew 479 A. thaliana accessions in an overwintering common garden that have previously been phenotyped in growth chambers by the 1001 Genomes Project (2016). Our findings suggest there is extensive GxE for flowering time between the overwintering common garden and the growth chamber environments. None of the large effect loci that we identified using a multivariate Genome Wide Association Study (GWAS) were shared across growth conditions. We find evidence of allelic differential sensitivity, conditional neutrality, and antagonistic pleiotropy contributing to GxE for flowering time between growth conditions. Our results also suggest that the effects of genetic variation across multiple flowering time regulatory pathways is revealed when grown in a more ecologically realistic environment. The effect sizes for the most significant 1% of SNPs are moderately correlated between the outdoor and growth chamber conditions which indicates a partially shared genetic basis. Overall, our findings highlight how making inferences about the genetic basis and evolution of complex traits may be dependent on conducting experiments in ecologically realistic environments.

articles.title: HER3 mediates metabolic reprogramming in metastatic colorectal and pancreatic cancer
articles.abstract: Liver metastases are a major cause of mortality in colorectal cancer (CRC) and pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), yet the oncogenic signals that shape tumor metabolism in the hepatic niche remain poorly understood. Here, we show that HER3 activation drives a liver metastasis-specific glycolytic program in both cancer types. Genetic or pharmacological HER3 inhibition suppresses cancer glycolysis while increasing dependence on oxidative phosphorylation (OXPHOS), rendering liver metastases vulnerable to OXPHOS inhibition. Combining the HER3 inhibitor sapitinib with distinct OXPHOS inhibitors led to in vitro synergy and durable tumor-free survival in orthotopic CRC and PDAC liver metastases models, with further validation in patient-derived xenografts. Mechanistically, HER3 promotes glycolysis through activating PFK2 and reduces OXPHOS through activating DRP1-mediated mitochondrial remodeling, both pathways were activated in liver metastases compared to matched primary tumors. Together, our findings identify the HER3-AKT/RSK-PFK2 axis as a driver of glycolysis and metastatic growth and reveal an OXPHOS dependency induced by HER3 inhibition that may be exploited through combined HER3 and OXPHOS targeting in metastatic CRC and PDAC. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. The Department of Defense, HT9425-23-1-0656, HT9425-23-1-0657 National Cancer Institute, https://ror.org/040gcmg81, CA278982

articles.title: HLAResolver: A statistical framework for resolving HLA ambiguity in T-cell response data
articles.abstract: Large-scale models of T-cell recognition require training examples that specify the complete T-cell receptor (TCR)-peptide-human leukocyte antigen (HLA) complex. Multiplexed Identification of T-cell Receptor Antigen Specificity (MIRA) is a high-throughput assay that identifies TCRs associated with responses to specific peptides, but does not determine which HLA presents each peptide. Because a donor can carry up to six distinct class I HLA-A, HLA-B, and HLA-C alleles, each response may have several candidate presenting HLAs. To narrow this set of candidate presenting HLAs, we developed HLAResolver, a statistical framework that combines MIRA response patterns across HLA-typed donors with NetMHCpan predictions of peptide presentation. For each peptide, HLAResolver uses negative-binomial regression to jointly estimate associations between HLA alleles and TCR response counts, accounting for differences in assay yield. NetMHCpan eluted-ligand predictions guide sparse regularization, favoring alleles with stronger predicted presentation while allowing strong MIRA response evidence to support alternatives. To assess whether this integration provides an advantage over either approach alone, we compared HLAResolver with NetMHCpan, which predicts peptide-HLA presentation, and the Restrictor Analysis Tool for Epitopes (RATE), which infers HLA associations from T-cell response patterns. Using held-out MIRA experiments, we assessed each method's ability to predict observed responses and the number of candidate HLAs it assigned. At matched specificity for predicting MIRA responses, HLAResolver achieved higher sensitivity while selecting fewer candidate HLAs per peptide than either comparator. ### Competing Interest Statement All authors are employees of Adaptive Biotechnologies.

articles.title: Hmox1/CO regulates retina regeneration via modulation of Wnt/β-catenin signalling and induction of vaspb in zebrafish
articles.abstract: Muller glia (MG) in the zebrafish retina retain a latent stem cell capacity that is absent in mammals, yet the injury responsive signals that drive this reprogramming remain incompletely defined. Here, we identify heme oxygenase-1 (Hmox1), the stress-inducible, rate-limiting enzyme of heme catabolism, as a previously unrecognized regulator of this process. Following injury, hmox1a is selectively and rapidly induced among the heme oxygenase gene family, localizing to photoreceptors with expression peaking during the MG proliferation window. Pharmacological inhibition and morpholino mediated knockdown of Hmox1 dysregulate the acute inflammatory response, impair Muller glia-derived progenitor cell (MGPC) proliferation, and produce lasting deficits in retinal lamination, establishing Hmox1 as a potentially non-redundant, early-acting node required for structural recovery. Exogenous delivery of carbon monoxide (CO), a bioactive Hmox1 metabolite, partially rescues each of these phenotypes, functionally implicating CO as a key downstream effector. Mechanistically, Hmox1/CO signalling stabilizes β-catenin likely via transcriptional repression of the Wnt antagonist dkk1b. This stabilized β-catenin is enriched at a predicted Tcf7l2 site in the promoter of vaspb, which encodes an actin binding protein and is newly identified here as an injury-induced Wnt target gene. Bioinformatic and functional analyses further implicate Nfe2l2a (Nrf2) as a candidate intermediary bridging Hmox1/CO to Wnt regulation, with putative antioxidant response elements identified within the dkk1b locus. Together, these findings outline a putative Hmox1→CO→Nrf2→dkk1b→β-catenin→vaspb relay coupling redox biology to Wnt-dependent glial reprogramming. Notably, HO-1 is similarly induced in stressed mammalian retina, yet Wnt/β-catenin activation fails to sustain regeneration, positioning the Hmox1/CO axis as a candidate target for future investigation in mammalian retina regeneration. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. Anusandhan National Research Foundation, Government of India, CRG/2022/001663 Defence Research and Development Organisation, https://ror.org/05k37v296, LSRB/01/15001/LSRB-409/SH&DD/2023

articles.title: Imipramine binds to amyloid-β and extends the survival of Alzheimer's disease patients
articles.abstract: Background Apolipoprotein E (apoE) plays numerous roles in the pathogenic pathway to Alzheimer's disease (AD). We previously performed a high-throughput screen and identified the antidepressant imipramine as an inhibitor of the interaction between apoE and amyloid-{beta} (A{beta}). We also found that imipramine use to treat depression in AD patients was associated with better Mini-Mental State Exam (MMSE) scores. Here we studied the mechanisms by which imipramine inhibits the AD pathogenic pathway and investigated its effect on mortality in AD patients. Methods Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy was used to characterize the interaction between imipramine and A{beta} monomers. Human induced pluripotent stem cell (hiPSC)-derived AD cerebral organoids (COs) and transgenic AD rats treated with imipramine underwent neuropathological evaluation, while rat learning and memory were assessed in the Morris Water Maze. AD patient mortality in the National Alzheimer's Coordinating Center's database was analyzed by Kaplan-Meier and Cox proportional hazards models. Results Imipramine inhibits the apoE-A{beta} interaction by binding directly to A{beta} monomers. Imipramine reduces A{beta} accumulation and neuronal cell loss in AD COs. Imipramine-treated female AD rats had enhanced reference memory and increased hippocampal cellularity and cholinergic neurotransmission. AD patients prescribed imipramine had reduced all-cause mortality over 10 years relative to those prescribed other tricyclic antidepressants (TCA), non-TCA antidepressants, or no antidepressants. Conclusions The findings support the conclusions that: a) the mechanism by which apoE confers risk for AD is by catalyzing the polymerization of A{beta} into neurotoxic species, b) targeting apoE is a promising, underappreciated strategy for the prevention of AD, c) imipramine should be used more frequently to treat depression in AD clinical practice, and d) imipramine should be evaluated in prospective trials, particularly in APOE4 carriers, as a potential method to improve cognition and reduce mortality in AD.

articles.title: Influence of antibody-antigen interaction on fluorescence of Rhodamine 6G conjugated to the antibodies measured in human serum
articles.abstract: Fluorescent dyes conjugated to monoclonal antibodies specifically trastuzumab (TRAS) and pertuzumab (PERT) serve as sensitive reporters of changes in the local energetic environment arising from antibody-antibody and antibody-antigen interactions. Upon covalent conjugation, the antibody local environment perturbates the energetic state of the dye, resulting in changes of the fluorescence emission energy and emission width of the dye. The dependence of these spectral parameters on antibody concentration was measured in HBS-8, diluted and undiluted human serum. In addition, the emission energy and emission width of dye-conjugated TRAS were investigated as a function of recombinant human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) extracellular domain concentration in HBS-8 and in diluted and undiluted human serum. Antibody-antibody and antibody-antigen interactions produce remarkable contributions into the emission energy and emission width. These contributions depend on the composition of the surrounding medium. Our study showed that the samples containing 100 nM TRAS in serum exhibited the largest spectral changes upon interaction with HER2 suggesting that antibody-antigen interaction are not linear across concentration range of the antibodies. Moreover, our results demonstrate that interactions between dye-conjugated antibodies and their binding partners can be detected under physiologically relevant conditions. These findings establish fluorescence emission energy and emission width analysis as a potential approach for probing antibody interactions in complex biological matrices. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors declare the following interests: Oleh Fedorych is founder, shareholder and holds patent covering the method. All other authors have no competing interests to declare.

articles.title: Inherited maternal memory T cells protect offspring from respiratory viral infection through disease tolerance
articles.abstract: Maternal immune transfer is a powerful mechanism for early-life protection from infection, yet the full repertoire of protective factors remains unknown. We discovered that maternal memory T cells are both necessary and sufficient to protect offspring from lethal respiratory infection. This antigen-specific protection operated independently of maternal antibodies and offspring T cell responses and required IL-10 produced by maternal T cells. Transfer of protective maternal T cells reduced offspring inflammatory responses and lung tissue damage without affecting viral burdens, indicating that maternal memory T cells directly suppress pathogenic innate inflammatory responses to preserve offspring health. Critically, maternal vaccination similarly protected offspring in a T cell-dependent manner. These findings reveal maternal antigen-specific T cell transfer as a complementary immunological defense mechanism to protect offspring against pathogens that escape maternal antibodies, with broad implications for maternal vaccination strategies.

articles.title: Integrated transcriptomic and epigenomic profiling of human cartilage reveals coordinated changes in fibronectin expression, splicing, and receptor signaling during osteoarthritis progression
articles.abstract: Osteoarthritis (OA) is defined by progressive loss of articular cartilage, but how chondrocytes change as the disease advances is unclear because most studies have focused on end-stage tissue. We profiled human knee articular cartilage across the full range of macroscopic OA grade, from young healthy to aged severe OA donors, by bulk RNA sequencing of 92 knees, single-nucleus RNA sequencing of 108,600 chondrocyte nuclei from 30 donors and single-nucleus multiome sequencing of 24 of these donors, treating grade as a continuous variable. With increasing grade, cartilage increased extracellular matrix (ECM) synthesis and remodeling genes, lost glucocorticoid-responsive, lipid-metabolic and antioxidant programs, and changed the splicing of a small set of ECM transcripts, led by the extra domain B (EDB) exon of fibronectin (FN1). Nine chondrocyte clusters were present in every disease stage and formed a continuum ordered by cartilage zone and hypertrophic differentiation, with PRG4+ superficial and COL10A1+ hypertrophic chondrocytes as the only distinct cell types at its ends and a pre-hypertrophic state between them. With grade, all clusters shared a response in which ECM production rose and homeostatic programs fell, and they differed in which of its components was strongest: ECM production in the superficial cells, the secretory pathway in the hypertrophic and CYTL1+ cells, and inflammatory signaling in the ANXA1+ and CRISPLD2+ cells. Inferred communication between chondrocytes was remodeled with stage. FN1 was induced in every cluster in excess of its fibril-assembly machinery, together with the fibronectin-cleaving protease HTRA1, and FN1 signaling shifted in receptor use from integrin α5β1 toward CD44 and, less robustly, αvβ8, accompanied by a rise in TGF-β/SMAD response genes. In four early-OA donors, tenascin-C was already largely induced and the FN1 receptor shift from α5β1 toward CD44 was partly present, whereas the rise of FN1 outside superficial chondrocytes, of FGF1 and of developmental and ossification programs came with progression. Chromatin accessibility changed in the same direction across clusters, with regions linked to FN1 opening and regions linked to ITGA5 closing. OA progression in human cartilage therefore appears to be a change of chondrocyte state that differs in emphasis along a zonal and hypertrophic continuum and includes changes in fibronectin regulation, production, processing, and receptor engagement. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. NIH Common Fund, https://ror.org/001d55x84, UC2 AR082186, NIH Common Fund, R01 AG049617

articles.title: Integrative taxonomy of the North American pink flat-backed millipedes (Polydesmidae: Pseudopolydesmus Attems, 1898)
articles.abstract: Millipedes of the genus Pseudopolydesmus Attems, 1898 are common millipedes in North America. They are the largest, in terms of body size, and most geographically wide-ranging of the family Polydesmidae, and are ubiquitous in eastern and central North American forests. Eight species have been named based on the morphology of the genitalia, but these have not been investigated genetically. Here, we take an integrated taxonomic approach, using five genes to infer a molecular phylogeny of Pseudopolydesmus species, and analyze a dataset of 15 morphological characters in an effort to delimit species in the genus. 1,148 Pseudopolydesmus specimens were newly collected for this study, and all known species were sampled. These specimens were used for analysis, and were combined with museum specimens and literature records into a database of 3,462 unique specimen records. This database was used to produce distribution maps for each species in the genus. The maximum likelihood phylogeny found support for the eight species in the genus, supporting previous morphological species hypotheses. However, previous morphology-based hypotheses regarding evolutionary relationships between the species were not supported by the analysis. The morphological analysis, performed with a modified PCA, did not delimit species clusters as well as the genitalic and genetic differences did, due to comparatively uniform somatic morphology in the genus. However, our results show that genitalic morphology, combined with genetic analysis, provide congruent species delimitation hypotheses for Pseudopolydesmus, and these lines of evidence may prove useful in delimiting species and generic boundaries in other Polydesmidae worldwide.

articles.title: KH1 Domain of Poly C Binding Protein 1 (PCBP1) Interacts with Utrophin-A mRNA and Modulates Utrophin-A Expression in Mouse Myoblasts
articles.abstract: Utrophin upregulation is an attractive strategy to ameliorate Duchenne Muscular Dystrophy (DMD). Here, we investigated whether the murine poly(C)-binding protein 1 (PCBP1) directly interacts with the utrophin-A mRNA, and how the interaction shapes the fate of utrophin-A in muscle cells. As no experimentally validated structure of the murine PCBP1 is available, AlphaFold2 was utilized to predict the structure of the full-length protein and the KH1-KH2 domain of the protein. The more stable and reliable model of the KH1-KH2 domain of PCBP1 was then docked with the 5′UTR of the utrophin-A mRNA, and the top-ranked docked complex was utilized for MD simulation to identify the most stable hydrogen bond-forming amino acid residues from PCBP1. ITC showed a thermodynamically favorable spontaneous interaction between the full-length PCBP1 and the 5′UTR of utrophin-A mRNA, but the deletion mutant of PCBP1, lacking the predicted contact region, failed to exhibit any interaction. This observation was also confirmed by an RNA-immunoprecipitation assay in C2C12 cells. However, the mutant PCBP1 was unable to alter the expression of the utrophin-A in the C2C12 cells. In cells, PCBP1 overexpression lowered utrophin-A expression, while shRNA knockdown produced reciprocal increases. A 5′UTR-luciferase reporter mirrored this observation. Finally, subcellular fractionation showed that PCBP1 promotes nuclear retention of utrophin-A transcripts and reduces their cytoplasmic availability, with reciprocal shifts upon PCBP1 knockdown. Considering earlier work on PCBP2, our data suggest both paralogs recognize the same 5′UTR element, and the KH1-dependent interaction represses utrophin-A by coupling nuclear retention to reduced protein output. Thus, the PCBP1-5′UTR interaction emerges as a potent target for utrophin de-repression in DMD. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest.

articles.title: LabWeaver: reliable agentic data analysis grounded in laboratory knowled
articles.abstract: Agentic systems powered by large language models are rapidly automating biological data analysis. However, their reliability remains questionable because they often overlook experimental context, such as disease domain and experimental protocol. Existing agentic systems organize context around individual users and projects, whereas research is organized around laboratories whose projects share experimental context. As a result, experimental context learned in one project remains unavailable to related projects. We introduce LabWeaver, an agentic data analysis framework with a laboratory-organized architecture of three tiers: laboratory, user and project. Further, LabWeaver distills experimental context into laboratory memory and skills, which are shared across users and projects after human-gated review. To isolate the contribution of experimental context, we analyzed a synovial sarcoma single-cell RNA-seq dataset in two sessions that differed only in whether laboratory memory and skills were available. The context-free session lost the fusion reporter at read alignment and misannotated the tumor cells. In contrast, the context-enabled session recovered reporter expression and resolved five fusion-anchored tumor cell states.

articles.title: Lesion-Derived Estimated Functional and Structural Connectomes Predict Post-Stroke Recovery Outcomes
articles.abstract: Accurate prognosis after stroke remains challenging, limiting the ability to predict individual recovery. While advanced connectome MRI can provide further prognostically-useful information regarding affected brain networks, its impractical nature has given rise instead to lesion-based estimates of network disruptions. Here, we present a novel pipeline that leverages our recently developed connectome analysis tools to estimate structural disconnection (eSDC) and functional connectivity (eFC) directly from N=96 patient lesion masks for use in predicting motor, language, attention and memory outcomes at multiple timepoints after stroke. Our approach jointly leverages our Network Modification (NeMo) Tool, a database of white matter tractography results that estimates structural disconnectivity (eSDC), and the Krakencoder, a joint autoencoder that estimates functional connectomes (eFC) from the NeMo Tool's output. Models based on eSDC and eFC predicted almost all outcomes, particularly motor outcomes, significantly better than models that used patients' fMRI-based observed FC (oFC) and models based on only lesion information and covariates. Estimated connectome measures also i) retained meaningful inter-individual variability when compared to observed functional connectomes, ii) reflected population-level, stroke-related changes in functional connectomes, and iii) resulted in outcome prediction models with feature importances that aligned with expected networks of relevance to the given outcome. Feature importance analyses also identified distinct predictive signatures across both modality and outcome domain, indicating that eSDC and eFC capture non-redundant, biologically meaningful information about post-stroke network disruption. Together, these findings establish our lesion-based estimates of post-stroke structural and functional connectomes as a practical, information-rich alternative to advanced imaging in patients. This approach allows for probing an individual's affected neural circuitry underlying stroke impairment and recovery, paving the way toward more efficient, accessible, and personalized approaches to post-stroke prognosis and intervention.

articles.title: Light-sheet fluorescence microscopy of optically cleared human head-and-neck organs: three-dimensional tissue assessment and histological correlation
articles.abstract: Conventional histology provides detailed cellular information but only a partial view of the three-dimensional (3D) organisation of head-and-neck tissues. We investigated whether optical tissue clearing combined with light-sheet fluorescence microscopy (LSFM) could visualise the microanatomy of large head-and-neck specimens and relate volumetric features to conventional histology. Non-neoplastic human palatine tonsil, cervical lymph node, tongue and parotid gland specimens were cleared with a solvent-based protocol, labelled with small-molecule dyes and imaged by LSFM, with haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology as a morphological reference. LSFM visualised the characteristic architecture of each tissue, including lymphoid follicles and crypt epithelium in tonsil, cortex, paracortex and follicles in lymph node, epithelium and intrinsic muscle fibres in tongue, and lobules, ducts and adipocytes in parotid. Following structures through successive optical sections revealed their continuity and branching over long distances, information not available from single sections. Tongue epithelial measurements were comparable with H&E, and segmentation enabled volumetric quantification of structures such as the tongue epithelium and parotid adipocytes. Optical clearing and LSFM thus provide a feasible single workflow for volumetric investigation of human head-and-neck microanatomy. These data establish a 3D morphological reference with potential applications in cancer research and staging, computational image analysis and anatomical education, to be further developed through larger donor cohorts and specific labelling. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. University Fund Limburg, CoBes2026-P-9

articles.title: Local chromatin, 3D genome folding and transposon cargo shape Sleeping Beauty transposition
articles.abstract: The cut-and-paste DNA transposon Sleeping Beauty (SB) is widely used for genome engineering, mutagenesis and gene delivery. When mobilized from a genomic donor position ("launch site"), SB preferentially reintegrates locally (< 2 Mb), but factors governing its transposition from genomic sites remain incompletely understood. Here we analysed local transposition experiments in mouse embryonic stem cells to determine the influence of chromatin context and transposon cargo on SB transposition. Transposons in launch sites with transcriptionally active, accessible chromatin showed lower transposition efficiency. Large cargo and cargo with higher transcriptional activity also result in reduced transposition efficiency. After excision, local reintegration patterns closely resembled 3D contact frequencies of the launch site. This indicates that chromosome folding is a major determinant of the transposition pattern. Surprisingly, we did not detect any effect of the destination chromatin composition on reintegration efficiency. Cargo sequence modified the reintegration patterns: promoter-containing cargo increased both very proximal (<10kb) and interchromosomal transpositions, while CTCF binding sites in the cargo increased reintegration on the launch chromosome. Together, these results define key determinants of SB transposition in chromosomes and inform the design of SB-based genome engineering strategies.

articles.title: Locus Coeruleus activity correlates with transient elevations in breathing during opioid-induced respiratory depression
articles.abstract: A history of use remains a key risk factor for opioid-related overdose deaths in the ongoing opioid epidemic. The locus coeruleus (LC) is the principal source of noradrenergic tone and a site for opioid neuromodulation and tolerance. How a history of opioid use affects LC activity and shapes opioid-induced respiratory depression (OIRD) remains poorly understood. Using plethysmography and fiber photometry, we assessed how fentanyl affects LC activity and OIRD before and after five days of repeat opioid use (ROU). Fentanyl increased the frequency of LC bursts independent of exposure history and was coupled to transient elevations in breathing. LC coupled ventilation (LC-Ve) persisted through ROU. After ROU, OIRD magnitude diverged across mice. Mice developing an adaptive ventilatory response (AVR) showed a smaller OIRD that coincided with improved ventilation outside LC bursts and reduced LC-Ve gain. Mice with the non-adaptive response (NVR) show no improvement in OIRD or ventilation outside LC bursts, resulting in an unchanged reliance on LC-Ve. While LC-Ve reflexively counters OIRD acutely, it may also drive oscillations to destabilize blood gas homeostasis, perpetuating pathophysiology with repeat use. Thus, LC-coupled breathing appears to be a physiological signature of divergent respiratory responses with a history of fentanyl exposure. ### Competing Interest Statement The authors have declared no competing interest. NIH Common Fund, https://ror.org/001d55x84, T32DA043469, R01HL163965, R01DA057767, R01DA061412, R01HL169679 University of Chicago, https://ror.org/024mw5h28, Safadi Pilot Grant

articles.title: A validated antibody toolbox for ALS research
articles.abstract: A substantial fraction of amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS)-associated proteins remains poorly characterized, in part because of the limited availability of validated research antibodies. We established knockout (KO)-based antibody characterization workflows and demonstrated that widely used antibodies against the major ALS-associated protein C9orf72 lacked specificity (Laflamme et al., 2019). We subsequently scaled this framework to systematically benchmark research antibodies, revealing that up to 61% fail to perform as recommended by manufacturers (Ayoubi et al., 2023b). Here, we extend this approach by establishing the ALS-Reproducible Antibody Platform (ALS-RAP), a comprehensive effort to generate a publicly available dataset of KO-validated antibodies targeting proteins encoded by ALS risk genes. In total, we characterized 303 antibodies against 33 ALS-associated proteins to identify high-quality reagents for use in western blot, immunoprecipitation, and immunofluorescence. Using these antibodies, we profiled protein levels across human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived and primary neurological cell types. These analyses revealed diverse cellular distributions and higher levels of several ALS-associated proteins in glial populations, consistent with emerging evidence for immune contributions to ALS. Together, ALS-RAP provides a validated antibody toolbox and protein expression resource to support the study of ALS-associated proteins.

articles.title: Class-wide sequence, structural, and docking-profile diversity of insect odorant receptors and structural specialization of Orco
articles.abstract: Insect olfaction is facilitated by a heterotetrameric odorant receptor–odorant receptor co-receptor (OR-Orco) complex. However, extensive sequence divergence and lineage-specific expansion have complicated large-scale comparisons of OR repertoires across insects. Here, we integrated sequence similarity, structural similarity, and molecular docking to analyze ORs from 115 insect species. OR repertoire size was associated with adult diet, larval diet, and habitat, but not with circadian rhythm. We developed a ‘trunk–branch’ network framework to classify ORs according to sequence and structural similarity and used large-scale molecular docking to derive comparative docking profiles. Despite marked differences in sequence- and structural-community composition, almost all sampled orders contained ORs assigned to all six docking-profile communities. Holometabolous insects showed higher OR sequence-community diversity than non-holometabolous insects, and docking-profile composition differed between extant lineages whose order-level origins predate or postdate the end-Permian mass extinction. Most notably, we identified a highly conserved extracellular β-sheet in Orco that restricts ligand access to the binding pocket and may contribute to its reduced capacity to bind natural odorants. The emergence of Orco represents a key evolutionary transition from homomeric receptors to heteromeric OR–Orco complexes, and our results suggest that this transition may have been accompanied by pronounced specialization of the extracellular domain and binding pocket. Together, these analyses provide a class-wide framework for comparing insect OR diversity and generate testable hypotheses for future experimental and evolutionary studies.

articles.title: Impacts of mutation accumulation and order on tumor initiation revealed by engineered murine colorectal cancer organoids
articles.abstract: Tumorigenesis typically follows a multi-hit trajectory, driven by accumulating oncogenic mutations. Colorectal cancer (CRC) has long served as a paradigmatic model of multi-hit tumorigenesis, characterized by adenoma-carcinoma transition accompanied by acquisition of specific oncogene and tumor suppressor mutations. However, how the temporal order of early mutations influences CRC initiation remains poorly understood. To address this, we established a CRC tumorigenesis model using murine intestinal organoids. By introducing defined combinations of key CRC driver mutations (Kras, Apc, and Trp53) in distinct orders, we systematically investigated how the order of mutation accumulation affects tumor initiation. Our results reveal that the mutation accumulation confers growth advantages in both in vitro and in vivo models. Strikingly, mutation order also influenced the tumorigenic properties of the organoids. Whereas organoids with Trp53 loss before or after Apc loss similarly affected organoid phenotypes in vitro or tumorigenicity in immunodeficient mice, organoids with Trp53 loss preceding Apc inactivation exhibited reduced tumor-forming potential in immunocompetent mice, likely due to their distinct immunological features. Collectively, our study reveals a critical role of ordered mutation accumulation in CRC initiation, an insight that may hold clinical relevance.

articles.title: Spyglass is a framework for reproducible and shareable neuroscience research
articles.abstract: Scientific progress depends on reliable and reproducible results. Progress can be accelerated when data are shared and re-analyzed to address new questions. Current approaches to storing and analyzing neural data involve bespoke formats and software that make replication and reuse of data difficult. To address these challenges, we created Spyglass, an open-source data management and analysis framework written in Python. Spyglass provides reproducible pipelines for common neuroscience analyses and sharing of raw data, intermediate analyses, and final results within and across labs. Spyglass uses the Neurodata Without Borders (NWB) standard and includes pipelines for spectral filtering, spike sorting, pose tracking, and neural decoding. Spyglass can be extended to apply existing and newly developed pipelines to datasets from multiple sources. We demonstrate these features in the context of a cross-laboratory replication by applying advanced state space decoding algorithms to publicly available data. New users can try out Spyglass on a Jupyter Hub hosted by HHMI and 2i2c: https://spyglass.hhmi.2i2c.cloud/.

articles.title: ACCURACY OF COMPRESSED SENSING ACCELERATED 3D-FLAIR IN THE DIAGNOSTIC WORK-UP OF MULTIPLE SCLEROSIS AT 1.5 T
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND: 3D-FLAIR is central to MR-based diagnosis and monitoring of MS, but long acquisition times remain a limitation. OBJECTIVES: This single-center prospective non-inferiority study evaluated whether compressed sensing (CS) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR at 1.5T provides lesion detection comparable to optimized Generalized Autocalibrating Partially Parallel Acquisition (GRAPPA) - accelerated 3D-FLAIR. Optimized CS- and GRAPPA-accelerated 3D-FLAIR sequences were incorporated into MRI examinations in patients with known or suspected MS. The primary endpoint was manual lesion count by two blinded readers using a 10% non-inferiority margin. Secondary endpoints included image quality, SNR, CNR, and automated lesion count and volumetry. RESULTS: Sixty-eight patients were included (mean age, 40.1+/-13.3 years; 61.8% women). CS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR reduced acquisition time by 31.8% compared with GRAPPA (4:00 vs 5:52 minutes). Non-inferiority for manual lesion count was demonstrated for both readers (reader A, p < .0001; reader B, p = .005). Interrater agreement was excellent for CS (ICC = 0.921; 95% CI, 0.837-0.957) and very good for GRAPPA (ICC = 0.851; 95% CI, 0.769-0.906). Subjective image quality was high for both techniques. GRAPPA showed higher objective signal-to-noise-ratio (SNR) and contrast-to-noise-ratio (CNR), whereas automated lesion counts and volumes were higher for CS. CONCLUSION: CS-accelerated 3D-FLAIR provided non-inferior lesion detection with substantial scan-time reduction.

articles.title: AI-Based MRI Radiomics for Preoperative Detection of Tumor Deposits in Rectal Cancer: A Bivariate Diagnostic Accuracy Meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background: In rectal cancer (RC), tumor deposits (TDs) are clinically important as they are associated with a negative impact on prognosis and affect risk stratification as well as management plans. MRI radiomics combined with artificial intelligence (AI) has been explored for non-invasive preoperative TDs detection. However, results vary across studies; therefore, we performed a systematic review and meta-analysis to pool their diagnostic test accuracy (DTA). Methods: This systematic review and DTA meta-analysis were conducted in accordance with the Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Diagnostic Test Accuracy and reported in adherence to the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses of Diagnostic Test Accuracy Studies (PRISMA-DTA).
