articles.title: Convergent genomic evolution of human gut bacteria along an industrialization gradient
articles.abstract: Analysis of globally diverse gut bacterial isolate genomes shows that host environments across the industrialization gradient shape genome remodeling and convergent selection, while industrialization is linked to increased HGT-driven gene acquisition and expanded genome size.

articles.title: Fatty acid desaturation controls cellular fate decisions between senescence and ferroptosis
articles.abstract: Polyunsaturated fatty acid metabolism shapes cell fate decisions: loss of DGLA favors senescence, whereas DGLA repletion triggers ferroptosis.

articles.title: Industrialization drives convergent microbiome and host physiological shifts in the human metaorganism
articles.abstract: Integration of microbiome omics and host data from globally diverse human populations shows that industrialization restructures gut microbial ecosystems and intestinal physiology. These shifts include reduced microbial diversity, compositional heterogeneity, and community stability; altered intestinal immune and physiological responses; and limited cross-population portability of microbiome-based disease predictors.

articles.title: Subsistence transition preceded population turnover in the eastern Colombian Andes
articles.abstract: Ancient DNA data and stable isotope data from the eastern Colombian Andes reveal that C4-enriched resources were incorporated into local food webs during five millennia of genetic continuity and that a later population turnover introduced people with ancestry admixed between that found in Chibchan-related groups and that found at the Amazonian-Andean interface.

articles.title: TECR palmitoylation triggers a necrotic cell death program driving acute liver injury
articles.abstract: We identify a TECR palmitoylation-dependent necrotic cell death (TPNCD) pathway. Blocking TPNCD genetically or pharmacologically protects against immune- and drug-induced liver injury, revealing a therapeutic strategy for hepatic injury.

articles.title: A single-cell comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment
articles.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) remains highly lethal, with treatment failure and relapse driven by dynamic cellular states and evolving interactions within the leukemic ecosystem. In this study, we built a comprehensive atlas of leukemia and its microenvironment (CALM) by integrating single-cell profiling from 73 AML samples and 9 healthy donors, bulk RNA sequencing (RNA-seq) from 87 newly diagnosed patients, and 4 paired bone marrow and peripheral blood single-cell data. All datasets were linked to clinical, cytogenetic, molecular, and treatment-response annotations. Immune analysis revealed diverse T cell distribution across disease status, where patients with persistent disease exhibited greater clonal expansion. Machine learning modeling on conventional T cells identified a T-cell signature pertinent to AML and outcomes, which were validated in two cohorts. CALM is a publicly accessible and interactive portal (calm.mdanderson.org) for exploring cellular compartments, cell-cell interactions, and longitudinal transcriptional and clonal dynamics to enable hypothesis generation, biomarker discovery, and target validation.

articles.title: Cell size asymmetry regulates neural stem cell proliferation and lineage expansion in the Drosophila brain
Circulating FABP4 promotes obesity-associated breast cancer lung metastasis through PIP2
articles.abstract: Obesity is a well-established risk factor for increased incidence and mortality in multiple cancers, including breast cancer. However, the key molecular mechanisms linking obesity to breast cancer progression remain incompletely understood. In this study, using several high-fat diet-induced obesity models, we demonstrate that obesity promotes breast cancer lung metastasis through elevated levels of adipocyte-derived circulating FABP4. Mechanistically, circulating FABP4 directly binds to a subset of breast cancer cells via the membrane lipid PIP2. This FABP4/PIP2 interaction activates PKC signaling and enhances mitochondrial ROS production, driving cancer cell migration. Genetic deletion of FABP4, either globally or specifically in adipocytes, markedly reduces obesity-associated metastasis. Moreover, therapeutic targeting of circulating FABP4 using a distinctive neutralizing monoclonal antibody significantly suppresses breast cancer metastasis in multiple preclinical models. Together, these findings identify the FABP4/PIP2 axis as a key mechanism underlying obesity-driven breast cancer and highlight it as a promising therapeutic target for treating metastatic breast cancer.

articles.title: Cysteine promotes islet α-cell glucagon secretion by limiting oxidative inhibition of voltage-gated sodium channels
articles.abstract: Cysteine serves as a robust α-cell secretagogue. While diabetes alters both plasma cysteine and glucagon levels, the mechanisms of α-cell cysteine action remain unclear. Here, we identified cysteine as a key regulator of islet glucagon secretion through redox control of α-cell electrical excitability. Short-term cysteine depletion markedly suppressed hypoglycemia-stimulated glucagon secretion from both human and mouse islets. Moreover, cysteine-depleted islets showed reduced hypoglycemia-stimulated α-cell calcium (Ca2+) influx. Islet glucagon secretion and α-cell Ca2+ influx rapidly normalized following cysteine restoration. Cysteine depletion also reduced α-cell voltage-gated sodium channel (NaV) conductance and action potential amplitude. Importantly, reducing agents restored NaV currents and glucose control of α-cell Ca2+ handling in islets without cysteine. Together, these findings identify reductive amplification of NaV channels as a key mechanism required for hypoglycemia-stimulated glucagon secretion, highlighting cysteine as a critical regulator of α-cell redox state, electrical excitability, and glucagon secretion.

articles.title: Exposure to immune stimuli augments alveolar macrophages to acquire neutrophil antimicrobial molecules to prevent bacterial pneumonia
articles.abstract: The protective adaptation of innate immune defenses against respiratory pathogens has been linked to previous exposure to immune stimuli; however, the underlying mechanisms of these adaptations are not yet fully understood. Here, we show that pre-exposure to a low dose of non-specific immune stimuli or infection protects against subsequent lethal methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) challenge. This enhanced protection concurs with increased alveolar macrophages (AMs) resulting from a self-renewal process in the lungs. Importantly, these AMs are programmed to acquire neutrophil-released antimicrobial enzymes from the extracellular space to clear MRSA, prevent tissue damage, and rapidly restore lung homeostasis. AM function depends on differential gene expression, including expression of the efferocytosis receptor Mer proto-oncogene tyrosine kinase (MerTK) and the anti-apoptotic regulator Bcl-xL. Thus, our data highlight that AMs acquire neutrophil enzymes as an integral component of innate immune adaptation.

articles.title: Rethinking lithium content in inorganic solid-state electrolytes
articles.abstract: Inorganic solid-state electrolytes are being developed for safer, energy-dense batteries, yet many contain nearly an order of magnitude more lithium than liquid electrolytes. This perspective proposes low-lithium-content electrolyte design and introduces a lithium-transport realization index connecting local ion motion with long-range conductivity. Evidence across existing materials shows that reduced lithium content does not necessarily sacrifice performance. The resulting design roadmap aims to preserve conductivity with less lithium, potentially easing resource, cost, and environmental burdens.

articles.title: Anions as catalysts: from organosilanes as pro-nucleophiles to base-embedding electrophiles
articles.abstract: Anions are efficient catalysts when combined with organosilanes as pro-nucleophiles or with base-embedding electrophiles, the latter is an emerging catalytic deprotonation strategy which disentangles turnover from acidity–basicity constraints.

articles.title: Chemistry-transforming applications of artificial intelligence
articles.abstract: This review critically assesses how AI is integrated into chemistry. We decompose the chemical research cycle, summarize the modern AI toolkit, and map them onto each other to discuss both near-term and longer-horizon prospects.

articles.title: Potassium-ion batteries for stationary energy storage solutions
articles.abstract: Potassium-ion batteries are a potentially sustainable and cost-competitive technology for large-scale stationary energy storage.

articles.title: Donor−Acceptor Engineering in Porphyrin-Based Two-Dimensional Polymers for Ultrafast Nonlinear Optical Response
articles.abstract: Leveraging their extended π-conjugation, structurally tunable backbones, and superior film-forming processability, two-dimensional (2D) organic polymers have emerged as a highly promising class of materials for third-order nonlinear optical (NLO) applications. Herein, a series of porphyrin-based donor−acceptor (D−A) 2D polymer films, namely, TAPP-TAPZ, TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA, are successfully fabricated via a liquid−liquid interfacial polymerization approach. These films exhibit broad absorption profiles across the visible region alongside markedly narrowed optical bandgaps, underscoring the extensive π-electron delocalization inherent to the 2D polymeric frameworks. Femtosecond open-aperture Z-scan measurements conducted at 515 and 800 nm unambiguously reveal pronounced reverse saturable absorption in all samples. Strikingly, the TAPP-TAPZ film delivers exceptional nonlinear absorption coefficients (β) of 8.8 × 103 cm GW−1 at 800 nm and 5.2 × 103 cm GW−1 at 515 nm, values that not only substantially outperform the analogous TAPP-BATD, TAPP-TDAT, and TAPP-BDTA counterparts but also rival or surpass those of numerous reported covalent organic frameworks, 2D inorganic nanomaterials, and small-molecule NLO systems. Complementary density functional theory calculations ascribe this remarkable performance to the incorporation of benzothiadiazole units, which stabilize a donor−donor−acceptor (D−D−A) electronic configuration and facilitate efficient intramolecular charge transfer. Collectively, our findings establish interfacial polymerization as a robust and generalizable route for constructing ordered, defect-minimized 2D films, thereby offering actionable design principles for the development of next-generation ultrafast photonic devices.

Performance of the PREVENT-HF Equations Across Heart Failure Subtypes in Community-Based and Ambulatory Healthcare Samples
articles.abstract: Background: The PREVENT-HF equations estimate 10-year risk of overall heart failure (HF), inclusive of both HF with preserved and reduced ejection fraction (HFpEF; HFrEF). Given differential risk factor profiles, pathophysiology, and therapeutic strategies for each HF subtype, we sought to examine the performance of PREVENT-HF for subtype-specific risk assessment. Methods: We included data from five pooled longitudinal cohort studies (baseline exam 1989 to 2013) and two longitudinal primary-care electronic health record-based samples (Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center [BIDMC], baseline 2004 to 2014; Mass General Brigham [MGB], baseline 2001 to 2018). We assessed the performance of the PREVENT-HF equations in predicting 10-year incident HFrEF and HFpEF, including model discrimination (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUROC]; average precision [AP]/event rate) and calibration (integrated calibration index [ICI]), in adults aged 30-79 years without prevalent cardiovascular disease or HF. Results: The pooled cohort studies included 23,652 (55% women, age 60 ± 13 years), of whom 1,232 developed HF (432 [35%] HFpEF, 522 [42%] HFrEF). The BIDMC sample included 29,815 (55% women, 50 ± 13 years), of whom 259 (1%) developed HF (133 [51%] HFpEF, 101 [39%] HFrEF). MGB included 138,999 (62% women, 52 ± 13 years), of whom 1050 developed HF (586 [56%] HFpEF, 381 [36%] HFrEF). PREVENT-HF demonstrated better discrimination for HFpEF than HFrEF across all samples: in the pooled cohorts, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.824 (95% CI 0.807, 0.839) versus 0.789 (95% CI 0.770, 0.807) for HFrEF; in BIDMC, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.897 (95% CI 0.874, 0.918) versus 0.833 (95% CI 0.791, 0.869) for HFrEF; in MGB, the AUROC for HFpEF was 0.864 (95% CI 0.848, 0.880) versus 0.797 (95% CI 0.771, 0.820) for HFrEF. Similar results were reflected in the AP/event rate ratios: 2.92 (95% CI 2.47, 3.54) for HFpEF compared to 2.66 (95% CI 2.33, 3.14) for HFrEF in the pooled cohorts; 8.08 (95% CI 6.12, 12.30) for HFpEF compared to 5.12 (95% CI 3.84, 8.17) for HFrEF in BIDMC; and 6.84 (95% CI 5.66, 8.28) for HFpEF compared to 4.12 (95% CI 3.37, 5.16) for HFrEF in MGB. Calibration was similar for HFpEF and HFrEF across samples. For example, in the pooled cohorts, the ICI for HFpEF was 0.041 (95% CI 0.039, 0.043) and for HFrEF was 0.038 (95% CI 0.036, 0.040). Conclusions: PREVENT-HF demonstrated excellent discrimination for both HF subtypes across community-based cohorts and real-world samples, with consistently better discrimination for HFpEF as compared to HFrEF. Given PREVENT-HF was developed to estimate overall HF risk rather than subtype-specific risk, future studies are needed to establish subtype-specific risk thresholds.

Broadscale Distribution and Pronounced Mitochondrial Phylogeographic Structure in the Freshwater Minnow Opsariichthys bidens Across China's Major River Basins
articles.abstract: China's complex river basins constitute a critical biogeographic setting for investigating genetic differentiation and lineage divergence in freshwater fishes. Opsariichthys bidens is broadly distributed among multiple, hydrologically isolated river basins, rendering it a well-suited system for assessing mitochondrial phylogeographic structure across major river basins. Here, we used newly generated mitochondrial data to characterize broad-scale genetic variation in O. bidens across China's major river basins. We analyzed 379 cytochrome b (cyt b) sequences sampled from 13 geographically distinct populations, including seven populations from the Yangtze River and one population from each of six other major rivers, complemented by complete mitochondrial genomes from one individual from each population. Mitochondrial diversity was high at the species level (haplotype diversity, H d = 0.942; nucleotide diversity, π = 0.02526), but varied markedly among populations, with some populations showing haplotype fixation and others retaining divergent haplotypes. Genetic differentiation was pronounced, with 83.84% of variation attributable to differences among populations; 93.6% of pairwise F st values exceeded 0.25. Haplotype-network and phylogenetic analyses showed two deeply divergent mitochondrial lineages, broadly distributed in northern and southern China, respectively, with further substructure broadly associated with major river basins. Complete mitochondrial genomes exhibited high structural conservation across lineages, and the clearest lineage-associated annotation differences were observed in the termination codons of nd1 and cox3. Overall, these results provide a broad-scale mitochondrial phylogeographic assessment of O. bidens and reveal a general association between river-basin geography and mitochondrial lineage structure across China.

articles.title: Characteristics of Professionals Involved in Open Science in Ecology and Evolution
articles.abstract: Open science aims to improve research transparency, reuse and societal impact, yet its adoption and reach ultimately depend on people. Understanding how personal characteristics such as gender, work experience or professional role influence familiarity with, attitudes toward and engagement in open science is critical for the effective, widespread implementation of open science practices. We surveyed 342 individuals who produce, mobilise or use scientific knowledge in ecology and evolutionary biology. Their engagement was analysed using the open science change framework, which conceptualises open science as a progression from familiarity and perceptions to practices and support for societal goals, as outlined in the UNESCO Recommendations. Familiarity with open science emerged as a strongest and most consistent predictor of engagement: higher familiarity was associated with more positive attitudes, greater participation in open science practices and stronger agreement with UNESCO principles. Although these relationships are correlational and likely bidirectional, they highlight the central role of familiarity in open science engagement. Years of professional experience were associated with slightly less positive perceptions of open science, particularly among knowledge creators, while gender effects were weak across all stages of engagement. Stakeholder groups differed most in their familiarity with open science, while attitudes and support for broader goals were more similar once familiarity was considered. Together, these findings suggest that increasing familiarity with open science may be more effective than managing resistance or targeting specific demographic groups. Aligning incentives and practical support to increase familiarity offers actionable opportunities to strengthen open science engagement across the research ecosystem in ecology and evolutionary biology and enhance its societal impact.

articles.title: DNA Metabarcoding Reveals Flying Arthropod Diversity and Community Turnover Across Ancient Tea Agroforestry Landscapes in Southwest China
articles.abstract: Ancient tea agroforestry landscapes in Southwest China are structurally complex systems that may support high arthropod diversity, yet their biodiversity value remains poorly documented. We used COI metabarcoding of Malaise‐trap bulk samples to assess flying arthropod assemblages at four tea‐associated sites in the Mengku Ancient Tea and Cultural System, Yunnan, China: a wild ancient tea tree community, a village‐adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, a forest‐adjacent cultivated ancient tea garden, and a young‐shrub tea plantation. Samples were collected from May to October 2024 and analyzed using OTU‐based diversity and community‐composition approaches. We recovered 5669 arthropod OTUs. Diptera dominated the assemblages, accounting for 57.5% of total OTU richness, followed by Hymenoptera, Lepidoptera, Hemiptera, Coleoptera, and other arthropod groups. OTU richness, alpha diversity, and community composition varied among the four sites. WJC had the highest total OTU richness and mean alpha‐diversity values, whereas DXS yielded the most compositionally distinct assemblage and the largest number of OTUs detected exclusively at that site during this survey. Dominant families included natural enemies, herbivores, and mixed‐function taxa. Seasonal patterns showed higher OTU richness in early summer and September, but lower richness during the main rainy‐season months and October. These findings document marked spatial and seasonal variation in Malaise‐trap‐sampled flying arthropod assemblages. Because each landscape context was represented by a single site, the observed differences cannot be attributed independently to forest association, habitat heterogeneity, or management.

articles.title: Diurnal Nest Site Selection and Thermal Buffering Capacity of Shelters for Rufous Bettongs in a Grazed Savanna Woodland
articles.abstract: Small‐ and medium‐sized mammals are vulnerable to temperature extremes due to their high surface‐area‐to‐volume ratios and elevated metabolic rates. Shelter sites that buffer ambient temperatures are critical for thermoregulation; however, shelter resources may be limited in agricultural landscapes. We examined shelter site selection and the thermal buffering capacity of rufous bettong (Aepyprymnus rufescens) shelters in a grazed tropical savanna woodland in Queensland, Australia. We radio‐tracked 15 rufous bettongs (nine females, six males) across five grazing strategies at Wambiana Station (2020–2021) to locate diurnal shelters. We assessed fine‐scale habitat composition at 133 shelter sites and 224 paired random locations using a MANOVA and NMDS ordination. We deployed iButton data loggers to record hourly temperatures within shelters and at paired ground‐level points 2 m away across wet and dry seasons, isolating the thermal effect of the constructed shelter at the locations the animals selected. Rufous bettongs selected shelter sites characterized by thorny shrubs (Carissa ovata), logs, and termite mounds. Grazing intensity did not significantly affect shelter site selection, though bettongs tended to avoid heavily grazed paddocks. Daytime shelter temperatures (0600–1800 h) were substantially less variable than those at random sites, with thermal buffering most pronounced during the day (0900–1700 h), when random sites exhibited 2–3 times greater temperature variability than bettong shelters. Shelters provided critical thermal refugia, buffering daily temperature extremes by over 20°C in a hot, seasonally variable environment. Retention of dense shrub thickets (C. ovata), logs, and adequate grass cover should be prioritised in grazing landscapes to support rufous bettong persistence under current and future climate conditions.

articles.title: Dynamic Resource Partitioning in a Marine Predator Community
articles.abstract: To avoid competition, species partition resource‐use along various niche axes. However, variable resource availability, especially within dynamic environments, may influence this partitioning. Theory predicts that species will contract their ecological niche to limit competition during times of resource scarcity. We analysed blood δ13C and δ15N composition in four albatrosses, four penguin, two giant petrel and two fur seal species breeding on sub‐Antarctic Marion Island, during two seasons (autumn and summer) over 3 years. Using the species' seasonal stable isotopic niche space as a proxy for trophic niche space, we investigated their trophic dynamics and maintenance of inter‐specific resource partitioning. There were significant variations in the seasonal and inter‐annual trophic niches of these predators. However, despite this high seasonal and annual variability, resource partitioning among the species was maintained over time. Between years, there was greater variability in the species' trophic niches in autumn than in summer. This might reflect species being better able to track productive dynamic oceanographic features during autumn, when most species are less spatially constrained by breeding commitments compared to during summer. Our results indicate that most of these marine predators have foraging behaviours that are either sufficiently flexible or general to cope with resources that are variable in space and time. Their foraging strategies minimise inter‐specific overlap in food or foraging habitat preferences, potentially resulting from historic or present competition for resources.

articles.title: Interspecific Interactions Constrain Individual Niche Divergence and Reveal Energetic Cost of Niche Expansion
articles.abstract: Individuals vary in resource use, generating trophic niche variation that shapes a population's niche width (PNW). Interspecific interactions are predicted to constrain PNW, though individual responses are often heterogeneous. The keystone niche individual (KNI) framework identifies individuals that disproportionately expand PNW by exploiting resources beyond the population's realized niche, but whether interspecific interactions limit their emergence is unknown. We tested this by comparing an allopatric and sympatric population of brook trout (Salvelinus fontinalis) and rainbow trout (Oncorhynchus mykiss). Fatty acid profiles from repeatedly sampled individuals were used to quantify individual trophic niches and their contributions to PNW. Individuals in sympatry exhibited more negative contributions to PNW (−2.70% ± 1.7%) than individuals in allopatry (−0.47% ± 1.8%) and showed a continuum of contributions rather than discrete KNI, indicating that interspecific interactions constrained niche expansion by reducing disproportionate contributions to PNW. Across both populations, individuals with greater contributions to PNW exhibited reduced trophic overlap with competitors and lower body condition, revealing energetic costs of niche expansion. These findings suggest that, in this study system, interspecific interactions can limit niche differentiation by reshaping how individuals contribute to population‐level trophic diversity, highlighting the need to evaluate the generality of these mechanisms across ecological contexts.

articles.title: Mapping Leopard Conservation Priorities in Southeast Asia
articles.abstract: The Indochinese leopard (Panthera pardus delacouri) is one of the most endangered leopard subspecies, restricted to < 4% of its historical range across Southeast Asia. With severe declines driven by poaching, habitat loss and fragmentation, and prey depletion, recovery requires urgent, spatially informed conservation action. This study presents the first connectivity analysis for the Indochinese leopard across its extant and former range, aiming to identify core habitats, priority connectivity areas and opportunities for population restoration. We used resistant kernel modelling through the CoLa Decision Support System to evaluate landscape connectivity across 14 forest complexes in the extant range and 11 potential reintroduction areas, considering scenarios of extant, reintroduction and combined range connectivity. Importance to connectivity was assessed based on Kernel Extent, Kernel Sum, movement density and protected area overlap. Our results confirmed the Dawna–Tenasserim landscape, spanning parts of Thailand and Myanmar, and Peninsular Malaysia as the most critical strongholds. In the former range, our analysis revealed potential for large‐scale metapopulation structural connectivity across Cambodia and Lao PDR, despite recent extirpations. We stress that reintroduction opportunities will require actions such as reducing poaching, restoring prey and improving habitat management. In some complexes, intensive landscape restoration may be needed to reconnect major core areas with smaller reintroduction complexes that could be critical for meta‐population connectivity. Despite increasing human pressure in the region, substantial habitat and connectivity potential remain. Our framework provides a spatial foundation to prioritise actions for preventing extinction of this subspecies and guiding large carnivore recovery across fragmented tropical landscapes.

articles.title: More Than Color: Floral Color Polymorphism Is Associated With Scent Differentiation and Pollination Success in the Deceptive Orchid Anacamptis pyramidalis
articles.abstract: Floral color polymorphism is widespread among flowering plants, yet the mechanisms underlying its maintenance remain poorly understood, particularly in food‐deceptive orchids where pollinator‐mediated selection may differ from that operating in rewarding species. Here, we investigated the relationship among floral color polymorphism, ploidy variation, floral scent composition, and pollination in the Mediterranean deceptive orchid Anacamptis pyramidalis. Cytotypes were determined by flow cytometry, and floral volatile organic compounds (VOCs) were analyzed using gas chromatography–mass spectrometry (GC–MS) in white‐ and pink‐flowered individuals from multiple populations. VOC profiles were compared using multivariate and univariate statistical approaches. Pollination success was assessed in mixed‐color diploid and tetraploid populations by quantifying the number of mature fruits produced per individual. Floral color morph was significantly associated with floral scent composition, accounting for approximately 6.5% of the total multivariate variation. Five VOCs differed significantly in relative abundance after correction for multiple comparisons, whereas total VOC emission did not differ significantly between morphs when cultivated in a common garden. No significant association between VOCs and cytotype was detected. White morphs consistently showed higher pollination success than pink morphs, producing significantly more fruits. By showing that floral color polymorphism is associated with both scent differentiation and differences in pollination success, our study highlights the importance of considering floral polymorphism as an integrated phenotype rather than a simple variation in flower pigmentation and helps explain its maintenance in the natural populations of this orchid.

articles.title: Resource Availability Shaped the Female‐Biased Floral Sex Allocation With Plant Size in Andromonoecious Capparis spinosa in Desert
articles.abstract: Although classic models of size‐dependent sex allocation (SDS) generally predict that among animal‐pollinated plants, female allocation increases with individual size, male‐and female‐biased allocation patterns have also been reported. We hypothesized that Capparis spinosa growing in resource‐poor desert habitats would exhibit a female‐biased sex allocation with increasing plant size, and that this pattern would be directly regulated by resource availability, because female function is generally more resource‐demanding to verify this conjecture. We examined SDS patterns at the flowering stage in the andromonoecious desert plant C. spinosa and assessed the role of resource availability in shaping these patterns through resource supplementation and pruning treatments. The results indicated that male plants with a low biomass occurred at low frequencies (0.021–0.051) in seven of the nine assessed populations. Among andromonoecious individuals across the nine populations, with increasing plant size, we recorded increases in the numbers of male and hermaphroditic flowers, the proportion of hermaphroditic flowers, and values of Lloyd's phenotypic gender index. These findings indicate a strong female‐biased sex allocation in C. spinosa plants of larger size. In addition, 2‐year resource manipulation experiments revealed that both the supplementation of water and nutrients and pruning treatments significantly enhanced the proportion of hermaphroditic flowers, thereby indicating that floral sex allocation is directly regulated by resource availability. Our findings in this study highlight the role of resource availability in shaping size‐dependent sex allocation patterns, particularly for plants in resource‐poor desert habitats, and sheds light on the evolution of sexual systems in plants.

articles.title: Spotted Patterns of Glass Frogs Can Disguise Imperfections in Transparency to Improve Camouflage
articles.abstract: Transparency could be considered the idealized version of camouflage, capable of producing effective concealment across heterogeneous habitats. However, although examples of highly transparent species do exist, ‘transparent’ species are highly variable and are often either only partially transparent or better described as translucent. Exactly how these different forms of ‘imperfect’ transparency may act as camouflage remains largely unknown. The glass frogs (Centrolenidae) have long been thought of as a classic example of transparent camouflage due to their see‐through ventral skin. Yet even in these seemingly exemplary cases, glass frogs are better described as translucent due to the presence of obligate opaque structures, such as the internal organs, within the body and opaque color patterns in their dorsal skin. These opaque patterns could be predicted to detract from transparency, with the potential to increase detectability and therefore predation risk. One potential explanation is that the addition of opaque patterning could help to conceal the internal organs from view while maintaining the cryptic effects of translucency. Here we tested whether the presence of opaque spots could reduce predation risk for translucent frogs by presenting model frogs, which differed in opacity and dorsal patterning, to wild birds and recording the rate at which these models were attacked. We found that the addition of opaque dorsal patterning reduced predation risk but there was no effect of translucency on survival. These data suggest that opaque patterning in glass frogs may help to conceal conspicuous internal structures but that partial translucency does not necessarily guarantee effective concealment. Future work is needed to explore the full range of dorsal patterning found in translucent glass frogs and to further examine how patterns comprised of both opaque and transparent elements may function as camouflage in a wider range of taxa.

articles.title: Temporal Changes in the Climatic Predictors of Hatching Success in Leach's Storm‐Petrels
articles.abstract: Climate change is rapidly altering ecosystems worldwide and can modify the demographic rates of long‐lived vertebrates. For seabirds, which rely on ocean productivity, reproductive success is particularly sensitive to climatic variability. Identifying the scale and stability of climate drivers is therefore critical for predicting population dynamics. Previous work on Leach's storm‐petrels (Hydrobates leucorhous) breeding on Kent Island, New Brunswick, showed that Annual Global Mean Temperature (AGMT) best explained hatching success between 1955 and 2010, with a nonlinear response peaking in the late 1980s. Here, we extend this dataset through 2024 to test whether AGMT remains a reliable predictor given the recent rise of ocean temperatures. Using mixed‐effects models, we compared hatching success with multiple climatic indices at regional, basin, and global scales. While AGMT retained some explanatory power, the best performing model for predicting variation in hatching success for the historical dataset (1955–2010) also included the Southern Oscillation Index (SOI), which was not evaluated in the original analyses, and the Atlantic Multidecadal Oscillation (AMO) for the full dataset (1955–2024). Different pathways may be involved: SOI could reflect non‐breeding conditions and have a carry‐over effect, whereas AMO could change prey availability and foraging conditions during egg formation and incubation. The relationships of hatching success with environmental indices changed over time. These results provide evidence that climate–biology relationships can be temporally dynamic, with the effects of some climatic drivers on hatching success changing over the study period. The AMO has also been linked to variation in adult survival for this population; its emerging importance for hatching success implies a compounded demographic impact with consequences for the population vulnerability.

articles.title: Bismuth electron buffering stabilizes alkaline hydrogen evolution under intermittent operation
articles.abstract: A bismuth overlayer reversibly buffers oxidative charge to protect NiCo cathodes. It suppresses metal dissolution and sustains alkaline hydrogen evolution during startup–shutdown and reverse-current cycling under industrially relevant conditions.

Reconstructing ancient ecosystems: guanaco and marine carrion as drivers of predator-prey networks in Southern South America
articles.abstract: Understanding ancient trophic dynamics and human integration in terrestrial high-latitude ecosystems requires moving beyond traditional taxonomic lists to evaluate structural biological interactions. This study presents the first probabilistic, trait-based bipartite network reconstruction of ancient predator-prey assemblages in northern Tierra del Fuego, Southern South America, based on archeological records. By integrating a comprehensive zooarcheological dataset spanning 50 spatial-temporal contexts from the late Pleistocene through the late Holocene across steppe and forest habitats, we model trophic interactions including human subsistence strategies. In this region, dominated by grassy steppes and the forest-steppe ecotone, terrestrial hunter-gatherer societies were embedded in a complex predator-prey network in which the guanaco (Lama guanicoe) played a central role. However, the trophic structure of these interactions and how the introduction of humans as an unprecedented predator affected community-level properties is poorly understood. Our results reveal a significant chronological transformation in network architecture and diet composition. During the late Pleistocene, communities exhibited lower interaction diversity and high specialization centered around megaherbivores and multiple large predators. Following megafaunal extinction and island isolation during the mid-Holocene, the guanaco emerged as an enduring keystone herbivore and dietary anchor, while marine-derived carrion and littoral resources (mollusks and pinnipeds) provided critical energy subsidies. Humans acted as highly plastic generalist consumers, influencing network architecture across diverse habitats. In the steppe, foragers employed broad-spectrum strategies, whereas forest assemblages reflected specialized reliance on coastal resources. Ultimately, this community-level framework demonstrates that despite intense environmental shifts and insularization, the guanaco and marine necromass served as foundational trophic stabilizers, maintaining ecosystem and subsistence resilience over millennia.

articles.title: Herbivore versus detritivore effect on decomposition through leaf conversion into faeces
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract In terrestrial ecosystems, plant residues can reach the soil as senesced leaf litter or green leaves, and both types can be transformed by invertebrates into detritivore or herbivore faeces. Yet, the consequences of this conversion on decomposition rates and soil fertility are largely unknown. To fill this knowledge gap, we collected faeces from caterpillars (Historis odius; herbivores) and millipedes (Anadenobolus monilicornis; detritivores), which were fed green and dead leaves of Cecropia schreberiana, respectively, in a tropical ecosystem context. We then incubated green leaves, herbivore faeces, dead leaves and detritivore faeces in a microcosm experiment for 180 days to measure their decomposition and underlying soil parameters. Our results showed significant effects of (1) leaf senescence, with green leaves decomposing faster than leaf litter, and of (2) leaf conversion to invertebrate faeces, with faeces decomposing faster than intact leaves for both herbivore and detritivore faeces. However, contrasting patterns emerged between carbon and nitrogen dynamics, as nitrogen cycling was generally slower for faeces than for litter, with a particularly notable reduction in nitrogen losses for herbivore faeces. Consequences for the biogeochemistry of the underlying soil, specifically soil mineral nitrogen, were also observed. This pioneering study on faeces decomposition in a tropical context suggests that leaf‐feeding invertebrates, whether herbivores or detritivores, accelerate decomposition processes by converting leaves into faeces. This consistent acceleration of decomposition could have important consequences for soil organic matter formation and nutrient returns to plants. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Résumé Dans les écosystèmes terrestres, les résidus végétaux atteignent le sol après la sénescence des feuilles sous forme de litière qui peut être consommée par les détritivores. Une autre voie de restitution est la chute des feuilles vertes suite à des événements météorologiques intenses (pluie, vent, sécheresse) ou à leur consommation par les herbivores dont les déjections atteignent le sol. Cependant, l’impact de ces transformations sur la dynamique de décomposition et le fonctionnement du sol demeure largement méconnu. Afin de combler ce manque de connaissance, nous avons mené une expérience en conditions contrôlées dans un écosystème tropical humide, en utilisant deux espèces d’invertébrés et une espèce végétale collectées en Martinique. Nous avons ainsi collecté des boulettes fécales produites par des chenilles herbivores (Historis odius) et des diplopodes détritivores (Anadenobolus monilicornis), nourris respectivement de feuilles vertes ou de litière de Bois Canon (Cecropia schreberiana). Ces quatre types de matière organique (feuilles vertes, boulettes fécales d'herbivores, litière et boulettes fécales de détritivores) ont ensuite été incubés en microcosmes pendant 180 jours afin d’évaluer leur décomposition et les effets sur les propriétés du sol sous‐jacent. Nos résultats montrent que la sénescence des feuilles influence fortement leur décomposition : les feuilles vertes se décomposent plus rapidement que la litière. De plus, la transformation des feuilles en boulettes fécales accélère significativement leur décomposition, que ce soit pour les herbivores ou les détritivores. Toutefois, nous avons observé des dynamiques contrastées entre la décomposition du carbone et celle de l’azote. Le cycle de l’azote s’avère généralement plus lent dans les boulettes fécales que dans les feuilles, avec une réduction particulièrement marquée des pertes d’azote pour les boulettes fécales d’herbivores. En outre, cette transformation influence significativement le fonctionnement du sol sous‐jacent, notamment en modifiant les niveaux d’azote minéral.…

articles.title: Plastic and adaptive mitochondrial responses help face hypoxia events in a freshwater fish
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Hypoxic events (i.e. reduction of dissolved oxygen in water) are natural events, which intensity and frequency have been amplified by human activities. As oxygen fuels aerobic metabolism, species unable to avoid those events must maintain their functions through phenotypic adjustments, that could occur both at the individual level (plasticity) and population genomic level (adaptation). To examine the adaptative and plastic responses to hypoxia, we exposed two generations of three‐spined sticklebacks, Gasterosteus aculeatus, from wild populations historically exposed to different oxygen levels, to two different experimental oxygen conditions (normoxia or intermittent hypoxia with 12 h normoxia: 12 h hypoxia; with nighttime O2 level at 20% for wild‐caught F0 during 4–6 weeks and at 35% for F1 throughout their entire 19‐month lifetime). By comparing the two generations, early‐life programming of the mitochondrial aerobic metabolism was revealed, conditioning the adult‐stage phenotypic and plastic response: F0 fish from the wild hypoxic environment had elevated pectoral muscle mitochondrial respiration and were able to increase their mitochondrial OXPHOS control efficiency under normoxia conditions at the adult stage. Signs of adaptations towards mitochondrial suppression were found in F1 hypoxia population fish livers while no differences were observed in their pectoral muscle, suggesting a downregulation of the hepatic, but not the pectoral muscle, aerobic activities through generations. In opposition to the adaptative trend, the plastic responses to experimental hypoxia were a decreased mitochondrial respiration in the pectoral muscle and an elevated liver mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation of the F1 fish, suggesting that inherited divergence rather countered than reinforced plastic responses. While both signs of adaptation and plasticity were found in the antioxidant defences of F1 fish, the absence of significant differences between experimental groups in terms of oxidative damage revealed that these fish were able to maintain oxidative balance. Our findings highlight that plasticity to hypoxia depends on the full organism life‐cycle, with the adult ability to face hypoxia depending on their early‐life environmental experience and provides valuable information on the potential evolutionary process of fish facing hypoxia. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Root‐associated fungi modulate plant recruitment in Mediterranean forests
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Established plants affect directly and indirectly the success of juvenile plants recruiting in their close vicinity, what is defined as a canopy–recruit interaction. Such interactions affect plant species demography and community dynamics. Root‐associated fungi (RAF) can influence plant performance and survival, thus contributing to the sign and intensity of canopy–recruit interactions. Pathogenic RAF negatively affect individual plants and their neighbours, while mycorrhizal fungi can positively counteract those effects. Additionally, saprotrophic RAF decompose organic matter, modifying nutrient availability in the soil, possibly enhancing recruitment. Therefore, understanding the role of RAFs in canopy–recruit interactions will help us understand their potential effect on the dynamics of natural plant communities. We combined information on canopy–recruit interactions for 24 woody species in two Mediterranean mixed forests with high‐throughput sequencing of root DNA from each species. We determined the relationships between plant recruitment and the similarity and richness of RAF communities among woody species associated with different mycorrhizal types. The probability of canopy–recruit interactions decreased between plants sharing more similar pathogenic RAF communities. However, their effect on the frequency of recruitment was modulated by the mycorrhizal association of the recruit, being negative for plant species associated with AM fungi but not significant for those associated with ECM. At the plant species level, plants hosting higher richness of pathogenic RAF presented scarcer recruitment and recruited under a narrower set of canopy species; on the other hand, canopy species associated with ECM fungi or hosting higher richness of saprotrophic RAF promoted denser recruit banks of any species in their vicinity. Our findings provide evidence of the importance of RAF for plant recruitment in natural habitats, and thus for plant population and community dynamics. They support the hypothesis that pathogenic RAF interact with mycorrhizal associations, and that plant species susceptibility to multiple pathogens limits its recruitment success. They also suggest that the positive effect of certain plant species on the recruitment of others (i.e. nurse effect) is likely mediated by a higher diversity of saprotrophic RAF. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Water amount, rather than watering frequency, structures root‐associated microbial communities and their links to plant performance
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Climate change is altering both the amount and temporal distribution of precipitation, yet drought is often simplified to a single gradient of water reduction. As a result, how experimentally imposed variation in water amount and watering frequency jointly shape root‐associated microbial communities and their links to plant performance remains poorly understood. Using a 3‐year full‐factorial drought experiment in a dry grassland system, we disentangled the individual and interactive effects of water amount, watering frequency and plant composition (conspecific stands versus two‐species mixtures) on root‐associated microbiome and tested whether microbial variation was linked to plant performance. Water amount emerged as the dominant driver of microbial structure, strongly shifting bacterial and fungal composition and reducing bacterial diversity. Watering frequency had weaker but detectable effects, acting mainly on bacterial communities and partly interacting with water amount, whereas the specific contrast between conspecific stands and two‐species mixtures had limited effects. Bacterial community composition was associated with root trait variation and plant fitness, suggesting that drought‐driven bacterial reassembly formed part of the pathway through which water regime influenced plant performance. Together, our results show that water amount and watering frequency represent distinct dimensions of experimental drought with partly independent effects and highlight bacterial reassembly as an important component of grassland responses to increasingly severe and temporally variable drought. articles.title: Within‐crown microclimatic variation and growth‐stage shape oak leaf chemistry with limited consequences for herbivore performance
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Mature trees exhibit distinct vertical gradients in temperature and light. These within‐crown microclimatic gradients have been linked to spatial variation in leaf chemistry and herbivory. However, phytochemical variation and resulting herbivore responses are also strongly influenced by tree phenology and genetic differences among individuals. In this study, we tested whether crown position influences the chemistry of mature leaves and whether these effects vary between distinct phenological stages within a growth cycle. We also examined whether microclimatic or growth‐stage‐related changes in phytochemistry influence herbivore performance. We exposed clonal pedunculate oak (Quercus robur) saplings within three crown strata (ground, middle and upper canopy) of mature trees at two forest sites in Germany and Switzerland. We measured targeted and untargeted leaf chemistry across growth stages and conducted bioassays with generalist spongy moth caterpillars (Lymantria dispar). We found that vertical crown position was a major driver of mature leaf chemistry. Growth stage had a significant additive effect on phytochemistry but explained less variation than crown position. We did not detect any interaction between crown position and growth stage on phytochemistry. Targeted analysis of flavonoids revealed differences among crown positions and between the two growth stages, with compounds showing distinct yet additive responses to these factors. Untargeted metabolomics revealed similar additive patterns, largely reflecting shifts in phenolic and terpenoid‐related metabolite classes. The relative growth rate of caterpillars (RGR) was affected by growth stage, declining during shoot elongation compared to the steady growth stage, but not by crown position. Among the measured metabolites, quercetin 3‐O‐glucuronide was negatively associated with caterpillar RGR, whereas higher triterpenoid levels were positively associated with RGR. Our findings demonstrate that within‐crown microclimatic variation and oak growth stage jointly shape mature leaf phytochemistry, but have only limited consequences for the performance of the generalist herbivore Lymantria dispar. Rather than reflecting broad metabolomic shifts, herbivore performance was associated with only a limited subset of measured metabolites, highlighting that pronounced chemical variation within‐tree crowns does not necessarily translate into equally strong ecological effects. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Intensification and Spatial Reorganization of Drought Risks for Global Rainfed Crops Under Climate Change
articles.abstract: Rainfed agriculture covers roughly 80% of global cropland and supplies more than half of global food production, yet uncertainty in how meteorological drying propagates into root‐zone water deficits and crop losses impedes robust risk assessment. Here, we establish an integrated, production‐weighted assessment framework coupling SPEI, SSI, and 12 GGCMI3 crop models to trace how meteorological drying propagates into root‐zone deficits and crop losses, explicitly separating affected area, conditional yield loss, and accumulated production loss across rainfed maize, soybean, and wheat. By 2070–2099, opposing‐direction SPEI–SSI change classes occupied 6.8%–28.4% of rainfed area across crops under SSP1‐2.6/default CO2 and 26.6%–48.2% under SSP5‐8.5/default CO2. Comparison with fixed‐2015 CO2 experiments (7.5%–27.6% and 21.7%–34.9%, respectively) indicates that elevated CO2 substantially expanded the spatial footprint of this hydrometeorological decoupling. Historically, SSI‐defined drought affected 12–16 million ha year−1 and was associated with annual production losses of 5–12 Mt year−1 (1.6–2.0% year−1). Under default CO2, affected area increased to 14–21 million ha under SSP1‐2.6 and 19–27 million ha under SSP5‐8.5, with production losses of 6–12 and 9–12 Mt year−1, respectively. Under SSP5‐8.5, median loss rates were higher under fixed‐2015 than default CO2 for maize (3.33 vs. 1.96% year−1), soybean (4.22 vs. 2.84% year−1) and wheat (5.41 vs. 2.90% year−1), as elevated CO2 reduces stomatal water loss and thus mitigates drought impacts, whereas SSP1‐2.6 estimates were similar. Severe drought became the largest loss contributor under both pathways and CO2 settings. Under default CO2, loss increases clustered in Central America, northeastern Brazil, western Europe and southern Africa; fixed‐2015 CO2 broadened the area of robust grid‐cell loss increases. These results show that drought‐related production losses are spatially uneven and sensitive to the modeled CO2 response, highlighting the value of crop‐ and region‐specific risk assessment.

articles.title: Plant‐ and Microbial‐Derived Soil Organic Carbon: Global Patterns and Divergent Climatic Associations
articles.abstract: Soil organic carbon (SOC) pools reflect the net balance of plant‐ and microbial‐derived inputs, transformation, and loss, yet a global‐scale assessment of distribution patterns, relative contributions, and hierarchical environmental correlates of microbial necromass carbon (MNC) and plant‐derived carbon (PdC) remains incomplete. Based on 1167 site‐level observations (1235 pool‐level records) across four ecosystem types, we applied variance partitioning, random forest, linear mixed‐effects models, and structural equation modeling to quantify global patterns and associative pathways of the two carbon pools. Unadjusted pooled comparisons showed higher MNC concentration and SOC contribution than PdC. However, covariate‐adjusted linear mixed‐effects models revealed significantly higher PdC. Paired observations showed the same directional trend, although statistical significance was not reached due to limited paired sample size (concentration: p = 0.104; contribution: p = 0.140). The apparent MNC dominance constitutes a Simpson's paradox driven by uneven ecosystem sampling, rather than a consistent within‐ecosystem pattern. Instead, the relative contribution of MNC and PdC was ecosystem‐dependent: MNC was marginally higher in forests, whereas PdC dominated in croplands and wetlands, with no significant difference in grasslands in paired observations. Edaphic variables were the strongest predictors (independent explanatory power: 61.1% for MNC, 47.4% for PdC), with total nitrogen, C:N ratio, pH, and mean annual temperature as key correlates. Our results reveal a hierarchical associative cascade in which geographic factors covary with climate, which in turn correlates with edaphic properties as the strongest direct predictors. Climate shows a weak but significant negative direct association with MNC only. This synthesis provides a hierarchical correlative framework and biome‐specific baseline parameters to support explicit representation of plant‐ and microbial‐mediated SOC pathways in Earth system models.

articles.title: Does the resource dispersion hypothesis predict grouping behaviour in a solitary megaherbivore?
articles.abstract: No authors have evaluated how the resource dispersion hypothesis applies to solitary herbivores although it may explain group formation and contribute to management. We found grouping behaviour of black rhinos, a solitary megaherbivore, largely adhered to predictions associated with the hypothesis, with implications for management of this critically endangered species. Abstract The resource dispersion hypothesis (RDH) predicts that when resources are abundant and heterogeneously distributed, multiple individuals may satisfy their resource needs in a shared area without imposing large costs on one another. Under such conditions, groups can form even in the absence of other benefits, and other life history traits may not entirely explain group composition. For example, groups forming under conditions associated with the RDH may not display a biased sex ratio even if otherwise expected. Solitary herbivores, which are unlikely to gain benefits from grouping, may be strongly subject to the RDH, especially during growing seasons when there is an abundance of resources. However, to the best of our knowledge, no study has evaluated whether grouping behaviours in any solitary herbivore follows RDH predictions. To explore this, we used 48,678 sightings of black rhinos (Diceros bicornis) from 13 reserves in southern Africa to assess whether grouping behaviour in this solitary megaherbivore aligned with predictions of the RDH, or reflected predictions informed by the species ecology. We found that group formation and size largely followed RDH predictions where groups were more likely to form when resources were heterogenous and of high quality. Additionally, groups were larger during the growing season and when resources were heterogeneous. In contrast, as resource quality increased, group size decreased. Similarly, two of the four group composition results followed RDH predictions, where increasing group size was associated with decreasing within‐group familiarity and an unbiased sex ratio in opposition to usual expectations. The other two followed species ecology predictions wherein increasing group size was associated with an increasing proportion of subadults and all large groups included at least one cow–calf pair. Ultimately, our results show that, in solitary herbivores, the RDH may be useful in predicting group formation and size and may explain instances when group composition diverges from species‐specific expectations. Understanding grouping behaviour in endangered solitary species such as black rhino may improve management by allowing managers to identify conditions under which individuals are more tolerant of conspecifics.

articles.title: Drivers of bird species turnover in the largest archipelago of China: Insights from zeta (ζ) diversity and multi‐site generalized dissimilarity modelling (MS‐GDM)
articles.abstract: The zeta diversity of bird assemblages in the Zhoushan Archipelago highlights the importance of dividing overall assemblages into separate ecological groups as the results of zeta diversity are different among bird groups. Our study also provides a transferable framework for other land‐bridge archipelagos and fragmented landscapes. Abstract Species turnover, the spatial dissimilarity in species composition, is a central concept in island biogeography and community ecology. Traditional pairwise beta diversity metrics are limited to two‐site comparisons and cannot fully resolve the mechanisms driving turnover across multiple communities. Zeta (ζ) diversity overcomes this limitation by quantifying multi‐site species sharing and capturing how both rare and widespread species contribute to species turnover along a continuum. However, existing applications of zeta diversity to birds have focused mainly on continental, urban or land‐use gradients, and have not examined island systems while simultaneously comparing phenological periods and migratory groups, nor have they separated richness differences from species replacement. As a typical land‐bridge archipelago containing multiple bird groups, the Zhoushan Archipelago of China provides an ideal system for addressing these research gaps. We surveyed forest bird assemblages across 40 islands in this archipelago. We combined zeta diversity, multi‐site generalized dissimilarity modelling (MS‐GDM) and generalized additive models, using both Sørensen and Simpson normalizations to distinguish the contribution of richness differences from that of species replacement. We classified forest birds by season (breeding vs. wintering) and by migratory strategy (resident vs. migrant), yielding five ecological groups: all forest birds, breeding birds, wintering birds, residents and migrants. We then tested whether the relative importance of island characteristics varied among these five bird groups. Zeta decay followed a pure power‐law form in all five bird groups, indicating a scale‐invariant pattern of species loss across sites. Comparing MS‐GDM results based on Sørensen‐normalized and Simpson‐normalized zeta diversity revealed a fundamental duality: island area primarily drove richness differences through selective species loss on small islands, whereas distance to the nearest mainland consistently governed true species replacement across all bird groups. Overall, our results demonstrate that deterministic assembly operates through two distinct pathways, that is area‐driven environmental filtering and isolation‐driven dispersal limitation, which jointly structure multi‐site species turnover. The richness difference and replacement duality identified here can be generalizable to other land‐bridge archipelagos and fragmented landscapes where area and isolation jointly shape community assembly, and provides a mechanistic framework for interpreting multi‐site species turnover beyond simple richness gradients.

articles.title: Fear generalization, cross‐sensitization and behavioural responses to multiple dangers in a freshwater snail
articles.abstract: We show that juvenile exposure to a danger can not only prime individuals to be more responsive to that same danger later in life but also to an ostensibly unrelated danger. These patterns of behavioural cross‐sensitization can have important ecological implications for how animals respond to multiple and novel stressors. Abstract Behavioural responses to multiple stressors play a major role in survival and fitness. In this context, an important issue that has rarely been tested is fear generalization, where responses to disparate threats are correlated at the individual level. Furthermore, while sensitization to stressors is well studied, cross‐sensitization, where exposure to one threat increases behavioural responsiveness to unrelated threats, is under‐studied. We exposed juvenile Physid snails (Physa acuta) to one of two disparate threats throughout their developmental period: predator cues and ash, a wildfire‐derived environmental stressor. We then assayed snails' responses, relative to control snails that had no experience with either threat, to three acute exposures of each stressor. We documented consistent individual differences in snails' avoidance of predation cues and of ash. Exposure to either stressor led to sensitization at short‐ and long‐term timescales. Importantly, snails exhibited fear generalization; individuals that avoided predation cues more strongly also avoided ash more strongly. We also documented cross‐sensitization; snails reared with ash showed heightened responses to predator cues while snails reared with predator cues showed heightened responses to ash. To our knowledge, this is the first study documenting behavioural cross‐sensitization for threats as disparate as predation risk and fire residue in a non‐human animal.

articles.title: Herbivore thermoregulation, movement behaviour and survival during a severe drought in Namibia
articles.abstract: of behavioural and physiological responses of plains zebra (Equus quagga) and blue wildebeest (Connochaetes taurinus) during the cool drought, hot drought, and recovery periods in Etosha National Park, Namibia. Arrows illustrate relative changes in movement, while temperature diagrams depict seasonal variation in minimum (T min) and maximum (T max) body temperatures and daily temperature amplitude (T max − T min). Despite behavioural adjustments during drought, both species experienced substantial physiological challenges, with drought-associated mortality reaching 27% in zebra and 15% in wildebeest. Following rainfall, improved resource availability coincided with reduced body temperature variability, indicating physiological recovery. Background photographs courtesy of Wendy Turner and Bernd Brell. Abstract Climate change is expected to increase the frequency and severity of droughts in dryland ecosystems, yet the mechanisms determining whether large herbivores survive these events remain poorly understood. We investigated how an extreme drought influenced movement, water use, body temperature and survival of two water-dependent grazing herbivores, plains zebra (Equus quagga) and blue wildebeest (Connochaetes taurinus), in Etosha National Park, Namibia. GPS collars and abdominal temperature loggers were deployed on free-ranging animals during the most severe drought on record. We quantified changes in movement, drinking behaviour, thermoregulation and survival across seasons classified as cool drought, hot drought and rainy season recovery periods. Both species exhibited substantial behavioural plasticity as drought intensified, including shifts in diel activity, shorter median intervals between visits to perennial water sources and highly variable drinking schedules among individuals. Zebra increased daily travel during the hot drought, whereas wildebeest reduced daily travel and shifted activity toward cooler periods of the day, reflecting contrasting strategies for balancing resource acquisition with thermoregulation. Despite these behavioural adjustments, both species exhibited their greatest body temperature variability during both the cool and hot drought periods, indicating that these behavioural responses were insufficient to fully buffer the physiological consequences of the drought. Following rainfall, increased vegetation greenness was associated with higher minimum body temperatures and reduced daily temperature amplitudes, consistent with physiological recovery. Nevertheless, drought-related mortality reached 27% in zebra and 15% in wildebeest, differences that were not statistically significant. Although this drought was considerably more severe than those reported from other African protected areas, grazer mortality was comparable to or lower than that documented during less severe droughts, suggesting that behavioural flexibility together with the large, heterogeneous landscape of Etosha partially buffered drought impacts. Our findings demonstrate that behavioural responses can delay, but not fully prevent, the breakdown of physiological homeostasis during extreme drought. Integrating movement, physiology and survival provides a mechanistic framework for identifying populations approaching their resilience limits as climate change increases the frequency of extreme drought events. Resumen El cambio climático ha causado el aumento de la frecuencia e intensidad de las sequías en zonas áridas. Sin embargo, aún se desconocen algunos mecanismos que determinan si los grandes herbívoros sobreviven a estos eventos. Investigamos cómo una sequía extrema afectó el movimiento, uso del agua, temperatura corporal y supervivencia de dos herbívoros pastadores dependientes del agua, cebra de llanura (Equus quagga) y ñu azul (Connochaetes taurinus), en el Parque Nacional de Etosha, Namibia.…

articles.title: The spatiotemporal effects of seasonal migration on passerine phylogenetic community structure
articles.abstract: The effects of mobile organisms on community structure and assembly are poorly understood. Distributional data show that seasonal migration in birds drives a complex continental redistribution of phylogenetic community structure. These results reveal a dynamic continental landscape of community structure directed by the movements of migratory birds. Abstract Seasonal migration in birds involves a substantial spatial redistribution of avian biodiversity each year and drives seasonal changes in community composition. Migrants experience different combinations of species interactions over space and time, generating regular disassembly and reassembly of bird communities throughout their annual cycles. However, the effects of seasonal migration on phylogenetic community structure remain poorly understood. We assess spatiotemporal variation in phylogenetic community structure of North American passerines to test how seasonal migration restructures the evolutionary relatedness and dominant assembly mechanisms in bird communities throughout the annual cycle. Using distributional projections, we calculated metrics describing the phylogenetic dispersion of passerine communities each week of the year. We then tested the relationship between seasonal turnover in community phylogenetic dispersion and seasonal variation in species richness and proportion of migratory species. Seasonal migration, by changing spatial patterns of avian diversity, simultaneously drives a complex continental redistribution of phylogenetic community structure. We find evidence of taxonomic scale dependency to our results, wherein throughout North America, the seasonal influx of migrant passerines yields communities that are overall more phylogenetically clustered, yet also exhibit greater phylogenetic overdispersion at smaller taxonomic scales. Seasonal shifts in phylogenetic dispersion, though complex, track changes in diversity, manifesting as fluctuations in phylogenetic dispersion between northern and southern regions as seasonal migrants move between these regions. Our findings reveal a dynamic continental landscape of phylogenetic community structure directed by the movements of seasonal migrants.

articles.title: Thermoregulation in Heliconius butterflies is determined by habitat association and morphology but not phylogeny
articles.abstract: The roles of morphology and phylogeny in thermoregulation were studied in mimetic Heliconius butterflies across habitats. Buffering ability differed among habitats, likely due to morphology. Live heating rate decreased with iridescence and forewing length. No phylogenetic signal was detected. This suggests Heliconius wing patterns may contribute to thermoregulation. Abstract Temperature determines butterflies' physiological processes and performance. It varies strongly across time and space, with tropical butterflies experiencing temperatures close to their thermal limits. Climate change with more frequent heat waves may push species closer to these limits. Butterflies are known to thermoregulate, which is influenced by their morphology and behaviour. However, in tropical butterflies, little is known about how thermoregulatory abilities vary across habitats and if morphology or species relatedness are their drivers. We conducted a field and laboratory study on buffering ability—the ability to regulate body temperature with respect to air temperature—, take‐off temperature and heating rate of mimetic Heliconius butterflies from different habitats. We tested whether butterfly thermoregulation varies across habitats and morphologies. We also tested whether closely related species exhibit more similar thermoregulatory abilities and explored the importance of behaviour. Mimetic Heliconius pairs are two species that have nearly identical wing coloration and are often in different phylogenetic clades. Studying these pairs allows us to quantify the contribution of morphology and phylogenetic relatedness to thermoregulation. Because mimetic species pairs are often restricted to specific habitats, thermoregulatory abilities can be compared across habitats. We found that butterflies from different habitats differed in their buffering ability, likely due to differences in morphology, such as wing colour. Take‐off temperature was lowest in the only high‐altitude species we studied, whereas species from lowland habitats did not differ. Live heating rate did not differ across habitats, yet it decreased with iridescence and forewing length. There was no phylogenetic signal in thermoregulatory abilities, indicating that more closely related species did not thermoregulate more similarly than expected by chance. Our results showed that the convergent wing patterns in Heliconius butterflies may contribute to thermoregulatory ability and that thermoregulation should be considered when investigating the habitat specificity of mimetic pairs. Furthermore, Heliconius thermoregulation is not constrained by shared ancestry, suggesting that the morphological traits observed in the different mimetic pairs may be advantageous in certain thermal environmental conditions. Overall, species differences in thermoregulatory abilities may shape how Heliconius distributions respond to climate change‐driven temperature shifts. Resumen La temperatura determina los procesos fisiológicos y el rendimiento de las mariposas. Esta varía considerablemente en el tiempo y el espacio, y en los trópicos las mariposas experimentan temperaturas cercanas a sus límites térmicos. En un escenario de cambio climático, las olas de calor más frecuentes podrían acercar aún más a las especies de mariposas a estos límites. Se sabe que las mariposas termorregulan y que su capacidad termorreguladora está influenciada por su morfología y comportamiento. Sin embargo, en las mariposas tropicales se sabe poco sobre cómo varían las capacidades termorreguladoras entre hábitats y si la morfología o el parentesco filogenético entre especies son sus factores determinantes.…

articles.title: A Biodegradable Metal–Organic Framework/Oligomer Composite for Sustainable Gold Recovery and Circular Water Management
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence and digital technologies is generating unprecedented e-waste streams rich in secondary gold resources, yet sustainable recovery strategies remain scarce. Here, we report a bioderived, environmentally degradable metal–organic framework (MOF)/oligomer composite (SU-102/pGSH) constructed via host–guest self-assembly of glutathione (GSH) within a Zr-ellagate framework. The composite integrates abundant electron-rich functional groups into a robust porous architecture, achieving a remarkable gold uptake capacity of 4385 mg·g–1, the highest reported for MOF-based adsorbents. It also exhibits outstanding selectivity in complex e-waste leachates. Mechanistic investigations reveal synergistic coordination with abundant electron-rich groups, followed by electron-transfer reduction of Au(III) to Au(0). Importantly, the spent adsorbent could degrade into benign mineral phases and natural metabolites with negligible phytotoxicity, ensuring a safe end-of-life pathway. Preliminary techno-economic analysis indicates favorable economic potential for practical implementation. By integrating efficient gold recovery with sustainable material design and end-of-life management, this work provides a viable strategy for circular water treatment.

articles.title: Computational Quantum Chemistry-Based Atmospheric Isotope Fractionation Prediction Framework: Application in Sulfate Aerosol Formation Mechanisms
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Atmospheric isotope serves as an effective source tracer for tracking the pollutants fate. Its precise source apportionment capability is constrained by the comprehensive assessment of isotope fractionation. This study aimed to propose a Computational Quantum Chemistry (CQC)-based Atmospheric Isotope Fractionation Prediction (AIFP) framework. It can quantify the isotope fractionation mechanisms. This framework utilizes CQC to perform a pipeline for reaction mechanism determination, atmospheric species geometry calculation, and parameter post-processing. It integrates the isotope-substitution method with the fractionation model to establish isotope fractionation standard equations in complex atmospheric chemical systems, providing a theoretical basis for atmospheric isotope tracing. This framework was applied to investigate sulfur (34S) fractionation and sulfate (pSO42–) formation. This application developed a localized 34S fractionation parameter scheme, revealing that pSO42– pollution is driven by NO2 and TMI oxidation. These oxidants account for 58.3 ± 1.0% of its pollution, highlighting the critical role of controlling the transformation conditions of key oxidants in haze pollution mitigation. Our framework extends the atmospheric isotope application, providing a rapid and efficient isotope fractionation prediction framework.
