articles.title: Recent progress in the computational study of supercooled and glassy water
articles.abstract: This Review discusses recent advances in the computational exploration of the properties of supercooled and glassy water.

articles.title: Peripheral neuroimmune dialogues underlying pain states
articles.abstract: This Review explores how neuroimmune crosstalk shapes pain responses. The authors describe the interactions between nociceptors and immune cells across different anatomical sites and discuss emerging therapeutic strategies for pain management.

articles.title: Predicting responses to prebiotic fibres: linking microbiota, function and clinical outcomes
articles.abstract: Prebiotics and dietary fibre show highly individualized effects on gut microbiota and clinical outcomes, challenging their consistent effectiveness across populations. This Review examines the drivers of this variability, presents predictive approaches and discusses strategies to optimize prebiotic responses across individuals.

articles.title: Synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials
articles.abstract: Atomically thin amorphous materials combine atomic-scale thickness with local structural disorder, creating unusual transport, interfacial, electronic and catalytic properties. This Review outlines the mechanism-guided synthesis of atomically thin amorphous materials, scalable manufacturing and structure–property relationships and discusses AI-assisted closed-loop strategies for application-oriented design and wafer-scale production.

articles.title: Management of Moderate Aortic Stenosis in Older Adults — The P in PICOT
TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features
articles.abstract: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown. We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population. A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement. Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

articles.title: Allometric scaling of adaxial–abaxial stomatal allocation in amphistomatous plants worldwide
articles.abstract: Adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities in amphistomatous plants follow a phylogenetically structured allometric scaling relationship, with species‐specific departures (ASR) associated with climate–soil context. Summary Amphistomatous plants distribute stomata between the adaxial and abaxial leaf surfaces, but whether this dual‐surface allocation follows a predictable scaling relationship, and why species deviate from it, remains poorly understood. Here, we compiled a global dataset of adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities for 559 species across 380 sites and 63 families. We quantified their allometric relationship using phylogenetic reduced major axis regression and calculated amphistomatal scaling residuals (ASR) as signed perpendicular deviations from the fitted scaling relationship. We then examined variation in ASR among plant functional groups and across climatic and edaphic gradients. Adaxial and abaxial stomatal densities showed a significant allometric relationship after accounting for phylogenetic nonindependence, with a slope significantly > 1. ASR showed a significant phylogenetic signal but did not differ significantly between woody and herbaceous species, evergreen and deciduous woody species, or annual and perennial herbs. Individual environmental associations with ASR were generally modest, whereas the selected phylogenetic model retained multiple interaction terms, indicating that associations between ASR and environmental conditions were strongly context‐dependent. By quantifying departures from adaxial–abaxial scaling, our study identifies a distinct dimension of stomatal allocation that is structured by evolutionary history and associated with multidimensional climatic and edaphic context. This framework provides a basis for testing the physiological and evolutionary mechanisms underlying variation in amphistomatous stomatal allocation.

articles.title: Cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction of conifer fine roots
articles.abstract: Yellow‐cedar has experienced widespread decline as climate change reduces the snowpack that insulates its roots, but the mechanism of injury is unknown. We tested two competing hypotheses in roots of four conifers: loss of xylem conductivity from freeze‐thaw embolism, or loss of radial conductivity from direct freezing injury that forms cortical lacunae. Embolism caused little loss of conductivity in any species or treatment (a–c). In contrast, extreme freeze–thaw pushed radial conductivity loss in yellow‐cedar beyond the 50% threshold for lethal hydraulic dysfunction (f). Root freezing injury, not embolism, may explain why yellow‐cedar is especially vulnerable to snowpack loss. Summary Winter snowpack loss exposes fine roots to freeze–thaw cycles at high latitudes and elevations, but the mechanisms of injury and reasons for species differences in vulnerability are not well understood. Motivated by yellow‐cedar decline, we evaluated competing mechanisms of freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction (xylem embolism and cortical lacunae) and whether root economics strategy predicts susceptibility. We subjected 96 seedlings of four co‐occurring Pacific Northwest conifers (mountain hemlock, western hemlock, western redcedar, and yellow‐cedar) to seven daily temperature cycles with minima of 3, −3, or −9°C, quantifying xylem and radial conductivity loss, cortical lacunae, and root economics traits. Xylem conductivity loss was low in all species and treatments (mean 11–14%). Yellow‐cedar averaged 58% simulated radial conductivity loss at −9°C, with lacunae occupying 20% of cortical area. Hemlocks (with pervasively lignified cortical walls) rarely formed lacunae, whereas cedars (with largely unlignified walls reinforced by phi‐thickenings) were more susceptible. More acquisitive roots were more vulnerable, among and within species. Our results indicate that cortical lacunae, not xylem embolism, drive interspecific differences in freeze–thaw hydraulic dysfunction, which was most severe in yellow‐cedar. Vulnerability corresponded to cortical wall construction and root economics strategy, providing a mechanistic basis for yellow‐cedar's unique susceptibility to snowpack loss.

articles.title: Emerging roles of inositol pyrophosphates in plants: from environmental stress acclimation to hormonal responses and terrestrialization
articles.abstract: Schematic presentation highlighting role of PP‐InsPs in orchestrating diverse physiological functions and an illustration highlighting the putative roles of InsP and PP‐InsPs in plant terrestrialization. Summary Diphosphate‐containing inositol phosphates, also known as inositol pyrophosphates (PP‐InsPs), are energy‐rich signaling molecules that orchestrate an ever‐expanding repertoire of cellular processes in eukaryotes. Recent advances in analytical methodologies have been instrumental in detecting these messengers in plant extracts and characterizing the enzymology underlying PP‐InsP metabolism in plants. Collectively, these developments have been critical to establishing PP‐InsPs as emerging cellular messengers that control a broad spectrum of physiological processes, including immunity, nutrient homeostasis, growth, and development in plants. In this Tansley insight, we synthesize current knowledge on the molecular basis of PP‐InsP metabolism and their physiological functions, and outline potential future research directions. We further discuss the putative role of PP‐InsPs in plant terrestrialization, a pivotal evolutionary transition that fundamentally reshaped Earth's biosphere approximately half a billion years ago.

articles.title: Four universal modules and their combinations for decoding amplitude and frequency of Ca2+ signals in plants
articles.abstract: Modelling of Ca2+ effects at the micro, macro, and cellular levels. (a) Ca2+ binding to a calcium-binding protein (CBP) with two EF hands. (b) Four basic Ca2+ sensor modules. (c) Combining Ca2+ decoding modules with opposite properties can restrict the activity of the target protein (TP) to frequency islands. Summary Calcium signals are fundamental for plants and play crucial roles in developmental processes and in rapid responses to environmental stimuli and stress factors. Nevertheless, the mechanisms underlying the decoding of calcium signals in plants are still largely unclear. We have addressed the question of Ca2+ signal decoding in a bottom-up modelling approach starting with the thermodynamics of Ca2+ binding to EF hands (EF: Glutamic acid–Phenylalanine) in Ca2+-binding proteins (CBPs). On this basis, we identified four universal, fundamental Ca2+ decoding modules, in which a CBP modulates the activity of a target protein (TP). Representatives of these basic modules are omnipresent in plant cells. Their Ca2+ dependent properties are mainly determined by the interaction of the CBP with the TP rather than the Ca2+-binding properties of the EF hands. Combinations of the modules generated complexes that are also observed in plants, which decode not only the amplitude but also the frequency of Ca2+ signals by setting specific ‘frequency islands’ in which a TP is active. The modelling approach presented here addresses the decoding of Ca2+ signals from the microscopic to the systemic level and could help to find the ‘Rosetta Stone’ for Ca2+ signalling in plants. Resumen Las señales de calcio son fundamentales para las plantas y desempeñan funciones cruciales en los procesos de desarrollo, así como en las respuestas rápidas a los estímulos ambientales y los factores de estrés. Sin embargo, los mecanismos implicados en la decodificación de las señales de calcio en las plantas siguen sin estar claros en gran medida. Hemos abordado el tema de la decodificación de las señales de calcio mediante un enfoque de modelado ascendente (bottom-up), partiendo de la termodinámica de la unión de Ca2+ a los dominios EF-hand (EF: ácido glutámico–fenilalanina) en proteínas con unión de calcio (CBP, por sus siglas en inglés, Ca 2+ -binding proteins). Sobre esta base, identificamos cuatro módulos universales y fundamentales de decodificación de Ca2+, en los cuales una CBP modula la actividad de una proteína diana (TP, del inglés target protein). Los representantes de estos módulos básicos son omnipresentes en las células vegetales. Sus propiedades dependientes de Ca2+ están determinadas principalmente por la interacción de la CBP con la TP, más que por las propiedades de unión de Ca2+ de los dominios EF-hand. Las combinaciones de estos módulos generaron complejos que también se observan en las plantas, lo que permitió decodificar no solo la amplitud, sino también la frecuencia de las señales de Ca2+, al establecer «islas de frecuencia» específicas en las cuales una TP está activa. El enfoque de modelado presentado en este trabajo aborda la decodificación de las señales de Ca2+ desde el nivel microscópico hasta el sistémico, y podría ayudar a encontrar la «piedra Rosetta» de la señalización por Ca2+ en las plantas.

articles.title: PELOTA at the crossroads of tomato fertility and viral resistance
articles.abstract: PELOTA (PELO), a conserved ribosome surveillance factor underlying the tomato resistance allele ty-5, plays key roles in TYLCV susceptibility and reproductive development. Complete loss of PELO function (pelo-1CR ) confers strong resistance to TYLCV but causes severe floral defects, impaired male and female fertility, and complete sterility. While ty-5 reduces disease severity, it also decreases fruit size. CRISPR-mediated promoter editing generates novel PELO alleles, with reduced expression that confers resistance while maintaining normal fertility and fruit size (PELOpro-31 ). Fine-tuning PELO expression therefore offers a promising strategy to improve tomato resistance without compromising reproductive development. Summary Tomato yellow leaf curl virus (TYLCV) is a major threat to tomato (Solanum lycopersicum) production, and durable resistance remains challenging to achieve. We show that complete loss of function of PELOTA (PELO), a conserved ribosome surveillance factor underlying the resistance allele ty-5, confers near-immunity to TYLCV. Unexpectedly, PELO is also required for reproductive development; pelo mutants display severe floral defects, impaired male and female fertility, and complete sterility, revealing a previously unknown role for PELO in tomato plant fertility. Using CRISPR-mediated promoter editing, we generated novel PELO alleles with reduced expression that maintain fertility while conferring enhanced resistance to TYLCV, providing a new strategy.

articles.title: Why be deciduous in a tropical savanna climate? Insights from leaf deployment, stem growth and sap flow dynamics
articles.abstract: Stem increment, sap flow and leaf phenology. Summary Savannas are ecosystems with hot and wet summers and warm and dry winters. How and why savanna trees partition their physiological activity through this seasonal cycle is unknown; yet it is important to understand this temporal partitioning in order to anticipate how anthropogenic climatic change will impact the functioning of savannas. In a South African savanna ecosystem, we examined the temporal pattern of leaf deployment, sap flow and stem increment phenology over three growing seasons for six species. We found that although the phenologies varied between years, there was a high degree of temporal overlap in leaf, sap flow and stem increment phenology between the six study species. Further, we found that a surprisingly large proportion of days on which the measured soil water potential was sufficient for physiological activity remained unused. Although our data are consistent with convergent selection for deciduousness, the unused soil water niche we detected suggests that climate should select for evergreen strategies. Possible explanations for the dominance of deciduousness in these savannas relate to the costs of leaf construction coupled with the risk of leaf destruction due to fire and/or foliovory.

articles.title: A mucosal barrier injury related six gene transcriptomic signature associated with ulcerative colitis using machine learning and public transcriptomic data
articles.abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is characterized by epithelial barrier disruption, mucosal immune activation, and sustained intestinal inflammation. We developed a biologically interpretable public-transcriptomic signature using Gene Expression Omnibus datasets GSE75214, GSE38713, and GSE92415. A literature-curated panel of 35 mucosal barrier injury-related genes was integrated with differential expression, LASSO regression, random forest prioritization, and ridge logistic regression. Six genes (LCN2, DEFB1, S100A8, MUC1, VIL1, and TJP3) were retained as a locked transcriptomic score. Because the original feature-selection steps used the complete development cohort, we added 50 repetitions of stratified five-fold outer cross-validation. All preprocessing and ridge tuning were restricted to each outer-training fold; the locked score achieved a mean out-of-fold AUC of 0.9660 (SD 0.0031). A stricter sensitivity analysis that repeated differential-expression filtering, LASSO, random-forest ranking, deterministic six-gene selection, and ridge fitting within each outer-training fold achieved a mean out-of-fold AUC of 0.9600 (SD 0.0094). The refitted locked model retained discrimination in GSE38713 (AUC 0.8974, 95% CI 0.8040–0.9909) and GSE92415 (AUC 0.9894, 95% CI 0.9744–1.0000) when one development-derived cutoff was applied unchanged. The six-gene score did not significantly outperform VIL1 alone in the development cohort (DeLong P = 0.4026). The signature should therefore be interpreted as a molecular pattern associated with UC mucosal inflammation and barrier remodeling rather than as a UC-specific clinical diagnostic test.

articles.title: A quantitative assessment of Chinese county high school policies using the PMC index model
articles.abstract: The county high school policies (CHSPs) is crucial for improving the quality of basic education in China’s counties and promoting rural social development. As policy documents are the foundational elements of policy systems, it is crucial to evaluate current policy texts, identify their shortcomings, and provide empirical evidence for future policy development. This study collected 55 policy texts from provincial and municipal governments, utilizing the Policy Modeling Consistency index model to evaluate 14 representative policies. The results indicate that all the assessed policies fall within the“pass”,“good”,or“with distinction” score category, with no substandard policies identified and none achieving a “perfect” score.A detailed analysis identifies critical policy shortcomings, including the prioritization of short-to-medium-term strategies over long-term planning, fragmented enrollment systems, insufficient campus culture development, as well as limited career guidance, mental health support,and policy guidance for home-school-community joint education. Local governments adopt a conservative stance on educational policy evaluation and systemic institutional reforms.To address these issues, this study recommends that local governments integrate the enrollment systems of public and private high schools within their jurisdictions, strengthen the prohibition of on cross-regional enrollment, increase investment in students’ career guidance and mental health education, and launch more programs to encourage parents and communities to participate in school education. Moreover, the central government should urge local authorities to accelerate reforms in the high school education system.

articles.title: A temperature-adaptive logit-standardized knowledge distillation for lightweight network intrusion detection
articles.abstract: The rapid growth of the Internet has made network attacks increasingly frequent, stealthy, and diverse, posing stringent requirements on the accuracy and latency of network intrusion detection systems (NIDS). Although deep-learning-based NIDS can achieve strong detection performance, their large parameter size and high computational cost hinder deployment on resource-constrained edge devices. To address this limitation, we propose a temperature-adaptive logit-standardized knowledge distillation framework for lightweight network intrusion detection. A high-capacity teacher network first learns discriminative representations from network traffic, and a compact student network is then trained to mimic the teacher under a tailored distillation scheme. During distillation, we apply per-sample Z-score standardization to the logits of both teacher and student models to mitigate scale mismatch and emphasize relative inter-class relationships. Moreover, we adapt the distillation temperature according to sample difficulty and training progress, enabling suitably smoothed soft targets across samples and stages, and jointly optimize the student with hard-label supervision. Experiments on benchmark datasets including NSL-KDD and CIC-IDS2017 demonstrate that the proposed method substantially reduces model complexity while maintaining stable and competitive detection performance. Additional repeated-run, ablation, and lightweight baseline analyses further indicate that the proposed framework achieves a favorable accuracy–complexity trade-off.

articles.title: Adoption, usage patterns, and perceptions of DeepSeek among medical interns: Evidence from a Chinese Teaching Hospital
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI)–driven chatbots based on large language models are increasingly entering medical education, but evidence on the real-world use of domestic systems such as DeepSeek among Chinese medical interns is still scarce. This cross-sectional study investigated the prevalence, patterns and perceptions of DeepSeek use among medical interns at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Anhui Medical University. A total of 634 interns from clinical medicine, preventive medicine and nursing completed an anonymous questionnaire. Overall, about one-third of interns reported using DeepSeek. Among users, most engaged with the tool regularly, with over half using it several times per week. DeepSeek was primarily employed for completing assignments, searching for information, translation and polishing of written texts, while a smaller subset of users reported using it for data analysis. Attitudes toward DeepSeek were mainly neutral or optimistic, and across majors most users perceived its advantages and disadvantages as broadly balanced, while only a minority considered the disadvantages to outweigh the advantages. After adjustment, residence and major remained associated with DeepSeek use, whereas age and sex were not. Urban interns were more likely to report using DeepSeek than rural interns. Compared with clinical medicine interns, preventive medicine interns were less likely to report use, whereas nursing interns were more likely to do so. Among users, overall attitudes differed across majors, while usage frequency and the perceived balance of advantages and disadvantages did not. These findings provide descriptive evidence on the use and evaluation of DeepSeek among medical interns and may inform future institutional guidance on responsible use, verification of AI-generated information and academic integrity.

articles.title: Agri-PIDNet-S: Lightweight semantic segmentation for field-structure and obstacle perception in seedling-stage cotton fields
articles.abstract: Reliable joint perception of crop rows, furrows, and obstacles is essential for autonomous inter-row operations in seedling-stage cotton fields. However, small and sparsely distributed plants, perspective-convergent rows, irregular furrow boundaries, and low obstacle pixel coverage jointly challenge fine-detail preservation, long-range structural modeling, and boundary discrimination under real-time constraints. This study formulated cotton-field perception as a four-class semantic segmentation task and constructed a dataset of 709 pixel-wise annotated images comprising background, crop rows, furrows, and obstacles. We developed Agri-PIDNet-S, a field-specific lightweight network based on PIDNet-S. A coordinate-aware multi-kernel inverted residual module (CA-MKIR) preserves shallow details and small-obstacle contours, a squeeze-and-excitation-enhanced deep-to-token module (SaE-D2T) models long-range row and furrow structures, and a boundary-guided window-attention refinement Bag (BWR-Bag) improves semantic–boundary fusion. The network was trained with a composite loss incorporating auxiliary boundary supervision. On the cotton-field test set, Agri-PIDNet-S achieved 92.37% mean intersection over union (mIoU) and 96.02% mean Dice coefficient (mDice) in the model-comparison experiment, while repeated training with three seeds yielded an mIoU of 92.35 ± 0.03%. Relative to PIDNet-S under the same comparison protocol, mIoU increased by 3.53 percentage points, while obstacle IoU improved from 79.60% to 88.67%. The model contained 8.048 million parameters, required 19.161 GFLOPs, and achieved 155.67 frames per second. Zero-shot external evaluation on tomato, watermelon, and maize fields yielded a structural mIoU of 86.29% for the background, crop-row, and furrow classes. Under the evaluated conditions, the task-oriented modifications achieved higher segmentation point estimates than PIDNet-S while maintaining computational efficiency; the external results provide preliminary evidence of cross-crop structural transfer.

articles.title: Bacterial urinary tract infections and urogenital schistosomiasis co-infection among primary school children in a Meatu district, Tanzania: A call for an integrated preventive approach
articles.abstract: Background Urogenital schistosomiasis (UGS) remains a significant public health issue in Tanzania, co-infection with urinary tract infections (UTIs) can complicate diagnosis due to overlapping symptoms. Additionally, gastrointestinal carriage of multidrug-resistant bacteria (MDRB) increases risks of self-infection and transmission to others. Primary school-aged children in rural settings are particularly at risk for both diseases due to poor water sanitation and risky behaviors. This study reports the prevalence and patterns of UGS and UTI co-infection, and MDRB gut carriage among primary school-aged children. Methodology A school-based cross-sectional study was conducted in Meatu district, Tanzania (Oct–Dec 2024). UGS was diagnosed using urine filtration, UTIs through urine culture while stool samples were screened for Extended spectrum beta lactamase (ESBL) producing bacteria. Descriptive analysis was done using STATA 15.0. Results Among 405 children enrolled, the prevalence of UGS, UTIs, and UGS–UTI co-infection was 44.1%, 12.8%, and 5.2%, respectively. Heavy UGS infection was associated with a greater likelihood of UTI than light infection. Haematuria was associated with UGS, whereas frequent and painful urination were common among children with UTIs and co-infection. Escherichia coli was the predominant UTI pathogen, with substantial resistance to third-generation cephalosporins. ESBL-producing bacteria and multidrug-resistant bacteria were also identified among UTI isolates. Conclusions Co-infection of UGS & UTI among primary school children is a noticeable problem in the study settings; fever, frequent urination and painful urination are good predictors for co-infection. Similarities in clinical symptoms among co-infected individuals may complicate diagnosis and management on the initial assessment. High proportion of MDRB carriage in rural settings indicates the extensive burden of antimicrobial resistance in developing countries.

articles.title: Cardiometabolic risk burden and associated behaviours in schoolchildren aged 7–10 years from public urban schools in the Federal District, Brazil
articles.abstract: Objective To assess cardiometabolic risk burden among schoolchildren aged 7–10 years attending public urban elementary schools in the Federal District, Brazil, and examine its association with health behaviours and socioeconomic characteristics. Methods This population-based cross-sectional study included 978 children, with a subsample of 315 undergoing biochemical assessment. Data were collected on dietary intake, eating and sedentary behaviours, physical activity, anthropometry, blood pressure, and biochemical markers. A composite cardiometabolic risk outcome was constructed and assessed only in the biochemical subsample. Analyses accounted for the complex sampling design. Results Among children included in the biochemical subsample, 89.9% presented at least one cardiometabolic risk factor and dyslipidaemia was present in 72.0%. In the full sample, overweight was observed in 30.2% of the children. Eating with distractions was associated with higher odds of cardiometabolic risk burden, increasing the likelihood of one to two risk factors (odds ratio = 2.98; 95% confidence interval: 1.62–5.47) and three or more risk factors (odds ratio = 2.52; 95% confidence interval:1.08–5.90). Consuming snacks or treats, compared with a homemade meal, was associated with lower odds of presenting one to two risk factors (odds ratio = 0.32; 95% confidence interval: 0.10–0.99), but no association was observed with three or more risk factors. Conclusions Within the non-random biochemical subsample of morning-shift students, a high burden of cardiometabolic risk factors was observed, and eating with distractions was associated with greater cardiometabolic risk burden. Early preventive strategies targeting modifiable behaviours are needed.

articles.title: Chickpea flour (Cicer arietinum L) improves viability of potentially probiotics Lactobacillus plantarum S180.7 and Lactobacillus plantarum SBR64.7 in milk-based formulations
articles.abstract: This study evaluated the effect of adding chickpea flour to milk-based formulations on physicochemical parameters, the survival, and viability of potentially probiotic microorganisms. Four formulations were prepared using skimmed milk (10%) and sucrose (10%), each containing Lactobacillus plantarum S180.7 (CF1) or L. plantarum SBR64.7 (CF2), with or without 4.5% chickpea flour (TF1 and TF2). Composition, physicochemical properties, total phenolic content, antioxidant activity, and bacterial viability were assessed during 24 hours of fermentation and 28 days of storage at 4°C. Formulations with chickpea flour exhibited a greater pH decrease (ΔpH, 24–0 h: TF1 = –1.81 and TF2 = –1.38) than controls (CF1 = –0.58 and CF2 = –0.52), along with higher titratable acidity after 6 and 9 hours, respectively. Chickpea flour enhanced bacterial growth, reaching 8 Log CFU/mL, and increased phenolic content without affecting antioxidant potential. Viability remained stable and higher than controls, confirming improved probiotic stability in milk-based formulations.

articles.title: Clinical and economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to peripheral artery disease in Italy: A nationwide analysis
articles.abstract: Peripheral artery disease (PAD) represents a major cause of non-traumatic lower-limb amputation and is associated with substantial morbidity, mortality, and healthcare costs. Despite advances in medical and revascularization therapies, major amputations remain frequent, and comprehensive nationwide estimates of their clinical and hospital-related economic burden within the Italian National Health Service (SSN) are limited. The objectives of this study were to estimate the hospital-related economic burden of major lower-limb amputations attributable to PAD in Italy and to assess revascularization patterns and in-hospital mortality within the SSN. We conducted a nationwide observational study using the Italian National Hospital Discharge Database. Acute hospital discharges between 2015 and 2021 with a major lower-limb amputation and Diagnosis Related Group 113 were identified. Inpatient volumes, length of stay, and costs were estimated by amputation level. A longitudinal cohort of patients amputated between 2015 and 2017 was followed for two years before and after the index hospitalization to assess prior revascularization and in-hospital mortality using age- and sex-adjusted Cox models. A total of 26,417 PAD-attributable major amputations were identified, 75.6% of which were above-knee procedures. Cumulative inpatient expenditure reached €294 million, corresponding to over 511,000 hospital days. Only 46.0% of patients underwent revascularization before amputation. In-hospital mortality increased steeply within the first six months post-amputation and remained higher after above-knee procedures and among patients with diabetes, reaching 16–25% at 180 days and 23–34% at two years. Major lower-limb amputation remains a severe and costly outcome of PAD in Italy. Improved implementation of guideline-recommended PAD management is needed to reduce avoidable amputations and their economic burden on the SSN.

articles.title: Cytokine profiles of aqueous humor from sequential bilateral cataract surgery: Impact of diabetes on inflammatory responses
articles.abstract: We investigated aqueous humor (AH) cytokine profiles in first- and second-operated eyes of patients undergoing sequential bilateral cataract surgery and explored these profiles according to diabetes mellitus (DM) status. This retrospective, within-subject, comparative observational study included 71 patients, comprising 39 without DM and 32 with DM but without diabetic retinopathy, who underwent uneventful sequential bilateral cataract surgery within a 2-week interval. The concentrations of vascular endothelial growth factor, angiopoietin-2, placental growth factor, interleukin (IL)-6, IL-8, monocyte chemoattractant protein-1 (MCP-1), and transforming growth factor–β2 (TGF-β2) in the AH were analyzed. In patients without DM, mean IL-6 concentrations were nominally lower in the second eye than in the first eye (P = 0.041), although this finding did not remain statistically significant after FDR adjustment. In patients with DM, there were no significant differences in cytokine concentrations between the first and second eyes. The eye-order × DM interaction for IL-6 was not statistically significant (P = 0.644). Compared with patients without DM, higher MCP-1 and TGF-β2 concentrations were observed in the first eye and higher TGF-β2 concentrations in the second eye, with the strongest statistical evidence observed for first-eye TGF-β2, which remained significant after FDR adjustment. Differences in AH cytokine profiles were observed between patients with and without DM during sequential bilateral cataract surgery. The lower mean IL-6 concentration observed in the second eyes of patients without diabetes represents a novel, although exploratory, observation. Whether this finding reflects pre-existing inter-eye variability or a biological response associated with sequential surgery remains to be determined.

Enablers and barriers to human papillomavirus vaccination implementation among key stakeholders in Ethiopia: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: Introduction Human papillomavirus (HPV) vaccination is an effective and lifesaving intervention against cervical cancer. However, achieving high, equitable, and sustainable uptake remains a significant challenge in low-resource settings, including Ethiopia. Therefore, this study aimed to explore the enablers and barriers to HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia. Methods An interpretive descriptive qualitative design was employed in purposively selected settings representing diverse socio-ecological contexts (Afar, Amhara, Addis Ababa, and Dire Dawa). Six focus group discussions were conducted with adolescent girls (n = 14), parents of eligible adolescent girls (n = 14), and community representatives (n = 14). In addition, nineteen key informant interviews (KIIs) were conducted with healthcare providers, Expanded Programme on Immunization (EPI) coordinators, and technical advisors from governmental and non-governmental organizations. Data were analysed using a combined deductive–inductive content analysis guided by the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research (CFIR 2.0). Results Multiple interacting factors influenced HPV vaccination implementation in Ethiopia, categorised as enablers and barriers across community, health system, and policy levels. Enablers included the Perceived Vaccine Attributes and Delivery Adaptability, Supportive Policy and Multisectoral Strategic Partnerships, Socio-cultural and Belief-based Drivers, and Health System Readiness and Workforce Motivation. However, several barriers limited implementation, including Suspicions About Targeting 9–14-year-old Girls and Consent-related Administrative Obstacles, Pervasive Misinformation and Cognitive Resistance, Health System Resource Constraints and Coordination Gaps, Donor Dependency Risks and Financial Sustainability Concerns, and Structural Access Constraints and Equity Gaps. Conclusions While policy shifts, external strategic partnerships, and frontline worker dedication have accelerated vaccine reach, the long-term sustainability of Ethiopia’s HPV vaccination program remains constrained by multi-level barriers. Progress toward the global 2030 cervical cancer elimination targets requires trust-building risk-communication strategies to counter fertility myths, simplified consent procedures, targeted domestic resource mobilization, and context-specific delivery models tailored to underserved pastoralist and urban sub-populations.

articles.title: Exploration of lymphoproliferative disease virus strains in wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) in Iowa, USA
articles.abstract: by Kelsey C. Smith, David Navarro, Julie A. Blanchong Wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) were nearly extirpated in the early 1900’s and extensive restoration efforts utilizing translocated wild turkeys were employed to restore populations. Although these efforts were successful, populations have again been in decline due to unknown causes. Lymphoproliferative disease virus (LPDV) was first detected in the United States in 2009. The coinciding appearance of LDPV and declining populations have led to studies in several states and provinces in North America to characterize its prevalence and distribution due to concerns about its potential role in population declines. The spread of disease agents is a common outcome during translocation programs and could be related to the spread of LPDV. Prior studies have performed phylogenetic analyses to examine genetic variation across and geographic clustering among strains. In this study we aimed to identify the diversity of LPDV strains present in wild turkeys in Iowa and if there was geographic clustering within the state or with other locations where LPDV has been detected. We sequenced a subset (n = 77) of hunter-harvested samples covering eight of the nine agricultural regions in Iowa that tested PCR positive with the viral gag gene. We performed phylogenetic analysis on 73 unique Iowan strains as well as previously catalogued strains from other regions retrieved from the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) GenBank database. Overall, Iowa strains did not show geographic clustering within the state or with any other specific geographic regions. Our study demonstrated that there is a high level of genetic diversity among LPDV strains in Iowa and did not provide evidence of connection with a particular location external to Iowa as a source of introduction of LPDV to the state.

articles.title: Female sexual dysfunction in premenopausal women with diabetes mellitus in northern Nigeria: A cross-sectional study from two tertiary hospitals examining associations with glycaemic control and reproductive hormones
articles.abstract: by Fatima M. Damagum, Amina H. Hassan, Andrew E. Uloko, Hauwa A. Habeeb, Hadiza B. Damagum, Zainab A. Umar, Hassan A. Murtala, Zainab Abdulkadir, Ibrahim Y. Ibrahim, Zainab U. Ibrahim, Umar F. Abdullahi, Hamisu M. Salihu, Muktar H. Aliyu, Phylis J. Kanki, Baba M. Musa Background Female sexual dysfunction (FSD) is a recognised complication of diabetes mellitus (DM), but evidence on its clinical and biological correlates in sub-Saharan Africa remains limited. FSD is defined as a disorder characterized by disturbances in sexual desire, arousal, orgasm, and/or pain that causes interpersonal difficulty or distress. This study examined associations between glycaemic control, reproductive hormonal status, and FSD among premenopausal women with diabetes in northern Nigeria. Methods We conducted a cross-sectional study among 180 premenopausal women aged 18–45 years attending diabetes clinics at two tertiary hospitals in Kano, Nigeria. Sexual function was assessed using the Female Sexual Function Index (FSFI), with scores ≤26 indicating FSD. Glycaemic control was measured using glycated haemoglobin (HbA1c), categorised as optimal (≤7.0%) or suboptimal (>7.0%). Reproductive hormones (FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) were measured at phase-specific points of the menstrual cycle. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to assess associations with FSD, and linear regression models were used to examine associations with FSFI domain scores. Results Overall, 51.7% of participants screened positive for FSD. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with higher odds of FSD (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 2.80; 95% CI 1.05–7.72). It was also associated with lower orgasm (β −0.77; p = 0.032) and satisfaction (β −0.88; p = 0.003) scores. No statistically significant associations were observed between reproductive hormonal imbalance (including FSH, LH, Oestrogen, testosterone, prolactin, and progesterone) and FSD or FSFI domain scores. Conclusions FSD was common among premenopausal women with diabetes in this setting. Suboptimal glycaemic control was associated with FSD and with lower orgasm and satisfaction scores, while reproductive hormonal measures were not associated with FSD. These findings provide evidence on clinical correlates of FSD in a sub-Saharan African population.

articles.title: Frontal alpha asymmetry and instructed satisfaction-rating changes after price presentation: An exploratory pilot study
articles.abstract: This exploratory pilot study asked whether frontal alpha asymmetry (FAA) recorded while a price is displayed varies with the satisfaction-rating change a consumer then makes. Twenty-one participants completed two blocks of 30 trials: view a product, give a pre-price rating (1–9), see the price, give a post-price rating, which they were instructed to change except at the scale limits. The change is described by its direction and magnitude (|Δ|, provisionally labeled Decision Momentum), two descriptions of one difference score. FAA was computed from relative alpha power at F3/F4 over 0–3 s after price onset on average-referenced data. Inference rests on 19 participants and 820 trials. The primary pooled test of the direction × magnitude interaction was inconclusive (β=−0.051, 95% CI [−0.111,0.009], p = 0.093). An exploratory block-stratified analysis found an interaction in the first block (β=−0.087, 95% CI [−0.152,−0.021], p = 0.010), although neither of its two component slopes differed clearly from zero. Support varied across specifications, and five alternative operationalizations of FAA did not reproduce it. The same model applied to the window before price onset, where the predictors cannot yet reflect the price, produced an interaction of comparable or larger size pooled and in the second block. In the first block, the direct comparison did not establish a difference between windows, and adjusting for pre-price FAA left the first-block estimate unchanged (p = 0.008); in the second block, the two windows did differ (p = 0.021), the association being present before the price and not after it. Single-trial classification of change direction showed modest performance with uncertain generalizability (ROC AUC 0.538; participant bootstrap 95% CI [0.476, 0.564]). The association is reported as hypothesis-generating; attributing it specifically to price-related processing is not supported by these data.

articles.title: Integrative network toxicology and machine learning reveal the potential role of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural in exacerbating pulmonary fibrosis
articles.abstract: Background 5-Hydroxymethylfurfural (5-HMF), a ubiquitous furan derivative formed during the thermal processing of carbohydrate-rich foods, represents a widespread dietary exposure. However, its potential contribution to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remains unclear. This study investigated the molecular links between 5-HMF and IPF using an integrated computational and experimental approach. Methods IPF-related genes were identified through transcriptomic analysis combining differential expression analysis and weighted gene co-expression network analysis. Candidate targets were obtained by intersecting IPF-associated genes with predicted 5-HMF targets. Functional enrichment analysis, ensemble machine learning, and SHAP interpretation were performed to prioritize candidate targets, while molecular docking was used to explore potential 5-HMF–target interactions. A bleomycin-induced mouse model of pulmonary fibrosis was further used to evaluate the effects of 5-HMF on fibrotic lung injury and the transcriptional expression of prioritized candidate genes. Results A total of 1,776 IPF-associated genes and 143 predicted 5-HMF targets were identified, yielding 12 overlapping candidate targets. Enrichment analysis implicated these genes in fibrosis-related pathways, including chemical carcinogenesis–receptor activation and estrogen signaling. Machine learning analysis prioritized seven core targets (CA2, CA4, ESR2, F10, HSP90AA1, PLA2G1B, and PTPRB), all of which accommodated 5-HMF in their orthosteric pockets in blind docking, albeit with weak, non-selective Vina scores (−4.5 to −5.4 kcal/mol). In vivo, 5-HMF significantly exacerbated bleomycin-induced pulmonary fibrosis, as demonstrated by aggravated lung injury, increased collagen deposition, and elevated expression of Hsp90aa1, Pla2g1b, Ca4, F10, Acta2, and Col1a1. Conclusion Our findings suggest that 5-HMF may exacerbate fibrotic lung injury through multiple fibrosis-related molecular targets and pathways. These findings provide preliminary evidence for a potential association between 5-HMF exposure and the aggravation of pulmonary fibrosis, while further studies are required to determine whether 5-HMF can independently initiate fibrotic pathology.

articles.title: Knowledge and experiences of overdose among formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and hazardous opioid use in South Africa: A qualitative study
articles.abstract: Background Drug overdose is a leading cause of death among people released from correctional facilities, and the risk of overdose is higher among people living with HIV (PLWH). Overdose remains understudied in people in South Africa despite the high burden of HIV and hazardous opioid use. The researchers aimed to qualitatively explore how formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and OUD in South Africa understand, experience, and respond to overdose. Methods People with HIV and self-reported hazardous opioid use prior to correctional facility release or shortly after release were enrolled in a convenience sample. Twenty-three formerly incarcerated people living with HIV and opioid use in or around Tshwane, South Africa completed sequential in-depth interviews that explored medication-assisted treatment for hazardous opioid use and HIV care delivery. Transcripts were analyzed thematically using both deductive and inductive coding, with a focus on participants’ knowledge and definition of overdose, personal experiences with overdose, and responses to overdose. Results All participants used the term “overdose”, but there was no unified understanding of what constitutes an overdose or how to manage an overdose. The period immediately following release from incarceration was identified as a key moment in which overdose occurred. Pouring water onto the person overdosing was reported to be the most prevalent response strategy. Only two participants contacted or watched their peers contact the ambulance. Fear of law enforcement involvement was perceived as a barrier to calling for emergency services. Conclusion The findings identify a gap in overdose knowledge among corrections-involved people living with HIV and hazardous opioid use in South Africa. There is a need to increase knowledge regarding overdose recognition and responses.

articles.title: Machine learning for predicting mortality in patients with sepsis and its associated complications: A systematic review and meta-analysis
articles.abstract: Background Sepsis remains a leading cause of death in intensive care units worldwide and may be accompanied by complex complications, including encephalopathy, coagulopathy, acute kidney injury, myocardial dysfunction, and delirium, each of which substantially increases the risk of poor outcomes. Machine learning, a promising approach for prognostic prediction, can capture complex nonlinear relationships among clinical risk factors. However, its predictive performance in sepsis and its specific complications remains unclear. Method We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library for relevant literature through April 2026. Studies that aimed to develop or validate machine learning models to predict mortality in adult patients with sepsis and its associated complications were included. The random-effects or bivariate model was used to calculate the AUC, sensitivity, and specificity. Results Overall, machine learning models show moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis, with a combined AUC of 0.82 for the training set (46 studies, 15 models) and 0.79 for the validation set (50 studies, 25 models). Logistic regression is the most widely evaluated model, demonstrating stable performance (validation AUC = 0.81). Integrated methods, including random forest and XGBoost, performed equally well, with AUCs between 0.81 and 0.83 in both groups. Although LightGBM and DL-CMT achieved the highest AUCs in the training and validation sets, respectively, both estimates were based on a single study.Among the complications, the evidence for sepsis-associated encephalopathy (AUC = 0.81, 3 studies) and sepsis-induced coagulopathy (AUC = 0.80, 4 studies) is the most conclusive and best demonstrated. Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury showed moderate and stable performance (validation AUC = 0.79, 4 studies). Sepsis-induced cardiomyopathy showed significant attenuation from training to validation (AUC 0.84 vs 0.78, all from a single study), and random forest performed well in training (AUC = 0.98) but was not widely reported. Septic shock reached the highest AUC (0.95), but this was based on a single study. The predictive utility of sepsis-associated delirium is limited (AUC = 0.67, 1 study), and sepsis-induced myocardial injury is moderate (AUC = 0.77, 1 study).For long-term mortality, evidence is extremely lacking. Only SAE (AUC 0.88 during training and 0.86 during validation) and SCRS (combined AUC 0.76) provided single study estimates, ruling out reliable conclusions. Conclusion In this meta-analysis, machine learning models showed moderate predictive performance for short-term mortality in sepsis. Among complications, SAE and SIC had the strongest evidence and best performance, whereas SAD showed limited utility. Evidence for long-term mortality was extremely scarce. These findings support the potential role of machine learning in early prognostic risk stratification, yet they also highlight the urgent need for rigorous external validation and higher-quality studies, particularly for under-investigated complications.

articles.title: Perceived quality teaching and student retention intention: The serial mediation of knowledge, skills, competencies, and student loyalty
articles.abstract: Student retention intention remains a concern for higher education systems worldwide and is relevant to institutional sustainability and Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4). Drawing on Human Capital Theory (HCT) and Expectancy–Value Theory (EVT), this study examines the direct and indirect associations between perceived quality teaching and student retention intention through students’ self-reported knowledge, skills, competencies and student loyalty. Cross-sectional survey data were collected from 395 final-year students across Pakistani universities using a multistage sampling approach, with institutions selected through stratified random sampling and participants recruited via convenience sampling. The proposed relationships were examined using structural equation modeling with SmartPLS 4. The results indicate that perceived quality teaching is positively associated with student retention intention, both directly and indirectly through students’ knowledge, skills, and competencies and student loyalty. Significant indirect associations were identified through each mediator separately and through the proposed serial mediation pathway. These findings highlight the relevance of considering students’ perceived capability development and institutional attachment together when examining retention intention. HCT provides a rationale for the relationship between perceived teaching quality and students’ knowledge, skills, competencies, while EVT offers an interpretive perspective; however, expectancy of success and subjective task value were not directly measured. The cross-sectional design also precludes conclusions about temporal ordering or causality. Practically, the findings suggest that faculty development, student-centered pedagogies, digitally supported teaching, and curriculum alignment with labor market needs merit consideration in institutional quality assurance. The findings provide context-specific evidence from Pakistani higher education (HE) and are relevant to SDG 4 through their focus on perceived teaching quality and students’ intentions to continue their studies. They do not establish effects on actual retention or broader educational outcomes.

articles.title: Multisensing photoreceptors: a cross-kingdom perspective
articles.abstract: Photoreceptors are classically depicted as monochromatic switches governed strictly by light. However, emerging biophysical and structural insights reveal that these proteins act as dynamic, multisensory hubs across kingdoms of life. Drawing primarily on plant and fungal systems, where mechanisms are most extensively characterized, this review synthesizes how photoreceptors integrate ambient temperature and cellular oxidative state alongside photon flux, with cross-kingdom examples extending this framework to bacteria. Thermal energy modulates dark reversion rates, quaternary assembly, and photobody phase separation, whereas reactive oxygen species alter the photocycle and trigger structural shifts through direct redox sensing. Under a ‘stress-first’ evolutionary model, ancestral stress-sensing scaffolds could be retrofitted with chromophores via exaptation, providing a unified biophysical rationale for how cells decode complex, fluctuating environments.

articles.title: Lessons from the UN Decade: from ecosystem restoration to regenerative transformation
articles.abstract: Although restoration science increasingly considers social–ecological complexity, many restoration projects still fall short of their ecological or social goals. We argue that such failures often stem from a lack of attention to long-term social–ecological dynamics within the target system. To overcome this problem, we propose ‘regenerative transformation’ as a new paradigm to guide ecosystem restoration. Regenerative transformation foregrounds the thriving of human and other forms of life and emphasizes healthy endogenous social–ecological dynamics rather than exogenous interventions. Facilitating regenerative transformation through restoration will require changes in how restoration is conceptualized, practiced, and governed—moving from a focus on abstract targets and simple outcome indicators toward developing supportive conditions for the long-term, equitable coevolution of healthy social–ecological dynamics.

articles.title: A Cross-Domain Matrix Engine for Signal Processing and Deep Neural Net Inference
articles.abstract: Matrix multiplication dominates both PHY signal processing and Deep Neural Network (DNN) inference, yet these domains place opposing demands on the matrix engine. Signal processing requires low-latency execution of relatively small matrix operations, whereas DNN inference, particularly at large batch sizes, prioritizes high throughput and energy efficiency for large matrix multiplications. While offering efficient memory access profile, a Systolic Array (SA) adds fill and drain delays per matrix. Those can be amortized for large matrices but not for small matrices. Conversely, a tensor unit completes the kernel in few cycles but would require repeated reads of same operand tiles over large matrices. This makes SA too slow for signal processing and tensor too inefficient for AI. We show that this need not be a choice between systolic and tensor structuring of Multiply-Accumulate (MAC) units. We propose a single engine that operates primarily as a SA and, through low-cost reconfiguration, transforms into a tensor-style engine on a per-operation basis. MUXes create both the spatial reduction adder tree and temporal reduction accumulators from the existing MACs and registers within the systolic array. The proposed reconfigurable SA simulated using modified SCALESim simulator, verified on an Zynq 702 FPGA and synthesized using ASAP 7nm FinFET library. SCALE-Sim simulations shows up to 7.5x lower latency for small complex value PHY kernels. Even on DNN workloads, it achieves up to 1.65x speedups over vanilla SA execution with trivial increase of memory accesses, retaining the systolic array's memory access advantage. Synthesis results estimate reconfigurable fabric costs only 8% power and 13.6% area overheads.

articles.title: A Hybrid Visitor Prediction Framework using Interpretable Temporal features, Integrating IQR and Anomaly Detection in Lakes in Nebraska
articles.abstract: For effective resource management, infrastructure planning, and sustainable tourism, it is really important to predict accurate visitors. This paper estimates the daily visitation of Nebraska lakes using spatial, basic temporal, and interpretable temporal features. Moreover, we evaluate the base models with multiple metrics. Using the best three models, our method will ensemble hybrid models and choose the best hybrid technique. Further, we investigate the impact of lag features and how the models work with different outlier detection techniques such as Interquartile Range (IQR) and anomaly detection. The models are evaluated using regression metrics (MAE, MSE, RMSE, MAPE, and R2). Experiment results show that, after removing anomalies, MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE are reduced. Adding lag features also shows some positive effects on the results. Moreover, anomaly detection techniques perform better than IQR in improving performance while preserving data. The reported anomaly-based cross-validation results favored the voting ensemble over the compared base models on the evaluated metrics. In anomaly-based cross-validation, VOTE improved prediction errors compared with MLP (256,128,64); improvements varied in the single-split comparison. Specifically, the hybrid model reduced MAE by 9.82%, MSE by 3.12%, RMSE by 1.76%, and MAPE by 6.77%. In the reported cross-validation comparison, the best anomaly-based hybrid model had lower MAE, MSE, RMSE, and MAPE than the best IQR-based hybrid model by 9.81%, 34.30%, 18.99%, and 0.66%, respectively.

articles.title: A Scaling Theory of Multi-Epoch Pretraining: Late-Time Overfitting and Ensembling
articles.abstract: In the near future language model pretraining will become bound by total data rather than total compute. Such a regime requires revisiting scaling laws and scaling law theory. Motivated by prior works that have found utility in ensembling, we study how the number of training epochs and ensemble size jointly shape generalization when training data are fixed. In language-model experiments on FineWeb, logit averaging reduces late-training deterioration, delays optimal stopping, and can outperform wider or deeper single models at matched parameter-token budgets over a common training horizon. To analyze this interaction between data reuse and ensembling, we derive a dynamical mean-field theory (DMFT) for multi-epoch stochastic gradient descent in power-law random-feature ensembles, tracking error correlations across epochs and models. Ensembling reduces the prediction variance responsible for late-time growth in expected test error, changing the optimal stopping time. We use these stopping times to derive compute-allocation laws at fixed data and individual model sizes. Under this allocation, ensemble size grows with compute at least as fast as training time per member, while excess test loss above the limiting loss decreases as a power of compute.

articles.title: An Agentic Framework for Automated Power System Studies and Grid Connection Assessment
articles.abstract: Connecting new generation and demand to the grid depends on two scarce skills: checking applications against a large, changing body of regulation, and running the network studies that decide where and how a project connects. We present Grid Agents, an AI system that brings both together, and the methodology we use to evaluate it. The Grid Ontology is its knowledge system. It represents the regulation, standards and engineering knowledge that grid work depends on, makes it searchable, and evolves as the agents learn from use. Every answer drawn from it rests on evidence the agents cite. Grid Studio is an agent system specialised for power-system engineering. It works in its own engineering environment with domain tools and a study framework, draws on the Grid Ontology, and relies on established solvers for every number it reports. In both, engineers make the decisions. We bring eight published power-system benchmark families, previously scattered across separate papers, into one suite of 519 tasks, and we verify not only each answer but the work behind it, by replaying the agent's tool calls. The Grid Ontology cites the right regulatory evidence more often than a general coding agent or retrieval pipelines, leads on LegalBench-RAG and ranks first on the public leaderboards of the Enterprise RAG Challenge and ViDoRe V3. Grid Studio scores highest on the 519 power-system tasks and is the fastest of all the systems we compare, both by a statistically significant margin. With an optimiser in the loop, its reinforcement packages cost 33-67% less on average than those the agent designs alone.

articles.title: Ask, Don't Equip: Question-Driven Coding Agents for Deep Kernel Optimization
articles.abstract: LLM agents for GPU kernel optimization sit at two ends of a structure-freedom tradeoff. Scripted agents fix what the model does at each step, via a learned policy, an optimization menu, or fixed roles, and are sample-efficient where the recipe applies and stall where it does not. Open-ended agents let a self-directed model mutate a population of kernels and pay for the freedom in trials: thousands of evaluations, repeated edits, and wrong candidates. Both respond to hard targets by equipping the agent with more: parsed profiler output, disassembly analysis, retrieval over documentation and libraries, and stores of lessons. We argue that both lack direction, a hypothesis about where the remaining gap is, and that a short question asked at the right moment supplies it without narrowing what the agent may do next. We present KernelSeek, a question-driven agent that makes an existing CUDA kernel faster with no operator-specific knowledge and no faster implementation to imitate: a general-purpose coding agent, a minimal harness that enforces a verifiable goal, and questions at decision points, first from a human, then from a bank the agent applies to itself. On the same task, evaluator, hardware, and week, a tool-rich autonomous agent built in the prevailing style plateaued at 0.50x FlashAttention-3 after 133 model-driven steps; KernelSeek reached 1.13x. It then produced dependency-free FlashAttention forward kernels for Hopper and Blackwell, single CUDA files with no CUTLASS, CuTe, cuBLAS, or cuDNN, correct on all 182 scenarios per architecture and 1.16x FlashAttention-3 and 1.46x FlashAttention-4 (geometric mean). Across 162 human messages and 11.5K agent tool calls, every large gain followed a question that moved the agent to a different layer of the system or rejected a claimed limit, never one that supplied information. We release the kernels, harness, question bank, and all traces.

articles.title: BISECT: Bilevel Spectral Decomposition for Low-Rank Continual Learning
articles.abstract: Exemplar-free continual learning on pre-trained Vision Transformers increasingly relies on Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA), yet prevailing methods govern the low-rank update space through strict subspace isolation. By projecting each incoming task into the approximate null space of historical token activations, isolation-based learners equate any cross-task feature overlap with catastrophic interference. We show that this orthogonality premise induces a structural bottleneck we term \emph{spectral starvation}: when down-projection bases are locked before task optimization, the gradient norm reaching the trainable up-projection is upper-bounded by the energy of current-task features captured by the chosen basis. Because natural visual tasks share low- and mid-level covariance structure, historical null tails contain barely $5.5\%$ of incoming task variance, starving new-class plasticity while blocking positive consolidation along shared directions. We propose BISECT (Bilevel Spectral Decomposition), a continual LoRA framework that partitions a fixed rank-$r$ budget into two orthogonal functional blocks: an invariant carrier spanned by the dominant modes of the joint historical-and-current Gram matrix, and a novelty complement extracted via generalized Rayleigh whitening followed by orthogonal complement projection. After single-task training, BISECT folds both blocks back into the frozen backbone using a closed-form precision gate that scales each rank-1 invariant atom by its current-to-joint Rayleigh ratio while preserving novelty atoms at unit gain. Across eight incremental settings on ImageNet-R, ImageNet-A, CIFAR-100, CUB-200, and DomainNet, BISECT outperforms prompt, adapter, and LoRA baselines with zero extra inference parameters or FLOPs, and remains complementary to sparse analytic expansion.

articles.title: Benchmark Prediction with Sparse and Unpaired Cached Responses
articles.abstract: Evaluating a generative model on all queries from all available benchmark tasks is prohibitively expensive. As such, models are often evaluated on different subsets of tasks and/or different subsets of queries from a given task. The resulting collection of responses and the corresponding (model, task) score matrix are sparse and unpaired. In this paper, we introduce the Product Kernel Perspective Space (PKPS), a collection of low-dimensional representations of models based on their embedded responses. PKPS generalizes existing methods for representing black-box generative models by comparing responses to similar -- rather than just identical -- queries and is therefore able to utilize sparse and unpaired information. Theoretically, we show that benchmark prediction using PKPS is query-efficient relative to methods that only use information from dense and paired portions of the evaluation data. Empirically, we show that PKPS-based methods outperform baselines on benchmark prediction across two large benchmark suites.

articles.title: Can AI Do Formal Demography? Why Vaccinating the Oldest Saves Both the Most Lives and the Most Years of Life
articles.abstract: Can AI contribute to formal demography? We report an experiment in which an AI model, Claude, was asked to explain and then simplify the proof of an earlier result: that vaccinating the oldest against COVID-19 saves both the most lives and the most years of life, because the years saved per person treated rise with age. The model proposed a new proof that is shorter, more intuitive, and somewhat more general than the original, built from a known life-table identity and the definition of convexity. It states the condition for the result as the convexity of the reciprocal of the hazard, which can be checked from the hazard alone and holds for most familiar parametric models, and it yields a lower bound on life expectancy whenever that condition is met. Prompted by a further question, the model also gave an exact form of the condition, showing how far convexity can be relaxed. The model traced these identities and related results in earlier literature. An edited record of the sessions is provided, and complete transcripts are available on request. The exercise suggests that AI can revisit established results, make them easier to understand, and prove valuable generalizations.

articles.title: Can LLM Agents Be Forward-Deployed Engineers? Requirement Discovery and Delivery for Enterprise Text-to-SQL
articles.abstract: LLM coding agents can increasingly automate model post-training, but whether they can act as forward-deployed engineer (FDE) agents, discovering customer requirements and turning them into deployment decisions, remains unclear. We study this on a real enterprise text-to-SQL engagement: a simulated customer, grounded in the real use case's requirements, starts with an ambiguous request. An agent must discover acceptance criteria, data permissions, and hardware constraints in the discovery phase, then plan and execute a post-training recipe in the delivery phase. Across 15 models, the strongest discover over 80% of withheld requirements and open-weight models discover 40-50%; in the delivery phase, only 25% of runs across eight coding-agent configurations pass all acceptance criteria. We identify four bottlenecks in this engagement: (1) incomplete discovery, with 40% of withheld requirements missing or misrepresented; (2) unreliable execution; (3) underused compute budgets and a lack of systematic comparisons across base models and post-training methods; and (4) benchmark accuracy does not guarantee production readiness. We suggest human review of discovered requirements, monitoring of the agent's plan during execution, and an explicit experiment-environment specification covering hardware, budget scope, and production checks.

articles.title: Can LLM Agents Improve Imperfect Earth System Model Parameterizations?
articles.abstract: Earth system models (ESMs) rely on parameterizations to represent unresolved processes such as convection, cloud microphysics, and turbulence. However, translating advances in physical understanding into stable, validated parameterizations and integrating them into ESMs often takes years. Agentic AI could accelerate this process and enable more systematic exploration of design choices. Using warm-rain collision-coalescence as a test case, we evaluate agents' ability to synthesize scientific literature, reimplement published bulk parameterizations, and propose new functional forms as differentiable JAX code. We compare conventional parameterizations, data-driven emulators, and agent-generated closures against high-fidelity superdroplet simulations, repeating unattended experiments across ten language models. With expert guidance or iterative feedback, agents produced executable, differentiable, mass-conserving code, although unattended performance depended strongly on the scheme and language model. Iterative feedback lowered median rollout error for eight of ten models. Retuned physical schemes matched or outperformed many learned parameterizations at substantially lower computational cost, but two of 100 unattended agent-generated closures achieved slightly lower rain-mass error than the most accurate retuned scheme on held-out simulations.

articles.title: Contrastive Adapter Training and Consensus Knowledge Distillation for Multi-Source-Free Domain Adaptation in Skin Cancer Diagnosis
articles.abstract: Skin cancer diagnosis, particularly differentiating melanoma from benign nevi, is challenging due to the visual similarity between lesions. Although convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and vision transformers (ViTs) have shown promising performance, their effectiveness often deteriorates on data from heterogeneous clinical sources. Conventional domain adaptation methods address domain shift but require access to source data during adaptation, which is often infeasible due to privacy regulations. Multi-source-free unsupervised domain adaptation (MSFDA) addresses this limitation by leveraging multiple labeled source domains to generalize to an unlabeled target domain without requiring access to source data. However, existing MSFDA methods rely on full backbone fine-tuning, leading to catastrophic forgetting and overfitting on small clinical datasets, and address domain shift at the aggregation stage without establishing a shared domain-invariant feature space. Furthermore, their reliance on hard pseudo-labels or confidence-weighted aggregation introduces noisy supervision signals under domain shift. To address these limitations, we propose CAT-CKD, consisting of two components: (1) contrastive adapter training (CAT), which trains lightweight ConvPass adapters within a frozen ViT backbone using supervised contrastive learning (SCL) to establish a shared domain-invariant feature space before source-specific model training, and (2) consensus knowledge distillation (CKD), which aggregates logits from multiple source models into a consensus supervisory signal and adapts a student model on unlabeled target data using KL divergence. Experiments on five publicly available skin lesion datasets show that CAT-CKD achieves an average AUROC of 86.1%, outperforming existing MSFDA methods while requiring only 4.3M trainable parameters. The code is available at https://github.com/A-Abedi/CAT_CKD.

articles.title: D&A: Decoupling Description and Assessment Enables VLMs as Zero-Shot Robotic Reward Models
articles.abstract: Vision-Language Models (VLMs) hold promise for zero-shot video task-progress estimation in robot learning, yet existing frameworks frequently suffer from confirmation bias, hallucinating progress in failed executions due to implicit success assumptions or relative temporal ranking designs. Naive prompting of frontier models collapses into a binary success detector that fails to capture nuanced, non-linear progress and failures. While post-training approaches can mitigate this through explicit training, they demand expensive real-world robotics data and require computationally intensive post-training for every individual base model. To resolve these limitations, we introduce D&A (Describe & Assess): our approach decouples progress estimation into an objective, task-grounded textual description of scene dynamics followed by an assessment phase using explicit rubrics. By compelling the VLM to synthesize an explicit, text-based definition of absolute success before scoring, the framework anchors evaluations to an external, global criterion rather than the video's internal timeline. Empirical results demonstrate that our method calibrates zero-shot estimates and mitigates confirmation bias, providing fine-grained, partial progress metrics that accurately penalize failed executions while correctly interpolating successful runs. Being purely prompt-based, D&A generalizes across tasks, embodiments, and benchmarks---matching or surpassing post-trained reward models---and its reward estimates enable efficient downstream reinforcement learning.

articles.title: DiabAgent: Toward Agentic Physiological Control
articles.abstract: As pretraining scales, medical language models have advanced rapidly in clinical question answering. Their ability to achieve effective physiological control through sustained intervention still lacks systematic quantitative evaluation. Type 1 diabetes provides a concrete setting: impaired insulin secretion creates dependence on exogenous insulin, with dosing continually adjusted using information about meals, exercise, illness, and glucose measurements. We introduce DiabAgent, a research suite for agentic physiological control comprising the Agentic Physiological Control (APC) framework, the DiabetSim simulator, and the SweetBench benchmark. APC controls glucose through medical-device tools, using ongoing observations to infer individual states, accumulate personal experience, and choose treatment actions. We build DiabetSim to simulate different patients, events, and device conditions for scalable virtual testing and training. Using DiabetSim, we construct SweetBench by instantiating 32 scenario designs as 212 glucose-control tasks. With Claude Opus 5.5 and a fixed decision interval of one hour, APC achieves a COGI of 73.5, compared with 71.2 for the open-source closed-loop baseline OpenAPS. Ablations further show that individual adaptation and contextual information improve glucose control. Combining high-frequency rule-based control with lower-frequency agent decisions shows potential for balancing control performance and computational cost. Our work provides a framework, simulator, and evaluation foundation for agents to participate in human physiological control.

articles.title: DistDebug-Bench: Can LLM Agents Diagnose Bugs in Distributed Systems?
articles.abstract: LLM agents show strong potential in software engineering tasks such as competitive programming and code synthesis. Existing benchmarks, however, largely focus on small-scale settings such as self-contained Python modules, leaving distributed systems, an essential class of production software, under-examined. We introduce DistDebug-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating agents' ability to diagnose complex-system failures at the code level. It curates 120 high-quality real-world bugs from 11 widely used distributed systems, spanning 5 programming languages and 10 failure patterns. Through an extensive evaluation of state-of-the-art LLMs and agents, we identify substantial gaps between current agents and real-world debugging tasks. A recurring gap is tunnel vision due to a lack of explicit reasoning structure and nondeterminism from inconsistent tool-use scope. The benchmark and evaluator are available at https://github.com/OrderLab/distdebug-bench, with agent traces and a leaderboard at https://distdebug.com.

articles.title: DynaSolver: A Neural Operator for Autoregressive 4D Flow Prediction with Dynamic Boundaries
articles.abstract: Neural operators provide efficient surrogates for computational fluid dynamics (CFD), but most are designed for static geometries and are not equipped to model unsteady flows induced by continuously moving boundaries.
