These results demonstrate a post-fabrication tuning knob based on externally applied control fields for the dynamics of the many-emitter ensemble.

articles.title: Inhomogeneous Synthetic Fluxes in Optical Lattices
articles.abstract: Synthetic gauge fields in optical lattices are usually engineered to realize a uniform magnetic flux. Here, we propose a scheme to generate spatially inhomogeneous fluxes and demonstrate how such fluxes reshape the single-particle spectrum. Within Wannier--Stark-assisted tunneling, onsite modulation produces a plaquette flux that depends on the orientation of the static tilt, whereas laser-assisted tunneling (LAT) does not. Using LAT, two coherent Raman processes with different momentum transfers imprint a dimerized Peierls phase that alternates the flux between neighboring plaquettes of a square lattice while keeping the mean flux fixed. A bond-selective Raman phase extends the scheme to the kagome lattice, where a parameter $ξ$ redistributes the flux between triangles and hexagons at fixed flux per unit cell. The Hofstadter--Rammal spectrum of the bipartite square lattice retains chiral symmetry for all $ξ$, whereas the kagome lattice lacks this symmetry, and its flux periodicity and reflection symmetries survive only at special values of $ξ$. As $ξ$ is reduced, the anomalous Landau levels of the kagome singular flat band are compressed toward the flat-band energy and evolve into a degenerate zero-energy manifold at $ξ=0$ with compactly localized states. The dynamical structure factor, accessible through Bragg scattering, resolves this evolution as a Rydberg-like series of peaks whose spectral span tracks the width of the anomalous-level tower and vanishes as $ξ\to0$. We discuss the frequency resolution and temperature required for its observation.

articles.title: Internal friction and frequency-dependent conductivity in the bivariate site energy model for the mixed alkali effect in glasses
articles.abstract: The mixed alkali effect is fundamental to understanding ion transport in glasses. It manifests itself in strong changes of various ionic transport properties when one type of ion is successively replaced by another type. Recently, we have developed a new theory of thermally activated hopping in bivariate random site energy landscapes that takes into account site occupation statistics according to generalized Fermi distributions and mixture kinetics in accordance with linear irreversible thermodynamics. The theory was successfully applied to predict the behavior of partial conductivities and their activation energies at low frequencies corresponding to the dc limit. Here we show that the theory is capable to capture the salient features of the mixed alkali effect observed in ac ion conductivities and in the peculiar behavior of the internal friction.

articles.title: Magnetic field as a tuning knob for edge mode interaction in integer quantum Hall interferometers
articles.abstract: The quantum Hall interferometer has been shown to be a powerful tool for probing both the nature of the chiral modes present at the edges of these systems and the interactions between them. Strong inter-edge mode interactions can lead the system into a regime where the period of the interferometer signal corresponds to an insertion of a half-quantum flux h/2e, rather than the standard flux quantum h/e. Using a highly tunable bilayer graphene device, we are able to measure the prevalence of both the h/e-period and the doubled-frequency regimes as a function of magnetic field, providing insight into the microscopic nature of the doubling mechanism. Furthermore, we are able to push our device to a regime where double-frequency oscillations coexist with a superimposed period-h/e pattern associated with the inner chiral modes farther from the edge. We argue that this regime has a natural interpretation in a picture of the frequency doubling being caused by strong capacitive couplings between the edge modes.

articles.title: Maximal correlation and optimal transformations of probability distributions in tensor-train format: a variational algorithm
articles.abstract: The correlation between two subsystems $A$ and $B$ of a many-body system is usually measured through a pair of observables chosen in advance. The Hirschfeld-Gebelein-Rényi maximal correlation removes the choice: it is the largest correlation coefficient between any function of the configuration of $A$ and any function of the configuration of $B$, and the two functions that reach it, the optimal transformations, are the observables that carry the correlation. Both follow from a singular value decomposition (SVD) of the joint distribution normalized by its marginals, a matrix whose dimension is the number of configurations. We show that this SVD can be computed variationally for a classical distribution of discrete variables, such as the Boltzmann distribution of a spin model, given in the tensor-train (matrix-product) format, without ever forming the matrix. The optimal transformations are sought as tensor trains; each step updates a single core in closed form, and the inverse of a small matrix contracted from the distribution and the remaining cores performs the division by the marginals core by core. Every iterate is a feasible pair, so the objective is a lower bound on the maximal correlation that increases monotonically, and the cost grows linearly with the number of variables. The algorithm reproduces the exact SVD on small systems, recovers the known nonlinear optimal transformations of synthetic distributions of up to ten angular variables ($10^{15}$ configurations), and, for the bipartite antiferromagnetic model with $2^{32}$ configurations, returns an optimal transformation that is a function of the group magnetization, linear above the transition and sign-like below it: the staggered order parameter is read off from the distribution instead of being postulated.

articles.title: Mechano-chemical control of enzymatic activity in crowded environments
articles.abstract: Macromolecular crowding has long been known to alter biochemical equilibria and enzyme kinetics, with reported catalytic activities that may increase, decrease, or vary non-monotonically with crowder concentration. Classical Michaelis--Menten kinetics does not by itself identify which of these responses should occur for a conformationally active enzyme. Here, we develop a minimal non-equilibrium mechano-chemical theory for a fueled enzyme embedded in a bath of passive crowders and uncover a fluctuation-induced effective force dipole acting on the enzyme subunits, akin to a generalized form of dispersion or depletion interaction. Since the preferred conformation of the model enzyme varies through the catalytic cycle, the fluctuation-induced mechanical load affects the relevant kinetic activation barriers and is sufficient to produce both monotonic inhibition and non-monotonic modification of turnover. The framework provides a thermodynamically consistent route for linking crowded environments to catalytic currents, suggesting how mechanical design principles could be leveraged to control enzymatic pathways.

articles.title: Membrane particle wrapping across methods and shapes
articles.abstract: Understanding the passive wrapping of adhesive particles by lipid membranes is a crucial step in untangling more complex endocytotic processes. However, despite the variety of computational approaches used to study passive endocytosis, a direct comparison of results across different modeling methods has never been performed. In this work, we present a comparative analysis of three distinct frameworks: numerical solutions of the axisymmetric membrane shape equation, a particle-based molecular dynamics model (MesoMem), and an energy-based triangulated surface model (FreeDTS). First, we validated our numerical solver for spherical particles against established literature and extended the implementation to include closed vesicle membranes and non-spherical particles. Next, we studied the same system with our two simulation methods, and found that the phase plots obtained from our numerical solution agree with those from our simulations. We then extended our study to anisotropic particles. By tracking engulfment pathways in MesoMem and FreeDTS, we observed a dynamic rotational transition where non-spherical particles initially bind in a horizontal ('submarine') orientation and subsequently rotate to a vertical ('rocket') orientation to complete wrapping - a behavior impossible to capture with standard axisymmetric models. Lastly, we considered the wrapping of soft vesicles with FreeDTS. Our simulations of a deformable, fixed-connectivity particle show that stronger adhesion promotes wrapping, whereas increasing membrane tension suppresses it. Complete engulfment is accompanied by a substantial reduction in particle volume, suggesting that particle compressibility provides an additional pathway for wrapping.

articles.title: Microscopic Origin of the Equation of Motion for Open Thermodynamic Systems
articles.abstract: In my previous work (arXiv:2609.07810) \cite{Aydiner_2026}, I derived a second-order equation of motion for open thermodynamic systems from the First Law of Thermodynamics and established its dynamical equivalence with mechanical oscillators and electrical RLC circuits. In the present study, I independently recover the same mathematical structure of the equation of motion from a mesoscopic model of particle transfer between two reservoirs connected by a channel. Starting from collective momentum balance, particle conservation, and reservoir chemical-potential response, I derive the inertial--dissipative--restoring dynamics and obtain explicit expressions for its effective coefficients in terms of the physical parameters of the system. The resulting equation predicts distinct damping regimes, characteristic relaxation time scales, and resonance under periodic driving. The natural frequency and resonance conditions are explicitly determined by the physical parameters of the particle-transfer system. In the slow-transport limit, the model recovers the conventional Onsager-type linear flux--force relation. The independent emergence of the same dynamical structure from two distinct physical approaches provides theoretical support for the previously proposed thermodynamic equation of motion. By identifying the physical mechanisms underlying its effective coefficients, the present study strengthens the physical foundations of the proposed framework and supports the possibility of describing open thermodynamic systems within a common dynamical framework shared with mechanical and electrical systems.

articles.title: Multiple windows of eigenstate-selective delocalization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice
articles.abstract: We investigate localization in a non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattice with a real quasiperiodic onsite potential of strength $W$ and a staggered imaginary quasiperiodic modulation of strength $λ$. Using the inverse participation ratio (IPR), normalized participation ratio (NPR), fractal dimension $D_2$, transfer-matrix Lyapunov exponent, and wave-packet dynamics, we find a strongly non-monotonic and state-dependent response. At fixed $λ$, varying $W$ yields two distinct delocalization windows, whereas varying $λ$ at fixed $W$ produces a single re-entrant delocalization window. These regimes arise within selected eigenstate sectors, where localized states coexist with extended or critical states, leading to mobility-edge-like behavior. The corresponding suppression of the Lyapunov exponent and enhancement of the dynamical RMS spreading are consistent with the IPR, NPR, and $D_2$ results. Finite-size scaling confirms the persistence of the re-entrant features, while the complex-energy spectrum resolves their state-selective structure. The resulting phase boundaries delineate distinct localization regimes in the $(W,λ)$ plane. Our results show that the interplay between quasiperiodicity and a staggered non-Hermitian modulation sharing the same quasiperiodic spatial structure can generate re-entrant, state-dependent localization, with implications for localization and dynamics in non-Hermitian quasiperiodic lattices.

articles.title: Mutual information to all orders from modular flow: a replica-free approach
articles.abstract: We derive an all-orders long-distance expansion of vacuum mutual information between two disjoint balls in generic $d$-dimensional CFTs. The derivation uses a novel radial sewing expansion of the joint vacuum density matrix, together with a modular response formula for relative entropy and the geometric modular flow of a single ball, without analytic continuation in replica number. The expansion coefficients are modular integrals of modular-flowed vacuum correlators. Our formula provides a systematic treatment of arbitrary multi-point sectors, and recovers known results on two-point sector derived from replica methods. The full two-point sector resums into a modular integral of the thermal partition function on $S^{d-1}$, with an effective temperature depending on ball configuration and modular time. We compute the expansion explicitly in CFTs. In two-dimensional Ising CFT, using analytic reductions and multidimensional numerical integration, we obtain the first ten radial orders in the long-distance expansion, which involve sphere correlators with up to twenty spin insertions. The truncated expansion agrees well with lattice data at finite separation, and approximately satisfies crossing symmetry. Analytic calculations also reproduce known expansion coefficients for 2d free compact boson at self-dual radius and its current sector, as well as for free scalars in higher dimensions.

articles.title: Noise-resilient collective order through temporal memory in self-propelled particles
articles.abstract: Temporal memory can stabilise collective motion by filtering noisy local observations, but persistent information can also impede adaptation when the collective state changes. We investigate this competition in Vicsek-type systems using two distinct alignment rules: a finite buffer of past observations and a recursive update of an internal directional state. In both models, increasing effective memory shifts the loss of polar order to stronger noise and can restore ordered motion under conditions for which the corresponding memoryless Vicsek model is disordered. The stationary responses of the two models show an approximate correspondence when parameterised by a kernel-based effective memory, consistent with temporal averaging playing a common role in their ordering behaviour rather than from the details of the memory implementation. Their transient dynamics, however, are not determined by effective memory alone. Following a collective perturbation, recovery is fastest at an intermediate memory depth and becomes slower when outdated observations are retained too strongly. Temporal integration therefore produces a trade-off: deeper memory improves noise resilience, whereas excessive persistence reduces responsiveness. These results identify memory depth as a control parameter that separates the optimisation of stationary order from that of dynamical recovery in noisy active systems.

articles.title: Observing oscillations using the non-magnetic and magnetic spin Hall effect in a non-collinear antiferromagnet
articles.abstract: In this study, it was observed that, in non-collinear IrMn3, both the non-magnetic spin Hall effect (NMSHE) and the magnetic spin Hall effect (MSHE) exhibit oscillations as the triangularly ordered magnetic moments of IrMn3 evolve with temperature. These oscillations are strongly influenced by the magnetic properties at the interface between IrMn3 and the adjacent material. Permalloy (Py), a ferromagnet, and platinum (Pt), a paramagnet, were employed as adjacent layers. Such experimental analyses demonstrate the pioneering nature of this phenomenon, which is validated through magnetoresistance measurements performed under different experimental conditions.

articles.title: Phonon Angular Momentum Multipoles and Nonlinear Thermal Responses
articles.abstract: Chiral phonons carry angular momentum and couple lattice dynamics to magnetic and transport phenomena. In magnets, however, a systematic classification of momentum-space phonon angular momentum (PAM) textures and experimental signatures of the resulting thermal responses remain elusive. Here we classify the PAM textures for all 122 magnetic point groups (MPGs) using two equivalent approaches: directly solving the linear symmetry constraints on the multipole expansion coefficients and constructing the allowed textures from group-representation basis functions. Both methods yield the same fivefold classification according to the leading nonzero order: $s$-wave (monopole), $p$-wave (dipole), $d$-wave (quadrupole), $f$-wave (octupole), and $g$-wave (hexadecapole). We further show that a temperature gradient generates a nonequilibrium PAM density whose $n$th-order term in $\nabla T$ contains an energy-weighted PAM $2^n$-pole tensor and a kinematic remainder, thereby linking the response order and partial-wave channel through exact selection rules. Because the Berry curvature obeys the same symmetry constraints, this taxonomy is in one-to-one correspondence with Berry-curvature multipoles and their nonlinear Hall responses. We propose a cantilever torque measurement whose allowed angular harmonics are fixed by the MPG, with period $2\pi/n$ for a pure $n$th harmonic, providing a direct probe of the partial-wave content of PAM in both nonmagnetic and magnetic materials.

articles.title: Polariton tweezers
articles.abstract: The non-invasive, deterministic manipulation of charge carriers remains a fundamental challenge in solid-state quantum technologies. Here, we demonstrate the concept of dynamic polariton tweezers capable of trapping and transporting electrons across a two-dimensional electron system via the long-range electrostatic potential of dipolar (d-) exciton-polaritons. By driving a semiconductor microcavity with a specifically engineered, non-collinear three-beam optical pump with TE-polarization, we synthesize a macroscopic polariton lattice with hexagonal symmetry. The spatially periodic field of this d-polariton condensate acts as a reconfigurable trapping landscape for the electrons. We show that introducing targeted frequency detunings between the continuous-wave pumps strictly breaks the spatiotemporal symmetry of the system, converting the stationary macroscopic interference pattern into a dynamically moving conveyor belt. By precisely customizing these frequency detunings, the entire lattice - along with the electrostatically trapped electrons - can be rigidly driven in any arbitrary in-plane direction. This precise phase-matching mechanism bypasses the need for a net kinetic momentum transfer, establishing a robust, optically controlled platform for the long-range routing of charged particles and topological defects in driven-dissipative quantum fluids.

articles.title: Polarity-Programmed Topological Gating of Knotting in Spatially Patterned Active Polymers
articles.abstract: Spatially patterned tangential activity provides a route to program polymer topology through both geometry and propulsion direction. We use Langevin-dynamics simulations of a flexible, self-avoiding linear polymer to determine how active-domain placement and independently assigned propulsion polarities control nonequilibrium knotting. Reversing the polarities of two terminal active blocks switches the steady state from a nearly always-knotted regime to effective knot suppression, changing the knotting probability by more than three orders of magnitude despite identical active-block positions and activity magnitude. Across symmetric terminal two-block architectures, we further identify an approximate zero-one-two free-end-alignment rule: zero, one, and two free-end-aligned active blocks correspond, respectively, to suppressed, intermediate, and high-knotting states. A two-state kinetic decomposition shows that the conditional knot-formation rate changes only by about threefold under polarity reversal, whereas the mean knot lifetime changes by several orders of magnitude, demonstrating that knot survival and passive-region storage dominate the polarity-controlled switch. Block placement provides an additional geometrical gate: moving an active domain from the chain interior to a terminal region strongly enhances both knot formation and survival. Knot-center residence, knotted-arc distributions, and episode-resolved kymographs reveal formation near free-end-aligned active blocks, directed contour migration, tightening, and long-lived retention in passive regions. Together, these results support a source-conveyor-reservoir-sink mechanism in which signed polarity and spatial activity patterning control whether knots are generated, transported, stored, or rapidly lost, providing a route to programmable topological states in nonequilibrium active polymers.

articles.title: Quantized pumping of boundary Hilbert space in chiral Floquet phases
articles.abstract: Chiral Floquet phases support quantized chiral flow along their boundaries even when the bulk is fully localized. In this Letter, we establish a complementary phenomenon, which we call Hilbert-space pumping: under a boundary condition twisted by time translation, a part of the boundary Hilbert space, of quantized dimension, is transferred between the opposite boundaries. The twist is the temporal analogue of Laughlin's flux insertion in the quantum Hall effect. For noninteracting fermions, the number of transferred boundary modes is determined by the winding number, as we show analytically for the boundary dynamics and numerically for the anomalous Floquet Anderson insulator. For interacting systems whose boundary dynamics is a quantum cellular automaton, the transferred dimension is set by the Gross-Nesme-Vogts-Werner (GNVW) index: the twisted boundary Floquet operator is the Floquet operator on a tilted time slice, whose Hilbert-space dimension is multiplied by the index for each period of twist. We derive this relation for matrix product unitaries and test it numerically in random unitary circuits. Applied to the matrix product operators of non-invertible symmetries, the same twisted rank returns the quantum dimension of the symmetry operator in addition to its flow index.

articles.title: Spin SYK-dot chains: entanglement bound and resource estimates towards a quantum advantage
articles.abstract: Ground states of Sachdev-Ye-Kitaev (SYK)-type models are volume-law entangled, which makes them costly both for tensor networks and for quantum hardware simulations. Thus, it remains unclear where quantum hardware could outperform classical simulation of such models. In this work, we study a spin SYK-dot chain, in which q dense SYK dots of p qubits are joined by single ZZ bonds of strength K. The entanglement across any cut is then bounded by floor(p/2) ln 2 plus the inter-dot entanglement, and the two-qubit depth of one Trotter step is set by p alone. A resource estimate shows that a quantum advantage for the ground state could appear only for dots of about 15 to 21 qubits or more. There, a single Trotter step already requires two-qubit error rates of order 10^{-6}, beyond the reach of noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) hardware. We test the assumptions of this estimate with an imaginary-time matrix product state (MPS) that applies each dot as one block. It agrees with exact diagonalisation at (p, q) = (6, 2). At (5, 2), a variational circuit with the same dot-plus-link layout comes within 3.6% of the exact energy, and noisy simulations show that its fidelity decays as assumed in the resource estimate. At (8, 5), i.e., N = 40 qubits, the energy converges at bond dimension chi = 768, far below the exact value 2^20, and the inter-dot entanglement stays small and is set mainly by K. Out-of-time-order correlators across the links decay on a time scale that shrinks rapidly with |K|. Thus, the dot size p and the inter-dot coupling K together set the entanglement of the chain, and with it where a quantum advantage could appear.

articles.title: Strain-tunable electronic transport in disordered borophene nanoribbons with line defects
articles.abstract: Resonant tunneling intrinsically exists in disordered borophene nanoribbons (BNRs) with randomly distributed line defects (LDs), providing a versatile platform for transport modulation. Here, we theoretically investigate the effects of in-plane mechanical strain on the electronic transport properties of disordered BNRs coupled to metallic electrodes. Our results demonstrate that the resonant peaks in disordered BNRs of different widths remain robust against variations in electrode parameters and can be efficiently modulated via mechanical strain. Specifically, uniaxial strain significantly modulates the energies, widths, and amplitudes of these resonant peaks, and can even suppress the peaks selectively and induce new ones. In particular, the response of the resonant energies to the applied strain exhibits remarkable anisotropy, where strains along the longitudinal and transverse directions induce opposite energy shifts. Moreover, identical resonant peaks recurring in different nanoribbon widths respond uniformly to applied strain. Biaxial strain enables highly efficient conductance switching across multiple distinct levels, with the modulation frequency increasing for wider nanoribbons. Our findings establish a promising defect-strain-engineering strategy for manipulating electronic transport in borophene and other gapless materials.

articles.title: Superinsulation, electric confinement in condensed matter
articles.abstract: Superinsulation is the confining phase of condensed matter systems. It is a genuine quantum state of matter, dual to superconductivity, just as confinement in particle physics is dual to the Higgs phase. In contrast to hadron physics, the gauge field that becomes confining is not colour SU(3) but the conventional U(1) electromagnetic field. Superinsulation arises in superconductors with an emergent granular condensate when core-less XY vortices between condensate grains become tensionless, unobservable Dirac strings and magnetic monopoles are liberated and condense. This magnetic condensate confines electric fields into flux tubes, strings that generate a linear potential between Cooper pairs. These dual Abrikosov flux tubes give rise to infinite electrical resistance, persisting up to a finite deconfinement temperature. We shall review the theoretical framework of superinsulation together with its experimental validation, including the direct observation of the linear confining potential and we shall stress how phase-only approaches and disorder-based ideas for the phases around the superconductor-to-insulator transition are hard to reconcile with recent experimental observations.

articles.title: Symmetry breaking from conformality loss on holographic Rényi defects
articles.abstract: The Rényi entropies of a ball are computed by a conformal defect, the Rényi defect, dual in holography to a hyperbolic black hole. At an index $n_*$ its charged operator merges with its alternate-quantization partner, and the defect loses conformality. Beyond $n_*$ it flows with no source to a conformal defect that breaks the U(1) symmetry; below $n_*$ that defect needs a symmetry-breaking source, so at large $N$, conformality loss makes the breaking spontaneous. The scalar hair beyond $n_*$, expected to break the symmetries of hyperbolic space, thus preserves them outside a thin layer at the entangling surface, as conformal symmetry requires. The region outside the layer sets the universal term of the Rényi entropy. We demonstrate the mechanism in the probe Abelian Higgs model in AdS$_5$ at the Bogomolny point, where the saddles are in closed form and numerical methods confirm the flows. On a sphere we prove that a positive source-free flow exists exactly when $n>n_*$ and the sphere is large enough; it is then unique and ends at the symmetry-breaking defect. The mechanism needs a scalar mass in a finite window, and for potentials attractive at small amplitude, the symmetry can break before conformality is lost. For operators of low enough dimension, already the second Rényi entropy lies beyond the merger. Classical backreaction does not move the merger at any order; we argue that away from $n_*$ the flows persist at first order.

articles.title: Synchronization and Spatiotemporal Phases in Driven Precessing Domain Walls
articles.abstract: The dynamics of extended magnetic domain walls driven by constant and alternating magnetic fields are studied using a collective coordinate $u$-$φ$ model. While purely constant-field driven systems exhibit deterministic spatiotemporal chaos and roughening, the alternating component can lock the precessional frequency via Shapiro-like steps. Using linear stability analysis and Floquet theory, the phase boundaries of stable, synchronized flat wall states are mapped. By studying the nonlinear dynamics of the extended system, a rich phase diagram is identified, composed of five dynamical regimes characterized by the combination of domain wall spatial order (flat, rough, or periodic) and domain wall precession temporal order (pinned, synchronized, or unsynchronized). Notably, the macroscopic temporal order of the synchronized phases can lead to a flat domain wall or to a periodic structure dominated by a narrow band of linearly unstable modes, both with coherent precession of the domain wall magnetization, while unsynchronized phases can be flat, with coherent precession, or rough with spatiotemporal chaos and incoherent precession.

articles.title: The Virasoro Bootstrap: from the $c\sim1$ desert to coupled Potts
articles.abstract: We develop a numerical conformal bootstrap for two-dimensional CFTs with $c>1$ based on Virasoro conformal blocks, computed with Zamolodchikov's recursion and optimal polynomial interpolation. As a first test we isolate an island around three decoupled Ising models. We then consider three 3-state Potts models coupled through their energy operators, a candidate irrational CFT. Mixed correlators isolate the decoupled theory in an island, and different gap assumptions, motivated by perturbation theory, yield a peninsula that contains the coupled fixed point but not the decoupled one. Finally, we explore the standard single-correlator bound on the lowest-dimension scalar primary in the OPE of two identical scalars. We find that for central charges just above $c=1$ the bound collapses over a wide range of external dimensions. This excludes any theory whose lightest scalar is absent from its own OPE and lies in this range, and supports the conjecture that no compact CFT exists in this region. We explain several features of these bounds analytically.

articles.title: The effects of an alternating bias on a single orbital spin impurity
articles.abstract: Electron spin resonance with the scanning tunneling microscope (ESR-STM) enables coherent manipulation and detection of individual atomic spins with atomic-scale spatial resolution, yet the microscopic mechanism by which the radiofrequency (RF) bias drives the spin remains under debate. We study this problem using a Redfield quantum-master-equation framework in which the oscillating bias enters explicitly through the electronic reservoirs rather than through an effective time-dependent tunneling amplitude. In the semiclassical limit, the RF voltage periodically sweeps the system through its static transport landscape, so that the transport regime depends jointly on the DC bias and RF amplitude. When the RF trajectory approaches or crosses a charge transition, the damping-like torque (DLT) associated with spin-polarized charge transfer is strongly enhanced. By contrast, the field-like torque (FLT) induced by the exchange field remains finite deeper in the Coulomb-blockade (CB) regime because it originates from virtual charge fluctuations. The RF trajectory also averages strongly bias-dependent static quantities over a finite voltage range, smoothing features such as the Lamb shift near the charge thresholds. These results establish the RF amplitude as a control parameter not only for the strength of the ESR drive, but also for the transport regime and the ratio between FLT and DLT.

articles.title: The maximum packing fraction of disordered bidisperse discs: theory and predictions
articles.abstract: Predicting the highest packing fraction that disordered packing of bidisperse discs can achieve, $φ_{max}$, is an important unresolved problem. Such a predictive theory is hindered by the density dependence on the packing protocol and by ensuring disorder. In bidisperse packings, this is more complicated because $φ_{max}$ is not a number but a function of the disc species size ratio, $D$, and one of the disc species concentration, $p$. These difficulties have been overcome in monodisperse disc packings by using the cell order distribution (COD)~\cite{Bl21}. Focusing on size ratios that prohibit rattlers, a COD-based theory is constructed here. It introduces bidisperse statistical closure equations, which combine an explicit disorder criterion with consistent cell and edge statistics, and yields $φ_{max}(p,D)$ and structural predictions. The a-priori disorder-guaranteeing criterion proposed here ensures fast exponential a decay of the occurrence probability of ordered clusters with size. Using a constrained maximum-entropy analysis to ensure maximum disorder, the occurrence probabilities of all the possible cell and edge configurations are derived in terms of $p$ and $D$ and they are found to be binomial. All the results are assembled to yield an exact prediction of $φ_{max}(p,D)$.

articles.title: The normal approximation to macroscopic dynamical fluctuations
articles.abstract: Under local detailed balance, the Lagrangian of macroscopic dynamical fluctuations has a canonical structure: its time-antisymmetric part is the entropy flux, and its time-symmetric part is a Legendre pair of kinetic and dissipation functions. We show what survives of that structure for normal (Gaussian) fluctuations around a nonequilibrium steady state. The quadratic Lagrangian keeps the canonical form, with the Hessian of the dissipation function as noise matrix. However, the force on the fluctuations differs from the linearized thermodynamic force by a term proportional to the driving and to the state dependence of the dynamical activity, so that local detailed balance is violated at the Gaussian level. Nevertheless, the Gaussian dynamics is gradient flow for the quadratic part of the nonequilibrium entropy, around an emergent nondissipative current. Finally, we show which parts of the Lagrangian can be reconstructed from measured Gaussian fluctuations.

articles.title: Theory of the Ferroaxial Charge Density Wave in 1T-TiSe$_2$
articles.abstract: Recent experiments using strain to probe the charge-density wave (CDW) of 1T-TiSe$_2$ have uncovered additional transitions and broken symmetries inside the CDW state. The elastocaloric effect reveals a second transition below $T_\mathrm{CDW}$, which elastoresistivity shows to be associated with ferroaxial order, breaking all vertical mirror symmetries while preserving inversion. In addition, at even lower temperatures, a diverging nematic susceptibility has been reported through elastoresistivity. In this work, we argue that this rich phenomenology cannot be explained by the standard $L_1^-$ CDW order parameter, and instead requires the existence of a secondary CDW order parameter. Based on symmetry, microscopic, and diffraction considerations, we propose this subleading CDW to have $L_2^-$ symmetry. By analyzing the Landau theory of coupled $L_1^-$ and $L_2^-$ orders in the presence of strain, we reproduce the phase boundaries observed in the elastocaloric measurements and the emergence of ferroaxial order below the CDW transition. Moreover, the model supports a third threefold-rotational symmetry breaking transition at lower temperatures, consistent with the reported divergence of the nematic susceptibility.

articles.title: Ultrafast X-ray-induced dephasing of valence electrons
articles.abstract: Diffract-before-destroy schemes for atomic-scale electron mapping assume that ultrashort X-ray pulses outrun radiation damage. Although atomic cores move over tens of femtoseconds, outer electrons respond much faster, compromising their locations. We test this limit in elemental silicon using broadband, energy-chirped X-ray pulses to encode time with few-femtosecond resolution. Comparing valence-sensitive structurally forbidden reflections with simultaneously measured core-dominated Bragg peaks reveals valence-bond dephasing on sub-20-fs timescales even at pulse energies where direct ionization effects are negligible. Our findings demonstrate that crystallography where outer electrons contribute substantially to Bragg peaks requires pulses shorter than today's standard $\sim50\,fs$ standard. They also establish a path to disentangle valence electron and lattice contributions to order and dynamics with hard X-rays, enabling studies across molecular biology, quantum matter and devices.

articles.title: Universality and Emergent Classicality in Krylov Space
articles.abstract: Krylov complexity grows linearly at late times for many systems. In this regime, we give a general spectral formula for the leading growth coefficients of Krylov complexity and its higher moments, without requiring detailed knowledge of the Lanczos coefficients. For states with a narrow energy distribution compared to the bandwidth, dynamics in the Krylov basis resembles motion along a classical trajectory. We demonstrate our results for the critical XY chain and double-scaled SYK. For the latter, we compute the leading late-time behavior of the chord-number moments through one-loop order.

articles.title: Variational Functional Neural Networks (vfNN)
articles.abstract: We present a variational functional neural network (vfNN) algorithm that optimizes physically motivated continuum functionals in integral form (e.g., Lagrangian, Hamiltonian, or free energy) to find the states of a system. That way, vfNN bypasses solving the equations of motion (a.k.a. the Euler-Lagrange equations), which are in the form of differential equations. To this end, our approach is fundamentally different from conventional physics-informed neural networks (PINN) that solve differential equations by minimizing a phenomenological loss function involving higher order derivatives and ad hoc weight factors. In contrast, vfNN merely evaluates lower order derivatives of the generating functional and replaces the weight factors with rigorous physical scales. This also fundamentally changes the loss landscape, and the desired solutions may become unstable. For this emergent nonconvex optimization problem, we develop a quasi-Newton optimization algorithm with simulated annealing that converges to the solutions of the corresponding Euler-Lagrange equations of the functional regardless of their stability properties. Our simulations using vfNN give accurate results for benchmark systems governed by linear or nonlinear ordinary differential equations.

articles.title: When will androids outnumber humans?
articles.abstract: Humanoid robots are increasingly discussed not only as machines but also as a potential technological population. We develop a nonlinear population-dynamical framework to examine their possible diffusion relative to humans, without assuming that large-scale adoption or numerical crossover is inevitable. The human population $H(t)$ is calibrated to the United Nations World Population Prospects 2024 median trajectory. The android population $A(t)$ is represented through the normalized stock $a=A/A_s$. A conventional, human-organized manufacturing and adoption channel is calibrated to a conditional scenario spanning approximately $10^4$ humanoids in 2025 to $10^9$ in 2050 and follows $\dot a=(q_M+r_Ma)\exp(K_Ma^γ)$. We separately introduce a hypothetical autonomous channel in which installed androids contribute materially to producing additional androids. Under the minimal canonical TZ closure, the corresponding production--feedback number is $\mathcal{P}(a)=(r_A/δ_A)\exp(K_Ra)$, where $r_A$ is the gross robot-mediated production coefficient, $δ_A$ the retirement rate, and $K_R$ the autonomous feedback parameter. This channel is locally self-amplifying if and only if $\mathcal{P}>1$, whereas numerical human--android parity, $A=H$, is a separate cumulative condition. Global uncertainty analysis shows that crossover dates remain strongly scenario-dependent, while the production--feedback threshold is more robust. An extreme early-autonomy stress test can produce parity by 2050, but this represents a conditional dynamical boundary rather than a technological forecast.

articles.title: Writing with Near-Field: towards Atomic Resolution in Material Processing
articles.abstract: Direct laser writing with ultra-short pulses is the most flexible route to two- and three-dimensional (2D/3D) material modification, yet its resolution is judged against the optical diffraction limit. This review argues the opposite: the finest, most reproducible modifications come not from shortening the wavelength but from localising the absorber. Through the threshold effect and a transient epsilon-near-zero (ENZ) state - the dielectric-to-metal (Die-Met) state of the excited solid - the deposited energy is confined to a dipole-like nano-seed whose near-field intensity falls as r^-6 (ideal point dipole). The localisation is thus set by the seed size, not the focal wavelength, and the final feature is shaped by the material response: post-pulse heat flow, cavitation and quenching. We show that polarisation controls the anisotropy of deposition: the quasi-static near-field and interface boundary conditions select the writing direction and the modification orientation, down to a single defect. We survey energy-deposition mechanisms from 100 nm to the single-nanometer scale and link them to working engineering: stitch-free large-area patterning and record aspect-ratio (10^3-10^4) dicing and wafering of transparent crystals. Finally, we conjecture guided volumetric deposition, in which laser-inscribed lossy nano-seeds act as antennas that let cavity microwaves anneal the modified nano-volumes from within, as a 2.45 GHz oven heats food through water-dipole absorption. Throughout, atomic resolution is used in a quantum-confined sense and denotes a direction of travel: 10-20 nm features are demonstrated, while deterministic single-defect and single-bond modification remain goals. The thesis is that ultrafast direct write beats diffraction-limited intuition because the material itself forms a transient nanoscale absorber whose near-field and boundary conditions govern energy deposition.

articles.title: Zero-field plasmon splitter: Controlled interaction between quantum anomalous Hall edge states
articles.abstract: The quantum anomalous Hall (QAH) effect provides chiral edge states without the need for an external magnetic field, but unlike in conventional quantum Hall systems, their trajectories cannot be readily controlled electrostatically. Here, we engineer Coulomb interactions between two spatially separated, counter-propagating QAH edge channels using a floating metallic island. Microwave measurements reveal frequency-dependent redistribution of injected edge plasmons between two output channels, demonstrating interaction-induced hybridization of the collective modes. A long-range interaction model quantitatively reproduces the response and reveals a very low plasmon velocity in the coupling region, strongly reduced by electrostatic screening. Our results establish engineered Coulomb coupling as a route to control collective excitations in QAH edge states and provide a building block for chiral plasmonic circuits and electron quantum optics in magnetic topological insulators.

articles.title: FACTO: fast atom-centered tensor operator for accurate and efficient foundational machine-learned interatomic potentials
articles.abstract: High-throughput inference remains a central challenge for equivariant machine-learned interatomic potentials. Here we introduce FACTO, an atom-centered equivariant architecture that confines evolving learned state and dense channel mixing to atoms, expressing neighbor interactions as fully fusible reductions. We complement this design with custom register-accumulated aggregation kernels and tensor-core FP32 emulation, accelerating inference while retaining FP32-level energy conservation under emulated arithmetic in molecular dynamics. Comprehensive evaluations on Matbench Discovery, MLIP Arena and MatCalc demonstrate high throughput alongside strong predictive accuracy and physical reliability. On Matbench Discovery, the four FACTO-OAM variants show top-tier performance by overall rank sum among 46 models with complete scores, advancing the accuracy-throughput Pareto frontier. On MLIP Arena, FACTO achieves state- of-the-art stability under extreme heating and compression, alongside high fidelity in hydrogen combustion. On MatCalc, FACTO outperforms the compared baselines in structural and elastic predictions while retaining competitive accuracy for energetic and thermal properties.

articles.title: FlowBatt: Flow Matching for Probabilistic Battery Degradation Prediction
articles.abstract: Battery degradation remains a central challenge in the development and broad application of sustainable energy technologies. Accurate degradation prediction is challenging, as battery aging emerges from complex and heterogeneous interactions among cycling behavior, operating conditions, and cell chemistry. Existing machine-learning approaches typically focus on deterministic end-of-life predictions or modeling degradation curves within fixed chemistry settings, leaving probabilistic state of health (SOH) trajectory modeling across heterogeneous chemistries underexplored. We introduce FlowBatt, a use-inspired conditional generative framework that adapts flow matching with a diffusion transformer (DiT) backbone to battery degradation trajectory modeling. FlowBatt models full SOH trajectories as probabilistic degradation processes conditioned on early-cycle capacity data. To strengthen this conditioning pathway, we use explainable AI analysis to diagnose and improve the encoder that maps early-cycle capacity matrices into conditioning vectors. We evaluate FlowBatt on five public benchmark settings spanning diverse chemistries and aging conditions, comparing it with supervised and diffusion-based trajectory models as well as established baselines for remaining useful life (RUL) prediction under shared data splits. FlowBatt achieves the best trajectory-wise SOH prediction performance on all five datasets, with errors below 2.5%, and delivers competitive RUL prediction performance. By generating multiple plausible trajectories, FlowBatt provides empirical prediction intervals for battery degradation modeling. These results indicate that flow-matching-based trajectory modeling is a promising framework for probabilistic battery health prediction.

articles.title: GPU infrastructure for ML/MM with electrostatic embedding for enzyme chemistry
articles.abstract: We present a fully GPU-native framework for machine learning/molecular mechanics (ML/MM) enhanced sampling simulations with electrostatic embedding, demonstrated on an enzymatic reaction. The framework combines a JAX port of the pretrained MACE-POLAR-1-M model, an electrostatic embedding scheme compatible with the MACE-POLAR architecture, and integration with JAX-MD and PLUMED-JAX for end-to-end compiled enhanced sampling. The implementation is developed using GPT-6.1-Sol within Codex, with reasoning effort set to high. Using replica exchange umbrella sampling, we calculate the free energy profile of nucleophilic substitution in haloalkane dehalogenase in approximately 200 H100 GPU hours, treating the entire protein and reactants with MACE-POLAR-1-M-JAX and most of the solvent with molecular mechanics.

articles.title: Relativistic Kohn--Sham Theory of Paramagnetic Magnetic-Resonance Properties
articles.abstract: A general density functional theory based relativistic theory for paramagnetic NMR (pNMR) shifts, EPR g-tensors and hyperfine coupling tensors as well as magnetizabilities is derived. The formulation uses spin--orbit exact two-component (X2C) theory, gauge-including atomic orbitals, and generalized complex Kohn--Sham response equations with all ingredients being implemented analytically with the help of Goldstone modes and an orientation-constrained shielding. Additionally, we describe a two-component augmented Roothaan--Hall (ARH) solver for robust and stable convergence, which ensures that both a stationary point and a minimum are found. This is crucial for the convergence of the response equations for properties of paramagnetic systems. The extension of common population analyses for the two-component theory to aid in the interpretation of the spectra is further described. Using these new techniques, we are able to analyze the success and failure of density functional theory for relativistic open-shell systems including actinide complexes.

articles.title: Shadow Molecular Dynamics for General Nonlinear Flexible-Charge Models
articles.abstract: Machine-learned interatomic potentials have greatly expanded the reach of molecular dynamics simulations, but complex chemical environments often require explicit treatment of long-range electronic response, including charge transfer and polarization. Physics-based flexible-charge models capture these effects but require global nonlinear charge equilibration at every time step to obtain Born-Oppenheimer energies and forces. This process is computationally expensive and can lead to instabilities unless tightly converged. Here, we introduce a shadow molecular dynamics framework for flexible-charge models with arbitrary local nonlinearities and long-range multipolar electrostatics. We replace the exact Born-Oppenheimer potential with a nearby shadow potential obtained by exactly equilibrating a partially linearized electronic energy functional. This provides conservative forces and reduces the global nonlinear equilibration to a quasi-diagonal linear problem that can be solved directly at low cost. Auxiliary dynamical electronic degrees of freedom, propagated through an extended-Lagrangian dynamics, capture the long-range electronic response and define the reference state for the linearization of the energy functional. GPU-accelerated simulations with over 100,000 atoms demonstrate that the shadow potential closely follows the tightly converged Born-Oppenheimer surface, while maintaining long-term stability at a computational cost approaching that of a fixed-charge model. These advances establish an efficient and broadly applicable framework for machine-learned interatomic potentials that explicitly incorporate long-range electrostatic interactions and environment-dependent electronic response.

articles.title: A Topology-Based Approach to Representative Volume Element Assessment in Solid Oxide Cell Anodes Using Large Volume Tomography and Persistent Homology
articles.abstract: Determining the representative volume element is essential for establishing statistically meaningful microstructure-property relationships. Conventional approaches rely on the convergence of selected geometric descriptors, which may yield different estimates of the representative volume. Here, we propose a topology-based framework for assessing the representative scale of a nickel-yttria-stabilized zirconia solid oxide cell anode reconstructed using plasma focused ion beam-scanning electron microscopy (121.8 um x 83.97 um x 45.99 um). Persistent homology was used to characterize the pore network, and normalized persistence images of subvolumes were compared with those of the largest available reference volume using the L1 distance. This provides a continuous measure of topological similarity across observation scales, rather than defining representativeness through a single convergence threshold. The topological distance decreases with increasing volume and is described by empirical exponential models over the investigated range (R2 in [0.972, 0.983]). Comparison with porosity and specific surface area highlights differences in the scale-dependent behavior of geometric and topological descriptors. The framework was also tested on three independent synthetic realizations, demonstrating its potential for quantitative assessment of topological similarity in porous microstructures.

articles.title: A combined segmented anode gas ionization chamber and time-of-flight detector for heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis
articles.abstract: A dedicated detector system for heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis at the Tandem Laboratory of Uppsala University is presented. Benefits of combining a time-of-flight measurement with a segmented anode gas ionization chamber are demonstrated. The capability of ion species identification is improved with the present system, compared to that obtained when using a single solid state silicon detector for the full ion energy signal. The system enables separation of light elements, up to Neon, based on atomic number while signals from heavy elements such as molybdenum and tungsten are separated based on mass, to a sample depth on the order of one micrometer. The performance of the system is discussed and a selection of material analysis applications is given. Plasma-facing materials from fusion experiments, in particular metal mirrors, are used as a main example for the discussion. Marker experiments using nitrogen-15 or oxygen-18 are specific cases for which the described improved species separation and sensitivity are required. Resilience to radiation damage and significantly improved energy resolution for heavy elements at low energies are additional benefits of the gas ionization chamber over a solid state detector based system.

articles.title: Amplitude-conserving frequency demultiplexer based on a spin wave delay line
articles.abstract: Propagating spin waves have emerged as promising candidates for signal processing and information transmission. We present a theoretical investigation of the generation, propagation and collection of spin-wave wave packets in micrometer-wide magnetic conduits, highlighting their potential for analogue frequency demultiplexing in space and time. We clarify the roles of the excitation duration and of the spin wave dispersion relation, as well as the influence of the spin-wave linewidth in setting the spatio-temporal evolution of propagating spin-wave wavepackets excited by Gaussian field pulses. We issue rules for the spatio-temporal separation of wavepackets that carry different frequencies. We finally propose an amplitude-conserving frequency demultiplexer based on a spin wave delay line of 60x5 $μ$m$^2$ footprint.

articles.title: Anion Engineering Enables Concurrent Optimization of Phonon and Carrier Transport in AMg$_2$X$_2$ Zintl Thermoelectrics
articles.abstract: The simultaneous suppression of lattice heat transport and enhancement of carrier transport is central to the development of high-performance thermoelectric materials. Here, we investigate the microscopic mechanisms governing phonon and carrier transport in CaAl$_2$Si$_2$-type AMg$_2$X$_2$ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba; X = P, As, Sb, Bi) Zintl compounds using first-principles calculations, machine-learning interatomic potentials, and Boltzmann transport theory. As X changes from P to Bi, the widening phonon band gap restricts three-phonon scattering channels and increases the relative importance of four-phonon processes. In CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ and BaMg$_2$Bi$_2$, four-phonon scattering dominates the relaxation of low-frequency heat-carrying modes at 900 K. The Bi-based series also exhibits an anomalous increase in lattice thermal conductivity from Ca to Ba despite the increasing cation mass. Mode-resolved analysis links the lower thermal conductivity of CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$ to reduced low-frequency group velocities and stronger anharmonic scattering, with Ca-related mid-frequency vibrations providing additional four-phonon scattering channels. Including both particle-like and coherent contributions, its lattice thermal conductivity reaches 0.23 W$\cdot$m$^{-1}$K$^{-1}$ at 900 K. Meanwhile, the increasing covalent character of the vertical Mg-X bonds is accompanied by enhanced band-edge dispersion and reduced carrier effective masses. These electronic changes, together with conduction-band convergence, favor n-type transport and yield a predicted peak $ZT$ of 3.68 at 900 K in CaMg$_2$Bi$_2$. These results elucidate the interplay of phonon spectral structure and higher-order anharmonicity in thermal transport, alongside the distinct electronic response to anion substitution.

articles.title: Cage-enforced i-wave altermagnetism in boron-carbon clathrates
articles.abstract: The spin splitting of an altermagnet arises from a rotation that relates its two magnetic sublattices. In known cases it is fixed by the crystal structure. Here we show that guest-host frameworks separate the two roles. In the boron-carbon clathrates $M$B$_3$C$_3$ the ordered cage removes the translation between the two guest sites and enforces cubic $i$-wave altermagnetism, with six symmetry-enforced nodal planes, for any magnetic guest in the compensated state; strain retunes the class to $d$- or $g$-wave. We demonstrate the platform with GdB$_3$C$_3$: its compensated antiferromagnetic ground state is a narrow-gap semiconductor with spin splitting of 0.19 eV at the conduction-band edge, and its weakly pinned Néel vector switches the helicity-resolved optical response on and off according to the magnetic point group. Thermodynamic stability at high pressure and dynamical stability at ambient pressure indicate that it can be made by the route established for this family.

articles.title: Characterisation of surface layers formed on plasma-facing components in controlled fusion devices: Role of heavy ion elastic recoil detection
articles.abstract: Wall components retrieved from the TEXTOR tokamak after tracer experiments with nitrogen-15 and molybdenum hexafluoride (MoF6) injection were studied to determine deposition patterns and, by this, to conclude on material migration. Toroidal limiter tiles made of carbon fibre composites and fine grain graphite were examined using time-of-flight heavy ion elastic recoil detection analysis. Molybdenum deposition patterns indicated migration based on erosion and prompt re-deposition. Nitrogen-15 was trapped together with the deposited molybdenum. Some information on the depth distribution of species in the top 400 nm layer of the limiters was obtained; however surface roughness of the samples strongly limited resolution. In the case of molybdenum, the largest concentration was found in the 100 nm outermost layer, whereas fluorine and nitrogen-15 displayed more irregular profiles. Other species, besides deuterium fuel and carbon-12, were also identified: boron-10 and boron-11 originating from boronisations, carbon-13 from earlier tracer experiments, nitrogen-14 from plasma edge cooling and metals eroded from the Inconel wall.

articles.title: Collective dipole effects amplify field-driven ion transport in amorphous Li$_3$PO$_4$
articles.abstract: Amorphous solid electrolytes often outperform their crystalline counterparts, but how disorder shapes ionic transport under strong electric fields is poorly understood. We use molecular dynamics with a machine-learned interatomic potential and a machine-learned Born-effective-charge model to measure Li mobility in amorphous Li$_3$PO$_4$ and in a crystal with Li vacancies, from the linear to the strongly nonlinear regime. The amorphous phase shows a much stronger field enhancement, and we trace this to a collective dipole effect. The migrating ion carries the same charge in both phases. Alone it would not make the amorphous phase respond more strongly. What makes the difference is the environment. In the amorphous network the surrounding atoms move with the hop. Their motion makes the work the field performs vary widely between hops. Since hopping rates grow exponentially with the work, the most strongly assisted hops can dominate the drift. Disorder thus enhances field-driven transport through the environment rather than the carrier itself, a mechanism that may operate in disordered ion conductors in general.

articles.title: Data-driven candidate structure ensemble generation beyond the convex hull with crystALL approach
articles.abstract: Real materials consist of multiple stable or metastable states under real-world conditions, existing as statistical ergodic ensembles of configurations rather than ideal crystals. Yet, data-driven computational materials discovery increasingly biases itself toward finding "new stable structures" from ground-state DFT calculations alone. This limits our long-term ability to discover materials whose properties emerge from metastable phases, to explain experimental observations, or to model thermodynamic behavior comprehensively. Predicting ergodic sets of atomic configurations of known and hypothetical solids is a fundamental challenge in theoretical crystallography, approached via many complementary methods. We discuss this conceptually and introduce crystALL, a pragmatic and powerful data-driven approach to discovering ensembles beyond the convex hull, embracing structural diversity over stability alone, enabling robust experiment matching in cases evading traditional methods. crystALL leverages 5 million relaxed structures from OPTIMADE and MPDD to rapidly generate a comprehensive candidate set by: (1) species substitutions; (2) ML feature-space analysis with pySIPFENN; (3) representative structure selection via clustering and energy-minimization or property matching; and (4) construction of the final candidate ensemble for experimental or ab initio validation. We also uniquely address the common challenge of experimental composition uncertainties spanning many integer stoichiometries by new efficient searches across anonymized compositional ranges rather than fixed formulas. Overall, crystALL's ensemble-focused philosophy provides critical advantages over the prevailing convex-hull-searching paradigm, which often fails to account for key experimental observations and increases AI/ML discovery bias over time - akin to model collapse in LLMs retrained on iteratively generated content.

articles.title: Defect Chemistry of Hafnia-Based Ferroelectrics under Oxide-Electrode Constraints
articles.abstract: HfO$_2$ heterostructures with La$_{0.67}$Sr$_{0.33}$MnO$_3$ (LSMO) epitaxial electrodes have attracted interest as ferroelectric systems with electrode-dependent defect chemistry. However, the formation and stability of defects under LSMO-constrained chemical conditions remain poorly understood. In this work, we use density functional theory calculations to systematically investigate oxygen vacancies and La-, Sr-, and Mn-related interstitial and substitutional defects in HfO$_2$ under chemical environments constrained by the LSMO electrode. We find that LSMO stability substantially narrows the accessible O chemical potential range relative to bulk HfO$_2$, altering the predicted defect formation energies. While La and Sr substitutional defects are governed primarily by preferred ionic valence states, oxygen vacancies and Mn substitutional defects exhibit charge states sensitive to the local atomic environment. In addition, defect-complex calculations in orthorhombic HfO$_2$ reveal negative binding energies, indicating favorable defect association. The La- and Mn-related defect complexes exhibit thermodynamic competition, with their relative stability depending on the Fermi level and oxygen chemical potential. Lastly, extending the analysis to Hf$_{0.5}$Zr$_{0.5}$O$_2$ and ZrO$_2$ reveals common oxygen-vacancy trends, while the stability of LSMO-derived defects depends more strongly on the host material and crystal phase. These results provide a thermodynamic basis for understanding how electrode-constrained chemical environments and host structures influence defect formation, charge compensation, and defect-complex stability in HfO$_2$-based materials.

articles.title: Derivation of Novel Isotropic Metamaterials at the Hashin Shtrikman Stiffness Limit Enabled by Physics Informed Neural Networks
articles.abstract: Current methods of deriving ultrastiff isotropic metamaterials require heuristics or topology optimization, which are highly inefficient and limited by human input. To circumvent this, Physics Informed Neural Networks are applied to analytical equations to systematically solve for plate orientations in closed cell lattices. Following a standardized procedure, the plate orientations were modelled and assembled into geometries resembling quasi random foams for validation via finite element simulations. Closed cell 6-plate geometries were also additively manufactured using LAPIS and experimentally characterized. The results indicate that a minimum of 6 plates is required to constitute an ultrastiff isotropic lattice, 7 plates would return the established plate Cubic Octet structure while 8 to 10 plate geometries did not show significant differences in properties. Despite the introduction of some plate bending due to sub-optimal plate placement strategy, relative stiffness of the PINNs lattices adheres closely to the Hashin Shtrikman upper bound, 90 percent of Hashin Shtrikman upper bound at a relative density of 0.4, and the lattices maintain near isotropic behaviour, achieving a Zener ratio of 0.95 at a relative density of 0.1. Benchmarking results show that specific stiffness of PINNs lattices is higher than the majority of isotropic architectures reported in the literature.

articles.title: Fermi surface and field-induced Lifshitz transition in the antiferromagnet NbMnP exhibiting an anomalous Hall effect
articles.abstract: We performed Shubnikov--de Haas (SdH) oscillation measurements on the $\mathbf{Q}=0$ antiferromagnet NbMnP, which exhibits a large anomalous Hall effect. The SdH frequencies observed in the low-field region up to 17.5~T are well described by first-principles band-structure calculations based on the $B_{3g}+B_{2u}$ noncollinear magnetic structure determined by neutron diffraction. The effective masses are enhanced by approximately a factor of two relative to the calculated band masses. High-field measurements up to 41.5~T reveal a Lifshitz transition accompanied by a pronounced evolution of the SdH frequency spectrum. These results confirm that first-principles calculations provide a reliable tool for the development of functional antiferromagnetic materials, while also demonstrating that field-induced changes in the Fermi surface itself need to be taken into account in understanding their high-field magnetotransport properties.

articles.title: High-Entropy A-Site Disorder Enhances Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity and Stability in Nickelate Thin Films
articles.abstract: Rare-earth nickelates are among the most active oxide electrocatalysts for the oxygen evolution reaction (OER), owing to their tunable Ni-O covalency, near-unity eg occupancy, and sensitivity to A-site chemistry, oxygen stoichiometry, and epitaxial strain. Here, we use epitaxial A-site high-entropy (La0.2Pr0.2Nd0.2Sm0.2Eu0.2)NiO3 thin films to reveal how epitaxial strain influences defect formation, Ni valence, electronic structure, and OER activity in a chemically disordered rare-earth (RE) sublattice. Tensile strain promotes Ruddlesden-Popper fault formation, interrupts the corner-sharing NiO6 network, and lowers the average Ni oxidation state. Although the occupied density of states near the Fermi level remains largely unchanged, O K-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy reveals increased low-energy unoccupied states under tensile strain. First-principles calculations suggest that tensile strain shifts RE 4f-derived states toward the Fermi level, enhancing RE 4f-O 2p-Ni 3d hybridization. These coupled structural and electronic changes lead to earlier OER onset, stronger pre-catalytic Ni redox features, and higher activity than compressively strained films and representative single-A-site nickelates. The high-entropy nickelate also shows enhanced resistance to OER-induced structural degradation compared with LaNiO3. These results suggest that A-site configurational disorder and epitaxial strain can jointly tune defect formation and rare-earth-derived electronic states, providing a route for improving perovskite oxide electrocatalysts.

articles.title: Identifying the Shear Piezoelectric Coefficient using Physics-Informed Neural Networks under Exact Boundary and Initial Constraints
articles.abstract: The shear piezoelectric coefficient $e_{15}$ governs the shear-mode electromechanical coupling in piezoelectric micromachined ultrasonic transducers (PMUTs) and surface acoustic wave (SAW) devices, but measuring it typically requires destructive resonance testing on dedicated specimens. On simulated data, $e_{15}$ can instead be recovered non-destructively from sparse, noisy subsurface wavefield observations using a constrained physics-informed neural network (PINN). By building exact spatial distance functions and temporal multipliers directly into the network output, the clamped, grounded boundaries and resting initial state hold automatically, leaving the loss with only the interior equations of coupled electro-elastodynamics and the data misfit. Non-dimensional scaling brings all governing coefficients within one decade of O(1), and the setup removes the boundary and initial-condition penalty weights that soft-constraint methods must tune. In a six-way comparison (plane-strain PZT-5H, manufactured wavefield, 30 dB noise), a soft-penalty baseline with adaptive weights converges to an erroneous $e_{15}$ in four of the five runs (51.7% mean error), and fixed penalties reach an error of 0.85% only after a second-order optimization stage. The constrained formulations reach mean $e_{15}$ errors between 0.15% and 0.51% with held-out displacement errors below 1%. Within these variants, the spatial multiplier gives rapid first-order convergence, and the quadratic temporal multiplier lowers the early-time electrostatic residual by a factor of 6.8 versus a linear one. On finite-element data along one subsurface line, the full formulation recovers $e_{15}$ with 1.19% mean error at 30 dB and keeps it between 0.65% and 2.71% across a 40 to 0 dB noise sweep. Finally, training on displacements alone still recovers $e_{15}$ with mean errors of 0.45% on finite-element and 1.64% on manufactured data.

articles.title: Local and itinerant orbital contributions to the gyromagnetic response of paramagnetic metals
articles.abstract: Orbitronics exploits orbital angular momentum to generate and manipulate angular-momentum currents for controlling magnetisation, offering new approaches to magnetic memory and logic. A quantitative description of this process requires establishing how orbital angular momentum contributes to magnetic moments and, consequently, to the gyromagnetic response that governs magnetisation dynamics. Here, we present a first-principles framework for calculating the effective gyromagnetic tensor (g') of paramagnetic metals, consistently incorporating local and itinerant orbital contributions, spin-orbit coupling, and both state- and occupation-change effects. Applying the framework to V and Pt, we find that orbital paramagnetic responses are comparable to or larger than spin contributions and substantially modify g' from the free-electron value. The atom-centered approximation can underestimate the orbital response by approximately a factor of two, while neglecting occupation changes produces significant errors in the calculated g'. Our calculated g' values for V and Pt agree with experiment, while their pronounced dependence on band filling reveals a route to engineering angular-momentum responses through electronic-structure control. The results establish the modern theory of orbital magnetism as an essential ingredient for describing gyromagnetic response and provide a framework for identifying materials with enhanced orbital functionalities.

articles.title: Machine-Learned Interatomic Potential for the Mo-S-Al-O System
articles.abstract: We develop a machine-learned neuroevolution potential (NEP) for the Mo-S-Al-O system, targeting MoS$_2$ heteroepitaxy on c-plane sapphire, $α$-Al$_2$O$_3$(0001). The potential is trained on 63,611 PBE+D3 structures distilled from about 1.1 million curated density-functional-theory (DFT) configurations, using an energy-difference loss function that directly targets interfacial and orientation-dependent energies. On held-out data, the energy and force errors are 29 meV/atom and 0.23 eV/$\mathring{A}$. Validated against DFT on a suite of physical properties, the NEP reproduces the lattice constants within 0.3 %, the elastic constants within 17 %, the phonon dispersions with mean deviations below 2.5%, and the surface energies within 1.3 %. At the MoS$_2$/sapphire interface, it reproduces the adhesion energy minimum within 0.8 %, the interfacial energy within 2.2 % and the most stable orientation of the monolayer. It preserves the DFT-predicted energetic ordering of edges, point defects (Spearman $ρ$ = 0.995) and mirror-twin boundaries ($ρ$ = 1.0), and reproduces tilt grain-boundary energies within 8 % ($ρ$ = 0.98) and stacking-fault energy barriers within 14 %. The resulting potential enables future studies of the atomic-scale mechanisms of defect formation in two-dimensional heteroepitaxy.

articles.title: Magnetic order in Co[Cr(CN)$_6$]$_{2/3}\cdot z$H$_2$O and its interplay with correlated vacancy order
articles.abstract: Prussian blue analogues (PBAs) are versatile hybrid framework materials that often exhibit local and long-range departures from their cubic parent structure, influencing their functionality. Long-range magnetic order is common in PBAs, owing to magnetic interactions between transition metal ions via bridging cyanide ligands in the structure. Here we report the magnetic structure of cobalt (II) hexacyanochromate, Co[Cr(CN)$_6$]$_{2/3}\cdot z$H$_2$O, determined using neutron powder diffraction. No evidence for magnetostriction at the magnetic ordering temperature is observed in contrast to the reported behaviour of a related PBA. Following experimental characterisation of the magnetic order of this PBA, we employ a simple Monte Carlo model to gain a better understanding of the relationship between hexacyanometallate vacancy distributions and magnetic ordering behaviour in these materials. This model shows that magnetic ordering is robust to the extent and nature of vacancy correlations, with only minor effects noticeable in the critical region, suggesting that PBAs with the same composition but different vacancy correlations might be expected to show similar magnetic behaviour.

articles.title: Magnetically and electrically tunable nonlinear Hall effect in Tt-symmetric antiferromagnets
articles.abstract: Tt-symmetric antiferromagnets can exhibit multiferroicity with coexisting ferroelectricity and magnetic order, and thus host multiple order-parameter configurations. However, how to electrically read out these configurations is an issue meriting further investigation. Here, by combining tight-binding and first-principles calculations, we propose electrically and magnetically tunable nonlinear Hall transport in ferroelectric Tt-symmetric antiferromagnets. Model calculations show that ferroelectric switching can reverse the sign of the Berry curvature dipole (BCD), whereas the Neel vector rotation modulates its magnitude, allowing both ferroelectric and magnetic order to be reflected in the nonlinear Hall signal. First-principles calculations of the VOCl2 monolayer confirm these behaviors and predict a sizable BCD that gives rise to a potentially detectable Hall voltage. Our findings open up opportunities to integrate electrical and magnetic modulations of the nonlinear Hall effect within a single material, with potential applications in multi-state information encoding and readout in antiferromagnetic spintronics.

articles.title: Moiré reconstruction at a twisted SrTiO3 interface
articles.abstract: Twisted oxide double layers have emerged as a promising platform for exploring moiré physics, including polar topologies and emergent electronic phases. However, the intrinsic complexity of oxide surfaces, such as contamination, roughness, and the presence of two distinct terminations (AO and BO2), can complicate the identification of buried interfacial structures. Here, using atomically flat SrTiO3 membranes with a predominantly SrO-TiO2 interfacial configuration, we directly visualize a moiré-periodic structural reconstruction at the buried interface that is distinct from the geometric moiré of rigid stacking. The reconstructed interface hosts head-to-head-like polar distortions, moiré-modulated Ti electronic structure, and enhanced microwave admittance in otherwise paraelectric and insulating SrTiO3. Our work demonstrates that, with a well-defined termination, moiré reconstruction could serve as a route to emergent electrical behavior in twisted perovskite oxides.

articles.title: Molecular Curvature Enables Tubular π-Stacked Pathways in Three-Dimensional Conductive Metal-Organic Frameworks
articles.abstract: Conductive metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) are commonly constructed from planar aromatic ligands, whose geometries favor conventional π-stacking arrangements. However, intrinsically twisted ligands offer an alternative geometric approach to directing aromatic packing and constructing unconventional framework architectures. Here, we employ intrinsically twisted, butterfly-shaped dibenzo[g,p]chrysene-2,3,6,7,10,11,14,15-octaol (DBC) ligands to construct a series of lanthanide MOFs. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals an interpenetrated three-dimensional framework in which π-π interactions between the aromatic fragments generate axially extended tubular π-stacked pathways, alongside one-dimensional channels rich in hydrogen-bonding sites. Lanthanide substitution preserves the overall tubular framework topology while modulating aromatic stacking distances and local pore environments. PrDBC single crystals exhibit mixed electron-proton transport, with electron and proton conductivities reaching 1.62 x 10-3 and 4.37 x 10-4 S cm-1, respectively, at 338 K and 30% relative humidity. This work highlights molecular curvature as a structural design strategy for constructing three-dimensional conductive MOFs that integrate tubular aromatic stacks with tunable pore environments for mixed electron-proton transport.

articles.title: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulation with external field
articles.abstract: Nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations with classical path approximation (CPA-NAMD) cannot simulate the carrier dynamics under an external field. We develop CPA-NAMD-extF, a first-principles density-matrix framework for calculating field-driven electronic responses along precomputed finite-temperature ionic trajectories.
