Using in vitro refolding assays with peptides and peptide libraries, determining thermostability and crystal structures, and analysing a chicken B21 cell line by immunopeptidomics, we found that BF2*21:01 will accommodate many possible combinations at P2 and Pc-2, as well as several hydrophobic amino acids at Pc. However, marked preferences for particular peptide lengths, particular amino acids at the three anchor residues, and particular combinations of amino acids at P2 and Pc-2 as well as at P3 and Pc-3 together lead to high frequencies of major peptides while still allowing the possibility of presenting a wide peptide repertoire. These simplifying principles may eventually allow predictions of pathogen peptides with stable binding for this iconic promiscuous class I molecule, as well as providing the data for more sophisticated peptide prediction methods.

articles.title: A Retrospective Real-World Assessment of Motor Status After Stroke Using a Home-Based Brain-Computer Interface
articles.abstract: Background: Upper extremity impairment persists in many stroke survivors, and few treatments are effective for severe chronic deficits. Brain-computer interface (BCI) therapy, which pairs decoded motor-intention-associated electrophysiology with sensory feedback, has improved upper extremity impairment in randomized trials, including in patients with severe paresis. Whether these benefits translate to routine care has rarely been evaluated. This study examined upper extremity motor recovery through 1 year among patients prescribed at-home BCI therapy in clinical practice. Methods: This retrospective observational study included adults who were prescribed the IpsiHand System, an electroencephalography-based BCI, through a commercial US home therapy program, had a baseline Upper Extremity Fugl-Meyer (UEFM) assessment, and averaged >1 session per week through their last assessment. Occupational therapists administered the UEFM by video every 4 weeks. The primary outcome was UEFM change from baseline to week 12. A mixed model for repeated measures estimated change through week 52, with multiple imputation sensitivity analyses for missing data. Results: Of 452 patients included in analyses (mean time since stroke, 5.4 +/- 5.4 years), mean baseline UEFM was 20.1 +/- 14.6, with 333 patients (73.7%) having severe motor impairment (UEFM 0-28). At week 12, mean UEFM change was 4.3 points (95% CI, 3.7-4.9; P<0.001), and 31.7% achieved the minimal clinically important difference (MCID) of 5.25 points. Mean change reached the MCID at week 16 (5.6, 95% CI [4.8, 6.4]). Model-estimated change in UEFM continued to improve through 1 year, being 6.1 (95% CI, 5.5-6.8) at week 24 and 8.1 (95% CI, 6.8-9.4) at week 52. Conclusions: Among regular users of at-home BCI therapy in routine care, most of whom had severe chronic impairment, UEFM scores improved by 12 weeks, reached MCID by 16 weeks, and continued to increase through 1 year. At-home BCI therapy merits evaluation in randomized trials with follow-up beyond 12 weeks.

articles.title: A decision-only model as a low-cost judge of medical AI answers
articles.abstract: Background. Testing and deploying medical AI systems at scale already results in more outputs than clinicians can review, and the use of large language models (LLMs) as judges is growing rapidly. Decision-only models, cheap and fast models that return structured probabilities rather than text, offer a potentially scalable option for that goal. Methods. In an OSF pre-registered evaluation, we tested TypeSafe Jev 1.13 as a judge on tasks from five validated clinical benchmarks: rubric grading (HealthBench), planted clinical errors (When Rubrics Fail), risk in AI-written clinical documents (MedVAL), counseling ratings and failures (CounselBench) and physicians' preferences between answers (Real-POCQi). Comparators were expert raters' agreement with each other, OpenAI Decisions, GPT-6 Luna, a proposed hybrid team combining decision models and a cheap LLM and, as frontier comparators, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Opus 5.5. The main outcome was plain agreement with the expert label. Results. The test comprised 25,091 units and 213,913 model calls. Jev's agreement with expert labels averaged 64.7% over six tasks. On 3,614 matched units it averaged 66.1%, against 65.0% for Opus and 60.7% for Sol, and it was non-inferior to both on four of six tasks. Jev judged the whole pool in 17 minutes for US$1.46; per judgment, it cost 1/34 of Sol's price and 1/152 of Opus's. A preset cutoff held its false-alarm rate on fresh planted-error answers, and in simulation, reviewing Jev's least-sure answers first found 1.4 times the errors of a random audit. Still, omissions were hard for both: at the same false-alarm rate, Jev missed 55.6% of planted omissions and Opus 48.1%, and Opus caught 8.8 points more planted errors overall. Conclusions. Across more than 200,000 model calls, a decision-only model was non-inferior to two frontier judges on most tasks at a small fraction of their cost and time, while reporting how sure it was of every call. With local cutoffs and expert oversight of omissions and clinical documents, judging every output of a deployed medical AI system becomes more affordable.

articles.title: A personal network analysis of health-advice seeking and dietary influence in a rural community
articles.abstract: Health advice circulates through everyday relationships. The sources of informal health authority are less clear: the adviser's knowledge and conduct, or their network position. We examine personal network data from 89 adults in a rural community (1,625 respondent-contact relationships). We distinguish contacts consulted for health advice from contacts who tried to change the respondent's eating, model both relations with multilevel and penalised regressions, and test their differences. Both relations are embedded in frequent, close, and commensal ties and point to contacts more educated than the respondent. We find no characteristic that is more strongly associated with one relation than with the other. Health advice seeking also correlates with co-residence, the marital relationship, and responsibility for cooking. Respondents perceive their advisers as healthier, but advisers' own reports give no evidence of healthier diets or lower body mass. Informal health authority here is constituted by relational position (intimacy, domestic food work, and a contact's higher education relative to the respondent). We find no evidence that it rests on demonstrated conduct. Interventions that work through nominated advisers should not assume that being consulted implies expertise. Our design is cross-sectional and single-site. Future dyadic and longitudinal studies should test whether advice is followed.

articles.title: Allostatic load as a potential pathway linking exposomic risk to early-onset cancer: a matched case-control study in the All of Us Research Program
articles.abstract: Background: Early-onset cancer (EoC) incidence is rising worldwide, yet risk models built on isolated exposures or rare pathogenic variants capture little of the cumulative environmental burden experienced by younger adults. Allostatic load (AL), the cumulative physiological burden of chronic stress, can be measured from routine laboratory values and vital signs and is a candidate biological pathway linking environmental exposures to carcinogenesis. Methods: We conducted a 1:4 matched case-control study nested within the NIH All of Us Research Program, including 7,550 participants and 1,510 cancers diagnosed before age 50, of which 298 were exposome-related (the primary outcome). We derived an exposomic risk score (ERS) from 12 survey-based measures and an eight-component AL score from electronic health record data, and used mediation analysis to estimate the proportion of the ERS-EoC association operating through AL. Results: A higher ERS was associated with higher AL ({beta}=0.18 standard deviations [SD] per SD; 95% CI 0.16-0.20), and each SD increase in AL was associated with 21% higher odds of EoC (odds ratio 1.21; 95% CI 1.15-1.28). For exposome-related EoC, AL mediated 17.0% (95% CI 7.4-49.5%) of the association between the ERS and EoC, with significant total, direct, and indirect effects that were robust to lag, scoring, and age-adjustment sensitivity analyses. Across all EoC, the proportion mediated was 48.8% (95% CI 21.2-186.5%). Conclusions: AL is a candidate biomarker and potential pathway through which cumulative environmental burden relates to EoC, warranting prospective validation in independent cohorts.

articles.title: Alzheimers disease and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers in a real-world young-onset dementia cohort.
articles.abstract: Background: Young onset dementia is frequently misdiagnosed, particularly where neurodegenerative and primary psychiatric disorders (PPD) overlap. Plasma biomarkers measure current pathology, whereas polygenic risk scores (PRS) capture lifelong genetic risk. Whether PRS derived from late-onset and population samples transfer to young-onset presentations, and how they relate to plasma biomarkers, is unknown. Methods: We studied 687 participants of European ancestry from the Markers in Neuropsychiatric Disorders (MiND) Study, a prospective young-onset neuropsychiatry cohort: 195 healthy controls (HC), 283 PPD, 55 Alzheimers disease (AD) and 154 non-AD neurodegenerative disease (oNDG). PRS for AD, a cross-disorder psychiatric factor (PSY), frontotemporal dementia, Lewy body dementia and Parkinsons disease were computed with PRS CS, excluding the APOE locus. Plasma NfL, GFAP and p-tau217 were available for 332 participants. Models were adjusted for age, sex and APOE e4 dose. Results: Relative to HC, the AD PRS was associated with AD (OR 1.69 per SD, 95% CI 1.17-2.45) but not PPD (0.95, 0.77-1.16). The PSY PRS showed the reciprocal pattern (PPD 1.29, 1.05-1.58; AD 1.00, 0.72-1.40). No PRS was associated with any plasma protein. In distinguishing PPD from oNDG, NfL was the strongest discriminator (OR 2.15, 1.62-2.83). The AD PRS was also associated with oNDG (1.38, 1.11-1.71), without improving discrimination (AUC 0.764 for NfL alone versus 0.773 combined). Conclusion: In young onset presentations, AD and psychiatric polygenic risk are disease-specific and independent of plasma biomarkers of neurodegeneration. Their combined diagnostic value requires evaluation in larger, longitudinal pre-clinical cohorts.

articles.title: Analytic Interoperability Framework for High-Fidelity Representation of Perioperative Electronic Health Record Data in the OMOP Common Data Model Using Clinical Representation and Analytic Concept Reconstruction
articles.abstract: Objective To evaluate whether complex perioperative electronic health record (EHR) data can be represented within the Observational Medical Outcomes Partnership (OMOP) Common Data Model (CDM) while preserving clinically meaningful analytic concepts. Materials and Methods Data from 31,158 consecutive adult elective surgical encounters (October 2015 - September 2025) were extracted from an academic medical center Epic Clarity database. Source concepts required for a postoperative respiratory failure dataset were manually mapped to OMOP using the OHDSI Athena vocabulary and classified by Health Level 7 equivalence categories under strict and lenient criteria. SQL-based workflows reconstructed clinical representations and analytic concepts, which were validated against the native Epic implementation. Results The reference dataset comprised 28 analytic variables derived from 538 source concepts. Under strict criteria, 40.7% of mappings were equal; under lenient criteria permitting clinical equivalence despite terminology or granularity differences, 97.4% were classified as equal. OMOP achieved >99% cohort concordance. Among 31,083 shared encounters, reconstructed analytic variables showed high agreement, with meaningful differences primarily involving vasopressor infusion identification, body mass index selection, and payer assignment; admission source accounted for most discordant cohort assignments. Discussion Concept equivalence alone incompletely characterized analytic interoperability. Reconstruction of clinical representations and analytic concepts from standardized OMOP concepts preserved analytic fidelity despite incomplete exact concept matching. Conclusions Complex perioperative EHR data can be represented within OMOP with high implementation fidelity despite imperfect concept equivalence. Evaluating preservation of clinically meaningful analytic concepts, rather than vocabulary equivalence alone, provides a practical framework for interoperable perioperative research.

articles.title: Associations Between Cannabis Use and Sleep Outcomes in a Sample of Pregnant Women
articles.abstract: Importance. Both sleep difficulties and cannabis use during pregnancy (CUP) are common and associated with adverse birth and offspring outcomes. Sleep problems are a commonly reported motive for cannabis use during pregnancy. Objective. Estimate associations between cannabis use during pregnancy and common sleep difficulties across trimesters. Design, Setting, and Participants. This cohort study recruited pregnant women with lifetime cannabis use who used (n=298) and did not use (n=143) cannabis during pregnancy. Women who reported heavy episodic alcohol consumption or use of other illicit substances were excluded. Some women tested positive for cotinine in urine drug screens. Exposures. Cannabis use was assessed at each trimester using self-report and urine drug screening. Presence of the nicotine metabolite, cotinine, was measured via urine drug screening at each trimester. Cannabis use during pregnancy (CUP) status was defined separately for each trimester as use versus no use and was treated as a time-varying exposure. The nicotine metabolite cotinine was included as a covariate in all models to account for nicotine exposure. Motivation for cannabis use during pregnancy was assessed during the first trimester. Main Outcomes and Measures. Insomnia symptoms (Women's Health Initiative Insomnia Rating Scale), daytime sleepiness (Epworth Sleepiness Scale), subjective sleep quality (Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index single item), and restless legs symptoms were assessed at each trimester. Results. A CUP Status x Trimester interaction was observed for insomnia symptoms (F(2,737.81)=4.98, PFDR=0.03) wherein use during the third trimester was associated with heightened insomnia. Women reporting sleep difficulties as a motive for use reported worse insomnia symptoms (F(1, 223)=13.09, PFDR=0.001) and worse sleep quality (F(1, 219)=7.86, PFDR=0.01), relative to those using for other reasons. Conclusion. Elevated third trimester insomnia symptoms among pregnant women using cannabis compared to women who did not use cannabis suggest a potential trimester-sensitive association. Despite perceptions that cannabis improves sleep, women who reported sleep as their motive for CUP during the first trimester experienced greater insomnia symptoms and poorer sleep quality across pregnancy than those using cannabis for other reasons. Additional studies are needed to determine whether sleep-related difficulties precede cannabis use, follow it, are modified by it, or represent an epiphenomenon.

articles.title: Critical roles of sublattice chemistry in governing mechanical behavior and deformation mechanism of L12-type chemically complex intermetallic alloys
Defect-Directed Regeneration of Spent LiNi0.8Co0.1Mn0.1O2 with Functional Disordered Surface
How Initial Out-of-Plane Texture Governs Mechanical Properties and Microstructure Evolution in Cu Sheets
Molecular descriptors-guided decoupling of Zn2+-polysulfide interactions enables kinetically accelerated zinc-sulfur batteries
Boosting Efficient Water Oxidation via Photothermal‐Enhanced High‐Entropy Oxides With Dual AEM and LOM Pathways
articles.abstract: High‐entropy oxides (HEOs) with photothermal conversion capability provide a promising platform for enhancing the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) in electrocatalytic water splitting. In this work, the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM), the lattice oxygen mechanism (LOM), and photothermal effects are integrated into a single reaction system through Fe doping into HEOs. By combining theoretical calculations and experimental characterizations, we reveal that Fe doping optimally tailors the adsorption/desorption energetics of intermediates along the AEM, while simultaneously introducing oxygen vacancies that modulate the metal‐oxygen electronic environment and promote LOM participation. This dual‐pathway activation, enabled by the high‐entropy rock‐salt structure, enhances catalytic activity. In addition, the photothermal effect of (FeMgCoNiCuZn)O1−x can accelerate interfacial charge‐transfer kinetics and facilitate OOH* deprotonation. Under Xe‐lamp irradiation, Fe doping lowers the apparent activation energy for OER from 15.3 to 11.2 kJ mol−1, and the catalyst achieves oxygen evolution current densities of 10 and 50 mA cm−2 at overpotentials of 159 and 247 mV. More importantly, it exhibits outstanding long‐term durability, maintaining stable operation for over 1500 h at 1 A cm−2. These findings underscore the potential of Fe‐doping hexanary HEOs as a highly efficient candidate for electrocatalytic water splitting.

articles.title: Unlocked Covalent Competition in Asymmetric La/Sr‐O‐Fe Motif Activates Lattice Oxygen for Selective Methane Oxidation
articles.abstract: Controlling lattice‐oxygen reactivity in transition‐metal (TM) oxides is essential for Mars‐van Krevelen selective oxidations, yet conventional strategies that tune TM1‐O‐TM2 bridges suffer from covalent competition between adjacent redox‐active cations, which generates site heterogeneity and degrades selectivity. Herein, taking Ruddlesden–Popper LaSrFeO4 (A2BO4) as a model, we demonstrate that constructing asymmetric A‐O‐B motifs (i.e., La‐O‐Fe and Sr‐O‐Fe) provides a distinct route to overcome this limitation. Combined experiments and DFT calculations reveal that the A‐O‐B configuration could convert redox‐inert A‐site cations into direct electronic contributors to oxygen, which unlocks the covalent competition, substantially enabling promoted electron density over oxygen and enhanced Fe─O bond covalency. Consequently, LaSrFeO4 displays much lower methane activation barrier (∼1.24 eV) than its perovskite counterpart, LaFeO3, with an Fe‐O‐Fe motif (1.90 eV), ultimately affording a 2.35‐fold increase in syngas yield with 97% selectivity. This discovery reveals that asymmetric A‐O‐B coordination may serve as a promising structural strategy, distinct from B‐O‐B modulation, for modulating the electronic properties and reactivity of lattice oxygen.

articles.title: Acoustic Levitation Engineered Au‐InSe Schottky Junctions for Single‐Molecule SERS Sensing
articles.abstract: Detecting single molecules with high sensitivity and specificity is of great scientific and practical interest. Surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is an ultrasensitive molecular detection technique for single‐molecule detection. However, the fabrication of ultrasensitive single‐molecule SERS substrates remains a key goal. Herein, we report an acoustic levitation assisted containerless strategy to construct InSe‐Au Schottky junctions with robust interfacial bonding, achieving single‐molecule detection of zeptomolar level and an EF of 1010. The controllable acoustic radiation pressure inside the levitated droplet induced robust interfacial coupling of InSe‐Au Schottky junctions, which was verified by HAADF‐STEM etc. The bianalyte Poisson‐binomial statistical model confirmed single molecule origin of Raman signals. Linear relationship between detection probability and ultralow Rhodamine B (RhB) concentration was established. Single molecule SERS mapping directly visualized molecular adsorption sites, identifying strongly bonded junction interface as critical signal enhancement region. The enhancement mechanism is primarily attributed to chemical enhancement, wherein the built‐in electric field facilitates multiple photoinduced charge‐transfer pathways, while the localized surface plasmon resonance of Au couples with out‐of‐plane dipole of InSe to enhance light harvesting. This strategy is material‐generalizable, as demonstrated by WSe2/GaSe‐Au systems with attomolar limits. This work provides new insights into engineering strongly bonded heterojunctions for single‐molecule sensing devices.

articles.title: Ag‐Se Synergistic Diffusion for Highly Homogeneous Elemental Distribution and Significantly Improved ACZTSSe Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The performance of Cu2ZnSn(SxSe1−x)4 (CZTSSe) solar cells is primarily limited by an inability to control the selenization process, where non-uniform selenium distribution leads to profound Cu–Zn cation disorder and associated performance losses. Compositional engineering, such as in (AgxCu1−x)2ZnSn(SxSe1−x)4 (ACZTSSe), can mitigate some defects; however, it fails to address the root cause: mastering the reaction kinetics to achieve elemental homogeneity. Herein, we introduce a self-sacrificing Ag2Se layer on Mo substrates that enables a bottom-up, cooperative Ag–Se diffusion pathway during grain growth. The rapid migration of Ag atoms modifies the local chemical environment, thereby acting as a kinetic driver that dramatically enhances the selenium diffusion flux. Molecular dynamics simulations confirm a 28.6% increase in the selenium diffusion coefficient (D Se), demonstrating that this kinetic enhancement activates the cooperative Ag–Se diffusion mechanism, thereby achieving a macroscopic improvement in material homogeneity. The resultant absorber exhibits an unprecedented, near-linear elemental distribution, which effectively suppresses Cu-related antisite defects (e.g., CuZn and CuSn). This superior homogeneity minimizes bulk recombination and facilitates efficient carrier transport, thereby providing a fundamental basis for the enhancement of photoelectric properties. Consequently, the champion device treated with 65 nm Ag2Se (ASe 65) achieves a power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.36% (certified as 13.91%), primarily due to a remarkable enhancement in short-circuit current density (J sc) and fill factor (FF). This work not only provides a foundational understanding of cooperative diffusion chemistry, but also establishes a novel paradigm for manipulating reaction kinetics in solid-state energy materials.

articles.title: Al3+/Ta5+ Co‐Doping Promotes Homogeneous Li+ Transport Enabling High Performance Ni‐Rich Layered Oxide Cathodes
articles.abstract: Ni‐rich layered oxide cathodes with high energy density are regarded as one of the most promising cathode candidates for achieving next‐generation high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs). However, increasing the Ni content introduces critical challenges, including undesirable phase transitions, sluggish Li+ transport, and intergranular cracking, which hinder their large‐scale application. This work demonstrates an Al3+/Ta5+ co‐doping strategy, enabling homogeneous Li+ transport in a Ni‐rich cathode by forming LiNi0.94Ta0.01Al0.05O2 (LNTAO) with refined grains and suppressed Li/Ni cation mixing. The achieved homogenization suppresses high‐voltage phase transitions and facilitates Li+ intercalation/deintercalation during cycling. It also preserves the Ni valence state and Ni─O coordination environment, maintains grain‐boundary integrity, and suppresses interfacial side reactions during prolonged cycling. Enabled by these advantages, the cycle and rate performance of the Ni‐rich cathode are effectively enhanced. This Al3+/Ta5+ co‐doping strategy provides fundamental materials‐design insights into enhancing the electrochemical performance of Ni‐rich layered cathodes through the homogenization of Li+ transport.

articles.title: Amphoteric Cu‐Doping Leading to High Thermoelectric Performance in p‐Type Bismuth Antimony Telluride
articles.abstract: The role of copper in Bi2Te3-based thermoelectric materials is not well understood, and there are conflicting results regarding its impact on thermoelectric properties. Some reports claim Cu is an electron donor after intercalating into the van der Waals-like gap of (Bi,Sb)2Te3, while others show it acting as an acceptor. Here, we help clarify this discrepancy experimentally and theoretically by demonstrating that Cu behaves as an amphoteric dopant (acceptor or donor) governed by its processing pathway. While kinetic pathways allow for Cu intercalation into the van der Waals-like gaps and electron donor behavior, thermodynamic equilibrium favors the substitution of Cu for Bi or Sb cations and acceptor behavior, which provides stronger chemical bonding and stability compared to intercalated Cu. When prioritizing thermodynamic stability, p-type Cu x Bi0.5Sb1.5Te3 exhibits high near-room-temperature zT values, with the best-performing composition among the investigated series reaching zT ≈1.36 ± 0.06 for four independently prepared x = 0.0025 samples. This arises from simultaneous improvements in both electronic properties (weighted mobility) and thermal properties (lattice thermal conductivity). Such improvements in zT for p-type (Bi,Sb)2Te3 in consistently manufactured materials would greatly benefit many applications for solid-state Peltier coolers and thermoelectric generators.

articles.title: An Ultramicroporous Ni‐Based MOF for Xe‐selective Capture and Ar/Kr/Xe Gas‐Phase Preparative Chromatography Separation in Liquid Fluoride Thorium Reactor Off‐Gases
articles.abstract: Efficient xenon separation is important for noble‐gas management in liquid fluoride thorium reactor (LFTR) off‐gas systems. Here, JUC‐86, an ultramicroporous Ni‐based metal‐organic framework, is investigated for Xe‐selective capture and Ar/Kr/Xe separation. JUC‐86 features a crystallographic aperture of approximately 5.2 Å and model‐derived pore widths of 4.1‐5.2 Å. At 298 K and 1 bar, the adsorption capacities of Xe, Kr, and Ar reach 75.6, 57.2, and 17.3 cm3 g−1, respectively. IAST calculations, isosteric heats of adsorption, and host–guest calculations consistently indicate a stronger affinity toward Xe. Under continuous‐flow conditions, JUC‐86 exhibits reproducible Xe/Kr breakthrough separation, with an average Xe capture capacity of 1.41 mmol g−1 and Kr productivity above 99.9% purity. The material also captures trace Xe from dilute Xe/Kr/Ar streams and enables effective preparative chromatographic separation of Ar, Kr, and Xe over varied operating conditions. Bonding‐based analysis further suggests a meaningful degree of intrinsic γ‐radiation tolerance. These results demonstrate the potential of JUC‐86 for Xe‐selective capture and chromatographic noble‐gas separation in advanced nuclear off‐gas management.

articles.title: BDNF‐Regulated Molecular‐to‐Material Transduction in an Ion–Electronic Memristive Biointerface for Modeling Addiction‐Related Neuroplasticity
articles.abstract: Addiction‐related memories are associated with dysregulated neurotrophic signaling and maladaptive synaptic plasticity. However, it still remains challenging in translating such disease‐relevant molecular regulation into history‐dependent and programmable material states. Herein, a brain‐derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)‐regulated ion–electronic memristive biointerface is developed by integrating a recognition module comprising a BDNF‐responsive aptamer and a tropomyosin receptor kinase B Fc chimera (TrkB‐Fc) with a photoactive sodium alginate (SA)/WO3 composite. Under 365 nm illumination, BDNF‐dependent interfacial regulation produces concentration‐ and history‐dependent conductance dynamics associated with W6+/W5+ mixed‐valence evolution. The device exhibits synaptic‐like responses, including paired‐pulse facilitation, learning–forgetting–relearning‐like dynamics, and reversible potentiation/depression‐like conductance modulation. These device‐state changes show functional correspondence with BDNF‐enhanced ΔFosB expression and morphine‐conditioned place preference, whereas ANA‐12 attenuates device‐state persistence and behavioral reinstatement in the respective experiments. Experimentally measured volatile responses are further used to construct reservoir states, while experimentally characterized nonvolatile conductance states provide a device‐informed basis for differential‐conductance readout‐weight representation in a software‐executed classification workflow, achieving a held‐out Fashion‐MNIST accuracy of 93.9%. Therefore, this work establishes a molecular‐to‐material transduction framework that converts neurotrophic regulation into programmable ion–electronic states and links biomolecular recognition, adaptive material dynamics, addiction‐related neuroplasticity, and proof‐of‐concept neuromorphic information processing.

articles.title: Back‐Contact Engineering via a MoO3/Ag Structure for Efficient Sb2(S,Se)3 Thin‐Film Solar Cells
articles.abstract: The quality of the back contact critically determines the hole extraction efficiency and interfacial recombination losses in Sb2(S,Se)3 thin‐film solar cells. High‐efficiency devices typically use the Spiro‐OMeTAD/Au structure, but the reliance on Au electrodes increases material cost, creating an efficiency‐cost trade‐off. Here, we develop a cost‐effective Spiro‐OMeTAD/MoO3/Ag composite back contact that enables the use of a low‐cost electrode while maintaining efficient carrier extraction. The Spiro‐OMeTAD/MoO3/Ag composite back contact establishes a more favorable rear‐contact configuration, facilitating hole transfer while reducing carrier accumulation and interfacial recombination. Mild annealing further improves the back‐contact properties. Transient absorption spectroscopy (TAS), electrical, and photovoltaic measurements are interpreted together and consistently support improved interfacial carrier transfer with suppressed detrimental recombination. The optimized device achieves a PCE of 10.0%, approaching the performance level of reported Au‐based Sb2(S,Se)3 cells while using a low‐cost Ag‐based electrode. This work demonstrates an effective, economical back‐contact engineering strategy that delivers high performance with cost‐effectiveness.

articles.title: Bioinspired Hydrogels with Broadly Programmable Mechanics for Soft‐Tissue Interfaces
articles.abstract: Matching the mechanical properties of repair materials to tissue-specific demands remains a major challenge in soft-tissue repair. Here we report bioinspired anisotropic gelatin hydrogels formed by directional freezing and mechanically programmed through subsequent ionic treatment. By regulating intermolecular interactions while preserving the aligned, hierarchical porous architecture, this approach spans stiffnesses relevant to brain, kidney, tendon, and cartilage. Ion identity and treatment duration enable coordinated tuning of Young's modulus from 9.7 kPa to 3.59 MPa and tensile strength from 6 kPa to 14.25 MPa, together with broad regulation of viscoelasticity, extensibility, and fracture resistance. Multiscale SAXS/WAXS characterization, molecular simulations, and finite-element analysis reveal that ion-regulated chain association and hierarchical anisotropic organization collectively govern directional load transfer and mechanical reinforcement. Sodium citrate-treated AGE-SC 36H reaches a Young's modulus of 3.59 MPa, a tensile strength of 14.25 MPa, and a fracture energy of 413,305 J m− 2, while subsequent microbial transglutaminase (MTG) stabilization improves cyclic mechanical retention and resistance to swelling and enzymatic degradation under aqueous conditions. In a rat Achilles tendon model, AGE-SC 36H (MTG) promotes organized collagen remodeling and improves functional recovery over surgical repair alone. Overall, ionic regulation offers a general strategy for programming anisotropic hydrogel mechanics across material classes.

articles.title: Boosting Selective Ammonia Electrosynthesis from Nitrate Over Noble Metal Catalysts Via Surface Oxidation Engineering
articles.abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction reaction to ammonia (NO3RR) represents a sustainable pathway for closing the nitrogen cycle. However, the inherent activity-selectivity dilemma and fierce competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) severely restrict the practical application of noble-metal-based catalysts. Here, we report a universal low-temperature surface oxidation engineering strategy to reconstruct noble-metal (Ru, Ir, Pd, Pt) electrocatalysts. The resulting modification achieves simultaneous enhancement of NO3RR activity and efficient HER suppression, addressing a key challenge that is difficult to balance in conventional noble-metal-based catalysts. The optimized carbon-supported core-shell catalyst consisting of a Ru core and ultrathin RuO2 shell (Ru@RuO2/C) enables excellent ammonia Faradaic efficiency of over 90.0% from 0.05 to −0.2 V vs. RHE, with a maximum Faradaic efficiency of 99.91% and a yield rate of 2.18 mg h−1 mgcat −1 at 0 V vs. RHE. In situ spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the Ru@RuO2/C effectively optimizes the adsorption of *NO3 and suppresses the HER owing to interfacial charge transfer and electron density redistribution across the Ru and RuO2 interface. Applying the Ru@RuO2/C as the cathode catalyst, the assembled Zinc−nitrate battery exhibits a peak power density of 60.5 mW cm−2 and a specific capacity of 829 mAh g−1 at 100 mA cm−2.

articles.title: Broad‐Spectrum Multifunctional Optoelectronic Transistor Enabled by a Type‐II Organic p‐n Heterojunction for Advanced Secure Information Processing
articles.abstract: Secure information transmission faces mounting challenges amid increasingly complex data processing and intrinsic physical limitations of conventional electronic systems. Multifunctional optoelectronic information platforms offer a promising route to overcome these constraints. Herein, we report a broad‐spectrum multifunctional optoelectronic transistor based on a type‐II organic p‐n heterojunction comprising p‐type C10‐DNTT and n‐type indandione‐terminated quinoidal compound Q4T‐4F. The extended π‐conjugation and quinoidal skeleton of Q4T‐4F significantly broaden its absorption spectrum, enabling the integration of broad‐spectrum photodetection, electrical synaptic emulation, and non‐volatile memory in a single device. The p‐n heterojunction transistor exhibits a broad spectral response from 300 to 1100 nm with a reconfigurable photoresponse modulated by both gate voltage and light intensity. Interface charge trapping endows the device with essential synaptic characteristics and robust multilevel non‐volatile memory performance. Leveraging these integrated functions, we demonstrate advanced applications including optical/electrical encryption‐decryption and reconfigurable logic gates. This work establishes a versatile platform for advancing optoelectronic systems toward secure and efficient information processing.

articles.title: Charge Transport Dynamics in Doped Organic Polymer: Effect of New Split‐Functional Dopant on an Amorphous Organic Semiconductor
articles.abstract: Understanding the microscopic mechanisms governing charge transport in electronically doped conjugated polymers is important from both fundamental and device perspectives. Here, we investigate an amorphous semiconducting polymer, PTB7‐Th, as a suitable host to incorporate a specific organic salt system. The electronically disordered polymer, when doped with a split functional dopant that consists of organic cation 4‐(acetylamino)‐2,2,6,6‐tetramethyl‐1‐oxo‐piperidinium (ATOP) and the bulky anion tetrakis[3,5‐bis(trifluoromethyl)phenyl] borate (BARF), undergoes a major enhancement in electrical transport. In addition to enhancing solubility, the BARF counterion effectively minimizes the coulombic interaction between the anion and the charge carrier on the polymer backbone, which facilitates efficient ion‐pair dissociation. A six‐order‐of‐magnitude enhancement in conductivity and a significant improvement in carrier mobility are observed in optimally doped samples. Temperature‐dependent DC conductivity measurements indicate variable‐range hopping transport, with improved hopping parameters upon doping. Additionally, AC measurements reveal faster carrier relaxation, systematic activation energy changes, and minimal ionic migration, highlighting improved electronic transport upon doping. Complementary molecular dynamics simulations capture ion–polaron and ion–ion correlations that rationalize the observed transport enhancement. The results highlight the connection from microscopic interactions to macroscopic enhancement in electrical performances while also identifying the origin of saturation beyond a critical dopant concentration.

articles.title: Correction to “Laser‐Controlled Ferrohydrodynamic Fluid Cavities for Modulation of Ultrasonic Waves”
Directional Electron Traction and Selective‐Sieving Effects Enabled by Biomimetic UIO‐66‐NH2‐Assisted Polyimide Electron Sponge for Ultra‐Durable Sodium‐Sulfur Battery
articles.abstract: Severe sodium polysulfides (NaPSs) shuttling and sluggish reaction kinetics substantially hinder the development of room‐temperature sodium‐sulfur (RT/Na‐S) batteries. Herein, a biomimetic uio‐66‐NH2‐assisted polyimide with carbon‐nanotube (uio@PI/CNT) for separator‐modification is proposed. Selective‐sieving effects induced via the inherent PI‐pore segmentation by uio‐66‐NH2 efficiently inhibit NaPSs shuttling and maintain a uniform Na+ flux for homogeneous Na‐deposition. Particularly, imide‐carbonyl and triazine moieties in PI, regarded as “electron sponge” capable of successive electron uptake and supply, exert the directional electron‐traction between external circuit and NaPSs to enable prompt electron‐donation to and electron‐extraction from NaPSs during discharging and charging, thereby remarkably reducing the sulfur‐conversion energy barriers. Integrating with enhanced electron‐conduction via CNT, effective binding with NaPSs, and high‐speed Na+ transport mediated via sufficient groups synergistically provided by PI and uio‐66‐NH2 for retaining active‐specie and timely replenishing reactants to PI catalytic centers, the fast reaction kinetics and highly stable anode are achieved. Consequently, a high reversible capacity (1248 mAh g−1) at 1 A g−1 with 96.7% cycling‐retention and an ultralow fading (0.0055%) per cycle even at 2 A g−1 are presented. The catalytic mechanism involving “electron sponge”, with the selective‐sieving effects, imparts a novel direction for exploiting the ultra‐durable sodium‐sulfur batteries.

articles.title: Donor‐Engineered Chiral Indium–Salen Complexes for Tunable Circularly Polarized Luminescence
articles.abstract: High-performance circularly polarized luminescent (CPL) materials with efficient emission and tunable chiroptical responses are highly desirable for emerging photonic and optoelectronic technologies, yet design principles for main-group CPL emitters remain underdeveloped. Here, we establish a donor-engineering strategy for chiral indium–salen complexes that controls electronic structure, excited-state relaxation, and chiroptical emission. Six enantiomeric In(III)–salen pairs bearing NMe2, NEt2, NPh2, carbazole, dibenzo[c,g]carbazole, or 9,9-dimethyl-9,10-dihydroacridine donors exhibit blue-to-green emission and solution-state CPL with |g lum| values on the order of 10− 3. In PMMA-doped films, mirror-image CPL is retained and |g lum| reaches 1.8 × 10− 2. Low-temperature measurements reveal PLQYs up to 95% and a long-lived phosphorescent contribution for the dibenzocarbazole derivative. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes the molecular structure and five-coordinate geometry of the indium–salen framework, while TD-DFT and natural transition orbital (NTO) analyses show that donor substitution systematically modulates HOMO localization and excited-state donor-to-salen charge-transfer character. These results establish donor electronics, conformational rigidity, and matrix restriction as complementary design parameters for controlling emission efficiency and CPL in molecular indium luminophores.

articles.title: Donor‐Engineered Chiral Indium–Salen Complexes for Tunable Circularly Polarized Luminescence (Adv. Funct. Mater. 88/2026)
articles.abstract: Circularly Polarized Luminescence Donor engineering transforms chiral indium–salen complexes into tunable circularly polarized luminophores. Diverse donor architectures regulate frontier‐orbital distributions, intraligand charge transfer, and excited‐state relaxation, enabling blue‐to‐green emission and enhanced CPL in rigid matrices. The cover illustrates donor‐controlled molecular design converging on a chiral indium platform and emerging as wavelength‐tunable circularly polarized light. More details can be found in the Research Article by Youngjo Kim, Min Kim, Youngmin You, Myung Hwan Park, and co‐workers (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.78009).

articles.title: Dopant‐Enhanced Inhibitory Negative Photoconductance and Hetero‐interfacial Switchable Synaptic Response in CsPbI3 Perovskite
articles.abstract: All‐inorganic halide perovskites, particularly CsPbI3, are excellent candidates for neuromorphic devices owing to their unique defect‐tolerant electronic structure and mixed ionic‐electronic transport. Here, we demonstrate that the inherent synaptic plasticity of CsPbI3 can be modulated by cationic doping and heterojunction engineering. By introducing transition metal dopants (Cu, Mn and Zn) into the perovskite lattice, we modify the trap‐state density and charge‐carrier dynamics. CsPbI3 naturally exhibits negative photoconductance (NPC) due to its defect‐mediated charge dynamics and Mn‐doping increases this effect manifold. First‐principles calculations reveal that Mn‐substitution creates highly localized states within the bandgap, significantly amplifying light‐activated charge trapping kinetics. This manifests as a robust negative photoconductance, enhancing biomimetic inhibitory responses with a high paired‐pulse depression index of 188%. Also, we show that the polarity of the optical synaptic response is not merely a bulk property but can be inverted via interfacial charge‐transfer at the CsPbI3/ZnO heterostructure. This transition from inhibitory to excitatory behavior underscores the role of material interfaces in controlling synaptic polarity. These findings establish a materials‐based strategy for developing CMOS‐compatible, dual‐mode neuromorphic architectures on monolithic substrates.

articles.title: Dual‐Interphase Engineering With Nano‐Alumina and CVD Carbon Enabling High‐Temperature Calendar Aging Mitigation in Silicon‐Oxide Anode
articles.abstract: The stability of high‐temperature storage in silicon‐based high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries (LIBs) is highly critical in the operation temperature beyond 40°C, typically in tropical and subtropical regions globally. The unexpected stability of high‐temperature storage would lead to severe self‐discharge, which accelerates the decay of remaining capacity, side reaction‐induced electrolyte decomposition, and fire‐hazard risk. To address such issues, a strategy of solid‐state mechanofusion‐chemical vapor deposition (SSM‐CVD) is proposed to construct a dual‐phase nano‐alumina (Al2O3) and dense carbon on the micron‐sized silicon oxide (SiO) particles (SiO@Al2O3/C), with the purpose of suppressing the self‐discharge behavior induced by charge transfer between graphite (Gr) and SiO in the negative electrode. With the presence of such dual‐phase coating, a stable solid electrolyte interphase has been constructed on both SiO@Al2O3/C and graphite. The electrochemical performance at high‐temperature storage (60°C for 14 days) suggests that the capacity retention reaches 97.81% with a capacity recovery rate of 99.46% in the as‐assembled commercial 18 650 cylindrical cells, which approaches a record‐setting value under the severe high‐temperature storage condition. This work also elucidates high‐temperature failure mechanisms and offers an SSM‐CVD engineering strategy for stabilizing both capacity and safety in silicon‐based high‐energy LIBs.

articles.title: EDTA‐Functionalized Metal‐Organic Framework With Synergistic Adsorption and Facilitated Iodine Conversion for High‐Performance Zinc‐Iodine Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc‐iodine batteries (ZIBs) have attracted significant attention due to intrinsic safety, low cost, and high energy density. However, practical deployment is hindered by the polyiodide shuttle effect, sluggish conversion kinetics, and instability of high‐valent iodine species. Accordingly, we design a multifunctional metal‐organic framework (MOF‐808‐EDTA) as a robust iodine host via a post‐synthetic modification strategy. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses demonstrate that EDTA functionalization preserves the crystalline framework and nanopores, ensuring spatial confinement of iodine species. Moreover, the strategy enhances the Lewis acidity of Zr−O clusters, optimizing the electronic structure of the MOF framework, and strengthens iodine chemical anchoring by multifunctional nitrogen sites. Through physicochemical confinement and electronic structure modulation, MOF‐808‐EDTA synergistically lowers the reaction barrier and promotes reversible iodine conversion. Meanwhile, nucleophilic Br− in the electrolyte activates and stabilizes I+, further extending the reaction pathway. Consequently, both two‐electron and four‐electron ZIBs exhibit rapid kinetics and excellent rate capability, delivering 47 000 cycles at 10 A g−1 and 100 000 cycles at 20 A g−1, respectively. The present work designs a functionalized MOF‐based host via single‐molecule modification, constructs a reaction environment favorable for iodine species adsorption and conversion, offering a new paradigm for cathode design in multi‐electron conversion ZIBs.

articles.title: Effects of LLZO Microstructure Porosity, LLZO/Li‐Metal Interfacial Polarization Resistance, and Applied Areal Current Density on Li‐Metal Dendrite Formation in LLZO Bilayer Symmetric Cells
articles.abstract: Idealized Li-Li symmetric cells utilizing porous-dense Li7La3Zr2O12 (LLZO) “bilayers” are simulated to characterize the risks for “interfacial” and “internal” Li-metal dendrite formation and provide insight for bilayer full cells. The higher interfacial area of the porous LLZO/Li-metal interface decreases the interfacial overpotentials and increases the Critical Current Density (CCD) for interfacial dendrites. Decreasing the polarization resistance (ASRpolar ) of the LLZO/Li-metal interface further increases the CCD for interfacial dendrites. Simultaneously, tortuous transport paths through the porous LLZO layer amplify the local ionic current densities, thereby increasing the risk of internal dendrite formation if internal defects/pores are present. Decreasing the ASRpolar value, the microstructure porosity of the porous LLZO layer, or the applied areal current density all decrease the risk for internal dendrites. If interfacial dendrites have the lowest CCD, the microstructure porosity in a bilayer full cell may be increased to increase the Li-metal anode areal capacity with minimal effect on the interfacial CCD. If internal dendrites have the lowest CCD, the bilayer full cell design should be tailored to the operating conditions, with higher microstructure porosity utilized for lower cycling rates and high energy density applications, and lower microstructure porosity utilized for higher cycling rates and high power density applications.

articles.title: Electrodynamics of Charge Balance in Quantum‐Dot Light‐Emitting Diodes
articles.abstract: Efficient quantum‐dot light‐emitting diodes are commonly thought to require balanced electron and hole injection, leading to device designs that suppress electron injection or enhance hole injection. Paradoxically, experimental studies frequently show that increasing electron injection does not compromise efficiency and can even improve it, a contradiction that has remained unresolved. Here, we systematically modulate electron injection by engineering the ZnMgO/Al contact and quantitatively evaluate charge balance in QLEDs. Despite a 3.98‐fold difference in current density between devices with suppressed and enhanced electron injection, both exhibit nearly identical external quantum efficiencies, exceeding that of the control device. We show that this counterintuitive phenomenon originates from electrodynamic redistribution of the internal electric field in the multilayer stacked device architecture. Specifically, enhancing the conductivity of one layer, such as the electron transport layer, reduces its voltage drop and redistributes the electric field toward the hole transport and emissive layers, thereby facilitating hole injection and restoring charge balance. These results uncover an electrodynamic mechanism of charge balance governed by internal field redistribution, challenge the conventional “weak electron” optimization paradigm, and suggest an alternative design strategy—enhancing rather than blocking electron injection—for simultaneously achieving high efficiency, low power consumption, and improved operational stability in QLEDs.

articles.title: Electronic‐State Regulation Enables Robust Infrared Camouflage at Extreme Temperatures
articles.abstract: Stable suppression of midwave infrared (MWIR, 3–5 µm) thermal emissivity at elevated temperatures is critical for advanced thermal camouflage applications. However, most infrared camouflage systems suffer from rapid emissivity rebound at high temperatures due to oxidative degradation, microstructural instability, or enhanced phonon-mediated radiation. Herein, a vacancy-associated electronic-state regulation strategy is developed to achieve robust low MWIR emissivity in perovskite SrZrO3. Electronic-state regulation modifies the MWIR optical response by modulating defect and carrier states while maintaining low infrared absorption. For optimized Co-doped SrZr1− x Co x O3- δ (SZCO), DFT calculations yield an electronic gap of approximately 0.51 eV, accompanied by oxygen-vacancy formation and a 67% increase in carrier concentration. Consequently, the optimized SZCO-3 sample exhibits an ultralow MWIR emissivity of 0.296 at room temperature and retains a low value of 0.394 even at 1100°C. High-temperature in situ characterizations and durability tests confirm the excellent thermal robustness of SZCO-3. Meanwhile, thermally activated charge transport and structural symmetry evolution contribute to maintaining its stable MWIR response at elevated temperatures. These findings establish vacancy-associated electronic-state regulation as an effective strategy for designing thermally robust, low-emissivity ceramics for high-temperature infrared camouflage applications.

articles.title: Enzyme Cascade Nanoreactor for Infection Clearance and Regenerative Immune Remodeling in Orthopedic Biofilm Infection
articles.abstract: Implant‐associated biofilm infection remains a major obstacle to orthopedic repair because persistent bacterial colonization and dysregulated innate immune responses hinder infection resolution and osseointegration. Here, an acid‐responsive enzyme cascade nanoreactor, CaO2@CuMOF‐GOx, is engineered to couple biofilm metabolic disruption with regenerative immune remodeling. The nanoreactor comprises an oxygen‐generating CaO2 component, a Cu‐based metal–organic framework catalytic interface, and immobilized glucose oxidase (GOx). In the acidic and oxygen‐limited biofilm microenvironment, CaO2@CuMOF‐GOx supplies O2 to sustain GOx‐catalyzed glucose consumption and generates H2O2 that undergoes Cu‐mediated Fenton‐like conversion into hydroxyl radical‐mediated oxidative stress. This cascade disrupts bacterial energy metabolism, redox homeostasis, and membrane integrity, thereby suppressing planktonic bacteria and mature biofilms. Importantly, CaO2@CuMOF‐GOx also reshapes the inflammatory microenvironment by promoting timely neutrophil apoptosis under metabolic and oxidative stress. These apoptotic neutrophils are efficiently cleared by macrophages, leading to efferocytosis‐associated macrophage reprogramming toward a pro‐reparative phenotype and inflammation resolution. Metabolomic profiling and neutrophil RNA sequencing substantiate bacterial metabolic collapse and activation of intrinsic apoptotic programs in neutrophils. In a rat implant‐associated infection model, local CaO2@CuMOF‐GOx treatment reduces bacterial burden, alleviates peri‐implant inflammation, and enhances bone regeneration and osseointegration. This study presents a biofilm‐responsive immunometabolic nanotherapy that integrates infection eradication with regenerative immune remodeling for orthopedic implant‐associated infections.

articles.title: Gate‐Tuneable Single‐Photon Emitters in WSe2 Monolayer Created via AFM Nanoindentation on Rigid SiO2/Si Substrates
articles.abstract: Single-photon emitters (SPEs) hosted by two-dimensional (2D) semiconducting materials are envisioned for next-generation quantum applications. However, SPE creation in 2D semiconductors on rigid substrates like SiO2/Si via nanoindentation is a technological gap, critical for interfacing SPEs with photonic circuits/cavities. Here, we report a protocol for deterministically creating SPEs in monolayer WSe2 on SiO2/Si substrates using a sharp diamond AFM (atomic force microscope) tip. A displacement-controlled indentation process is developed, allowing indent depths > 150 nm necessary for creating SPEs. Sharp defect peaks (∼200 µeV) are observed in cryogenic (4 K) photoluminescence (PL) spectrum at the nanoindented sites and are stable up to ∼120 K. 76% of sites exhibit sharp defect-bound peaks confirmed by power-dependent, temperature-dependent, and time-resolved PL (TRPL). AFM and PL mapping link these peaks to the indent periphery. The peaks show sub-linewidth spectral jitter, no blinking, and single-photon nature in second-order autocorrelation (g( 2 )) measurements. SPEs can be switched on or off and classical background emission suppressed by electrical gating. Gate-voltage dependent TRPL shows that SPE dynamics are electrically tuneable, pointing the way toward high-purity SPEs. The protocol is also extended to other 2D materials and photonic-circuit compatible substrates, advancing the scalable integration of 2D semiconductor-based SPEs.

articles.title: Giant Magnetization Enhancement at the Ultrathin Limit of an Orthoferrite
articles.abstract: Low-dimensional magnetic systems have received significant interest due to their high scalability and energy efficiency for future electromagnetic applications. However, low-dimensional magnetism at finite temperature is subject to Mermin–Wagner fluctuations, which make its realization highly challenging. Here, we propose structural modulation in the thin-film structure of an orthoferrite system to achieve a high low-dimensional magnetic response at room temperature. ErFeO3 epitaxial thin film with atomically precise thickness control demonstrates that the magnetic response at 300 K can be significantly enhanced compared to its bulk counterpart. The magnetic response reaches its maximum value of 3.7 µ B/f.u. for the 2 nm-thick epitaxial film. The characteristic domain structure resulting from epitaxial strain and orbital reconstruction at the surface, both arising from the thin film geometry, has been proposed as the microscopic origin of the giant magnetization enhancement. We show that magnetic ordering can indeed be realized in the 2D limit, with deliberate structural control of orthoferrite systems.

articles.title: Giant Magnetization Enhancement at the Ultrathin Limit of an Orthoferrite (Adv. Funct. Mater. 88/2026)
articles.abstract: Low‐Dimensional Magnetism Contrary to conventional expectation, orthoferrite ErFeO3 is shown to exhibit giant magnetic enhancement as it approaches ultrathin limit. In the Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.78476), Sungkyun Park, Sang Ho Oh, Woo Seok Choi, and co‐workers propose two microscopic origins: suppression of magnetic domains near the interface which minimize magnetic pinning, and orbital reconstruction at the surface which modifies the exchange interaction. These results demonstrate how structural modulation can dramatically alter magnetic response in low dimension.

articles.title: Heteroatom Acceptor Engineering Boosts NIR‑II Phototheranostics of Quinoid–Donor–Acceptor Semiconducting Polymers
articles.abstract: Multimodal phototheranostics utilizing a single, integrated molecular platform represents a streamlined and efficient strategy for precise cancer therapy. Herein, we first report a rationally engineered quinoid–donor–acceptor (Q–D–A) molecule, designated PAQM-PT, through deliberate heteroatom acceptor modulation. This designed system concurrently delivers absorption redshift, reduced aggregation tendency, and second near-infrared (NIR-II) emission enhancement. The resulting PAQM-PT nanoparticles (NPs) exhibit an excellent molar extinction coefficient (ε) of 2.82 × 105 M− 1 cm− 1 and decent fluorescence quantum yield (FLQY) of 0.054%, boosting NIR-II brightness to 152.28 M− 1 cm− 1 (ε × FLQY). Furthermore, under 808 nm laser irradiation (1.0 W cm− 2), PAQM-PT NPs show an extremely high photothermal conversion efficiency (PCE) of 87.3%. This work reports a breakthrough polymer that combines strong NIR-II fluorescence brightness with high PCE—a dual achievement previously unreported for polymeric agents. These properties enable precise tumor delineation and effective tumor ablation without any relapses with high biosafety via NIR-II fluorescence imaging (FLI)–photoacoustic imaging (PAI)–photothermal imaging (PTI) trimodal to guided photothermal therapy (PTT) in an orthotopic mouse breast tumor model. This work not only presents a pioneering Q–D–A-type phototheranostic agent with multimodal imaging but also provides a new design perspective for developing high-performance phototheranostic systems for practical cancer treatment.

articles.title: Hierarchically Aligned Core–Shell Yarn‐Shaped Triboelectric Yarns With Coupled High‐Density Charge Trapping and Efficient Transport
articles.abstract: Yarn-shaped triboelectric materials (Y-TENGs) hold great promise for high-performance wearable electronics, but conventional designs suffer from low charge density due to limited internal macro- and microscale structures. Here, an aligned side-by-side triboelectric yarn (ASS-TY) is developed through a one-step conjugate electrospinning strategy. It synergistically combines reduced interfacial charge transfer resistance and enhanced axial charge transport along the core yarn, enabled by the continuous alignment of the conductive cores in the side-by-side (SBS) structure. COMSOL simulations (2D and 3D) confirm that the SBS configuration significantly increases the surface potential and outperforms randomly oriented fiber layers. The ASS-TY achieves a deep trap energy of 1.02 eV and a deep trap density of 1.83 × 1021 eV−1 m−3, about five times higher than non-SBS structures, effectively suppressing charge leakage. The ASS-TY device delivers a stable output of 197 V and 131.20 mW m− 2, and when integrated into gloves, enables reliable self-powered sensing. This work provides a structural design paradigm for high-performance triboelectric materials and new insights for wearable electronics.

articles.title: Hierarchically Integrated RGO/CNT Aerogel and Graphene Film in Aramid Honeycomb for Synergistic Microwave Absorption and Thermal Management
articles.abstract: The development of multifunctional composites that combine microwave absorption (MA) with effective thermal management in lightweight structural materials is essential for electronic systems. However, achieving this integration presents significant challenges due to the conflicting demands of electromagnetic attenuation, heat dissipation, and mechanical integrity. Herein, a multifunctional composite material incorporates a reduced graphene oxide/carbon nanotube (RGO/CNT) aerogel within a perforated aramid honeycomb structure was presented, enhanced by a highly thermally conductive graphene film (GF) on its lower surface. The honeycomb facilitates multiple reflections and scattering of electromagnetic waves, while the perforated walls enable a continuous 3D conductive network across adjacent cells. Meanwhile, the interconnected RGO/CNT framework contributes to a high density of heterogeneous interfaces and conductive pathways, which collectively enhance electromagnetic attenuation, with conduction loss acting as the dominant mechanism supplemented by polarization loss. This results in a minimum reflection loss of –63.91 dB alongside an absorption bandwidth of 6.12 GHz. The GF demonstrates an in‐plane thermal conductivity of 1550 W m−1 K−1, promoting rapid heat spreading and achieving a 25% reduction in the surface temperature gradient. This work offers a strategic approach to creating multifunctional composites that realize microwave absorption, thermal management, and structural reinforcement concurrently.

articles.title: High‐Entropy Materials for Gas Sensing in Extreme Environments: Mechanisms, Performance Regulation, and Design Strategies
articles.abstract: Gas sensors are increasingly required for distributed and unattended applications, where low power consumption, reliable calibration, and environmental robustness are as important as sensitivity. Temperature extremes, high humidity, chemically aggressive atmospheres, and coexisting gases can perturb adsorption/desorption, surface‐reaction kinetics, carrier transport, interfacial barriers, and long‐term baseline stability. This Review critically assesses high‐entropy materials (HEMs) as compositionally tunable platforms for gas sensing under such conditions. Structurally validated high‐entropy oxides and alloys, together with emerging high‐entropy‐derived or compositionally complex MXene‐, MOF‐, carbonaceous, and non‐oxide systems, provide diverse design spaces for regulating local coordination, defect chemistry, active sites, and interfacial electronic structure. An application‐oriented framework is established to link HEM design with gas‐sensing mechanisms, evidence‐based evaluation, and extreme‐environment operation. Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing high‐entropy‐design‐related contributions from conventional multicomponent, element‐specific, defect‐mediated, and interfacial effects. Performance and reliability are considered across high‐temperature, high‐humidity/marine, low‐temperature/cold‐chain, and corrosive/poisoning environments, with material stability and sensing‐signal stability evaluated separately. Environment‐specific criteria are discussed for thermal and humidity cycling, mixed‐gas interference, recovery completeness, long‐term drift, and multi‐stressor operation. Overall, this Review advances mission‐oriented strategies for reliable and environment‐tolerant high‐entropy gas sensors.

articles.title: High‐Mobility Wireless Light‐Controlled Biosyncretic Manta Ray
articles.abstract: Biosyncretic robots hold great promise for intelligent actuation but face challenges, including low output force of artificial muscle tissues, poor mobility, and restricted movement scenarios. To address these issues, we develop a wireless light‐controlled biosyncretic manta ray driven by Rana catesbeiana gracilis muscles. Under the optimal electrical stimulation conditions (1 Hz, 5 V, 10 ms), the muscle exhibited outstanding contractile performance (contractile force: 6.5 N; strain: 0.25). The robot integrates a gallium arsenide solar cell module that converts a near‐infrared laser into electrical energy. The generated electrical signals are delivered to the nerves on the muscle surface, thereby stimulating muscle contraction and driving the pectoral fin flapping. Performance tests demonstrate that the robot achieves a high swimming velocity (average linear velocity of 0.54 body length s−1), excellent maneuverability and agility (minimum turning radius of 0.8 body length), a maximum turning angular velocity of 21°s−1, and environmental adaptability in water‐related scenarios (water surface, underwater with load), with limited locomotion on rigid ground. This study validates isolated skeletal muscle as a high‐performance biological actuator, providing a novel paradigm for high‐mobility biosyncretic robots and advancing their practical application.

articles.title: High‐Mobility Wireless Light‐Controlled Biosyncretic Manta Ray (Adv. Funct. Mater. 88/2026)
articles.abstract: Biosyncretic Robots Inspired by manta rays, in their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77713), Chuang Zhang and co‐workers present a biosyncretic manta ray utilizing isolated Rana catesbeiana gracilis muscle as bio‐actuator. Near‐infrared laser energy is converted by GaAs solar cells to trigger muscle contraction for pectoral‐fin flapping. This robot realizes high‐speed, agile multi‐scenario swimming and promotes high‐mobility biosyncretic robot development.

articles.title: Hydration‐Induced Environmentally‐Adaptive Thermal Management with Microphase Separated Hydrogel
articles.abstract: The heat stress associated with extreme weather has paved the way for the rapid development of passive cooling techniques, but they are unable to tolerate fluctuating thermal and hydric environments, and their cooling power is more than halved under harsh conditions. Reliable multimodal thermal management techniques to couple with dynamic weather conditions are highly sought‐after. Herein, we develop a phase‐separated hydrogel via water‐induced microphase separation of waterborne polyurethane with the assistance of a hygroscopic layered network for hierarchical structure engineering. The obtained hydrogel undergoes hydration‐induced structural evolution from a compact solid monolith to a layered porous architecture, delivering a solar modulation capacity of ∼0.8 together with a high mid‐infrared emissivity of ∼0.95. Such optical features enable the hydrogel to achieve dynamic thermal regulation with a 9°C temperature span and sub‐ambient radiative cooling (∼6°C) under direct solar radiation. Additionally, via in situ incorporation of a light absorber or hygroscopic agent, the hydrogel is endowed with dual‐mode solar heating/cooling functionality and synergistic dehumidification‐cooling performance, respectively. Furthermore, the manufacturing process for the as‐proposed hydrogel is green, sustainable, and scalable, which permits industrial‐size hydrogels with combinations of stability, durability, sustainability, and processability. This work provides a promising candidate to meet the need for integrated thermoregulatory systems for environment‐specific adaptation.

articles.title: Hydrogen Selenide Gas Therapy Integrated With NIR‐II Multimodal Imaging for Precision Theranostics of Cervical Cancer
articles.abstract: Cervical cancer treatment is hindered by drug resistance, systemic toxicity, and poor real‐time monitoring of therapy. Herein, we present an intelligent nanotheranostic platform, recombinant human serum albumin (rHSA)‐indocyanine green (ICG)‐Bi2(SeO3)3 (HIB) based on hydrogen selenide (H2Se) gas therapy and multimodal imaging. In response to high glutathione (GSH) levels in the tumor microenvironment and under 808 nm laser irradiation, HIB NCs achieve on‐demand H2Se release, which sensitizes photothermal/photodynamic therapy and promoted autophagy by regulating heat shock proteins 70 (HSP70) and oxidative stress pathways, as validated by bioinformatics. Distinct from conventional gas agents, HIB NCs enable real‐time, non‐invasive dynamic monitoring of H2Se distribution and therapeutic responses using an integrated near‐infrared II (900–1700 nm, NIR‐II) fluorescence/computed tomography (CT)/photoacoustic (PA)/laser speckle contrast imaging (LSCI) multimodal strategy, overcoming the lack of in vivo H2Se sensing. In the cervical cancer lymph node metastasis model, HIB NCs could identify diseased lymph nodes more quickly for tracing and exhibit good biocompatibility. This study explored H2Se as a potent anti‐metastatic gas messenger and constructed a clinically translatable platform that combines precise gas release, multimodal dynamic monitoring, and synergistic phototherapy.

articles.title: In Situ Generated Asymmetric Charge‐Polarized Pdδ−‐Oδ−‐Zn Sites for Highly Selective Photocatalytic Oxidation of Methane to Formaldehyde
articles.abstract: Direct conversion of CH4 into liquid oxygenates remains a great challenge due to the inert C─H bond and the difficulty in achieving unity selectivity toward C1 liquid oxygenates. Current photocatalytic systems mainly focus on C─H activation, while the continuous conversion of oxygenated intermediates toward desired products is rarely addressed. Herein, we propose a mechanism mediated by electronically asymmetric and polarized interfacial Pd‐O‐Zn sites (Pdδ−‐Oδ−‐Zn) that inhibit the reverse hydrogenation of methoxy (*OCH3) intermediates, thereby enabling highly efficient direct conversion of CH4 to HCHO. In situ spectroscopic characterizations combined with DFT calculations uncovered that, compared with Pd NPs‐ZnO, the construction of Pdδ−‐Oδ−‐Zn sites significantly lowers the C─H bond activation barrier of CH4 (from 0.08 to −0.1 eV). Meanwhile, the strong Pd d‐O p orbital interactions facilitate CH3OH dehydrogenation to form *OCH3 intermediates. More encouragingly, these Pdδ−‐Oδ−‐Zn sites effectively promote *OCH3 dehydrogenation to HCHO, thereby suppressing the reverse hydrogenation pathway that regenerates CH3OH. As a result, PdZn‐ZnO delivers an excellent HCHO yield of 8320.5 µmol·g−1 h−1 with a selectivity of 91.6% at room temperature. This work provides a novel strategy for the rational design of high‐performance photocatalysts for the highly selective conversion of CH4 into HCHO.

articles.title: Interface‐Engineered Giant Multistate Resistance Switching in Altermagnetic Multiferroic Tunnel Junctions
articles.abstract: Altermagnets enable spin–split transport without stray magnetic fields, yet converting their momentum‐dependent spin splitting into a strong tunnel‐junction response requires interface‐selected tunneling channels. Here, using density functional theory combined with nonequilibrium Green's function calculations, we demonstrate giant multistate resistance switching in CrSb/α$\alpha$‐In2Se3${\rm In}_2{\rm Se}_3$ altermagnetic multiferroic tunnel junctions. The response is governed not by the bulk spin splitting of CrSb alone, but by a symmetry‐selected interfacial mechanism in which Cr/Sb terminations and h‐BN or graphene insertion layers determine spin‐channel matching, while ferroelectric polarization reshapes the electrostatic barrier. Symmetric and asymmetric terminations reverse the correspondence between parallel/antiparallel Néel‐vector configurations and high‐/low‐resistance states, showing that the actual alignment of interfacial Cr moments selects the dominant tunneling channels. Monolayer‐In2Se3${\rm In}_2{\rm Se}_3$ junctions exhibit four nonvolatile resistance states, with tunneling magnetoresistance (TMR) and tunneling electroresistance (TER) reaching 1626% and 2206%, respectively, and increasing to 9576% and 4144% upon Fermi‐level shifting. Finite‐bias calculations further reveal robust spin filtering and tunable spin‐polarized currents. Extending the barrier to bilayer In2Se3${\rm In}_2{\rm Se}_3$ introduces interlayer polarization coupling, enabling eight resistance states with maximum TMR and TER values of 3.77×104%$3.77\times 10^{4}\%$ and 4.18×105%$4.18\times 10^{5}\%$, respectively. These results establish interface symmetry, spin‐channel matching, and ferroelectric barrier reconstruction as design principles for stray‐field‐free multistate spintronic tunnel devices.

articles.title: Interfacial‐Water‐Activated Hyperbranched Polyhedral Oligomeric Silsesquioxane (POSS) Adhesives via Entropy‐Driven Molecular Rearrangement
articles.abstract: Transforming interfacial water from a detrimental factor into an active contributor to adhesion remains largely unexplored. Herein, we report an entropy‐driven, interfacial‐water‐activated hyperbranched polyhedral oligomeric silsesquioxane (POSS) adhesive that simultaneously enhances interfacial adhesion and bulk cohesion through cooperative molecular rearrangement. The adhesive integrates rigid hydrophobic POSS cages, flexible hydrophilic segments, and catechol adhesive groups within one molecular architecture. Upon exposure to a small amount of interfacial water, the hydrated interface promotes the outward migration and enrichment of hydrophilic segments and catechol moieties, thereby increasing the density of exposed adhesive groups at the bonding interface. Meanwhile, the hydrophobic POSS cages undergo inward contraction and self‐aggregation to form compact internal domains, reinforcing the cohesive phase of the adhesive. This coupled “interfacial activation‐cohesion reinforcement” mechanism converts interfacial water from an adhesion barrier into a functional trigger, enabling stronger bonding on water‐bearing interfaces than under dry conditions. The resulting POSS‐based hyperbranched adhesive exhibits broad substrate adaptability, reliable bonding on wet, rough, and dusty surfaces, and long‐term durability over 30 days. This work presents a distinct molecular design principle for wet‐surface adhesives by exploiting environmental water as an active driving force, offering opportunities for heavy‐duty structural bonding and repair of damaged materials under complex conditions.

articles.title: Laser‐Stabilized Atomically Dispersed Ru on Co3O4 Nanosheets for C1/C2 Selectivity in PET Electro‐Upcycling
articles.abstract: Herein, we present a rapid and one‐step CO2 laser irradiation strategy that stabilizes Ru single atoms (RuSAs) on two‐dimensional Co3O4 nanosheets (RuSA/Co3O4) within 3 min under ambient conditions. The Co3O4 substrate was derived from microwave‐synthesized α‐Co(OH)2 (2.45 GHz, 1 min) followed by thermal oxidation at 350°C for 1 h, affording a spinel oxide with ordered Co2+/Co3+ sites. Distinct from carbon‐supported single‐atom catalysts (SACs) systems, the oxide support functions as both an anchoring matrix and active redox component during the ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR). Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that α‐Co(OH)2 promotes C2‐selective C─H bond oxidation to glycolate, Co3O4 favors C─C bond cleavage toward C1 products (formate), and RuSA/Co3O4 enables tunable and balanced C1/C2 product formation during the EGOR, highlighting the role of RuSA sites in regulating EGOR pathways with excellent stability over 100 h. Beyond the EGOR, practical polyethylene terephthalate (PET) waste upcycling was demonstrated using PET hydrolysate feedstock; the RuSA/Co3O4 catalyst achieves high recovery yields of terephthalic acid (88.0%), formate as potassium diformate (90.6%), and glycolate as potassium glycolate glycolic acid (91.3%). This study elucidates laser‐induced defect–SA interactions for rapid SAC fabrication and establishes an integrated platform coupling SA engineering with plastic waste upcycling.

articles.title: Laser‐Stabilized Atomically Dispersed Ru on Co3O4 Nanosheets for C1/C2 Selectivity in PET Electro‐Upcycling (Adv. Funct. Mater. 88/2026)
articles.abstract: Topochemical Polymerization In their Research Article (DOI: 10.1002/adfm.77076), Myong Yong Choi and co‐workers report that CO2 laser‐stabilized Ru single atoms on Co3O4 nanosheets enable selective PET upcycling via ethylene glycol oxidation into value‐added C1/C2 chemicals, achieving circular plastic valorization.
