articles.abstract: Drawing on experiences across diverse settings, this issue of Nature Medicine explores the challenges of and lessons learned from the deployment of artificial intelligence models into healthcare.

articles.title: Personalized neoantigen-targeting cancer vaccines in ovarian cancer: a phase 1 trial
articles.abstract: A phase 1 trial shows that treatment of patients with high-grade serous ovarian cancer with personalized neoantigen vaccines combined with PD-1 blockade was feasible and led to tumor-specific immune responses in many patients and putative mechanisms of resistance related to antigen presentation were identified via cell-free DNA analysis.

articles.title: Talazoparib plus enzalutamide in high-volume metastatic hormone-naive prostate cancer: a randomized phase 2 trial
articles.abstract: In the randomized multicenter phase 2 ZZ-FIRST trial, patients with high-volume metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer treated with poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor talazoparib combined with androgen receptor inhibitor enzalutamide had an improved prostate-specific antigen response compared with enzalutamide alone, and spatial transcriptomic analyses of paired biopsies linked AR inhibition-induced suppression of HRR-related programs to proliferation arrest rather than functional HRR deficiency.

articles.title: Integrating sex as a biological variable into one’s science
articles.abstract: Addressing sex-related variation might seem like an experimental or data analysis time-sink. It’s not.

articles.title: LoL-align: sensitive and fast probabilistic protein structure alignment
articles.abstract: The ubiquitous availability of protein structures permits replacing sequence alignment with more accurate and sensitive structure alignment algorithms. LoL-align maximizes a local log-odds score for proteins to be homologous, given their intra-protein C α − C α distances. Here we show that LoL-align is markedly more sensitive in detecting remote homologs than TM-align and Dali on single- and multidomain benchmarks and achieves better alignment quality at 5–20 × their speed. LoL-align is fully integrated into Foldseek.

articles.title: MassNet: billion-scale AI-ready mass spectral corpus empowering scalable deep learning in proteomics
articles.abstract: This Article presents MassNet, a large-scale AI-ready corpus of 1.5 billion MS/MS spectra spanning 35 species, paired with a standardized storage format called Mass Spectrometry DDA Tensor (MSDT). Built on this resource, XuanjiNovo is a nonautoregressive transformer for de novo peptide sequencing that substantially outperforms previous methods.

articles.title: Cryogenic shock exfoliation for ultrahigh mobility rhombohedral graphite nanoelectronics
articles.abstract: A scalable cryogenic shock exfoliation method for the fabrication of large and uniform rhombohedral graphene flakes is demonstrated.

articles.title: Evidence for an excitonic insulator
articles.abstract: Using local probes and impurities on Ta2Pd3Te5 two experimental groups prove and characterize the presence of an excitonic gap via the impurity-induced breaking of excitonic pairing.

articles.title: Gate-induced layer sliding drives non-volatile switching of magnetism in tetralayer graphene
articles.abstract: Gate-voltage sweeps drive a first-order sliding transition between Bernal-dominant and rhombohedral–Bernal mixed stacking in marginally twisted double-bilayer graphene, which allows for non-volatile on/off switching of the low-temperature ferromagnetic phase.

articles.title: Sliding ferroelectricity scales up
articles.abstract: Wafer-scale growth of a metastable rhombohedral boron nitride polytype takes sliding ferroelectricity from handcrafted structures in the laboratory towards integrated devices.

articles.title: Ring attractor networks go full circle
articles.abstract: Clark et al. demonstrate that heterogeneous data-driven models implement head-direction selectivity through the same dynamical principles as classical ring networks. In doing so, the authors reconcile biological realism with theoretical simplicity, unifying existing frameworks and broadening the space of connectivity structures to be searched in data.

articles.title: Symmetries and continuous attractors in disordered neural circuits
articles.abstract: Head-direction cells are far more disorderly than classical continuous-attractor models allow. Clark et al. show that this disorder is nevertheless compatible with these models and that the underlying connectivity matrix hides a circular symmetry.

articles.title: A dynamic ruler for positional memory in regeneration
articles.abstract: Zebrafish can determine the amount of tissue to regrow after appendage amputation. Now, a study shows that a signal gradient that scales with the amount of tissue left to regenerate ensures that an amputated tailfin regrows to the correct length.

articles.title: Fusion digital twins from imperfect models
articles.abstract: Digital twins could transform how fusion plasmas are predicted, designed and controlled. We argue that realizing this promise requires multi-fidelity frameworks that systematically combine imperfect models and data while quantifying uncertainty.

articles.title: FDA new drug approvals in Q3 2026
Atomically ordered dual atomic pairs in CuAuZn2 intermetallics for efficient urea electrosynthesis
articles.abstract: Atomically ordered CuAuZn2 intermetallics with high-density Cu–Zn and Au–Zn dual atomic pairs are developed for urea electrosynthesis. The Cu–Zn sites facilitate nitrate reduction to *NH2, while neighbouring Au–Zn sites enhance CO2 reduction to *COOH and urea formation. This overcomes the kinetic mismatches between carbon and nitrogen intermediates, enabling the selective production of urea.

articles.title: Enantioselective synthesis of π-extended carbo[17]helicene via sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions
articles.abstract: Sequence-controlled quadruple [2+2+2] cycloadditions, followed by onward Scholl reactions, enable the enantioselective synthesis of a giant π-extended carbo[17]helicene from a dodecayne substrate. This Ni-catalysed process forms a chiral nanocarbon that exhibits strong circularly polarized luminescence.

articles.title: Mechanoradical-chain C(sp3)–C(sp2) coupling with unactivated arenes
articles.abstract: Mechanically generated radicals are often considered detrimental in materials. Now, a method for mechanically generating reactive carbon-based radicals and applying them in selective C(sp3)–C(sp2) bond formation is reported. Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons and polymers are compatible with the process, forming benzylated arene products without the need for a solvent.

articles.title: Electric-Field-Induced X-Ray Nonreciprocal Dichroism in Hematite
articles.abstract: X-ray absorption spectroscopy under an applied electric field uncovers signatures of hidden higher-order magnetic multipoles in hematite (Fe2O3), supported by theoretical calculations.

articles.title: Topological Phase Transitions and Their Thermodynamic Fate in Arbitrary-$S$ Classical Pyrochlore Spin Ice
articles.abstract: A theoretical framework for arbitrary-spin pyrochlore spin ice reveals that S = 3/2 magnets alone switch abruptly between two distinct spin-liquid states, a transition that survives the thermal fluctuations that wash all the other transitions into crossovers.

articles.title: Synergistic metal halide perovskite–metal-organic framework heterostructures: interfacial engineering for stable and multifunctional next-generation devices
Fast Feature Field (F3): A general predictive representation of events for robot perception
articles.abstract: This paper develops a mathematical argument and algorithms for building representations of data from event-based cameras that we call Fast Feature Field (F 3 ). We learned this representation by predicting future events from past events and show that it preserves scene structure and motion information. F 3 exploits the sparsity of event data and is robust to noise and variations in event rates. It can be computed efficiently using ideas from multiresolution hash encoding and deep sets, achieving 120 hertz at high-definition (HD) resolution and 440 hertz at video graphics array (VGA) resolution. F 3 represents events in a contiguous spatiotemporal volume as a multichannel image, enabling a range of downstream tasks. We obtained state-of-the-art performance on optical flow estimation, semantic segmentation, and monocular metric depth estimation, on data from three robotic platforms (a car, a quadruped robot, and a flying platform) and across different lighting conditions (daytime and nighttime), environments (indoors, outdoors, urban, and off-road), and dynamic vision sensors (resolutions and event rates). Our implementations can predict these tasks at 25 to 75 hertz at HD resolution.

articles.title: MonoRace: Robust monocular AI for champion-level drone racing
articles.abstract: Autonomous drone racing represents a major frontier in robotics research. It requires an artificial intelligence (AI) that can run onboard lightweight flying robots under tight resource and time constraints while pushing the physical system to its limits. The state of the art in this area consists of a system with a stereo camera and an inertial measurement unit (IMU) that beat human drone-racing champions in a controlled indoor environment. Here, we present MonoRace, an onboard drone-racing approach that generalizes to a competition environment without any external motion tracking system, using only a monocular rolling-shutter camera and an IMU. The approach features robust state estimation that combines neural network–based gate segmentation with a drone model. Moreover, it includes an offline optimization procedure that leverages the known geometry of gates to refine any state estimation parameter. This offline optimization is based purely on onboard flight data and is important for fine-tuning the extrinsic camera calibration parameters. Furthermore, the guidance and control are performed by a neural network that forgoes inner-loop controllers by directly sending motor commands. This small network runs on the flight controller at 500 hertz. The proposed approach won the Abu Dhabi Autonomous Drone Racing Competition 2025, outperforming all competing autonomous drone race teams and three world champion human pilots in a direct knockout tournament. It reached speeds up to 100 kilometers per hour on the competition track and successfully coped with problems such as camera interference and IMU saturation.

articles.title: System design of the Ultra Mobility Vehicle: A driving, balancing, and jumping bicycle robot
articles.abstract: Trials cyclists and mountain bike riders can hop, jump, balance, and drive on one or both wheels. This versatility allows them to achieve speed and energy efficiency on smooth terrain and agility over rough terrain. Inspired by these athletes, we present the design and control of a robotic platform, Ultra Mobility Vehicle (UMV), that combines a bicycle and a reaction mass to move dynamically with minimal actuated degrees of freedom. We used a simulation-driven design optimization process to synthesize a spatial linkage topology with a focus on vertical jump height and momentum-based balancing on a single wheel contact. Using a deep reinforcement learning (RL) framework, we demonstrate zero-shot transfer of diverse athletic behaviors, including track stands, jumps, wheelies, rear-wheel hopping, and front flips. This 23.5-kilogram robot is capable of high speeds ( v max = 8 meters per second) and jumping on and over large obstacles (1-meter tall or 130% of the robot’s nominal height).

articles.title: Editorial Expression of Concern for the Research Article “In vivo CRISPR activation screen identifies acyl-CoA–binding protein as a driver of bone metastasis”
From code to cure: Harnessing AI for antibiotic discovery and design
articles.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) now enables the exploration of vast chemical and sequence spaces, the design of synthesizable antibiotics, and the prioritization of safe, mechanism-diverse candidates through integrated modeling and accelerated testing. Here, we survey recent advances in AI for both small-molecule and peptide antimicrobial drugs, highlight emerging data and reporting standards, and outline translational pathways and regulatory hurdles needed to bring these agents to patients.

articles.title: Innovative roadmaps for sustainable antimicrobial resistance interventions
articles.abstract: Integrated strategies to combat antibiotic-resistant bacteria and fungi require innovative commercial models, new discovery platforms, standardized genomic surveillance, and streamlined clinical trials. Machine learning and other new technologies will accelerate the development of diagnostics and therapeutics (small molecules, antibodies, and vaccines) to combat antimicrobial resistance. Next-generation approaches should align societal impact with investment to ensure rapid global public health gains.

articles.title: Metabolomic aging and mortality clocks based on ensemble learning identify systemic aging risk across the human life span in 18,476 individuals
articles.abstract: Aging is characterized by progressive functional decline, yet metabolomic signatures across the human life span remain incompletely defined. Here, we profiled plasma metabolomes from 18,476 participants aged 1 to 96 years across six centers in China using nano-assisted laser desorption/ionization mass spectrometry (LDI-MS) and identified 56 representative age-associated metabolites. In a healthy cohort, we developed a stacking ensemble model to estimate metabolomic age and quantified metabolomic age acceleration (mAA) as each individual’s deviation from chronological age. Higher mAA was associated with health deterioration and unfavorable lifestyles. During follow-up from 2019 to 2025, individuals with accelerated mAA showed increased risk of incident chronic diseases, such as fatty liver disease, hypertension, and diabetes, as well as increased all-cause mortality. In a disease cohort, we further developed a mortality-linked metabolomic metric (age deviation) that quantified individualized departures from age-expected mortality risk inferred from plasma metabolites. Age deviation was associated with established composite health measures and increased with multisystem disease involvement and higher multimorbidity burden. Together, these findings support the potential of plasma metabolomic profiling as a scalable, life span–wide approach for deriving clinically interpretable metabolomic aging metrics associated with health status, chronic disease risk, and mortality.

articles.title: Orthogonal Fc engineering enables multiplexed delivery of mRNA-encoded bispecific antibodies that constrain viral escape
articles.abstract: The continuous antigenic evolution of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) has repeatedly undermined the effectiveness of monoclonal antibody (mAb) therapies, underscoring the need for innovative approaches that improve therapeutic mAb breadth and durability of protection. Here, we engineered messenger ribonucleic acid (mRNA)–encoded bispecific antibodies (bsAbs) that, upon intravenous administration in lipid nanoparticles, achieved high serum concentrations, extended half-life, and serum neutralizing titers exceeding 1:10,000 in human neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn)–expressing mice. To enhance resilience to viral escape, we used structure-guided computational design to introduce Fc modifications that promoted selective homodimerization, thereby enabling codelivery of multiple mRNA-encoded bsAbs with cognate heavy chain pairing. In vivo expression of a triple bsAb combination resulted in broad serum neutralization of historical and contemporary SARS-CoV-2 variants, including the highly mutated BA.3.2.2 lineage. Preexposure prophylaxis with the mRNA-delivered bsAb combination conferred protection against SARS-CoV-2 XBB.1.5 challenge, preventing weight loss and decreasing viral burden in the lungs compared with vehicle control treatment. Together, the results provide proof of principle for mRNA-based delivery of Fc-engineered bsAb combinations to combat SARS-CoV-2 and potentially other rapidly evolving pathogens.

articles.title: Preclinical and first-in-human evaluation of VG-3927/SAR448851, an oral small-molecule TREM2 agonist for Alzheimer’s disease
articles.abstract: Microglial dysfunction is increasingly implicated in Alzheimer’s disease (AD) pathogenesis, with loss-of-function variants in the microglial receptor TREM2 as major risk factors for late-onset AD. We report VG-3927, an oral, CNS-penetrant small-molecule TREM2 agonist that engages the transmembrane domains of TREM2 and its adaptor DAP12 to promote higher-order receptor complex formation and downstream signaling. VG-3927 and tool compound VG-3909 exhibited (sub)nanomolar potency, cooperated with endogenous ligands including amyloid-β (Aβ), and restored signaling in disease-associated TREM2 variants. In human iPSC-derived neuron-microglia-astrocyte cultures, VG-3927 reduced inflammatory cytokines and markers of neuronal damage. In 5xFAD amyloidosis mice expressing the common variant of hTREM2 (5xFAD;hTREM2 CV ), VG-3909 induced neuroprotective transcriptional reprogramming of microglia, particularly in the plaque niche; enhanced Aβ phagocytosis; and boosted brain glucose metabolism. By contrast, a TREM2 agonist antibody, which may be sequestered by soluble TREM2 (sTREM2), failed to engage plaque microglia. In a first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 1 trial (NCT06343636, n = 115), VG-3927 was well tolerated across single and multiple ascending doses of up to 140 milligrams. Pharmacokinetics supported once-daily dosing with high CNS penetration (CSF-to-unbound plasma ratio of 0.91). VG-3927 induced dose-dependent reductions in CSF sTREM2, a biomarker of target engagement, consistent across healthy and elderly participants and participants with AD, supporting further clinical development in AD under the new designation SAR448851.

articles.title: Prevention is better than cure
articles.abstract: Wider access to clean water and sanitation is needed in the battle to combat bacterial diseases.

articles.title: Quinolinic acid contributes to maladaptive kidney injury and acute kidney injury–to–chronic kidney disease transition
articles.abstract: The transition from acute kidney injury (AKI) to chronic kidney disease (CKD) remains a major clinical problem with unclear underlying mechanisms. Emerging evidence suggests that alterations in tryptophan metabolism, particularly in the production of downstream metabolites such as quinolinic acid (QA), play a role in renal pathophysiology. QA, an intermediate in de novo nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide biosynthesis, is metabolized by quinolinate phosphoribosyltransferase (QPRT). We investigated whether QA contributes to kidney injury using models of folic acid–induced AKI-to-CKD transition and cisplatin-induced AKI, genetic and exogenous approaches to alter QA, and clinical observations. Untargeted kidney metabolomics identified QA as one of the most elevated metabolites after folic acid injury. After folic acid injury, Qprt haploinsufficiency exacerbated kidney injury and fibrosis-related gene expression; aged Qprt -haploinsufficient mice exhibited increased fibrosis-associated gene expression without overt renal dysfunction. Exogenous QA administration increased serum creatinine in uninjured mice and worsened renal dysfunction and fibrosis-related gene expression in the folic acid AKI-to-CKD model. Conversely, mice deficient in either 3-hydroxyanthranilate 3,4-dioxygenase (HAAO) or kynurenine 3-monooxygenase (KMO), which reduce flux toward QA, showed improved renal outcomes after folic acid injury and cisplatin-induced AKI. Multimodal spatial metabolomics analysis of kidney biopsies from patients with AKI revealed QA accumulation in regions of inflammatory infiltration. Last, children with CKD exhibited higher urinary QA compared with healthy individuals. These findings underscore QA as a potential mediator of kidney injury and a therapeutic target for preventing the progression from AKI to CKD.

articles.title: Restoration of PP2A AαB56αC trimer formation by RPT04402 molecular glue in high-grade uterine cancer
articles.abstract: The incidence and mortality of high-grade endometrial cancers are increasing, and heterozygous hotspot mutations in PPP2R1A are drivers of the most aggressive forms of uterine cancer. PPP2R1A encodes the Aα scaffolding subunit of the heterotrimeric phosphatase PP2A. These recurrent mutations, specifically at the Pro 179 and Ser 256 residues, disrupt the binding of tumor-suppressive substrate-directing B56 and B55 subunits to the PP2A scaffolding subunit while maintaining binding to other regulatory subunits. Here, we identified a series of molecular glues that correct PP2A trimer formation in the context of the P179R (Pro 179 →Arg) and S256F (Ser 256 →Phe) mutants. A small-molecule library was designed to fit into the pocket at the binding interface of the Aα/B56α/C heterotrimer. The lead molecule, RPT04402, promoted B56α heterotrimerization to the Aα P179R and Aα S256F mutant scaffolds. In mice, RPT04402 treatment drove tumor regressions and extended median survival in multiple independent mutant cell lines and patient-derived xenografts, proving a robust single-agent activity. This activity was abrogated upon knockout of B56α. Combined, these data demonstrate that PP2A molecular glues are a promising first-in-class therapy that might benefit patients with PPP2R1A mutant uterine cancer by targeting a driver of this aggressive disease.

articles.title: Retraction of the Research Article “SARS-CoV-2 S2–targeted vaccination elicits broadly neutralizing antibodies”
Rifampicin-resistant TB: An inflection point in antimicrobial resistance
articles.abstract: Rifampicin-resistant TB should be integrated into the global AMR response through diagnostics, surveillance, and optimized treatment regimens.

articles.title: A Ferrier sesquicentenary
APOE, p-tau217, and cognitive impairment in diverse cohorts
Antibody-mediated encephalitides: distinct diseases with transdisciplinary implications
articles.abstract: The discovery of antibody-mediated glial and neuronal disorders has transformed the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases previously considered idiopathic or not recognised as immune-mediated. Antibody-mediated disorders targeting glial aquaporin-4 and myelin oligodendrocyte glycoprotein are distinct nosological entities, defined by specific targets, mechanisms, syndromes, and therapeutic implications. By contrast, antibody-mediated disorders targeting neuronal antigens (ie, autoimmune encephalitides) are still frequently analysed collectively, with data from different disorders pooled as if they represent a single disease rather than distinct entities. Evidence from anti-NMDA receptor encephalitis, anti-LGI1 encephalitis, and anti-IgLON5 disease (used here as exemplars of autoimmune encephalitides) indicates that individual autoimmune encephalitides differ in demographics, triggers, mechanisms, clinical manifestations, post-acute trajectories, and treatment requirements. The broad, heterogeneous presentations of autoimmune encephalitides require coordinated multidisciplinary care within and beyond neurology, involving specialists in paediatrics, infectious diseases, epilepsy, movement disorders, sleep medicine, intensive care, cognitive rehabilitation, and other relevant disciplines. Such interdisciplinary collaboration facilitates the recognition of new diseases and elucidation of the causes of previously unclassified disorders. Improving patient care requires not only aetiological and mechanistic insight to enable development of targeted therapies but also strengthened cross-specialty expertise to optimise diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Climate change: aggravation and adaptation in neurology
From syndrome to antibody-defined autoimmune encephalitides
Katrin Andreasson: rethinking neurodegeneration
Lara M Lange
Learn From Us: stepping into the spotlight after brain injury
Neurotrauma as a chronic disease: a call for integrated care
Progress in exon skipping for Duchenne muscular dystrophy
Reframing traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury as chronic multisystem disorders: toward integrated, long-term care
articles.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) and spinal cord injury (SCI) affect more than 220 million people worldwide and are associated with cardiometabolic, endocrine, neurological, and psychiatric sequelae for years to decades after an acute injury. However, most health systems still treat neurotrauma (TBI and SCI, collectively) as a time-limited event, leaving long-term surveillance of these patients fragmented or absent, which leads to preventable mortality and avoidable readmissions. TBI and SCI in adults should be reclassified as acute-onset multisystem chronic-risk conditions. Existing cardiovascular, endocrine, and psychiatric services do not capture neurotrauma-specific risks, including trauma-induced hypopituitarism, autonomic dysregulation, accelerated ageing, and cognitive-behavioural impairment, so neurotrauma care is best framed as a missing node in chronic neurological care. We propose a risk-stratified pathway of care navigation, multisystem screening, and telehealth; convergence with adjacent stroke, cardiometabolic, memory, psychiatric, pain, and epilepsy services; and the financing, workforce, and registry reforms needed to deliver measurable reductions in 5-year mortality, avoidable rehospitalisation, and long-term disability.

articles.title: Safety and efficacy of delpacibart zotadirsen in Duchenne muscular dystrophy mutations amenable to exon 44 skipping in the USA (EXPLORE44): a randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase 1/2 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundThere are no approved exon skipping therapies to treat Duchenne muscular dystrophy due to DMD variants amenable to exon 44 skipping (DMD44). Delpacibart zotadirsen (del-zota, also known as AOC 1044) is a first-in-class antibody-oligonucleotide conjugate designed to deliver an exon 44-skipping phosphorodiamidate morpholino oligomer to muscle to restore dystrophin expression for individuals with DMD44. EXPLORE44 was a first-in-human trial to evaluate del-zota's safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and efficacy.MethodsEXPLORE44 was a two-part randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 1/2 study in healthy adult men (aged 18-55 years; part A) and ambulatory and non-ambulatory male participants with DMD44 (aged 7-27 years; part B) at ten clinical research sites in the USA. Dosing in part B was informed by safety, pharmacokinetic, and pharmacodynamic data from part A. In part B, participants with DMD44 were randomised (3:1 del-zota:placebo) within two dose cohorts to receive three intravenous doses of del-zota (5 mg/kg every 6 weeks, or 10 mg/kg every 8 weeks) or matching placebo. A computer-generated permuted-block randomisation schedule was prepared by an independent statistician with no further role in the study. Infusions were prepared by an unmasked pharmacist under supervision of the masked investigator; other site staff, participants, and sponsor team members were masked to allocation. The primary objective was safety and tolerability measured by the incidence of treatment-emergent adverse events. Secondary endpoints assessing target engagement were change from baseline in exon skipping (ie, defined as the percentage of dystrophin mRNA transcripts in which exon 44 is excluded from the mature mRNA relative to total dystrophin mRNA transcripts) and dystrophin level to month 4 (5 mg/kg cohort) or month 5 (10 mg/kg cohort). The trial was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05670730) and is complete.FindingsBetween Dec 5, 2022, and June 27, 2024, we enrolled and randomly assigned 45 healthy volunteers and 26 men and boys with DMD44. In part A, three (30%) of ten healthy volunteers who received placebo and 21 (62%) of 34 who received del-zota reported at least one adverse event, none of which were severe or serious. In part B, nine participants with DMD44 received del-zota at 5 mg/kg, ten at 10 mg/kg, and seven received placebo; mean age 13·3 years (SD 4·2). 16 (84%) participants with DMD44 treated with del-zota and six (86%) treated with placebo reported at least one adverse event, most of which were mild or moderate; two participants, both in the 5 mg/kg del-zota group, discontinued due to adverse events (anaphylactic reaction and infusion-related reaction). Mean increases from baseline in exon 44 skipping were 36·6% (95% CI 20·8 to 52·4, SD 17·1, nominal p=0·0013) at 5 mg/kg, 43·4% (32·8 to 54·0, 14·9, nominal pInterpretationDel-zota had an acceptable safety profile, produced increases in exon 44 skipping and dystrophin expression, and decreased biomarkers of muscle damage in participants with DMD44. Findings from this study support further investigation of del-zota in a phase 3 study to assess efficacy and long-term safety.FundingAvidity Biosciences, A Novartis Company.

articles.title: Staged bilateral focused ultrasound pallidothalamic tractotomy for Parkinson's disease
Staged bilateral focused ultrasound pallidothalamic tractotomy for Parkinson's disease – Authors' reply
Beyond attention: performance pressure shifts information-processing complexity
articles.abstract: Why does performance pressure sometimes cause choking but sometimes elicit exceptional performance? We propose that pressure shifts the complexity of information-processing rules that guide action. Performance improves when shifts move processing toward task-matched complexity and deteriorates when they promote maladaptive simplification, overcomplexification, or the use of rules that exceed available processing resources.

articles.title: From ‘magic traits’ to diversification mechanisms
articles.abstract: Species richness is markedly uneven across the tree of life, and traits have long been invoked to explain this pattern. Expanding phylogenetic and trait datasets enable broader comparisons, but trait–diversity associations alone do not reveal how differences in richness arose. We argue that such associations should be reframed as process hypotheses about three non-exclusive processes: lineage origin, access to ecological or geographic opportunity, and persistence. Mixed trait–diversity associations are expected when the same trait influences multiple processes whose relative contributions vary across contexts. This process-based framework makes alternative diversification histories explicit and specifies contrasting temporal predictions that can be evaluated with complementary evidence. It clarifies what findings would weaken each hypothesis and when available data leave alternative histories unresolved.

articles.title: Precipitation timing matters for flowering communities
articles.abstract: Flowering times have long been a harbinger of the changing seasons and, more recently, of a changing climate. Among the cues that trigger flowering, precipitation timing has been relatively little-studied. Tsafon et al. show that the timing of precipitation shapes flowering in complex ways. Much work remains to disentangle this complexity.

articles.title: Turnover frequency (TOF) in catalysis: it's hard to say goodbye or is it?
articles.abstract: The concept of turnover frequency (TOF) had its merits, however, there is thus a need to move from TOF to advanced procedures aimed at revealing complex mechanisms and linking reactivity and surface composition.

articles.title: A high-dimensional population code in the bat motor cortex during natural dexterous flight
articles.abstract: Bats use their hand-like wings to reproduce natural flights with wingbeat-level precision. Rather than mainly tracking the wingbeat cycle, the wing motor cortex generates sparse, distinct population states with little shared variance across wingbeats, resulting in a high-dimensional code distinct from that typically observed in constrained tasks.

articles.title: Mechanisms of transcription control by distal enhancers from single-gene nanoscopy
articles.abstract: High-resolution real-time imaging of enhancer-promoter communication reveals how the two genomic loci are actively brought together through cohesin-mediated loop extrusion and how E-P interactions are temporally coordinated with transcriptional bursts. Unexpectedly, components of the RNA Pol II general machinery form nanoscale clusters at distal enhancers, and embedding the promoter into such clusters boosts GTF activities and triggers burst initiation.

articles.title: PTPRS mediates invasion of tetanus neurotoxin into the central nervous system
articles.abstract: Tetanus neurotoxin enters the central nervous system through motor neurons. This study identifies PTPRS as the long-sought retrograde transport receptor that directs toxin trafficking in motor neurons into the spinal cord, uncovering a host pathway that can be targeted for post-exposure treatment and for drug delivery into the central nervous system.

articles.title: Rare k-mers reveal centromere haplogroups underlying human diversity and cancer translocations
articles.abstract: By defining centromere haplogroups from rare k-mer variation, Shiraishi et al. uncover extensive hidden diversity and link centromere structure to human evolution and disease-associated genomic instability.

articles.title: Structural basis and rational engineering of a thermophilic Cas13a for robust RNA detection
articles.abstract: Oladeji et al. determined the cryo-EM structure of the TccCas13a ternary complex and leveraged structural insights to engineer a thermophilic Cas13a variant with 100-fold enhanced sensitivity. The engineered nuclease retains programmability and thermostability, enabling highly sensitive RNA detection in different biological matrices.

articles.title: A mechanically robust high-index oxide-glass platform enabled by interchangeable seventh-principal-component design
Chain-length effects and selectivity in alkaline polyol electrooxidation from glycerol to xylitol
Fabrication of highly dye-loaded protein nanofibril films for UV shielding and down-conversion
Matrix-guided recovery of FePO4 for battery materials from incineration sewage sludge ash
Rethinking circular food-contact materials by integrating safety, design, and regulation in closed-loop recycling
Mouse Cutaneous Melanoma Induced by Mutant BRaf Arises from Expansion and Dedifferentiation of Mature Pigmented Melanocytes
Rapid CAR-T manufacturing with low-intensity priming enhances CAR-T cell fitness and limits inflammatory programming in a phase 1 study
articles.abstract: Yang and colleagues show that low-intensity priming during rapid chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T manufacturing preserves T cell fitness while restraining inflammatory programming. PrimeCAR cells maintain stemness-associated and proliferative responses with reduced myeloid-activating inflammation, and early-phase studies in B cell malignancies demonstrate encouraging clinical activity with few severe cytokine release syndrome (CRS) or immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome (ICANS) events.

articles.title: Single-cell CRISPR screen maps epigenetic regulators of lineage specification and malignancies in human HSPCs
articles.abstract: Yuan et al. establish a scalable single-cell CRISPR platform in primary human HSPCs, linking 322 regulator perturbations to cell states and gene programs. The atlas identifies regulators associated with long-term repopulation and lineage-biased outputs and nominates PRDM10 as a candidate AML dependency.

articles.title: Transplantation of Expanded Fetal Intestinal Progenitors Contributes to Colon Regeneration after Injury
Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations of solid-state photon upconversion describe an anticorrelation between emission yield and threshold intensity
articles.abstract: Kinetic Monte Carlo simulations are used to model solid-state triplet-triplet annihilation photon upconversion, which consists of a sensitizer doped into an annihilator matrix. The simulations incorporate solid-state activated processes, where the process of Förster resonance energy transfer is independently benchmarked against experimental data. Our results show that both upconversion efficiency and threshold intensity are coupled through the sensitizer concentration, limiting their simultaneous optimization. Thus, the triplet-state lifetime is a key parameter in solid-state upconversion.

articles.title: Ultrafast water transport through densely fluorinated foldamer channels
articles.abstract: Extensively fluorinated aramid polymers fold into discrete single-chain nanoparticle tubes with continuous internal lumens. Stabilized by F–H–F interactions, these abiotic channels enable ultrafast and highly selective water transport across membranes, surpassing natural aquaporins while maintaining excellent salt rejection.

articles.title: Marine Carbonate System Observing and mCDR: New Processes, Needs, and Systems
articles.abstract: Marine carbon dioxide removal (mCDR) techniques have the potential to remove legacy emitted carbon dioxide from the atmosphere and store it durably in ocean reservoirs. While the ocean’s vast surface area and buffering capacity offer benefits for scaling removal, monitoring remains challenging. This comprehensive review of marine carbonate system observing and monitoring technologies finds that mCDR processes span multiple scales, often at the edges of existing platform and sensing capability. While some mCDR observing and monitoring is possible today, challenges will arise as experiments and operations expand. Leaps forward in assessing the novel scales of mCDR processes will emerge from low-energy, low-cost, highly durable sensors; innovative deployment platforms; cooperative sensing networks; dedicated model validation programs; and decision support tools. This review is intended to serve as a guide to the history, ongoing innovation, and transformative vision of future marine carbonate system observing and monitoring informed by mCDR.

articles.title: Activating Interstitial Oxygen Conduction in Sr3V2O8 Palmierite Oxides Through Minimal Mo-Substitution
articles.abstract: The palmierite oxides are a promising family of ion conductors, and understanding how compositional modification affects their structure and, in turn, their ionic conductivity is pivotal for unlocking high ionic conductivity in these solid electrolytes. Here, we investigate the Sr3V2-xMoxO8+x/2 series (0 ≤ x ≤ 0.4), establishing a solubility limit at x = 0.2, and demonstrating that Mo-substituted compositions exhibit bulk O2– conductivity approximately 2 orders of magnitude higher than the pristine composition at 600 °C. Combined X-ray and neutron diffraction refinement shows little change in the average crystallographic structure, prompting questions about its local structure and dynamics. Using ab initio molecular dynamics, bond-valence site-energy calculations, and 51V and 17O solid-state nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy supported by density functional theory calculations, we demonstrate that Mo6+ incorporation generates a new oxygen environment consistent with the formation of a charge-compensating interstitial O3 site. While V5+ remains tetrahedrally coordinated throughout the series, Mo6+ exhibits both MoO4 and distorted trigonal bipyramidal MoO5 coordination polyhedra, with the latter arising from the occupation of O3. This O3 site is proposed to bridge neighboring MOn polyhedra along the ab-plane, shortening the O2– jump distances and shifting the conduction mechanism from a 3D cooperative rotational mechanism to a 2D interstitial-based one.

articles.title: Magnetic and Electrochemical Properties of the Altermagnetic Layered Antiperovskite Na2Mn2OS2
articles.abstract: Incorporating multiple anions into perovskite-type frameworks provides a handle to design innovative lattices and trigger exotic properties. Inverse Lieb lattices have been receiving substantial interest as hosts for d-wave altermagnetism. One mixed-anion system in which these lattices have been experimentally realized is layered oxychalcogenides. By employing a high-pressure, high-temperature synthesis method, we introduce Na2Mn2OS2 as an additional member of this family of compounds. Na2Mn2OS2 adopts an antiperovskite-derived structure, consisting of layers of face-sharing MnO2S4 octahedra. Magnetization and neutron diffraction data reveal that the phase undergoes magnetic ordering below 144 K. The low-temperature magnetic structure has zero net magnetization and is invariant under a combination of rotation and time reversal, thereby fulfilling the symmetry criteria to be considered as an altermagnet candidate. Electronic band structure calculations demonstrate that the phase contains spin-polarized bands, providing further evidence that Na2Mn2OS2 can be described as an altermagnet. An electrochemical investigation of this compound was performed, aiming both to tailor the physicochemical properties of the material through desodiation and to yield a possible Na-ion cathode material. While there are indications of Na-deintercalation, the charge compensation mechanism appears to involve irreversible sulfur oxidation rather than manganese oxidation, thus preventing the application of Na2Mn2OS2 as a positive electrode for Na-ion batteries.

articles.title: Metastable Inorganic Materials through Reactive Molten-Salt Ion Exchange
articles.abstract: Material discovery is the foundational process for fundamental investigations and useful applications of functional and structural materials. It is the prerequisite for all downstream processes including property determination, synthetic optimization and scale-up, doping, defect engineering, morphology control, and surface and interfacial tuning. Through extensive experimental and, more recently, computational exploration, the number of yet-to-be-discovered thermodynamically stable compounds in low-order phase spaces has rapidly shrunk. However, new materials are needed to foster advances in established and emerging applications, particularly those related to energy storage, conversion, and efficiency. Thinking beyond equilibrium phase diagrams, a much larger phase space of metastable compounds exists if such phases can be synthetically accessed. This Perspective highlights the role of reactive molten-salt ion exchange (MSIX) as a technique for metastable inorganic material discovery. We discuss the thermodynamics, kinetics, crystal chemistry, and atomic-scale characterization of reactive molten-salt ion exchange. Emergent phenomena in ion exchange such as interdiffusion and the mixed-ion effect and challenges associated with characterizing mixed-ion and heterogeneous systems receive extra attention. In consideration of the breadth of MSIX, fundamental principles and general reaction schemes are used where possible with specific examples extensively referenced. MSIX is contextualized by comparisons to adjacent fields that involve molten salts, ion transport, and metastable materials. Opportunities and missed opportunities associated with computational approaches to molten-salt reactions and metastable materials are discussed. Unique prospects for in situ diffraction and NMR crystallography are highlighted along with future directions, including extensions to solid-state ion exchange (SSIX).

articles.title: Unprecedented Pd(II) Metal–Organic Cages for Simultaneous Adsorption of Iodine Species
articles.abstract: Metal–organic cages (MOCs) with unconventional topologies remain rare owing to the challenges associated with controlling coordination-driven self-assembly. Herein, we report the self-assembly of two unique Pd(II)-based coordination cages–peanut-shaped cage (C1, M18L14) and hemicage (C2, M12M2L22), from semiflexible tetratopic pyridyl ligands incorporating 9,10-dihydroanthracene and benzene backbones, respectively. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction studies reveal that cage C1 adopts a rare peanut-shaped structure comprising two interconnected cavities and both inward- and outward-oriented Pd(II) nodes, generating a highly electron-rich confined environment. In contrast, C2 forms an unprecedented boat-shaped architecture assembled through the cooperative incorporation of 90° and 180° Pd(II) acceptors within a single discrete cage. Despite their amorphous and nonporous nature, these assemblies demonstrate exceptional dual-capture performance toward volatile iodine species. Notably, C1 achieves iodine uptake capacities of 2.62 g g–1 under static vapor-phase conditions and 1.21 g g–1 under dynamic flow conditions, together with efficient CH3I adsorption of up to 1.05 g g–1 at 75 °C. Spectroscopic investigations and theoretical calculations reveal that the adsorption process is driven by synergistic charge-transfer interactions, polyiodide formation, electrostatic stabilization, and cavity confinement. Furthermore, both cages display excellent retention capability and recyclability, highlighting their potential as robust materials for radioactive iodine sequestration and environmental remediation.

Individual bumblebee foraging repertoires: Implications for disease persistence
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Generalist species may be comprised of individual specialists. Individual specialization can impact disease transmission at shared resources by shaping contact patterns. Mathematical models of pollinator diseases that spread via flowers have shown that R 0 can be greatly amplified when each forager specializes on one flower species at a time with slow turnover. Yet, such behaviour has not been empirically demonstrated in generalist bumblebees. Here, we used palynology from sequential pollen loads of individual common eastern bumble bees (Bombus impatiens) to assess their foraging preferences over time. We used an automated monitoring system to greatly improve recapture rates, hence allowing a more complete characterization of each bee's foraging behaviours. Individuals in a bumblebee colony exhibited unique foraging repertoires of two to three flower species while the full-colony diet breadth was up to three times larger depending on time of year. Individual repertoires exhibited roughly 50% turnover, on average, over 10 days. Implications for disease transmission when individual repertoire sizes are greater than one may differ from specialization on a single flower species. Hence, we developed mathematical models where each bee has an effective repertoire size of two, and found that ignoring individual specialization still resulted in an underprediction of R 0, although to a smaller extent compared to a single-specialty model. Our results provide novel insights into the foraging behaviours of social bumblebees and improve predictions of how diseases are transmitted and persist in complex plant–pollinator networks. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Milder winters alleviate seasonal challenges for a migratory goose facing Arctic warming
articles.abstract: By combining extensive body mass records with population‐wide migration counts spanning several decades, this study uncovers long‐term improvements in body condition associated with progressively milder winters, alongside earlier spring departure in an Arctic migrant, highlighting the importance of the full annual cycle in determining species' responses to climate change. Abstract Many migratory birds now reach their Arctic breeding grounds earlier in response to advancing springs and shifting nutrient peaks, either by departing earlier from non‐breeding grounds or by travelling faster. For dark‐bellied brent geese, there is limited potential to travel faster, as their spring migration is already among the fastest of Arctic geese and swans. Earlier departure would require reaching departure body mass earlier, either through a faster accumulation of energy stores during spring staging in the Wadden Sea or via adjustments earlier in the annual cycle. We examined long‐term shifts in spring staging phenology and changes in winter and spring body mass trajectories of brent geese at the population level, with particular emphasis on the effects of winter temperature on body mass and spring body mass on departure timing. We used more than five decades of body mass measurements from individuals caught in the United Kingdom and France and in the Dutch Wadden Sea to reconstruct changes in winter and spring mass trajectories, respectively. These data were combined with over five decades of migration counts in the Netherlands and more than two decades of counts in Denmark to quantify changes in arrival and departure timing, respectively. We found that brent geese were heavier during and after milder winters and that their body mass trajectories flattened over the years: they no longer lose body mass during winter; during spring staging, fuelling rates have declined (in the so‐called ‘fattening phase’), while they also no longer lose body mass in the 1–2 weeks prior to departure (‘plateau phase’). Brent geese have not shifted their spring arrival in the Wadden Sea but have advanced departure timing. Annual variation in body mass was not related to annual departure timing. These results suggest that milder winters have relaxed energetic constraints and improved body condition in brent geese throughout the non‐breeding season. Our findings highlight the importance of considering the full annual cycle when assessing how migratory animals respond to global change, in particular those with limited capacity to adjust migration timing or speed.

articles.title: Legume presence outweighs functional group richness in determining community invasibility under nitrogen enrichment
articles.abstract: These findings reveal that FGR provides a structural template for biotic resistance, whereas functional identity determines whether this template translates into resource pre‐emption or community vulnerability. In nutrient‐enriched ecosystems, low‐biomass legumes can inadvertently convert nutrient pulses into invasion opportunities by elevating the baseline resource environment and presenting limited above‐ground suppression. Restoring invasion‐resistant communities under N enrichment therefore requires functional‐identity screening—prioritizing strongly competitive non‐legumes rather than relying solely on FGR. Abstract Anthropogenic nitrogen (N) enrichment often promotes plant invasions by increasing resource availability, yet why resident communities differ in their resistance to the same resource pulse remains poorly understood. Here, we manipulated native plant functional group richness (FGR = 1–3) and community composition while holding species richness constant and assessed the performance of the nitrophilous invader Bidens alba under ambient and N‐enriched conditions to determine whether biotic resistance is driven by diversity per se or specific functional identities. N enrichment consistently increased invader biomass, but its interaction with FGR was not significant across the full richness gradient, indicating that FGR alone was insufficient for predicting biotic resistance. Instead, functional identity strongly governed plant invasion outcomes. Non‐legume communities (grasses and forbs) sustained high biotic resistance under N enrichment through strong above‐ground neighbour suppression. Conversely, legume‐containing communities exhibited weak biotic resistance under N enrichment, permitting a considerable increase in invader biomass. Legumes facilitated plant invasion through a coupled below‐ and above‐ground mechanism: they maintained a high baseline soil nitrate availability while experiencing competitive suppression under N enrichment, resulting in low biomass and minimal physical canopy presence. Combined with N enrichment, this created a favourable resource window that enabled B. alba to reduce its root: shoot ratio—a morphological plasticity response constrained in non‐legume communities by dense native neighbour biomass. Synthesis. Our findings reveal that FGR provides a structural template for biotic resistance, whereas functional identity determines whether this template translates into resource pre‐emption or community vulnerability. In nutrient‐enriched ecosystems, low‐biomass legumes can inadvertently convert nutrient pulses into invasion opportunities by elevating the baseline resource environment and presenting limited above‐ground suppression. Restoring invasion‐resistant communities under N enrichment therefore requires functional‐identity screening—prioritizing strongly competitive non‐legumes rather than relying solely on FGR.

articles.title: Molecular regulation of Frenkel defect pairs enables phase-stable wide-band-gap perovskites for tandem photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Light-induced phase segregation limits the efficiency and stability of wide-band-gap mixed-halide perovskites. This work demonstrates that multi-site molecular regulation can cooperatively manage Frenkel defect-pair dynamics, thereby suppressing phase segregation. This stabilization is achieved by thermodynamically suppressing Frenkel defect-pair formation and dissociation while kinetically restricting subsequent halide redistribution.

articles.title: Transposable element splicing reveals a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts
articles.abstract: Li et al. systematically map splicing within and between transposable elements (TEs) across cancers and define TEtrans, a tumor-enriched class of gene-independent transcripts. TEtrans display distinct regulatory programs and can function as oncogenic RNAs or encode immunogenic tumor antigens, expanding the functional landscape of TE reactivation in cancer.

articles.title: Two families of multi-planet systems with distinct architectures and stellar hosts
articles.abstract: The rapidly growing census of exoplanets now includes over a thousand multi-planet systems, revealing architectures that span more than four orders of magnitude in mass and five in orbital scale. Explaining the origin of this striking diversity remains a central challenge for planet formation theory, compounded by observational biases that limit access to Solar System-like regimes. Here we introduce architecture-agnostic metrics to uniformly analyse four independently defined samples of multi-planet systems, uncovering unifying patterns across their diversity. We identify a clear bimodality in system masses, dividing known architectures into two distinct families. The lower-mass family, predominantly hosted by subsolar-to-solar stars, exhibits tightly packed configurations with mass distributions consistent with the ‘peas-in-a-pod’ pattern and modal dynamical excitation comparable with that of the Solar System. By contrast, the high-mass family forms in metal-rich environments around solar-to-supersolar stars, displays gravitationally compact architectures and is an order of magnitude dynamically hotter than both the Solar System and the lower-mass counterparts. Their high level of dynamical excitation points to violent evolutionary pathways driven by global instabilities and planet–planet scattering. Together, these results show that the architectures of planetary systems are born from the combined influence of formation processes and host star properties. Signatures of these roots are preserved across the post-formation dynamical evolution that reshaped most known multi-planet systems.

articles.title: Near-infrared photochromic miniprotein enables photoacoustic molecular imaging of acute inflammation and intracellular antigens
articles.abstract: Using near-infrared photoswitchable photochromic genetically encoded probes, differential photoacoustic tomography (PAT) enables deep-tissue imaging with high resolution and sensitivity; however, current bacteriophytochrome-based probes are bulky multidomain proteins exceeding 55 kDa, which constrains their use for designing PAT molecular reporters. Here we engineer rsmiRFPnano, a compact cyanobacteriochrome-derived photoswitchable PAT probe. With a molecular weight below 19 kDa, rsmiRFPnano efficiently incorporates biliverdin, exhibits high extinction coefficients in both photochromic states and demonstrates robust performance in live cells. We established rsmiRFPnano-based reporters for NF-κB and AP-1 pathways, which display low basal activity and strong activation-dependent responses. These reporters effectively visualized acute inflammation using noninvasive PAT in vivo, further validated through cellular-level spatial omics mapping. We then created photoswitchable nanobody probes, rsNIR-Fbs, stabilized upon antigen binding and rapidly degraded otherwise, enabling selective photoacoustic immuno-imaging of intracellular antigens in vivo. Together, these results establish rsmiRFPnano as an ultracompact and versatile platform for molecular PAT.

articles.abstract: Quantum dots — semiconductor nanocrystals whose optical and electronic properties can be tuned by controlling their size, composition and surface chemistry — have found commercial success for display technologies. Their transition from nanophotonics research into an applied modern nanotechnology exemplifies the bottlenecks that many emerging technologies must overcome on the path to commercialization.

articles.title: How lipid nanoparticles evolved from models of biological membranes to systems that enable RNA therapeutics
articles.abstract: Curiosity-driven studies of lipid organization and lipid asymmetry in biological membranes led to scalable methods for making liposomes, efficient loading of drugs and ionizable cationic lipids. In turn, these advances led to lipid nanoparticles enabling the RNA medicine Onpattro and the COVID-19 mRNA vaccines, and they are now facilitating gene therapies that can potentially treat most human diseases.

articles.title: How single-atom catalysis transformed from a nanoscience curiosity into a new paradigm for heterogeneous catalysis
articles.abstract: Single-atom catalysis has reshaped heterogeneous catalysis by shifting its central focus from surface and interface to isolated atom-centred active sites. This transition establishes a new paradigm for understanding reactivity, integrating experiments and theory, and advancing heterogeneous catalysis from empirical observations toward a more predictive and precise science.

articles.title: Degenerative cervical myelopathy: early detection and the potential for preventing disability
articles.abstract: Degenerative cervical myelopathy (DCM), the most common non-traumatic spinal cord injury, is a prevalent, progressive, and highly disabling neurological disease, causing heterogeneous impairment ranging from sensory loss and impaired hand dexterity to gait, balance, and autonomic dysfunction. Disability often persists despite surgical decompression, and untreated disease can progress to irreversible neurological injury, including tetraplegia. Current clinical management is largely reactive, with diagnosis and intervention typically only after neurological deterioration has become clinically apparent and radiographic evidence of cervical myelopathy is established. Advances in multimodal diagnostics over the past 5 years are now enabling the detection of subtle spinal cord injury, biological disease activity, and subclinical neurodegeneration before overt clinical disability. Quantitative spinal cord MRI, advanced neurophysiological assessments, dynamic biomechanical metrics, and sensitive functional testing provide complementary tools for early detection, risk stratification, and prognostication. Together, these approaches are redefining DCM as a disease that should be managed proactively. Evidence supports decompressive surgery in patients with moderate-to-severe disease, whereas in milder disease or in spinal stenosis that might develop into DCM, the management of patients should be interdisciplinary, with active surveillance to detect early deterioration or decompressive surgery in selected cases. Improved prediction of disease trajectories and clearer evidence on long-term outcomes could enable selective earlier intervention and help to prevent neurological disability.

articles.title: Emerging landscape of antibody–drug conjugates in lung cancer: a clinical review
articles.abstract: Lung cancer is a heterogeneous disease, and while targeted therapies and immunotherapies have improved patient outcomes, 5-year overall survival remains poor at approximately 20%. Antibody–drug conjugates (ADCs) target tumors using a targeted antibody that delivers a cytotoxic payload with clinically proven antitumor activity, and over a dozen ADCs are under consideration for solid tumors. Recent clinical trial data in metastatic non-small cell lung cancer have led to FDA approval of three ADCs: trastuzumab deruxtecan for patients with human epidermal growth factor receptor 2-mutated disease, telisotuzumab vedotin for MET-overexpressing tumors, and datopotamab deruxtecan for patients with epidermal growth factor receptor-mutated disease. In this article, we review the trajectory of individual ADC targets in lung cancer, describe the latest clinical trial results, and discuss future innovations in ADC therapies and potential mechanisms of resistance.

Applications of Single-Atom Alloys in Thermal, Electro, and Photo Catalysis
articles.abstract: Single-atom alloys (SAAs) are an emerging class of heterogeneous catalysts that maximize atom efficiency by embedding isolated reactive metal atoms within a host metal surface, creating well-defined active sites. Atomic isolation imparts unique catalytic properties, including high selectivity, resistance to poisoning, coking, and sintering, and in some cases the ability to circumvent conventional scaling relationships that limit traditional catalysts. This article focuses on progress in the SAA field since our 2020 review (Chem. Rev.2020, 120, 12044−12088.), while incorporating earlier foundational studies where relevant. We first examine the fundamental principles governing SAA formation, stability, electronic structure, reactivity, and selectivity, drawing on insights from experimental single-crystal model systems and theoretical studies. We then review the application of SAAs in a wide range of industrially important reactions, including hydrogenation, dehydrogenation, selective oxidation, water–gas shift, Fischer–Tropsch synthesis, and dry reforming, among others. Beyond thermal catalysis, SAAs demonstrate great promise in electrocatalysis and plasmon-driven chemistry. Their structurally simple active sites have also enabled the rational design of novel catalysts and promoters that challenge conventional catalytic intuition. Looking ahead, recent advances in computing, including machine-learning potentials, offer the opportunity to explore vast compositional spaces and discover new alloy chemistries for challenging reactions using the SAA concept.

articles.title: Nonaqueous Redox Flow Batteries: Opportunities and Challenges for Sustainable Energy Storage
articles.abstract: Redox flow batteries (RFBs) have emerged as promising electrochemical energy storage technologies for long-duration stationary applications. Although aqueous RFBs represent the most commercially mature class, they are inherently limited by a narrow electrochemical stability window and high temperature sensitivity. Nonaqueous RFBs (NRFBs) expand the accessible voltage and temperature ranges, offering a promising route toward high-energy-density storage for long-duration and extreme-environment applications. However, their practical deployment remains impeded by several challenges, including high costs, insufficient power density, limited cycling stability, and safety concerns. This review offers a systematic synthesis of recent advances in key NRFB components, encompassing solvents, supporting electrolytes, membranes, electrodes, and redox-active molecules. We also highlight emerging methodologies expected to accelerate development, including machine-learning-enabled screening, advanced characterization, and life cycle assessment. Finally, this review compares aqueous and nonaqueous systems from commercialization and sustainability perspectives. Collectively, this review aims to advance design principles and optimization strategies for NRFBs, providing guidance for next-generation low-cost, high-energy-density flow battery technologies.
